The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 1:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Praise be to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "Praise be to God," He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: complete praise belongs to God alone, who has no partner, to the exclusion of all rivals (andad) and gods, and to the exclusion of whatever else is worshipped by the disbelievers among His creatures, such as idols and images.

This statement is in the form of a report, but it is meant as a command. It means: "Devote praise and thanksgiving to the One who created you, O people, and created the heavens and the earth, and do not associate with Him in that anyone or anything [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "ahadan shay'an" (anyone, a thing), but the context requires what is adopted here.]], for He is the one who deserves your praise because of His bounties upon you and His blessings toward you, not those you worship besides Him and make into partners from among His creation."

* *

We have already explained the distinction between the meaning of "praise" (hamd) and "thanks" (shukr), with its evidence, earlier. [[See the explanation of "hamd" above, 1: 135–141.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿and made the darknesses and the light﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Praise be to God, who created the heavens and the earth, and who darkened the night and lit up the day, as:

13040 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "and made the darknesses and the light," he said: "The darknesses" is the darkness of the night, and "the light" is the light of the day.

13041 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: As for His words, "Praise be to God, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light," He created the heavens before the earth, the darkness before the light, and the Garden before the Fire.

* *

If someone says: What then is the meaning of His saying "made" (ja'ala)?

It is said: The Arabs use it as a vessel for a report and for an action, so they say "ja'altu af'alu kadha" (I began to do such-and-such) and "ja'altu aqumu wa aq'udu" (I began to stand and sit), indicating by "ja'altu" the continuity of the action, just as one says "alaqtu af'alu kadha" (I began to do such-and-such), not that it is in itself an action. The evidence for this is the speaker's saying "ja'altu aqumu," where there is no "making" there other than standing, and he only indicated by "ja'altu" the connection and continuity of the action. [[See what I wrote on the report no. 8317, vol. 7: 547, note 6, and then the report no. 12834, vol. 11: 128, note 1, concerning His saying "fadhahaba yanzilu" and His saying "tadhhabu fatakhtalitu," where I called these "words of assistance." Abu Ja'far expressed this meaning well, precisely and memorably.]]

Among that is the saying of the poet: [[I do not know who said it.]]

"You claimed that you would travel alone, while death was closing in on the path of the capable one...

So make your oath's release, for the breaking of an oath falls only on the sinful wicked one." [[I have not found these two verses in the books available to me, though I recall having read them before, and I do not know where. In the printed edition the first verse read: "wa za'amta annaka sawfa tasluku qadiran... wal-mawtu mutta si'an tariqi qadiri," which is meaningless. The manuscript had it thus: "wa za'amta annaka sawfa tasluka mal ra... al-mawtu mulsa'an tariqi qadiri." I preferred the reading as given here, as I conjecture its meaning: he was a man who wished to go alone on his way and swore that he would do so, so his companion mocked him and said what he said. "Fard" means alone, cut off from your companion and friend. "Wal-mawtu muktani'" means death has drawn near and is about to overtake you; it is said "kana'a al-mawtu wa iktana'a," meaning it drew near and approached. The rajiz said: "And the mother of al-Luhaym drew near and approached." "Umm al-Luhaym" is a kunya for death, because it devours everything. This is my own effort to correct the verse, until another source is found.]] He says: "fa'-ja'al tahallul" meaning: "release (something) bit by bit" — not that there is a "making" apart from the releasing. Thus every "ja'l" in speech is only an indication of an action that has continuity, not that it has any share in the meaning of action.

* *

So His saying "and made the darknesses and the light" means only: He darkened their night and lit up their day.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, marvelling at His believing servants concerning the disbelievers among His servants, and arguing against the unbelievers: Indeed, the God whose praise is obligatory upon you, O people, is the One who created the heavens and the earth, who made from them your livelihood and your sustenance, and the sustenance of your livestock, by which your life is sustained. From the heavens He sends down rain upon you, and in them the sun and the moon run in succession and alternation for your benefit. From the earth grows the grain by which you are nourished, and the fruits in which is your delight, along with other matters in which lie your interests and benefits. And those who deny God's favour upon them by what He has bestowed on them of creating all this for them and for you, O people — "ya'dilun" (ascribe equals) to "their Lord," who did that and brought it into being — they make a partner for Him in their worship of Him, worshipping alongside Him gods, rivals, idols and images, none of which shares with Him in creating any of this, nor in bestowing these favours upon them; rather He alone is singular in all of it, while they associate others with Him in worship. Glory be to God, how eloquent is this proof, and how concise its admonition, for whoever reflects upon it with reason and contemplates it with understanding!

* *

It has been said that it is the opening of the Torah.

Those who said so:

13042 - Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Aziz ibn Abd al-Samad al-Ammi narrated to us, from Abu Imran al-Juni, from Abdullah ibn Rabah, from Ka'b, who said: The opening of the Torah is the opening of "al-An'am": "Praise be to God, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light; then those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord." [[Report 13042: Abd al-Aziz ibn Abd al-Samad al-Ammi, Abu Abd al-Samad, a trustworthy and retentive transmitter, one of the teachers of Ahmad, whose narrations were recorded by the authors of the six canonical books. Biographized in al-Tahdhib.

Abu Imran al-Juni is Abd al-Malik ibn Habib al-Azdi, trustworthy, passed as no. 80.

Abdullah ibn Rabah al-Ansari, trustworthy, passed as no. 4810.

Ka'b is Ka'b al-Ahbar, famous for his Israelite reports.]]

13043 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Hubab narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, from Abu Imran al-Juni, from Abdullah ibn Rabah, from Ka'b, the like of it; and he added to it: "and the seal of the Torah is the seal of Hud."

* *

It is said, regarding the equating of one thing with another: "I equated this with that" (adaltu hadha bi-hadha) when you made it equal to it, "adl" (equivalence). As for judgment, when you are just in it, you say "adaltu fihi a'dulu 'adlan" (I was just in it). [[See the explanation of "al-'adl" above, 2: 35 / 11: 43, 44.]]

Experts in interpretation have said things similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of His words "ya'dilun" (ascribe equals).

Those who said so:

13044 - Ibn Muhammad Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "ya'dilun," he said: they associate (partners).

* *

Then the experts in interpretation differed about who is meant by this:

Some of them said: It refers to the People of the Book.

Those who said so:

13045 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Ibn Abza, who said: A man from the Kharijites came to him reciting this verse: "Praise be to God, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light; then those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord." He said to him: Do not those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord? He said: Yes! The man then left him. A man from the people said to him: O Ibn Abza, this man wanted to interpret this in a way other than this! He is a Kharijite! He said: Bring him back to me. When he came, he said: Do you know concerning whom this verse was revealed? He said: No. He said: It was revealed concerning the People of the Book. Go, and do not place it outside its proper meaning. [[Report 13045: Ya'qub al-Qummi is Ya'qub ibn Abd Allah al-Ash'ari al-Qummi, trustworthy, passed as nos. 617, 8158, 8269.

Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah al-Khuza'i al-Qummi, trustworthy, passed as nos. 87, 617, 4347, 7269.

Ibn Abza is Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza al-Khuza'i, trustworthy, passed as nos. 9656, 9657, 9672.

The Kharijite questioner intended by his question to use the verse as evidence for declaring the People of the Qibla to be disbelievers, regarding the matter of the arbitration of Ali ibn Abi Talib. This was the view of the Kharijites.]] Others said: Rather, it refers to the polytheists, the worshippers of idols.

Those who said so:

13046 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "then those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord," he said: [These are: the people of Sarahiyah.] [[In the printed edition: "hā'ulā' ahl sarāha" (these are the people of sarahah), which is words without meaning. The manuscript has what is given in brackets; I was unable to decipher its symbols, so perhaps it will be found later in a book other than those in our hands, and its correctness will be shown.]]

13047 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "then those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord," he said: They are the polytheists.

13048 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words "then those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord," he said: The gods they worshipped, they made equal to God. He said: God has no equal nor rival, nor does He have gods with Him, nor has He taken a consort or a son.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions in my view is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, informed that those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord, thereby encompassing all disbelievers, and He did not single out some of them over others. All of them are included: their Jews, their Christians, their Magians, and the idol-worshippers among them and among others of the various kinds of disbelief.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 2:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿It is He who created you from clay﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, "It is He who created you from clay," may His remembrance be exalted, He means: that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, made their night dark and their day bright, and then the disbelievers disbelieved in Him despite His bounties upon them [[In the printed edition: "fa-kafara bihi" (then they disbelieved in Him). As for the manuscript, it contains what I have recorded, except that it was written "thumma kafara bihi" (then disbelieved in Him) with "thumma" joined to "kafara," and this is one of the oddities of copying and the subtleties of scribes.]] and set up as equals with Him those who neither benefit them nor harm them. "It is He who created you, O people, from clay." He means by this, may His remembrance be exalted: that mankind are the offspring of the one who created them from clay, and so this was expressed in the form of address to them, since they were His offspring.

* *

And in accordance with what we have said, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

13049. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "It is He who created you from clay," the beginning of creation: Allah created Adam from clay.

13050. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "It is He who created you from clay," he said: He is Adam.

13051. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: As for "created you from clay," it is Adam.

13052. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumaylah narrated to us, from Ubayd ibn Sulayman, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, who said: Adam was created from clay, and mankind was created from an extract of water, despised.

13053. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "created you from clay," he said: Adam was created from clay, then we were created from Adam when He took us from his loins.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Then He decreed a term, and a named term is with Him﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: The meaning of His saying, "Then He decreed a term," is: then He decreed for you, O people, "a term." That is the period between your creation and your death. "And a named term is with Him" is the period between your death and your being resurrected.

Mention of those who said that:

13054. Ibn Wakī' and Hannad ibn al-Sarri narrated to us, both saying: Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from al-Hasan regarding His saying: "decreed a term," he said: what is between one's creation and one's death. "And a named term is with Him," he said: what is between one's death and one's resurrection. [[The report 13054: "Waki'" is "Waki' ibn al-Jarrah ibn Malih al-Ru'asi." His father "al-Jarrah ibn Malih al-Ru'asi" have both passed in various places. And "Abu Bakr al-Hudhali" is disputed regarding his name; it is said he is "Salma ibn Abd Allah ibn Salma," and it is said "Rawh ibn Abd Allah." It has passed under numbers 597 and 8376, and he is weak.]]

13055. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "Then He decreed a term, and a named term is with Him," he used to say: the term of your life until you die, and the term of your death until you are resurrected. So you are between two terms from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted.

13056. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumaylah narrated to us, from Ubayd ibn Sulayman, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim: "decreed a term and a named term is with Him," he said: He decreed the term of death, and every soul has its term, death. He said: And Allah will not delay a soul when its term comes. "And a named term is with Him," meaning: the term of the Hour, the passing of the world, and the arrival before Allah.

* *

And others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Then He decreed the world, and with Him is the Hereafter.

Mention of those who said that:

13057. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "a term," he said: the world. "And a named term is with Him," the Hereafter.

13058. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from Zakariyya ibn Ishaq, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "decreed a term," he said: the Hereafter is with Him, "and a named term," the world.

13059. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "a term," he said: the Hereafter is with Him, "and a named term," he said: the world.

13060. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "a term," he said: the Hereafter is with Him, "and a named term," he said: the world.

13061. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah and al-Hasan: "Then He decreed a term and a named term is with Him," both said: He decreed the term of the world, from the time He created you until you die, "and a named term is with Him," the Day of Resurrection.

13062. Hannad narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Mujahid and Ikrimah: "Then He decreed a term and a named term is with Him," he said: He decreed the term of the world, "and a named term is with Him," he said: it is the term of the Resurrection.

13063. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Mujahid and Ikrimah: "Then He decreed a term," he said: death, "and a named term is with Him," the Hereafter.

13064. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah and al-Hasan regarding His saying: "decreed a term and a named term is with Him," both said: He decreed the term of the world, from the day You were created until you die, "and a named term is with Him," the Day of Resurrection.

13065. Ibn Wakī' and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: "decreed a term," he said: the term of the world, "and a named term is with Him," he said: the Resurrection.

13066. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: "Then He decreed a term, and a named term is with Him," meaning: the term of death, "and the named term," the term of the Hour and standing before Allah.

13067. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "decreed a term," he said: As for "decreed a term," it is the term of death, "and a named term is with Him," the Day of Resurrection.

* *

And others said concerning that:

13068. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "Then He decreed a term and a named term is with Him," he said: As for His saying, "decreed a term," it is sleep, in which the soul is seized, then it returns to its owner at the time of wakefulness. "And a named term is with Him," it is the term of a person's death.

* *

And others said:

13069. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us regarding His saying: "It is He who created you from clay, then decreed a term, and a named term is with Him, then you doubt," he said: He created Adam from clay, then created us from Adam, took us from his loins, then took the term and the covenant in one named term in this worldly life.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings in my view is the saying of the one who said: its meaning is: then He decreed the term of the worldly life, "and a named term is with Him," and it is the term of the Resurrection with Him.

We said this is more correct because He, may His remembrance be exalted, alerted His creatures to the place of His proof against them from themselves, saying to them: O people, the One whom your disbelievers set up as equal to the gods and rivals, is the One who created you, originated and produced you from clay, made you forms, bodies, living beings, after you were clay, inanimate, then decreed the terms of your lives for your annihilation and death, that He might return you to dust and clay as you were before He produced and created you; "and a named term is with Him" for your restoration alive and as bodies, as you were before your death. [[See the interpretation of "al-ajal" in what has preceded: 5:7; 6:43; 76; 8:548. And the interpretation of "musamma" in what has preceded: 6:43.]] This is similar to His saying: "How can you disbelieve in Allah, when you were dead and He gave you life? Then He will cause you to die, then give you life again, then to Him you will be returned" [Surah al-Baqarah: 28].

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Then you doubt﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His remembrance is exalted, saying: Then you doubt the power of the One who was able to create the heavens and the earth, and to darken the night and illuminate the day, and to create you from clay until He made you in the form you are in, [[In the printed edition: "wa-ala insha'ihi" with an added waw, which is a corruption and a mistake of grammar, not understanding the context of Abu Ja'far; for his saying "ala insha'ihi iyyakum" is connected to "thumma antum tashukkuna fi qudrati man qadara..." i.e., you doubt the power of the one who did that, regarding His producing you.]] regarding His producing you after your death and annihilation, and His bringing you into being after your non-existence.

* *

And "al-miryah" in the speech of the Arabs is doubt. I have explained that with its evidence in other places previously, in a way that suffices without repeating it. [[See the interpretation of "al-imtira'" in what has preceded: 3:190, 191; 6:472.]]

* *

And:

13070. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "Then you doubt," he said: doubt. He said: And he recited the saying of Allah: "in doubt concerning it" [Surah Hud: 17], he said: in doubt about it.

13071. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Then you doubt," similarly.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And He is Allah in the heavens and on the earth. He knows your secret and your open, and He knows what you earn﴾ (3).

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: Indeed, the One who alone deserves worship, to whom no one else is fitting, the One who is owed by you, O people, sincere praise for His bounties upon you, the One whom your disbelievers set equal to others, is Allah, who is in the heavens and in the earth, who knows your secret and your open, so nothing is hidden from Him. He says: Your Lord, who is owed praise by you and whose worship you must sincerely render, is this One whose attribute is such, not one who cannot bring you harm or benefit, nor one who does anything, nor one who can repel from himself an evil directed at him.

* *

As for His saying: "and He knows what you earn," He says: He knows what you do and what you commit, so He records that against you in order to recompense you for it when you return to Him. [[See the explanation of "kasb" above, 10: 297, footnote 2, and the references there.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And there does not come to them any sign from the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it﴾ (4).

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: No sign of their Lord's signs comes to these disbelievers, who set their idols and gods equal to their Lord, "from the signs of their Lord," meaning a proof, a sign, and an indication from the proofs of their Lord, His indications and markers of His oneness and of the reality of your prophethood, O Muhammad, and the truth of what I brought them from Me, "except that they turn away from it," meaning: except that they turn away from it, that is, from the sign, so they refuse to accept it and to acknowledge what it testified to as true and what it indicated as valid, out of ignorance of Allah and deluded by His forbearance toward them. [[See the explanation of "i'rad" (turning away) above, 9: 310, footnote 1, and the references there.]]

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And He is Allah in the heavens and on the earth. He knows your secret and your open, and He knows what you earn﴾ (3).

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: Indeed, the One who alone deserves worship, to whom no one else is fitting, the One who is owed by you, O people, sincere praise for His bounties upon you, the One whom your disbelievers set equal to others, is Allah, who is in the heavens and in the earth, who knows your secret and your open, so nothing is hidden from Him. He says: Your Lord, who is owed praise by you and whose worship you must sincerely render, is this One whose attribute is such, not one who cannot bring you harm or benefit, nor one who does anything, nor one who can repel from himself an evil directed at him.

* *

As for His saying: "and He knows what you earn," He says: He knows what you do and what you commit, so He records that against you in order to recompense you for it when you return to Him. [[See the explanation of "kasb" above, 10: 297, footnote 2, and the references there.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And there does not come to them any sign from the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it﴾ (4).

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: No sign of their Lord's signs comes to these disbelievers, who set their idols and gods equal to their Lord, "from the signs of their Lord," meaning a proof, a sign, and an indication from the proofs of their Lord, His indications and markers of His oneness and of the reality of your prophethood, O Muhammad, and the truth of what I brought them from Me, "except that they turn away from it," meaning: except that they turn away from it, that is, from the sign, so they refuse to accept it and to acknowledge what it testified to as true and what it indicated as valid, out of ignorance of Allah and deluded by His forbearance toward them. [[See the explanation of "i'rad" (turning away) above, 9: 310, footnote 1, and the references there.]]

**The interpretation of His saying:** ﴿But they have denied the truth when it came to them. So there will come to them the news of that which they used to mock.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: These who associate others with God have denied the truth when it came to them. That "truth" is Muhammad (ﷺ) [[See the explanation of "al-Haqq" above, vol. 10, p. 377, note 1, and the references there.]]. They denied him and rejected his prophethood when it came to them. God said to them, threatening them for their denial of him and their rejection of his prophethood: "So there will come to those who deny you, O Muhammad, from your people and others, the news of what they used to mock," meaning: there will come to them reports of their mockery of what they used to mock, namely My signs and proofs that I brought them [[See the explanation of "al-naba'" (news) above, vol. 10, p. 391, note 2, and the references there.

= And the explanation of "al-istihza'" (mockery) above, vol. 1, pp. 301–303.]] Then He fulfilled His threat against them when they persisted in their error and rebelled against their Lord, and He killed them with the sword on the day of Badr.

**The explanation of His words:** ﴿Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, generations We had established on the earth in ways We have not established for you, and We sent down abundant rain upon them from the sky and made rivers flow beneath them? Then We destroyed them for their sins and produced after them other generations.﴾ (6:6)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Have these deniers of My signs, these rejecters of your prophethood, not seen the multitude of those whom I destroyed before them of the generations, meaning the nations, whom I settled in the lands and the earth with a settling I did not give to you, and whom I gave in it what I did not give them?

As related to us:

13072. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words, "We established them on the earth in ways We have not established for you," he said: "We gave them what We did not give you."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: He sent rain upon them, and the trees brought forth their fruits for them, the earth gave them the yield of its plants, they hewed the rocks of its mountains, the sky poured its rains upon them, and springs of water gushed up from beneath them by My leave. Yet they were ungrateful for their Lord's blessing, disobeyed the messenger of their Creator, opposed the command of their Maker, and transgressed, until My word was fulfilled against them. So I seized them for what they had committed of their sins, and punished them for what their hands had earned, destroying some of them with the earthquake, some with the Cry, and others with various kinds of punishment.

* *

The meaning of His words, "And We sent down the sky upon them in abundant rain," is rain. By His words, "abundant" (mid-rar), He means copious and continuous. His words, "and produced after them other generations," mean: We brought into being, after those whom We destroyed, other generations, and We originated others besides them.

* *

If someone says: What is the sense of His words, "We established them on the earth in ways We have not established for you"? And who is being addressed by that? For the report at the beginning of the verse began about an absent group with His words, "Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them?"

It is said: The one addressed in His words, "in ways We have not established for you," is the same party reported about in His words, "Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them." However, the report contains the sense of speech, and its meaning is: Say, O Muhammad, to these people who denied the truth when it came to them: Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, generations whom We established on the earth in ways We have not established for you?

When the Arabs report a matter about an absent party and insert "qawl" (saying) into it, they do so: sometimes they direct the report toward the report about the absent, and sometimes toward direct address. You say: "I said to Abdullah: how generous he is," and "I said to Abdullah: how generous you are." And they sometimes report about him in the manner of reporting about an absent party, then return to address. And they report in the manner of addressing him, then return to reporting about the absent. This is abundant and widespread in their speech and poetry. We have mentioned some of this earlier, enough to dispense with repeating it here. [Refer to what preceded: 1:153–154 / 2:293, 294, 357, 388 / 3:170 / 6:564.]

* *

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say about this: It is as if He reported to the Prophet (ﷺ), then addressed him together with them. And He said: ﴿until, when you were in the ships and they sailed with them with a good wind﴾ (10:22), so He used the third-person form, and then addresses them, because they are the ones addressed.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And even if We had sent down to you a written scroll on paper, and they had touched it with their hands, those who disbelieved would have said, "This is not but obvious magic."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is an informing from God, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) concerning those people who ascribe equals to their Lord: idols, deities, and images. God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: How, then, would they comprehend the signs, or how would they reason out the falsity of what they persist in, namely disbelief in God and denial of your prophethood, by the proofs, signs, and evidences of God? For, due to their obstinacy against the truth and their remoteness from right guidance, even if I had sent down to you, O Muhammad, the revelation which I sent down to you along with My messenger, on a paper which they could see and touch with their hands [[See the explanation of "touching" (lams) above: 8:399 / 10:83.]], and look at it and read it from it, suspended between heaven and earth, with the reality of what you call them to and the truth of what you bring them of My monotheism and My revelation, those who ascribe equals to Me and associate others with Me in My unity would still have said: "This is not but obvious magic," meaning: what you have brought us is nothing but magic with which you have bewitched our eyes, having no reality or truth [[See the explanation of "magic" (siḥr) above: 2:436-442.]]. "Obvious" (mubin) means: it is evidently, to whoever reflects on and contemplates it, magic with no reality. [[See the explanation of "obvious" (mubin) above: 10:575, note 3, and the references there.]]

* *

Scholars of interpretation other than those mentioned have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

13073 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's saying, may His remembrance be exalted, "a written scroll on paper, and they touched it with their hands": He said: They touched it and looked at it, and still did not believe in it.

13074 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "And even if We had sent down to you a written scroll on paper, and they had touched it with their hands": He says: They witnessed it directly, "those who disbelieved would have said, 'This is not but obvious magic.'"

13075 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "And even if We had sent down to you a written scroll on paper, and they had touched it with their hands": He says: Even if We had sent down from heaven pages containing a writing, and they had touched it with their hands, it would only have increased them in denial.

13076 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "And even if We had sent down to you a written scroll on paper": the pages.

13077 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "on paper": He says: on a page, "and they touched it with their hands, those who disbelieved would have said, 'This is not but obvious magic.'"

**The explanation of His words:** ﴿And they say: "Why has an angel not been sent down to him? Even if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and they would not be reprieved."﴾ (6:8)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: These deniers of My signs, who ascribe equals and gods to Me, say, O Muhammad, to you, if you summon them to My Oneness and to acknowledgment of My Lordship, and bring them the signs and lessons that you have brought them, and argue against them with what you have argued with, by which you have cut off their excuse: "Why has an angel not been sent down to you from heaven in his own form," [[See the explanation of "lawla" (why not / if only) above, 2:552-553; 10:448; and what follows, p. 343.]] to confirm you in what you have brought us, and to bear witness to the truth of your claim that God has sent you to us? This is like what He, may His remembrance be exalted, said, reporting of the polytheists' statement to the Prophet of God ﷺ: ﴿And they say: "What is this messenger who eats food and walks about in the markets? Why has an angel not been sent down to him to be a warner with him?"﴾ (25:7).

As for His words, ﴿Even if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and they would not be reprieved﴾: this means, even if We had sent down an angel in response to what they asked, and then they disbelieved and did not believe in Me and My messenger, the punishment would have come to them immediately, without delay. [[See the explanation of "qada" (decided) above, 2:542; 4:195; 9:164.]] They would not have been given respite, so that the punishment would be postponed to allow them to return to repentance, [[See the explanation of "nazar" (to wait / respite) above, 3:264; 6:577.]] as I did with the nations before them who asked for signs and then disbelieved after those signs came: I hastened the vengeance and withheld respite. As related:

13078 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿even if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and they would not be reprieved﴾: he said, the punishment would have come to them.

13079 – Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿even if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and they would not be reprieved﴾: he said, that if We had sent down an angel to them, and then they did not believe, they would not be reprieved.

13080 – Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God, may His remembrance be exalted, ﴿Why has an angel not been sent down to him﴾ in his form, ﴿even if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided﴾: the Hour would have been established.

13081 – Ibn Wakī' related to us, from his father, saying: Abu Usamah related to us, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿the matter would have been decided﴾: he said, the Hour would have been established.

13082 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿even if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided﴾: he said, he says: if God had sent down an angel and then they did not believe, He would have hastened the punishment for them.

* *

Others said regarding this:

13083 – Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id related to us, saying: Bishr ibn Ammarah informed us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words, ﴿even if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and they would not be reprieved﴾: they both said, if an angel had come to them in his form, they would have died, and would not have been delayed even for the blink of an eye.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 9:

The explanation of His words: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And if We had made Our messenger to these deniers of Me, who say, "Why was not an angel sent down to Muhammad to confirm him?", an angel who would descend to them from the heaven, bearing witness to the truth of Muhammad ﷺ and commanding them to follow him, ﴿We would have made him a man﴾, meaning: We would have made him in the form of a man from among mankind, because they are not able to see an angel in his own form. He means: Since that is so, it makes no difference whether We send down to them an angel or a human being, for if We sent down an angel to them, he would come in the form of a human being, and My proof against them in both cases stands firm: that you are truthful, and that what you have brought them is true.

* *

Some of the people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said.

Those who said so:

13084 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Umara narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man", meaning: He would not have come to them except in the form of a man, because they cannot bear to look at the angels.

13085 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man", in the form of a man, in the creation of a man.

13086 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʻ narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: "And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man", he says: If We had sent to them an angel, We would have made him in the form of Adam. [[In the printed edition: "Adami", and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

13087 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: "And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man", he says: in the form of a human being.

13088 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, the like of it.

13089 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man", he said: We would have made that angel in the form of a man, and We would not have sent him in the form of the angels.

* *

The explanation of His words: ﴿And We would have confused them as they confuse﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "And We would have confused them", He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: If We had sent down an angel from the heaven confirming you, O Muhammad, bearing witness for you before these deniers of Me, who reject Your signs as to the reality of Your prophethood, and We had made him in the form of a man from the sons of Adam, since they cannot endure seeing an angel in the form in which I created him, the matter would have been confused for them, so that they would not know whether he was an angel or a human being! Thus they would not be certain that he was an angel, nor would they believe in him, and they would say: "This is not an angel!" And We would have confused for them what they confuse for themselves regarding the reality of your matter and the soundness of your proof and your witness to your prophethood.

* *

It is said of it: "I confused the matter for them, confusing it (albisuhu labsan)", meaning: I mixed it up for them; and "I put on the garment, wearing it (alabisu labsan)", and "al-labus" is the name of garments. [[See the explanation of "al-labs" above, 1:567–568, 6:503–505, and the explanation of "al-libas" above, 1:567–568, 3:489–490.]]

* *

Those people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said. [[See another report on the explanation of this verse above, number 882 (vol. 1, p. 567), which he did not mention among the explanatory reports; it is one of the ways in which he abbreviated his tafsir.]]

13089 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: "And We would have confused them as they confuse", he says: We would have made them confused, obscuring the matter for them.

13090 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "And We would have confused them as they confuse", he says: No people confuse themselves except that Allah confuses them. And confusion (al-labs) is only from people.

13091 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And We would have confused them as they confuse", he says: We would have made them confused regarding what they confuse for themselves.

* *

Another report has also been transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas on this, namely:

13092 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: "And We would have confused them as they confuse", he said: They are the People of the Book, who departed from their religion and denied their messengers, and this is the distortion of speech from its places.

13093 - I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak regarding His words: "And We would have confused them as they confuse", meaning: the distortion; they are the People of the Book, who divided their books and their religion, and denied their messengers, so Allah confused for them what they had confused for themselves.

* *

We have already explained earlier that these verses from the beginning of the surah are, regarding the matter of the polytheists who worship idols, more fitting than regarding the matter of the People of the Book, Jews and Christians, sufficiently so that it need not be repeated. [[See what has preceded, p. 254.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 10:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And indeed, messengers before you were mocked, but those who mocked them were encompassed by that which they used to mock.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), consoling him with His threat to those who mock him, a retribution for the harm of mockery and disparagement of him concerning God that he encounters from them: "Be at ease, O Muhammad, regarding what you encounter from these mockers of you, those who make light of your right concerning Me and concerning obedience to Me. Proceed with what I have commanded you of calling to My Oneness, acknowledging Me, and submitting to My obedience. For if they persist in their error and insist on remaining in their disbelief, We shall deal with them in the way of their predecessors from among the other nations: by hastening retribution upon them and the descent of punishments upon them. Nations before you mocked messengers whom We sent to them with the like of what We sent you to your people, and they did to them the like of what your people did to you." ="But those who mocked them were encompassed by that which they used to mock," meaning by His words "encompassed" (fa-haqa): it descended upon and surrounded those who ridiculed their messengers ="that which they used to mock," that is, the punishment they used to scoff at and deny would befall them as their messengers warned them.

* *

It is said of it: "This matter encompasses them (haqa bihim hadha al-amr yahiqu bihim haqqan wa-huyuqan wa-hayaqanan)."

* *

Similar to what we have said regarding this, a group of the people of interpretation said.

Mention of those who said that:

13094- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "But those who mocked them were encompassed" — from the messengers — ="by that which they used to mock," meaning: the punishment they had mocked fell upon them.

**On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Say: "Travel through the earth and see what was the end of those who denied."﴾ (6:11)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His exalted remembrance says: "Say," O Muhammad, to these people who ascribe equals to Me, idols and rivals, who deny you and reject the truth of what I have brought them from Me: "Travel through the earth," meaning: roam through the lands of those who denied their messengers and rejected My signs before them, from among their peers and kinds of people. "Then see what was the end of those who denied," meaning: then look at how their denial brought upon them destruction, ruin, and the disgrace and shame of this world, and what befell them of the wrath of God against them, of annihilation, the ruin of their homes, and the erasure of their traces. So take warning from it, if your reason does not restrain you and the proofs of God against you do not deter you from the denial in which you persist [[The addition between the parentheses is necessary for the sentence to be sound.]]. Beware of the likes of their fate, and guard against what befell them befalling you.

* *

Qatadah used to say concerning this:

13095. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "Say: travel through the earth and see what was the end of those who denied," that God destroyed them, annihilated them, and then sent them to the Fire.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 12:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Say: To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth? Say: To Allah. He has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "Say", O Muhammad, to these who ascribe equals to their Lord: "To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth?" That is: To whom does the dominion of what is in the heavens and the earth belong? Then inform them that it belongs to Allah, who has subjugated everything and overpowered everything by His dominion and authority, not to the idols and rivals, nor to what they worship and take as gods among the images, which possess no power to benefit themselves and cannot repel harm from themselves.

As for His saying: "He has prescribed for Himself mercy", that is: He has decreed that He is merciful to His servants, that He does not hasten to punish them, and that He accepts their repentance and their return. [[See the explanation of "kataba" above, vol. 10, p. 359, note 1.]]

This is an address from Allah, exalted is He, inviting those who turn away from Him to turn toward Him in repentance.

Exalted is He says: Indeed, these who ascribe equals to Me and deny your prophethood, O Muhammad, if they repent and return, their repentance will be accepted, and I have decreed concerning My creation that My mercy encompasses all things, as in what has been narrated:

13096 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Dhakwan, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "When Allah finished creating, He wrote a book: 'Indeed My mercy precedes My wrath.'" [[The report 13096: its isnad is sound. It is a well-known hadith. "Dhakwan" is "Abu Salih". It was narrated by al-Bukhari (al-Fath 13: 325) through the route of Abu Hamza, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, with different wording, in a longer form. See the note of my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad on the Musnad, numbers 7297, 7491, 7520.]]

13097 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Abu Uthman, from Salman who said: When Allah, exalted is His remembrance, created the heavens and the earth, He created a hundred mercies, each mercy the filling of what is between the heaven and the earth. With Him are ninety-nine mercies, and He distributed one mercy among the creatures. By it they show compassion to one another, and by it the wild beasts and birds drink water. When that day comes [[In the printed edition: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, He limits them", and I have affirmed what is in the manuscript. The other sources mention what is in the printed edition. What is in the manuscript is permissible, for "that" refers to a known and familiar matter, namely the Day of Resurrection.]], Allah restricts them to the God-fearing and adds to them ninety-nine. [[The two reports 13097 and 13098: "Dawud" is "Dawud ibn Abi Hind", who has passed several times. "Abu Uthman" is "Abu Uthman al-Nahdi": "Abd al-Rahman ibn Mal ibn Amr ibn Adi al-Nahdi", a trustworthy Successor who lived in the Jahiliyya. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

13098 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Dawud, from Abu Uthman, from Salman, similarly, except that Ibn Abi Adi did not mention in his report: "and by it the wild beasts and birds drink water." [[The two reports 13097 and 13098 are as above.]]

13099 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Asim ibn Sulayman, from Abu Uthman, from Salman who said: "We find in the Torah two verses of mercy": that Allah created the heavens and the earth, then created a hundred mercies [or: made a hundred mercies] before He created the creatures. Then He created the creatures, placed among them one mercy, and kept ninety-nine mercies with Himself. He said: By it they show mercy to one another, by it they bestow gifts on one another, by it they show compassion, by it they visit one another [[In the manuscript, above "yatazawwarun", there is the letter (ta), indicating doubt or error. I do not know what he intended by this, and what is in the manuscript and the printed edition is the same as in al-Durr al-Manthur.]], by it the she-camel yearns, by it the cow lows [[In the printed edition: "tanti' al-baqara", and in al-Durr al-Manthur: "tantij al-baqara", which is an error. What is in the printed edition is correct in meaning: it is said "na'aja al-thawr yan'aju" when it roars. As for what is in the manuscript, it is also correct, and therefore I have affirmed it: it is said "thaajat al-baqara tathaj and tathuj, thawjan and thawaajan": it vocalized. The author of Lisan al-Arab said: "It may be pronounced with a hamza, and that is more well known. However, Ibn Duraid said: leaving out the hamza is higher."]], by it the sheep bleats [[It is said "ya'arat al-shah ta'ar ya'aran": it cried out.]], by it the birds follow one another, and by it the fish follow one another in the sea [[I am in doubt regarding his saying "tatabi' al-tayr" and "tatabi' al-hitan", but so it is in the printed edition and the manuscript, and it is a meaning close to correctness. See the following note.]]. When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah gathers that mercy together with what He has. His mercy is superior and more expansive.

13100 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Asim ibn Sulayman, from Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman, concerning His saying: "He has prescribed for Himself mercy", the verse. He said: "We find in the Torah two verses of mercy" — then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: [[In the printed edition: "except that he did not say", with "ma" added, because the statement was problematic for him, since what he said in this report is what he said in the earlier report. The apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is that the first is as I vocalized it there, "tatabi'" (with a fatha on the ta, a shadda on the second, and a fatha on the ta), and that this second one is "tatabi'" (with the second ta fatha, not shadda) by omitting one of the three ta's.]] "By it the birds follow one another, and by it the fish follow one another in the sea." [[The two reports 13099 and 13100 were recorded by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 3: 6, who said: "Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim recorded from Salman..." and mentioned the report.]]

13101 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar who said: Ibn Tawus said, from his father: When Allah, exalted is His remembrance, created the creatures, no thing was joined to another until He created a hundred mercies, placed one mercy among them, and so some of the creatures show compassion to others.

13102 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, the like of it.

13103 - Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar who said: al-Hakam ibn Aban informed me, from Ikrima, I think he traced it back, who said: When Allah, mighty and majestic, finishes the judgment among His creatures, He brings out a book from beneath the Throne in which is written: "Indeed My mercy precedes My wrath, and I am the Most Merciful of the merciful." He said: Then there will come out of the Fire the like of the people of Paradise — or he said "two like" the people of Paradise, and I do not know him to have said anything but "like," and as for "mithl" I have no doubt — written here, and al-Hakam pointed to his throat: "the freed ones of Allah." A man said to Ikrima: O Abu Abd Allah, but Allah says: "They wish to come out of the Fire, but they will not come out of it, and theirs is a lasting punishment" [Surah al-Ma'ida: 37]? He said: Woe to you! Those are its people, who are its people.

13104 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrima, I think he traced it back, who said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah brings out a book from beneath the Throne — then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: A man said: O Abu Abd Allah, what do you say about His saying: "They wish to come out of the Fire"? The rest of the report is like the report of Ibn Abd al-A'la.

13105 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih who said: I heard Abu Hurayra say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah decreed the creation, He wrote in a book which is with Him above the Throne: 'Indeed My mercy precedes My wrath.'" [[The report 13105 was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad with this isnad, number 8112, and its wording is: "has overcome My wrath." See the note of my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad on it there, and see the note on the earlier report, number 13096.]]

[[The report 13106 was recorded by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 3: 6, and he attributed it additionally to Abd ibn Humayd and Abu al-Shaykh.]]

[[The report 13108: "Muhammad ibn Awf ibn Sufyan al-Ta'i", the teacher of al-Tabari, has passed, under number 5445 and 12194. * *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿He will surely gather you on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This "lam" in His saying "la-yajma'annakum" is the lam of oath.

* *

Then the grammarians differed about what governs it. Some Kufan grammarians said: If you wish, make "the mercy" the end of the statement, then begin afresh with "la-yajma'annakum". He said: And if you wish, make it in the accusative position — meaning: "He has decreed that He will surely gather you" — as in His saying: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy, that whoever among you does evil in ignorance﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 54], meaning: "He has decreed that whoever among you..." He said: The Arabs say, regarding the particles with which the answer of an oath may be governed, with "an" with fatha and with "lam", "arsaltu ilayhi an yaqum" and "arsaltu ilayhi la-yaqumanna". He said: Likewise His saying: ﴿Then it seemed good to them, after they had seen the signs, to imprison him for a time﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 35]. He said: It is abundant in the Qur'an. Do you not see that if you said "it seemed good to them to imprison him", it would be correct? [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 328. This is the text of his statement.]] And some Basran grammarians said: The "lam" of "la-yajma'annakum" is in the accusative because the meaning of "kataba" [: decreed, obligated, and it has the meaning of an oath], [[The addition between the brackets I inferred from the context of the commentary so that the statement is coherent. It is missing from the manuscript and the printed edition.]] as if he said: "By Allah, He will surely gather you."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter in my opinion is that His saying "He has prescribed for Himself mercy" is the end of the statement, and that His saying "la-yajma'annakum" is a new independent statement. The meaning of the speech then becomes: Allah will surely gather you, O you who ascribe equals to Allah, to the Day of Resurrection about which there is no doubt, to take vengeance upon you for your disbelief in Him.

I only said this view is more correct than making "kataba" govern "la-yajma'annakum", because His saying "kataba" has already governed "the mercy", and it is not permissible for it to govern "la-yajma'annakum" as well, since it does not transitively take two objects.

* *

If someone says: What do you say about the reading of those who read: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy, that He﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 54], with fatha on "anna"?

It is said: That, when it is read thus, "anna" is an explanation of "the mercy" and a rendering of it. For the meaning of the speech is: He has prescribed for Himself mercy, that He will show mercy to [whoever repents] among His servants after committing evil in ignorance, and pardons, [[This addition in brackets is necessary for the statement to be coherent; I inferred it from the meaning of the verse. See what will come in its explanation, pp. 392, 393.]] and "the mercy" is rendered and its meaning explained by its description. And it is not a description of mercy that "He will gather you to the Day of Resurrection", so that it would explain it. Since that is the case, nothing remains except that it be put in the accusative by implying a repetition of "kataba" once more with it, and there is no need in the speech for that, so it is directed to what is not apparent in its surface.

As for the interpretation of His saying "about which there is no doubt", it means there is no doubt in it, that is, in the fact that Allah will gather you to the Day of Resurrection, assembling you all toward Him, and then every doer among you will be given the reward of what he did, whether good or evil.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Those who have lost themselves, they do not believe﴾ (12)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted is His remembrance, "those who have lost themselves", He means those who ascribe to Him idols and images as equals. The meaning: Allah will surely gather "those who have lost themselves", that is, those who destroyed themselves and defrauded themselves by claiming for Allah rivals and equals, and so ruined themselves by earning the wrath of Allah and His painful punishment in the Hereafter. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript it is "bi-ijabihim sakhat Allah", which is not correct; what I have affirmed is the right reading.]]

* *

The root of "khisar" is "ghabn" (defrauding). It is said of it: "khasara al-rajul fi al-bay'", when he was defrauded, as al-A'sha said:

He does not take a bribe in his judgment, and he does not care about the loss of the loser. [[His Diwan: 105, and Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu Ubayda 1: 187. Thus it came in the manuscript and printed edition as "khasar al-khasir", but the version in his Diwan and elsewhere is "ghabana al-khasir" with the ba' vocalized with fatha. What the lexicographers stated is that "al-ghabn" with fatha and sukun is in trade, and "al-ghabn" (with two fathas) is in opinion, meaning weakness of it. So what came in the version of al-A'sha's Diwan appears to be a poetic necessity, vocalizing the ba', which is sakin, to fatha. As for the version of Abu Ja'far, it is correct: it is said "khasira khasran" (with fatha then sukun) and "khasaran" (with two fathas).]]

This verse is from his poem satirizing Alqama ibn Ulatha and praising Amir ibn al-Tufayl; I have mentioned its story in verses passed before, among them 1: 474/2: 131/5: 477, 478. Before the verse: "You made me judge, so he decided between you, a bright one like the shining moon."

We have explained this in another place, which suffices instead of repeating it. [[See the explanation of "al-khisar" above, vol. 10, p. 409, note 3, and the references there.]]

* *

The position of "those who" in His saying "those who have lost themselves" is accusative, as an apposition to the "kaf and mim" in "la-yajma'annakum", as an explanation of it. For those who have lost themselves are those who were addressed by His saying "la-yajma'annakum".

* *

As for His saying "they do not believe", it means: "they", because of their destruction of themselves and their defrauding of its share, "do not believe", that is, they do not affirm the oneness of Allah, nor do they believe in His promise and threat, nor do they acknowledge the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 13:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And to Him belongs whatever dwells in the night and the day; and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: These who ascribe equals to God, the idols, will not believe, so that they would make monotheism sincere for Him, single Him out in obedience, and acknowledge His divinity, out of ignorance. "And to Him belongs whatever dwells in the night and the day": that is, to Him belongs the dominion of everything, for there is nothing among God's creation except that it dwells in the night and the day. It is thus known from this that its meaning is what we have described. "And He is the All-Hearing": that is, He hears what these polytheists say about Him, of their claim that He has a partner, and what others of His creatures say beside that [[In the printed edition: "min khilaf dhalik" (other than that), which differs from what is in the manuscript, through his bad opinion.]]. "The All-Knowing": of what they conceal within themselves and what they manifest with their limbs; nothing of that is hidden from Him. He counts it against them, so that He may pay every person the reward of what he has earned and the recompense for what he has done.

* *

The commentators have said things similar to what we have said regarding His words "dwells" (sakan).

Among those who said this:

13109 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "And to Him belongs whatever dwells in the night and the day" — he says: whatever settles/remains in the night and the day.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 14–15:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Say: Shall I take as a protector other than Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, while He feeds and is not fed?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "Say," O Muhammad, to these polytheists who equate idols and images with their Lord, and who reject your devotion of pure monotheism to your Lord, and who call to the worship of gods and idols: Shall I take as "a protector" other than Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, to seek His help and aid against calamities and misfortunes? [See the explanation of "al-wali" (protector) above, 10:424, footnote 1, and the references there.] As related:

13110 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "Say: Shall I take as a protector other than Allah?" He said: As for "the protector," it is the one they take as protector and acknowledge as Lord.

* *

"The Originator of the heavens and the earth" means: Shall I take as a protector something other than Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth? "The Originator of the heavens" is an attribute and description of "Allah," and for this reason it is in the genitive case. [See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:328, 329.]

By "Originator of the heavens and the earth" He means the one who brought them into being, initiated them, and created them, as related:

13111 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Mujahid, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: "I did not know what 'Originator of the heavens and the earth' meant until two Bedouin came to me disputing over a well, and one of them said to the other: 'I am the one who originated it (fatartuha),'" meaning: I initiated it.

13112 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "Originator of the heavens and the earth," he said: the Creator of the heavens and the earth.

13113 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words "Originator of the heavens and the earth," he said: the Creator of the heavens and the earth.

* *

It is said regarding this: "fatarahā Allah, yafturuhā and yafthiruhā, fatran and futuran" [This explanation of the meaning of "fatara" is extremely corrupt, and I have no doubt that some text has fallen out of it. I have left it as it is, fearing that there may be something in Abu Ja'far's text that the lexicographical books have not recorded. Whoever wishes to pursue this should consult the lexicons.] — and from it is His words: "Do you see any rifts?" (Surah al-Mulk: 3), meaning cracks and fissures. It is said "sword futar" when it has many cracks, and that is a defect in it. From it is the verse of 'Antarah:

"My sword is like the 'aqiqah, it is my ... weapon, neither notched nor futtar"

[From his poems, in Ash'ar al-Sitta al-Jahiliyyin: 384, and Amali Ibn al-Shajari 1:19, and al-Lisan (f-t-r) ('-q-q) (k-m-') (f-l-l), from his verses in which he threatened 'Umarah ibn Ziyad al-'Absi, who envied 'Antarah's bravery, showed contempt for him, and said to his people, the Banu 'Abs: "You have mentioned him too much, and I would love to meet him alone to relieve you of him and to show you that he is a slave!" 'Antarah replied: "Does your buttock shake its two wings for me... so that you kill me? Here I am, O 'Umarah!" ...]

From it is also said: "fatara the camel's tooth," when the flesh splits and comes out. From it is His words: "The heavens are almost torn apart from above them" (Surah al-Shura: 5), meaning they split and break apart.

* *

As for His words: "while He feeds and is not fed," it means: He provides sustenance to His creation and is not provided for, as related:

13114 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "while He feeds and is not fed," he said: He provides sustenance and is not provided for.

* *

It has been mentioned from some of them that they recited it: [In the printed and manuscript editions: "that he used to say that," which is a serious error; the correct reading is what I have recorded. These readings were mentioned by Ibn Khalawayh in Shawadhdh al-Qira'at: 36, attributing it to al-A'mash, and Abu Hayyan mentioned it in his Tafsir 4:85, 86, also attributing it to Mujahid, Ibn Jubayr, Abu Haywa, 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd, and Abu 'Amr in one narration from him.] ﴿and He feeds and is not fed﴾, meaning: He feeds His creation, and He does not eat. But there is no meaning to this, given how rarely it is recited that way.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Say: Indeed I have been commanded to be the first to submit, and do not be among the polytheists﴾ (14)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "Say," O Muhammad, to those who call you to take gods as protectors besides Allah, and who urge you to worship them: Shall I take as a protector other than Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, who provides for me and for others while no one provides for Him? Shall I take as a protector one who is a servant owned by Him and a creature created by Him? And say to them also: Indeed my Lord has commanded me "to be the first to submit," meaning: the first to submit to Him in servitude, and to humble myself to His command and prohibition, and to submit to Him from among the people of my age and time. "And do not be among the polytheists," meaning: And it was said to me: Do not be among those who associate partners with Allah, who make gods and rivals into partners.

[Placing "commanded" in place of "it was said to me" is because His word "commanded" means "it was said to me." So it is as if it were said: Say, it has been said to me: Be the first to submit, and do not be among the polytheists. He has therefore sufficed with mentioning "command" in place of mentioning "saying," since "command" is known to be a form of "saying."]

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Say: Indeed I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day﴾ (15)

He described it, may He be exalted, as "tremendous" because of the magnitude of its terror and the severity of its matter.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 16:

The explanation of His words: ﴿Whoever is spared from it on that Day, He has indeed shown him mercy. That is the manifest triumph.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed regarding the reading of this.

The majority of the reciters of Hijaz, Medina and Basra read it: مَنْ يُصْرَفْ عَنْهُ يَوْمَئِذٍ, with the "ya" vowelled with a damma and the "ra" with a fatha, meaning: whoever has the punishment turned away from him on that Day.

* *

The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it: ﴿مَنْ يَصْرِفْ عَنْهُ﴾, with the "ya" vowelled with a fatha and the "ra" with a kasra, meaning: whoever Allah turns the punishment away from on that Day.

* *

The more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of the one who reads ﴿يَصْرِفْ عَنْهُ﴾ with the "ya" vowelled with a fatha and the "ra" with a kasra, because of the evidence of His words "then He has indeed shown him mercy" confirming its soundness, and that the reading there is with the agent named. Had the reading of His words "man yusraf" been in the passive form, the correct wording for "fa-qad rahimahu" would have been "fa-qad ruhima," with its agent unnamed. The naming of the agent in "fa-qad rahimahu" is clear proof that it is likewise in "man yasrif 'anhu."

* *

Since this is the preferred reading, the meaning of the statement is: whoever Allah turns away from His creation the punishment on that Day, He has indeed shown him mercy, "and that is the manifest triumph." By His words "that," He means that Allah turning the punishment away from him on the Day of Resurrection and His mercy to him is "the triumph," i.e., deliverance from destruction and attainment of the object sought, "the manifest," meaning that which shows to whoever sees it that it is the attainment of the need and the reaching of what is sought. [See the explanation of "al-fawz" above, p. 245, note 2, and the references there.] [See the explanation of "mubin" above, p. 265, note 3, and the references there.]

In the same sense as what we have said regarding His words "whoever is spared from it on that Day," the people of interpretation said:

Mention of those who said that:

13115 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words "whoever is spared from it on that Day, He has indeed shown him mercy," he said: whoever has the punishment turned away from him.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And if Allah touches you with harm, there is none to remove it but He; and if He touches you with good, then He is over all things competent.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): O Muhammad, if Allah afflicts you [[See the explanation of "al-mass" (touching) earlier, 10:482, note 3, and the references there.]] with "harm", meaning: with hardship in your worldly life, and roughness and constraint in your livelihood, [[See the explanation of "al-darr" (harm) earlier, 7:157 / 10:334.]] then none will remove that from you except Allah, the One who commanded you to be the first of your people to submit to His command and prohibition, and to humble yourself before Him, rather than to what those who ascribe equals to Him call you to worship, namely the idols and images, and rather than everything else of His creation. "And if He touches you with good", meaning: and if He afflicts you with good, that is, with ease in living, abundance of provision, and multitude of wealth, so that you acknowledge that He has bestowed it upon you, "then He is over all things competent", meaning: Exalted is He, the Allah who has bestowed that upon you, is over all things competent. He is capable of benefiting you and of harming you, and He is capable of everything He wills; nothing He wills is beyond His power, and nothing He seeks is withheld from Him. He is not like the humiliated, contemptible gods, who have no power to bring benefit to themselves or to others, nor to ward off harm from themselves or from others. Exalted is He says: How then can you worship one such as this, or how is it that you do not devote worship sincerely and acknowledge Him to whom belong harm and benefit, reward and punishment, complete power, and manifest might?

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He is the Wise, the All-Aware﴾ (6:18)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying "And He," He, may His mention be exalted, means Himself. He says: "And Allah is the Dominant above His servants." [[In the printed edition: "And Allah is the Subduer" (al-qahir); I have adopted what is in the manuscript, which is the correct reading in the tafsir.]] By "the Subduer" (al-Qahir) He means the One who humbles and enslaves His creation, the One who is exalted above them. He said "above His servants" because He described Himself, may His mention be exalted, as subduing them, and it is a characteristic of every subduer over something that he is elevated above it.

The meaning of the statement, then, is: "And Allah is the Overpowering over His servants, the One who humbles them, exalted over them by His subjugating them, and by His creating them; so He is above them through His subduing them, while they are beneath Him." "And He is the Wise" means: Allah is Wise in His exaltedness over His servants, and in His subduing them by His power, and in all His management. "The All-Aware" means: (He is aware) of the benefits and harms of things, the One from whom the consequences and beginnings of matters are not hidden, in whose management no defect occurs, and into whose judgment no flaw enters. [[See the explanation of "al-Khabir" in the earlier lexical indexes, root (kh-b-r).]]

**The discussion on the interpretation of His words:** ﴿Say: "What thing is greatest as a testimony?" Say: "God is witness between me and you."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who deny and reject your prophethood from among your people: What thing is greater and mightier as a testimony? Then inform them that the greatest thing in testimony is "God," who cannot have in His testimony what may occur in the testimony of any other of His creatures of forgetfulness, error, mistake, and lying. [[The words between the brackets are necessary for the context.]] Then say to them: Indeed He, who is the greatest of things in testimony, is a witness between me and you, regarding who among us is the rightful and who the falsifier, and who among us is rightly guided in his deeds and words and who is foolish. We have accepted Him as judge between us.

* *

Those of the people of interpretation (ta'wil) who said the same as what we have said include:

We were told by a report from Muhammad ibn Amr, who said: Abu Asim told us, who said: Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God, Exalted is His remembrance: "What thing is greatest as a testimony?" He said: Muhammad was commanded to ask the Quraysh, then he was commanded to inform them, saying: "God is witness between me and you."

We were told by al-Muthanna, who said: Abu Hudhayfa told us, who said: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

* *
