The discussion on the interpretation of His words: ﴿And this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say to these polytheists who deny you: "God is witness between me and you," and "This Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you by it" of His punishment, and warn thereby whoever among the rest of mankind besides you it reaches, if they do not refrain from acting upon what is in it, and from making lawful what it makes lawful and unlawful what it makes unlawful, and from believing in all of it, that the vengeance of God will descend upon them. [[The word "descend" (nuzul) is in the accusative, the direct object of the preceding words: "and warn thereby whoever it reaches." See also the explanation of "revelation" (al-wahy) above, p. 217, note 1, and the references there.]]

Those of the people of interpretation said the same as what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so include:

We were told by Bishr, who said: Yazid told us, who said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His words: "What thing is greatest as a testimony? Say: God is witness between me and you. And this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you by it and whoever it reaches." It was related to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) used to say: O people, convey, even one verse from the Book of God, for whoever receives a verse from the Book of God has received the command of God, whether he takes it or leaves it. [[In the manuscript: "akhadhahu aw tarikahu" (he took it or left it), and it is possible to read it as "akhidhuhu aw tarikuhu" (the one who takes it or leaves it).]]

We were told by al-Hasan ibn Yahya, who said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words: "that I may warn you by it and whoever it reaches," that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: Convey from God; whoever receives a verse from the Book of God has received the command of God.

We were told by Hannad, who said: Waki' told us, and Ibn Waki' told us, who said: My father told us, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, regarding "that I may warn you by it and whoever it reaches," he said: Whoever the Qur'an reaches, it is as if he saw the Prophet (ﷺ). Then he recited: "And whoever it reaches—do you truly bear witness that there are other gods with God?"

We were told by Ibn Waki', who said: Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman told us, from Hasan ibn Salih, who said: I asked Layth: Has anyone remained whom the call has not reached? He said: Mujahid used to say: Wherever the Qur'an arrives, there is a caller and a warner. Then he recited: "that I may warn you by it and whoever it reaches—do you truly bear witness?"

We were told by al-Muthanna... (He said:) We were told by Muhammad ibn Amr, who said: Abu Asim told us, who said: Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "and whoever it reaches," refers to those among the non-Arabs and others who have embraced Islam.

We were told by al-Muthanna, who said: Abu Hudhayfa told us, who said: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

We were told by al-Muthanna, who said: Ishaq told us, who said: Khalid ibn Yazid told us, who said: Abu Ma'shar told us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b regarding His words: "that I may warn you by it and whoever it reaches," he said: Whoever the Qur'an reaches, Muhammad (ﷺ) has conveyed to him.

We were told by al-Muthanna, who said: Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, who said: Mu'awiya ibn Salih told me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "And this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you by it," meaning the people of Mecca; "and whoever it reaches," meaning: whoever this Qur'an reaches, it is a warner to him.

We were told by Yunus, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: I heard Sufyan al-Thawri narrating, whom I know only from Mujahid, that he said regarding His words: "And this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you by it": the Arabs; "and whoever it reaches": the non-Arabs.

We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, who said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi regarding "that I may warn you by it and whoever it reaches": as for "whoever it reaches," it is whoever the Qur'an reaches, to whom it is a warner.

We were told by Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you by it and whoever it reaches," he said: He says: Whoever the Qur'an reaches, I am his warner. And he recited: "O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you all" (Surah al-A'raf: 158). He said: So whoever the Qur'an reaches, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is his warner.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of this statement is: "that I may warn you by the Qur'an, O polytheists, and warn all of mankind whom the Qur'an reaches."

* *

"Man" (whoever) is in the accusative position as the object of the verb "warn" falling upon it, and "reaches" is in its relative clause. The pronoun "hu" (it) referring back to "man" in His words "reaches" has been dropped, because the Arabs use this with the relative clauses of "man," "ma," and "alladhi." [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an, vol. 1, p. 329.]]

* *

The discussion on the interpretation of His words: ﴿Do you truly bear witness that there are other gods with God? Say: "I do not bear witness." Say: "He is only one God, and I am innocent of what you associate."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say to these polytheists, who deny your prophethood and equate others with God as Lord: "Do you truly," O polytheists, "bear witness that there are other gods with God?" That is, do you bear witness that with Him there are other deities, from idols and images?

* *

He said "other" (ukhra), feminine, and did not say "ukhar" (masculine plural), and "gods" (alihah) is plural, because plurals take the feminine form, as He, Exalted, said: "What then of the former generations?" (Surah Ta-Ha: 51), and He did not say "al-awwal" or "al-awwalin." [[See the explanation of "other" (ukhra) above, vol. 3, p. 459 / vol. 6, p. 173. See also Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra', vol. 1, p. 329.]]

* *

Then He said to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Say," O Muhammad, "I do not bear witness," to what you bear witness: that there are other gods with God. Rather, I deny and reject that. "Say: He is only one God," that is, He is only one worshipped being, with no partner in what He deserves from His creatures of worship. "And I am innocent of what you associate," that is, say: And I am innocent of every partner you claim for God, and ascribe to His partnership, and worship alongside Him. I do not worship anything besides God, nor call upon any other as a god.

* *

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a specific group of Jews, by a chain not established as sound. That is what:

We were told by Hannad ibn al-Sari and Abu Kurayb, who both said: Yunus ibn Bukayr told us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, who said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, told me, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrima told me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Al-Nahhham ibn Zayd, Qardam ibn Ka'b, and Bahri ibn Umayr came and said: "O Muhammad, do you know of any god with God other than Him?" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: There is no god but God; I was sent with that, and to that I call! Then God, Exalted, revealed concerning them and their saying: "Say: What thing is greatest as a testimony? Say: God is witness between me and you," up to His words: "they will not believe." [[Report 13129: Sirat Ibn Hisham, vol. 2, p. 217, following the previous report no. 12284. This chain has been mentioned hundreds of times: it is Abu Ja'far's chain to Ibn Ishaq, and then from Ibn Ishaq to Ibn Abbas. This is the first time Abu Ja'far mentions that this chain has not been established as sound according to him, as he mentioned earlier.]]

**The interpretation of His saying:** ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recognize it as they recognize their own sons. Those who have lost their souls, they do not believe.﴾ (6:20)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "Those to whom We gave the Book," meaning the Torah and the Gospel, "recognize" that He is one God, not a plurality of gods, and that Muhammad is a prophet who has been sent, "as they recognize their sons."

His saying, "Those who have lost their souls," is a qualifying description of the first "those."

\* \*

By His saying, "They have lost their souls," He means that they destroyed them and cast them into the fire of Hell, by denying that Muhammad is a messenger sent by God, while they truly know this reality [see the explanation of "khasara" (to lose) earlier, p. 281, note 1, and the references there]. "So they do not believe" means: because of their loss of their own souls in this way, they do not believe.

\* \*

It has also been said that the meaning of "their losing their souls" is that every servant has a place in Paradise and a place in the Fire. When the Day of Resurrection comes, God gives the people of Paradise the places of the people of the Fire in Paradise, and gives the people of the Fire the places of the people of Paradise in the Fire. That is the loss of the losers among them, because they exchanged their places in Paradise for the places of the people of Paradise in the Fire, on account of their past disobedience to God and their wronging of themselves. This is the meaning of the saying of God, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿those who will inherit Paradise, the Firdaws; therein they will abide forever﴾ (23:11) [see the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:329, 230].

\* \*

In accordance with what we have said regarding the meaning of His saying, "Those to whom We have given the Book recognize it as they recognize their sons," the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken. [See the interpretation of a similar verse earlier, 3:187, 188, (Surat al-Baqarah 2:146).]

Those who said this:

13130. He related to us: Bishr ibn Mu'adh said, Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying, "Those to whom We have given the Book recognize it as they recognize their sons": they recognize that Islam is the religion of God and that Muhammad is the messenger of God, finding it written among them in the Torah and the Gospel.

13131. He related to us: al-Hasan ibn Yahya said, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah regarding His saying, "Those to whom We have given the Book recognize it as they recognize their sons": the Christians and the Jews recognize the Messenger of God in their Book as they recognize their sons.

13132. He related to us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn said, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi regarding "Those to whom We have given the Book recognize it as they recognize their sons" [meaning: the Prophet ﷺ], "as they recognize their sons" [because his description is with them in the Torah]. [The report 13132 is truncated in the printed edition and the manuscript; the addition in parentheses is from al-Durr al-Manthur 3:8, from al-Suddi's tafsir, through the narration of Abu al-Shaykh. It appears that this lacuna is old in the copies of Abu Ja'far's tafsir, and that al-Suyuti's copy was also truncated here, which is why this report is attributed only to Abu al-Shaykh and not to Ibn Jarir.]

13133. He related to us: al-Qasim said, al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj regarding His saying, "Those to whom We have given the Book recognize it as they recognize their sons": it means the Prophet ﷺ. He said: The people of Medina claimed, concerning the People of the Book who had embraced Islam, that they said: "By God, we recognize him better than we recognize our sons, because of the attribute and description which we find in the Book. As for our sons, we do not know what the women have produced!" [That is: they do not know whether their sons are truly theirs, from their own loins, or whether illegitimate intercourse has mixed with them. For the narration of this, see the report about 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and his question to 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, and God knows best its authenticity, in the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:329.]

The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah or denies His signs? Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.﴾ (6:21)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And who is more transgressive, more mistaken in action and more mistaken in speech, than "one who fabricates a lie against Allah," meaning: one who invents a false saying about Allah [[See the explanation of "al-iftira' (fabrication)" above, p. 136, note 2, and the references there.]] and originates a lie from himself against Him [["Ikhtaraqa," "iktalaqa," and "iftara" all mean to originate a lie. In the revelation: "And they attributed to Him sons and daughters without knowledge. Glorified is He and exalted above what they describe" (al-An'am: 100).]], so that he claims that He has a partner from among His creation and a god worshipped besides Him, as the idolaters who worship idols say, or attributes to Him a son or a companion, as the Christians say; "or denies His signs," meaning: or denies His proofs, indications and evidences which He gave to His messengers as confirmation of the truth of their prophethood, which the Jews denied [[See the explanation of "al-ayah (sign)" above in the linguistic indexes, root (ʼ-y-y).]]. "Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed," meaning: indeed, those who speak falsehood about Allah will not succeed, nor will they attain to remaining in the Gardens, nor will those who fabricate lies against Him and those who deny the prophethood of His prophets [[See the explanation of "al-falah (success)" above, p. 97, note 2, and the references there.]].

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 22–23:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And the day We shall gather them all together, then We shall say to those who associated others with Allah: "Where are your partners whom you used to claim?"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the exalted One's words is: Indeed these who fabricate lies against Allah and deny His signs will not prosper today in this world, nor on the day We gather them all together, meaning: nor in the Hereafter.

So there is an omission in the speech, the omitted part being dispensed with by mention of what appears of it.

* *

The sense of the speech is: Indeed the wrongdoers will not prosper today in this world, "and the day We gather them all together." The phrase "and the day We gather them" is referred back to the intended meaning of the speech. For although it has been omitted, it is in effect present, since the listeners know its meaning. "Then We shall say to those who associated others with Allah: 'Where are your partners?'" – meaning: Then We shall say, when We have gathered these who fabricate lies against Allah by claiming for Him a partner in His dominion, and who deny His signs and messengers, and have gathered them all together on the Day of Resurrection [[See the explanation of "al-hashr" above, p. 89, footnote 2, and the references there.]] – "Where are your partners whom you used to claim" that they are gods besides Allah, a fabrication and a lie, and call upon them as lords besides Him? "Bring them forth, if you are truthful!"

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Then there was no result of their trial except that they said, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the exalted One's words is: Then their answer was not, when We said to them, "Where are your partners whom you used to claim?", a response from them to our question to them, when We tested them and examined them [[See his explanation of "al-fitnah" above, 10:478, footnote 2, and the references there.]] – "except that they said, 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists,'" lying in their oaths regarding this statement of theirs.

* *

Then the reciters differed regarding the reading of this.

A group of the reciters of Madinah and Basra and some of the Kufans recited it: ﴿thumma lam takun fitnatuhum﴾ with the ta', in the accusative, [[In the printed edition, the phrase "with the ta'" is omitted, for no good reason.]] meaning: their testing by Us was only their statement – "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists." However, they read "takun" with the feminine ta' – though it refers to the statement rather than to the trial, because it is adjacent to "the trial," and it is a predicate. [[See Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:188.]] This, according to the people of Arabic, is anomalous and not eloquent usage. A verse has been transmitted by Labid with something similar, namely his saying:

So he passed on and advanced her, and it was his habit / when her advance turned aside... [[From his brilliant mu'allaqah. See what Ibn al-Shajari said about the verse and the line in his Amali 1:130.

The pronoun in his saying "fa-mada" refers to the wild ass, and in his saying "wa-qaddamaha" refers to his she-ass which he drives to the water.

"'Arradat": fled and deviated from the path toward which he directed her. The poetry of Labid is not separated from one another in this ode, so I have not mentioned what precedes it and what follows it. Refer to his mu'allaqah.]]

He said "wa-kanat" with the feminine of "al-iqdam," because it is adjacent to his saying "'adah."

* *

And a group of the reciters of Kufa recited it: ﴿thumma lam yakun﴾ with the ya', ﴿fitnatahum﴾ in the accusative, ﴿illa an qalu﴾, with approximately the meaning intended by the others whose reading we have mentioned.

However, they made "yakun" masculine to agree with the masculine "an" [the clause].  [[See Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:188.]]

Abu Ja'far said: This reading is, in our view, the more correct of the two readings, because "an" is more definite than "al-fitnah." [[Abu Ja'far omitted the reading with raf' in "fitnatuhum," which is the reading in our codex, the reading of Hafs. I incline to think that Abu Ja'far omitted it deliberately, and he has fully discussed this verse and its like above, 7:273–275. See also the tafsir of Abu Hayyan 4:95.]]

* *

The interpreters differed regarding the interpretation of His saying: "Then there was no result of their trial."

Some of them said: its meaning is: then their statement was not.

Those who said this:

13134 – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: Qatadah said regarding His saying: "Then there was no result of their trial," – their statement. Ma'mar said: I heard someone other than Qatadah say: their excuse.

13135 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: "Then there was no result of their trial," – he said: their statement.

13136 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: "Then there was no result of their trial except that they said," the verse, – it is their speech: "They said, 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.'"

13137 – Al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj narrated to us from: I heard Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Khalid say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak: "Then there was no result of their trial," meaning: their speech.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: their excuse.

Those who said this:

13138 – Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah: "Then there was no result of their trial," – he said: their excuse.

13139 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "Then there was no result of their trial except that they said, 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists,'" – meaning: their excuse with falsehood and lying.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement on this matter is to say: its meaning is: Then their statement at the time of Our testing them was not, as an excuse for what had preceded from them of associating others with Allah, – "except that they said, 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists,'" – so "the trial" is placed in the position of "the statement," because the listeners know the meaning of the speech. And "the trial" is only testing and affliction. [[See his explanation of "al-fitnah" shortly above, p. 297, no. 2, and the references there.]] But since the answer from the people did not occur there except at the time of testing, "the trial," which is testing, was placed in the position of the report of their answer and their excuse.

* *

The reciters also differed regarding the reading of His saying: "except that they said, 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.'"

The majority of the reciters of Madinah, some of the Kufans and the Basrans recited it: "wa-Allahi rabbina," with a kasrah (genitive), making "the Lord" an attribute of Allah.

* *

Others among the Successors recited it: ﴿wa-Allahi rabbana﴾ with the accusative, meaning: "By Allah, O our Lord." This is the reading of the majority of the reciters of Kufa. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:330.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of the one who recited: ﴿wa-Allahi rabbana﴾ with the accusative of "the Lord," meaning: "O our Lord." This is because this is the answer of those who were questioned, to whom it was said: "Where are your partners whom you used to claim?" And the answer of the people to their Lord was: "By Allah, O our Lord, we were not polytheists" – so they denied that they had said that in the world. Allah the exalted says to Muhammad ﷺ: "Look how they lied against themselves, and what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them."

* *

And by His saying "we were not polytheists" is meant: we did not call upon any partner for You, nor did we call upon anyone other than You. [[See what preceded, nos. 9520–9522 (vol. 8: 373, 374).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 22–23:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And the day We shall gather them all together, then We shall say to those who associated others with Allah: "Where are your partners whom you used to claim?"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the exalted One's words is: Indeed these who fabricate lies against Allah and deny His signs will not prosper today in this world, nor on the day We gather them all together, meaning: nor in the Hereafter.

So there is an omission in the speech, the omitted part being dispensed with by mention of what appears of it.

* *

The sense of the speech is: Indeed the wrongdoers will not prosper today in this world, "and the day We gather them all together." The phrase "and the day We gather them" is referred back to the intended meaning of the speech. For although it has been omitted, it is in effect present, since the listeners know its meaning. "Then We shall say to those who associated others with Allah: 'Where are your partners?'" – meaning: Then We shall say, when We have gathered these who fabricate lies against Allah by claiming for Him a partner in His dominion, and who deny His signs and messengers, and have gathered them all together on the Day of Resurrection [[See the explanation of "al-hashr" above, p. 89, footnote 2, and the references there.]] – "Where are your partners whom you used to claim" that they are gods besides Allah, a fabrication and a lie, and call upon them as lords besides Him? "Bring them forth, if you are truthful!"

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Then there was no result of their trial except that they said, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the exalted One's words is: Then their answer was not, when We said to them, "Where are your partners whom you used to claim?", a response from them to our question to them, when We tested them and examined them [[See his explanation of "al-fitnah" above, 10:478, footnote 2, and the references there.]] – "except that they said, 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists,'" lying in their oaths regarding this statement of theirs.

* *

Then the reciters differed regarding the reading of this.

A group of the reciters of Madinah and Basra and some of the Kufans recited it: ﴿thumma lam takun fitnatuhum﴾ with the ta', in the accusative, [[In the printed edition, the phrase "with the ta'" is omitted, for no good reason.]] meaning: their testing by Us was only their statement – "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists." However, they read "takun" with the feminine ta' – though it refers to the statement rather than to the trial, because it is adjacent to "the trial," and it is a predicate. [[See Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:188.]] This, according to the people of Arabic, is anomalous and not eloquent usage. A verse has been transmitted by Labid with something similar, namely his saying:

So he passed on and advanced her, and it was his habit / when her advance turned aside... [[From his brilliant mu'allaqah. See what Ibn al-Shajari said about the verse and the line in his Amali 1:130.

The pronoun in his saying "fa-mada" refers to the wild ass, and in his saying "wa-qaddamaha" refers to his she-ass which he drives to the water.

"'Arradat": fled and deviated from the path toward which he directed her. The poetry of Labid is not separated from one another in this ode, so I have not mentioned what precedes it and what follows it. Refer to his mu'allaqah.]]

He said "wa-kanat" with the feminine of "al-iqdam," because it is adjacent to his saying "'adah."

* *

And a group of the reciters of Kufa recited it: ﴿thumma lam yakun﴾ with the ya', ﴿fitnatahum﴾ in the accusative, ﴿illa an qalu﴾, with approximately the meaning intended by the others whose reading we have mentioned.

However, they made "yakun" masculine to agree with the masculine "an" [the clause].  [[See Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:188.]]

Abu Ja'far said: This reading is, in our view, the more correct of the two readings, because "an" is more definite than "al-fitnah." [[Abu Ja'far omitted the reading with raf' in "fitnatuhum," which is the reading in our codex, the reading of Hafs. I incline to think that Abu Ja'far omitted it deliberately, and he has fully discussed this verse and its like above, 7:273–275. See also the tafsir of Abu Hayyan 4:95.]]

* *

The interpreters differed regarding the interpretation of His saying: "Then there was no result of their trial."

Some of them said: its meaning is: then their statement was not.

Those who said this:

13134 – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: Qatadah said regarding His saying: "Then there was no result of their trial," – their statement. Ma'mar said: I heard someone other than Qatadah say: their excuse.

13135 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: "Then there was no result of their trial," – he said: their statement.

13136 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: "Then there was no result of their trial except that they said," the verse, – it is their speech: "They said, 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.'"

13137 – Al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj narrated to us from: I heard Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Khalid say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak: "Then there was no result of their trial," meaning: their speech.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: their excuse.

Those who said this:

13138 – Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah: "Then there was no result of their trial," – he said: their excuse.

13139 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "Then there was no result of their trial except that they said, 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists,'" – meaning: their excuse with falsehood and lying.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement on this matter is to say: its meaning is: Then their statement at the time of Our testing them was not, as an excuse for what had preceded from them of associating others with Allah, – "except that they said, 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists,'" – so "the trial" is placed in the position of "the statement," because the listeners know the meaning of the speech. And "the trial" is only testing and affliction. [[See his explanation of "al-fitnah" shortly above, p. 297, no. 2, and the references there.]] But since the answer from the people did not occur there except at the time of testing, "the trial," which is testing, was placed in the position of the report of their answer and their excuse.

* *

The reciters also differed regarding the reading of His saying: "except that they said, 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.'"

The majority of the reciters of Madinah, some of the Kufans and the Basrans recited it: "wa-Allahi rabbina," with a kasrah (genitive), making "the Lord" an attribute of Allah.

* *

Others among the Successors recited it: ﴿wa-Allahi rabbana﴾ with the accusative, meaning: "By Allah, O our Lord." This is the reading of the majority of the reciters of Kufa. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:330.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of the one who recited: ﴿wa-Allahi rabbana﴾ with the accusative of "the Lord," meaning: "O our Lord." This is because this is the answer of those who were questioned, to whom it was said: "Where are your partners whom you used to claim?" And the answer of the people to their Lord was: "By Allah, O our Lord, we were not polytheists" – so they denied that they had said that in the world. Allah the exalted says to Muhammad ﷺ: "Look how they lied against themselves, and what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them."

* *

And by His saying "we were not polytheists" is meant: we did not call upon any partner for You, nor did we call upon anyone other than You. [[See what preceded, nos. 9520–9522 (vol. 8: 373, 374).]]

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Look how they lied against themselves, and what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them﴾ (6:24)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Look, O Muhammad, and know, how these polytheists, who equated their Lord with idols and images, lied in the Hereafter, at the meeting with God, against themselves, by their saying: "By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists," and they employed there the traits they had cultivated in the world, [[In the printed edition: "bihā mutakhalliqīn" (بها متخلقين), and in the manuscript: "bihā mutakhalliqūn" (بها متخلقون). The manuscript reading is correct.]] of lying and fabrication.

* *

The meaning of "look" (al-nazar) in this place is looking with the heart, not looking with the eye. Its meaning is: be clear, and know how they lied in the Hereafter.

* *

He said: "they lied" (kadhabū), and its meaning is "they lie," because when the report had already passed in the verse before it, it became like something that has already happened and been found.

* *

"And what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them" means: the rivals and idols departed from them, and they disowned them, and so they took a path other than theirs, because they had perished. [And those who used to worship them were restored, as an act of audacity.] [[What I have placed between the brackets is as it appears in the printed edition, whereas in the manuscript it reads: "wa-'abadū al-ladhīna kānū ya'budūnahā iṣran" (وعبدوا الذين كانوا يعبدونها إصرا), without diacritics. I have not been able to determine the correct reading, and I fear that a line or part of a line may have fallen out of the text. For this reason I have preferred to place what is in the printed edition between brackets, and because I am in doubt about its wording.]] Then they took up what they used to fabricate about them, saying concerning them against God, and worshipping them, and associating them with God's authority; so it went astray from them, and its worshippers were punished for their fabrication.

* *

We have already explained above that the meaning of "going astray" (al-ḍalāl) is taking a path other than guidance. [[See the explanation of "al-ḍalāl" above at 10:124, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

It has been mentioned that these polytheists would say this saying when they witnessed the vastness of God's mercy on that day.

Mention of the narration to that effect:

13140. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Hakkam told us, saying: 'Amr told us, from Mutarrif, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A man came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "I heard God say: 'By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists,' [[In the printed edition: "A man came to Ibn 'Abbas and said, God said: By God, our Lord..." The manuscript has a lacuna; it reads: "A man came to Ibn 'Abbas and said in another verse," and so the publisher altered the text. What I have established is correct, and it is the text of the report that Abu Ja'far transmitted earlier, as will come in the takhrij. I have corrected some letters in this report from the earlier narration and did not indicate them here.]] and in another verse He says: 'and they will not hide from God a word' (4:42)?" Ibn 'Abbas said: As for His saying: "By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists," when they saw that none would enter Paradise except the people of Islam, they said: "Come, let us deny," and so they said: "By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists." Then God sealed their mouths, and their hands and feet spoke, "and they will not hide from God a word."  [[The report: 13140. This report has already passed as number 9520 (vol. 8: 373). Abu Ja'far has abridged these reports of Ibn 'Abbas, for he narrated two other reports there, numbers 9521 and 9522, which show that the questioner was Nafi' ibn al-Azraq, who used to come to Ibn 'Abbas to put to him the ambiguous verses of the Qur'an. This is one of the forms of Abu Ja'far's abridgment in this tafsir. Also, reports will come here on the interpretation of the verse of Surat al-Nisa' 4:42 (vol. 8: 371–375) that he did not mention there, as you will see in the following reports.]]

13141. Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of God, exalted is His remembrance: "By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists," he said: It is the saying of the people of polytheism, when they saw sins being forgiven, and God does not forgive a polytheist. "Look how they lied against themselves," by God's denial of them.

13142. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, in similar wording.

13143. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih told me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, his saying: "By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists," then he said: "and they will not hide from God a word" (4:42), with their limbs.

13144. Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: My father told us, from Hamza al-Zayyat, from a man called Hisham, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Then their temptation was only that they said: By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists" (6:23). He said: They swore and made excuses, they said: "By God, our Lord." [[The report: 13144. "Hisham," from whom Hamza al-Zayyat narrates, I did not identify.]]

13145. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Qubaysa ibn 'Uqba told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: They swore and made excuses: "By God, our Lord."

13146. Hannad told us, saying: Wakī' told us, from Hamza al-Zayyat, from a man called Hisham, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, in similar wording.

13147. Hannad told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya told us, from Sufyan ibn Ziyad al-'Usfuri, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His saying: "By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists," he said: When an order was given to bring out men from the Fire, from the people of monotheism, those among the polytheists in it said: "Come, let us say: There is no god but God, perhaps we will come out with these." He said: But they were not believed. He said: So they swore: "By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists." He said: Then God said: "Look how they lied against themselves, and what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them." [[The report: 13147. "Sufyan ibn Ziyad al-'Usfuri," has passed as number 2331.]]

13148. Bishr ibn Mu'adh told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada: "and what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them," i.e., they associate. [[In the printed edition: "they associate with Him," with the addition; I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

13149. Al-Harith told us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz told us, saying: al-Minhal ibn 'Amr told us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: "By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists," he said: When the polytheists saw that none would enter Paradise except a Muslim, they said: Come, if we are asked we will say: "By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists." So they were asked, and they said that, and God sealed their mouths, and their limbs bore witness against them by their deeds. "Those who disbelieved, on that day, would wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they will not hide from God a word" (4:42).

13150. Al-Harith told me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz told me, saying: Muslim ibn Khalaf told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: There will come upon people on the Day of Resurrection a moment, when the people of polytheism see the people of monotheism being forgiven, and they say: "By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists." He said: "Look how they lied against themselves, and what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them." [[In the printed edition: "lamā ra'ā ahl al-shirk" (لما رأى أهل الشرك), and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is a permissible dialect form of the Arabs.]] [[The report: 13150. I did not find a biography of "Muslim ibn Khalaf," and I fear his name may be distorted.]]

13151. Al-Harith told me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from a man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he used to say: "By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists," lowering it (his voice). He said: They swore and made excuses. Al-Harith said: 'Abd al-'Aziz said: Sufyan said again: Hisham told me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 6, verse 25:

**On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you, but We have placed over their hearts coverings (akinnah) lest they understand it, and in their ears a deafness (waqran).﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And among these who ascribe equals to their Lord, the idols and images, from your people, O Muhammad, are those who ﴿listen to you﴾," meaning: those who listen to the Qur'an from you, and listen to what you call them to, of the Oneness of their Lord, His command and His prohibition, but do not understand what you say, nor retain it in their hearts, nor reflect upon it, nor lend their hearing to it so that they might comprehend it and understand the proofs of God against them in His revelation which He sent down to you. They only hear your voice, your recitation and your speech, and do not grasp from you what you say, because God has placed over their hearts "coverings."

* *

"Akinnah" is the plural of "kinan," which is a covering, like "sinan" and "asinnah." It is said of it: "akanantu al-shay'a fi nafsi" (with the alif), and "kannantu al-shay'" when one covers a thing. [See what preceded at 5:102, 103.] From the same root is ﴿bayd maknun﴾ [Surah al-Saffat: 49], meaning covered. [The better form would be to say "wa huwa al-mughatta" (and it is that which is covered), and it seems that it was so, and that what is in the printed and manuscript editions is a distortion. However, the early scholars sometimes expressed themselves in such a way, so I have left it as it is. Al-Tabari said in vol. 5, p. 102, when mentioning the verse: "i.e., hidden."] From it is the saying of the poet: [He is 'Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah.]

*taḥta ʿaynin, kinānunā ... ẓillu burdin muraḥḥalu*
("Beneath a cloud, our covering ... the shade of a striped, saddle-marked garment")

[It is not in his diwan, but it is from his poem found in his diwan, pp. 125–126, and it is in al-Aghani 1:184, Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:46, 188, and Lisan (k-n-n), and elsewhere. Among his verses, the first of which is: "What stirred the heart was a dwelling, its traces worn, its signs faded..."

And before it, in the version of Abu al-Faraj in his Aghani: "She sent [her companions] urging, ransoming, and reproaching: 'Which of us spent a night between two branches of a palm-tree?'"

His version of the verse:
*taḥta ʿaynin, yukinnunā ... burdu ʿaṣbin muhalhalu*

Ibn Bari's version, and he corrected the version of Abu 'Ubaydah and Abu Ja'far: *taḥta ʿaynin, kinānunā ... burdu ʿaṣbin muraḥḥalu*

"Al-ʿayn" in the verse means the cloud. "Al-murahhal" among garments is that which bears images of saddles.]

He means: their covering which conceals them. [See Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:188, which is similar to the text of his statement.]

* *

﴿And in their ears a deafness﴾: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: He placed in their ears heaviness and deafness from understanding what you recite to them, and from lending ear to what you call them to.

* *

The Arabs pronounce the *waw* of *al-waqr* (in the ear) with a fatha, meaning heaviness in it, but they pronounce it with a kasra in the sense of a load, so they say: "huwa wiqru al-dabbah" (it is the load of the beast). It is said of loading: "awqartu al-dabbata fa-hiya muwqarah" (I loaded the beast, so it is loaded). And of hearing: "waqartu sam'ahu fa-huwa mawqur" (I made his hearing heavy, so he is hard of hearing), and from it is the saying of the poet: [I have not been guided to its speaker, though I recall having read this verse somewhere.]

*wa-li hāmatun qad waqqara al-ḍarbu samʿahā*
("And I have a skull whose hearing the blow has made heavy")

It has been reported from transmitted usage that "wuqirat udhnuhu" (his ear became heavy), so it is "mawqurah" (heavy). And "awqarat al-nakhlah, fa-hiya muwqir" (the palm-tree bore fruit heavily), as it is said: "imra'ah tamith and ha'id" (a woman who menstruates and one who is menstruating), because there is no share in it for the masculine. If one wishes to say that God made it heavy, it is said "muwqarah."

* *

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings lest they understand it﴾, meaning: lest they not understand it, just as He said: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 176], meaning: lest you go astray, because the covering is only placed over the heart so that it does not understand, not so that it does understand. [See the explanation of "faqiha" in what preceded at 8:557.]

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

13152 – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding ﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings lest they understand it, and in their ears a deafness﴾: He said: They hear it with their ears but retain nothing of it, like the beast that hears a call but does not know what is being said to it.

13153 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding ﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings lest they understand it, and in their ears a deafness﴾: As for "akinnah," it is the covering that conceals their hearts, so they do not understand the truth. "And in their ears a deafness," he said: deafness.

13154 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding the saying of God, ﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾, he said: Quraysh.

13155 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it, until, when they come to you disputing with you, those who disbelieve say: "This is nothing but the fables of the ancients."﴾ (25)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And if these who ascribe equals to their Lord, the idols and images, those upon whose hearts coverings have been placed lest they understand from you what they hear from you, ﴿see every sign﴾, meaning: every proof and indication that guides people of intellect and understanding to the Oneness of God, the truthfulness of your word, and the reality of your prophethood [See the explanation of "ayah" in what preceded in the indexes of language (a-y-y).] ﴿they will not believe in it﴾, meaning: they will not affirm it, nor acknowledge that it indicates what it indicates. ﴿Until, when they come to you disputing with you﴾, meaning: until, when they come to you after witnessing the signs that show the reality of what you brought them, ﴿disputing with you﴾, meaning: contending with you [See the explanation of "jadala" in what preceded at 4:141 / 9:190, 193.] ﴿those who disbelieve say﴾, meaning by this: those who denied the signs of God and rejected their reality, who say to the Prophet of God ﷺ when they hear the proofs of God by which he argued against them, and the clarification which he made clear to them: ﴿This is nothing but the fables of the ancients﴾, meaning: this is nothing but the fables of the ancients.

* *

"Al-asatir" is the plural of "uslurah" and "usturah," like "uhfukuhah" and "udhakah." It is also permissible that the singular be "ustar," like "abyat" and "ababit," and "aqwal" and "aqawil," [He means by "ustar" the plural of "satr," as is clear.] from the saying of God, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And a written book﴾ [Surah al-Tur: 2], from "satara yasturu satran" (he wrote a line).

* *

Given this, its interpretation is: "This is nothing but what the ancients wrote."

* *

It has been reported from Ibn 'Abbas and others that they interpreted it in this way, saying: its meaning is: "This is nothing but the tales of the ancients."

13156 – Al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim narrated to me this, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas.

13157 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: As for "asatir al-awwalin," it is "asajic al-awwalin." ["Al-asajic" is the plural of "usjuwah," meaning the soothsayers in the form of their speech.]

* *

Some people of knowledge, namely Abu 'Ubaydah Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna, who was expert in the speech of the Arabs, said: "Al-Istarah" is a dialect form, and its metaphorical sense is that of trivialities (al-tarahat). [In the printed edition: "a dialect form; the fables and trivialities," which differs from the manuscript and is the text of Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an 1:189. This is from the bad tampering with books!]

* *

Al-Akhfash said: Some said: its singular is "usturah." Others said: "istarah." He said: I do not think it is except from the plural that has no singular, like "al-'abadid" [In the printed edition: "ʿabaiyid," which is correct, but I have kept what is in the manuscript. It is said: "the people came ʿabadid and ʿababid," meaning scattered.] and "al-madhakir," and "al-ababil." ["Al-madhakir" is also said of the singular. It is reported that a slave saw his master's concubine, so the master castrated his genitals, and he used it for a single man, meaning his thing and what was attached to it.

"Ababil": groups from here and groups from there.] He said: Some said: the singular of "al-ababil" is "ibbil," and some said "ibbawl," like "ijjawl," [It is said: "ijl" and "ijul" (with a kasra on the ayn, a shadda on the jim with fatha, and a sukun on the waw): the calf of a cow, and its plural is "ʿijajil."] and I have not found the Arabs knowing a singular for it; rather, it is like "abadid," which has no singular. As for "al-shamatit," they claim that its singular is "shamatat." ["Shamamit": scattered pieces. It is said: "the people went shamamit": when they scattered in groups.] He said: All of these have a singular, but it was not used nor spoken, because this pattern only occurs in the plural. [In the printed edition: "jam'an," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.] He said: I heard the eloquent Arabs say: "He sent his horses ababil," meaning groups, and they do not speak of it in the singular. [In the printed edition: "they do not speak of it as a unity," and I have kept what is in the manuscript; I dislike the publisher's tampering with the text of Abu Ja'far!]

The disputation with the Messenger of God ﷺ which God mentioned in this verse was, as was mentioned, that:

13158 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated this to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: ﴿Until, when they come to you disputing with you﴾, the verse. He said: They are the polytheists, who dispute with the Muslims concerning the slaughtered animal, saying: "What you slaughter and kill, you eat; but what God kills, you do not eat! And you follow the command of God, may His remembrance be exalted!" [At this point ended a part of the old division from which our copy was taken, and in it is the following text:

"Followed by the discourse on the interpretation of His words

﴿And they forbid it and keep away from it, and they destroy none but themselves, and they do not perceive﴾

And may God bless Muhammad the Prophet and his family and grant them abundant peace. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds." Then followed by the text: "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. My Lord, make it easy."]

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 26:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves; yet they destroy none but themselves, and they perceive it not (26).﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the interpretation of His saying: "And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves."

Some of them said: Its meaning is: these polytheists who denied the signs of Allah forbid people from following Muhammad (ﷺ) and from accepting what he brought, "and keep away from it," they distance themselves from it.

Mention of those who said this:

13159 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath and Hani' ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Hajjaj, from Salim, from Ibn al-Hanafiyyah: "And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves," he said: They hold back from the Prophet (ﷺ) and do not respond to him, and they forbid people from him.

[Note on the report: 13159 - Hani' ibn Sa'id al-Nakha'i, saduq in narration (salih al-hadith), mentioned in al-Kabir 4/2/233 and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/102. "Hajjaj" is Hajjaj ibn Arta'ah, already mentioned many times. "Salim" is Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, also already mentioned. "Ibn al-Hanafiyyah" is Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, also already mentioned.]

13160 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves," meaning: they forbid people from Muhammad, that they should believe in him, "and keep away from it," meaning: they distance themselves from him.

13161 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves," that Muhammad be followed, and they themselves distance themselves from him.

13162 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves," he says: They do not meet him, and they do not let anyone who would come to him.

13163 - It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say regarding His saying: "And they forbid others from it," he says: from Muhammad (ﷺ).

13164 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves," they combined forbidding and distancing. And "al-nay" is distancing. [In the manuscript: "wa-al-nahy al-taba'ud" (and the forbidding is distancing), which is an error; its correct form is what is in the printed edition without doubt.]

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: "And they forbid others from it" from the Qur'an, that it be listened to and acted upon in what it contains.

Mention of those who said this:

13165 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "And they forbid others from it," he said: they forbid others from the Qur'an and from the Prophet (ﷺ), "and keep away from it," and distance themselves from it.

13166 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "And they forbid others from it," he said: Quraysh, from the Reminder. "And keep away from it," he says: they distance themselves.

13167 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves," Quraysh, from the Reminder. "Keep away from it," they distance themselves.

13168 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves," he said: they forbid others from the Qur'an and from the Prophet (ﷺ), and they distance themselves from it.

13169 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "And keep away from it," he said: "And they keep away from it," they distance themselves from it. [In the printed edition: "yubʿidun" (they distance), and in the manuscript: "yubʿidunahu" (they distance him); I preferred to read it as I have established it.]

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "And they forbid others from it" from harming Muhammad (ﷺ), "and keep away from it," they distance themselves from his religion and following him.

Mention of those who said this:

13170 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Waki' and Qabisah narrated to us, and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from one who heard Ibn Abbas say: It was revealed concerning Abu Talib; he used to forbid others from harming Muhammad, and he kept away from what he brought so as not to believe in it.

13171 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said: One who heard Ibn Abbas say narrated to me: "And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves," he said: It was revealed concerning Abu Talib; he forbade others from harming him, and kept away from what he brought.

13172 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from one who heard Ibn Abbas: "And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves," he said: It was revealed concerning Abu Talib; he used to forbid the polytheists from harming Muhammad, and he kept away from what he brought.

13173 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abdah narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Qasim ibn Makhimarah, who said: Abu Talib used to forbid others from the Prophet (ﷺ) and would not confirm him.

13174 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father and Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Qasim ibn Makhimarah regarding His saying: "And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves," he said: It was revealed concerning Abu Talib. Ibn Waki' said, Ibn Bishr said: Abu Talib used to forbid others from harming the Prophet (ﷺ) and would not confirm him.

13175 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Abu Muhammad al-Asadi, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said: One who heard Ibn Abbas say regarding the saying of Allah, exalted is His remembrance: "And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves," it was revealed concerning Abu Talib; he used to forbid others from harming Muhammad, and kept away from what he brought so as not to follow him.

13176 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Qasim ibn Makhimarah regarding His saying: "And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves," he said: It was revealed concerning Abu Talib.

13177 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Siyah, from Habib, who said: That is Abu Talib, regarding His saying: "And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves."

13178 - Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub narrated to me, saying: Ata' ibn Dinar said regarding the saying of Allah: "And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves," that it was revealed concerning Abu Talib; that he used to forbid people from harming the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and kept away from the guidance he brought.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most probable of these sayings for the interpretation of the verse is the saying of the one who said: its interpretation is: "And they forbid others from it," from following Muhammad (ﷺ) among the rest of the people, "and keep away from following him."

This is because the verses before it dealt with the mention of the group of polytheists who associated others with Allah, and the report of their denial of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and their turning away from what had come to them of Allah's revelation and inspiration. Therefore it is necessary that His saying "And they forbid others from it" be a report about them, since nothing has reached us indicating that the report turns away from them to others. Rather, what precedes this verse and what follows it confirms what we have said: that it is a report about the group of polytheists of the people of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), not a report about a specific individual among them.

* *

Since that is so, the interpretation of the verse is: And if these polytheists, O Muhammad, see every sign, they will not believe in it, until, when they come to you disputing with you, they say: "This is nothing but the fables of the ancients!" And they forbid others from listening to the revelation, and keep away from you, distancing themselves from you and from following you. "Yet they destroy none but themselves," meaning: they do not destroy anyone but themselves, by their turning away from the path of Allah, their aversion to His revelation, and their disbelief in their Lord, for by that deed they earn for themselves the wrath of Allah and His painful punishment, which they have no power to bear. "And they perceive it not," meaning: they do not know what destruction and ruin they are bringing upon themselves by their deeds.

* *

The Arabs say of everyone who has distanced himself from something: "He has kept away from it (qad naʼa ʻanhu), so he keeps away (yanʼa), a distancing (naʼyan)." It is heard from them: "nayaytuka" (I distanced you), meaning "nayaytu ʻanka" (I distanced myself from you). And when they intend "I made you distant from me," they say: "anʼaytuka." Among the instances of "nayaytuka" in the sense of "nayaytu ʻanka" is the saying of al-Hutay'ah:

Umamah has kept away from you, except for a request, and you have seen from her, through a phantom, a vision.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And if you could see when they are made to stand before the Fire, and they say, "Oh, would that we were returned, and would not deny the signs of our Lord, and would be among the believers."﴾ (27)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And if you could see," O Muhammad, these who ascribe equals to their Lord, worshipping idols and images, who deny your prophethood, whose description I have given you, "when they are made to stand" — meaning: when they are held back — "before the Fire," meaning: in the Fire. Here "ʿalā" (on) is placed in the position of "fī" (in), as in His saying: ﴿and they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 102], meaning "during the reign of Solomon." [[See the explanation of "ʿalā" in the sense of "fī" in earlier passages: 1:299; 2:411-412; 11:200-201, and other places; seek them in the indexes of grammar and Arabic.]]

* *

It has also been said: "And if you could see when they stood," meaning: "when they stood," in accordance with what we have described earlier: that the Arabs sometimes place "idh" (when) in the position of "idha" (whenever/if), and "idha" in the position of "idh," although the proper usage of "idh" is to accompany reports of what has already occurred and been decided, and the proper usage of "idha" is to accompany reports of what has not yet occurred. [[See "idha" and "idh" in earlier passages, p. 236, note 1, and the references there.]] But this is as the rajaz poet, Abu al-Najm, said:

"Your Lord extended for us His life, O Lord of Ṭahā...
Then Allah rewarded him on our behalf when He rewarded,
The Gardens of Eden in the highest heights."

[[Two lines of it passed earlier, p. 235. The first line of the rajaz is in Lisan al-Arab (ṭahā), which says: "He meant: Lord of Ṭah, so he dropped the alif." The printed edition and the manuscript wrote it as "Ṭah"; I have preferred the spelling given by the author of Lisan (ṭahā).]]

So he said: "Then Allah rewarded him on our behalf when He rewarded," placing "idh" in the position of "idha."

* *

It has also been said: "waqafū" (they were made to stand), and not "ūqifū," because the former is the eloquent usage of the Arabs. One says "waqaftu al-dābba wa ghayrahā" (I held back the riding-beast or other things), without an alif, when one holds it back. Likewise, "waqaftu al-arḍ" (I endowed the land), when one makes it a permanent charitable endowment, without an alif. And indeed:

13179 - Al-Ḥārith narrated to me, from Abu ʿUbayd, who said: Al-Yazidi and al-Asmaʿi both informed me, from Abu ʿAmr, who said: "I never heard any of the Arabs say 'awqaftu al-shay'' (with an alif)." He said: "Except that if I saw a man in a place and said, 'What made you stop here?' (ma awqafaka hā hunā), with an alif, I would find it good." [[Report 13179: this report is found in Lisan al-Arab under "waqafa." In the printed edition it read "al-Ḥārith ibn Abi ʿUbayd," which is an error; the correct reading is from the manuscript. This chain has appeared many times before.]]

"Then they said, 'Oh, would that we were returned,'" meaning: then these polytheists who ascribed equals to their Lord, when they were held back in the Fire, said: "Oh, would that we were returned" to the world, until we repent and return to obedience to Allah. "And would not deny the signs of our Lord," meaning: and would not deny the proofs of our Lord, nor reject them. "And would be among the believers," meaning: and would be among those who affirm Allah, His proofs, His messengers, and who follow His command and prohibition.

* *

The reciters differed regarding the reading of this.

The majority of the reciters of Hijaz, Madina and Iraq read: ﴿Oh, would that we were returned, and we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers﴾ — with the meaning: "Oh, would that we were returned, and we are not denying the signs of our Lord, but we would be among the believers."

* *

Some of the reciters of Kufa read it: "Yā laytanā nuraddu wa lā nukadhdhiba bi-āyāti rabbinā wa nakūna min al-mu'minīn," with the meaning: "Oh, would that we were returned, and that we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and that we would be among the believers." They interpreted this in a certain way:

13180 - Aḥmad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Hārūn, who said: In the reading of Ibn Masʿud: ﴿Oh, would that we were returned, then we would not deny﴾ — with the fa' (then).

* *

It has also been reported from some reciters of Syria that they read it: "wa lā nukadhdhibu" (in the nominative) and "wa nakūna" (in the accusative), as if they directed its interpretation to the sense that they wished to be returned and to be among the believers, and informed that they would not deny the signs of their Lord if they were returned to the world.

* *

The scholars of Arabic differed regarding the meaning of this in the accusative and the nominative.

One of the grammarians of Basra said: "wa lā nukadhdhiba bi-āyāti rabbinā wa nakūna min al-mu'minīn" is in the accusative, because it is an answer to the wish, and what follows the "wa" is like what follows the "fa." He said: If you wish, you may put it in the nominative and make it not a wish, as if they said: "and we do not deny, by Allah, the signs of our Lord, and we are, by Allah, among the believers." In this case, it would be a new clause separate from the first. He said: The nominative is the proper form of the expression, because if it is in the accusative, the "wa" becomes a conjunction of coordination. If the "wa" is a conjunction of coordination, then it is as if they wished not to deny and to be among the believers. He said: This, and Allah knows best, cannot be, because they did not wish for this; they only wished for return, and they informed that they would not deny and would be among the believers.

* *

One of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: If "nukadhdhiba" and "nakūna" were put in the accusative as an answer with "wa," it would be correct. He said: The Arabs answer with "wa" and "thumma" just as they answer with "fa." They say: "Would that I had wealth, then I would give you" (fa-u'ṭiyaka), "Would that I had wealth and I would give you" (wa-u'ṭiyaka), and "thumma u'ṭiyaka." He said: It may also be in the accusative as a "ṣarf" (a change of construction), as in your saying: "Nothing can contain me and I fail to reach you." [["Ṣarf," whose explanation has passed earlier: 1:569, note 1; 3:552, note 1; 7:247, note 2.]]

* *

Another of them said: I do not favor the accusative in this, because it is not a wish from them; it is a report that they gave about themselves. Do you not see that Allah, exalted is He, has denied them, saying: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾? Denial applies to a report, not to a wish.

* *

Some of them denied that the answer could be with "wa" and with a particle other than "fa." He used to say: "wa" is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), as in "lā yasaʿunī shay' wa yaḍīqa ʿanka" (nothing contains me while it is narrow for you), meaning: "and it is narrow for you." He said: The same applies to the ṣarf throughout the Arabic language. As for "fa," it is an answer to a conditional: "mā qumtu fa-natiyaka" (I did not stand up, so that we would come to you), meaning: if I had stood up, we would have come to you. He said: This is the rule of ṣarf and "fa." As for His saying "wa lā nukadhdhiba" and "wa nakūna," it is permissible only because they said "Oh, would that we were returned" in a condition other than the one in which we were made to stand before the Fire. Their standing was in that condition, so they wished that they had not been made to stand in that condition.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speaker of this statement, in his saying, seems to be: "And if you could see when they were made to stand before the Fire, and they said: 'We have been made to stand before it, denying the signs of our Lord, as disbelievers; oh, would that we were returned to it, so that we would be made to stand before it not denying the signs of our Lord and not as disbelievers.'"

This is an interpretation that the apparent wording of the revelation refutes, namely the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars.﴾ So Allah informed that in their saying that they are liars, and denial does not occur in a wish. But I think the holder of this view did not carefully reflect on the interpretation and clung to the patterns of Arabic grammar.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The reading that I do not choose other than it is: ﴿Oh, would that we were returned, and we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers﴾ with the nominative in both, meaning: "Oh, would that we were returned, and we are not denying the signs of our Lord if we are returned, but we would be among the believers" — as a report from them about what they would do if they were returned to the world, not as a wish from them that they not deny the signs of their Lord and be among the believers. Because Allah, exalted is He, has informed about them that if they were returned they would return to what they were forbidden, and that they are liars in their saying that. If their saying were a wish, its denial would be impossible, because a wish is not denied; affirmation and denial apply only to reports.

* *

As for the accusative in this, I think its reader intended the interpretation of the reading of ʿAbd Allah that we have mentioned from him, [[In the printed edition: "I think its reader sought by it the interpretation of ʿAbd Allah's reading," which is weak speech. In the manuscript: "...that he *barḥā* the interpretation of ʿAbd Allah's reading," undotted; the correct reading is what I have adopted.]] namely his reading: ﴿Oh, would that we were returned, then we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers,﴾ as an answer to the wish with "fa." When it is read that way with "fa," there is no doubt about the soundness of its grammar. Its meaning, when read thus, is: "If we were returned to the world, we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers." If what those who transmitted from the Arabs have reported, that the answer with "wa" and "thumma" is like the answer with "fa," is sound, then there is no doubt about the soundness of the reading of whoever reads: "Yā laytanā nuraddu wa lā nukadhdhiba bi-āyāti rabbinā wa nakūna" in the accusative as an answer to the wish with "wa," interpreting the reading of ʿAbd Allah with "fa." Otherwise, the reading in that way is far from the meaning of the revelation. I do not know of a sound report of that usage from the Arabs; rather, what is known of their speech is the answer with "fa" and the ṣarf with "wa."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 28:

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿But there has become apparent to them what they used to conceal before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, means: What afflicts these who ascribe equals to their Lord [[In the printed edition: "ma qasd hā'ulā'" ("what is the intent of these"), which is meaningless; what led me to this reading is that the manuscript has "mā hā'ulā' al-ʿādilīn," and I have deemed the correct reading from His saying afterward: "lakin bihim al-ishfāq."]] and deny your prophethood, O Muhammad, in their saying when they stand over the Fire: "Would that we were returned, and we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers," is regret and remorse over abandoning faith in God and affirming you, [[The context: "mā bi-hā'ulā' al-ʿādilīn bi-rabbihim ... al-asā wa al-nadam ..."]] but rather for them is apprehension of what is descending upon them of God's punishment and His painful torment, for their sins which they used to conceal from the eyes of people and hide from them, so God manifested them from them on the Day of Resurrection and displayed them before the witnesses, exposing them by them, then recompensed them for them with their due recompense.

He says: "Rather, there has become apparent to them what they used to conceal" of their evil deeds which they used to hide "from before," that is, in the world, so they appeared. "And even if they were returned," he says: even if they were returned to the world and given respite, "they would return to what they were forbidden," he says: they would return to the like of the deed they used to do in the world before that, of denying the signs of God, disbelieving in Him, and doing what angers their Lord. "And indeed they are liars," in their saying: "If we were returned, we would not deny the signs of our Lord and we would be among the believers," because they said it when they said it out of fear of punishment, not out of faith in God.

* *

And the people of interpretation have said in accordance with what we have said regarding that.

Mention of those who said that:

13181 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Rather, there has become apparent to them what they used to conceal before," he says: their deeds became manifest to them in the Hereafter, which they had concealed in the world.

13182 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "Rather, there has become apparent to them what they used to conceal before," he said: from their deeds.

13183 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden," he says: even if God gave them a worldly life like their worldly life, they would return to their deeds, evil deeds.

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿And they say, "There is nothing but our life of this world, and we will not be resurrected."﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from God, may His remembrance be exalted, about these polytheists, who associate others with Him, worshipping idols and images, whom this surah began by describing.

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And they say, "There is nothing but our life of this world"﴾. He reports that they deny God gives life to His creatures after He causes them to die, and they say, "There is no life after death, no resurrection and no rising after perishing." By their denial and their rejection of God's reward and punishment in the Hereafter, they do not care what sins and disobedience they commit, because they do not hope for reward for faith in God, belief in His Messenger, and righteous deeds after death, nor do they fear punishment for their disbelief in God and His Messenger, or for any evil deed they do. [[In the printed edition: "wa-shay' min 'amal" (and some deed). In the manuscript it is undotted, and the correct reading is what has been adopted here.]]

* *

Ibn Zayd used to say: This is a report from God, may His remembrance be exalted, about those unbelievers who were made to stand over the Fire: that if they were returned to the world, they would say, ﴿"There is nothing but our life of this world, and we will not be resurrected."﴾

13184 - Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words, ﴿"And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden"﴾, and they would say when they are returned: ﴿"There is nothing but our life of this world, and we will not be resurrected."﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 30:

The explanation of His words: ﴿And if you could see when they are made to stand before their Lord. He will say, "Is this not the truth?" They will say, "Yes, by our Lord." He will say, "So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: "And if you could see," O Muhammad, those who said: "There is nothing but our life of this world, and we will not be resurrected," "when they are made to stand," on the Day of Resurrection, that is, they are detained [[See the explanation of "waqafa" earlier, p. 316.]] "before their Lord," meaning before the judgment and decree of Allah concerning them. "He will say, 'Is this not the truth?'" He says: It will be said to them, "Is this not the resurrection and raising after death, which you used to deny in the world, true?" They will answer and say, "Yes, by Allah, indeed it is the truth." "He will say, 'So taste the punishment,'" He says: Allah, may He be exalted and remembered, will say to them: "So taste the punishment with which you were threatened in the world, which you used to deny [[See the explanation of "dhaqa al-adhab" earlier, p. 47, note 1, and the references there.]]" "for what you used to disbelieve," He says: because of your denial of it and your rejection of it, which you used to do in the world.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Those who denied the meeting with God have certainly lost, until, when the Hour comes upon them suddenly, they say, "Oh, our regret over what we neglected concerning it!"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, "Those who denied the meeting with God have certainly lost," He, exalted is His mention, means: they have perished and been cheated in their trade of faith for disbelief [[See the explanation of "khasira" (to lose) in what has preceded, p. 294, footnote 1, and the references there.]] — "those who denied the meeting with God," meaning: those who rejected resurrection after death, and the reward and punishment, and Paradise and Hell, from among the polytheists of Quraysh and whoever followed their path in that — "until, when the Hour comes upon them," that is: until the Hour comes upon them, the Hour in which God raises the dead from their graves.

* *

The definite article was put on "the Hour" because its meaning is known to those addressed, and because what is intended is the specific Hour that has been described.

* *
