[[The verse and its takhrij and explanation were given earlier at 1:509; I did not there indicate its appearance in the tafsir at this place, then at 21:18 (Bulaq). I add that it appears in Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu ʿUbayda 1:192 and Maʿani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:335.]]

So the interpretation of His saying "wa-ablasa," according to those who claimed that "ibласs" means the cutting off of proof and silence therein, meaning: he did not produce a reply. [[This is al-Farra' in Maʿani al-Qur'an 1:335.]]

Others interpreted it to mean humility, and that its people left him standing in his place.

And others [interpreted it to mean] grief and remorse.

From it is said: "abalasa al-rajul ibla'san" (the man was dismayed), and from it is named Iblis, "Iblis." [[See what Abu Ja'far said in the explanation of "Iblis" earlier: 1:509, 510.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 45:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, exalted is His remembrance, "So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off," He means: the people who rebelled against their Lord, denied His messengers, and opposed His command were completely uprooted, every last one of them, so that none of them was left except that they were destroyed suddenly when the punishment of Allah came upon them.

* *

Some commentators of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

13242 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off," he says: the root of those who did wrong was cut off.

13243 - Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: "So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off," he said: they were uprooted.

* *

And "dabir al-qawm" (the last remnant of the people) is the one who comes after them, and it is the one who is at their rear and end. It is said in speech: "Fulan dabara al-qawm, yadburuhum, dabran wa dabuuran" (Fulan came last among the people), when he is their last, and from it is the verse of Umayya:

"So they were destroyed with a punishment that shaved off their last remnant, and they could not avert it nor were they helped."

* *

"And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds," he says: complete commendation and perfect thanks are due "to Allah, Lord of the worlds," for His favour upon His messengers and the people of His obedience, by manifesting their proofs against those who opposed them from among the people of disbelief, and by fulfilling their promises, which they had made to them, of the vengeance of Allah and His swift punishment, on account of their disbelief in Allah and their denial of His messengers.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 46:

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Say: "Have you considered: if Allah were to take away your hearing and your sight and seal up your hearts, what god other than Allah could bring them back to you? Observe how We vary the signs; yet they turn away.">

Abu Ja'far said: May He be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to these who ascribe equals to Me, idols and images, and who deny you: "Have you considered, O polytheists who associate others with Allah: if Allah deafens you and takes away your hearing, blinds you and takes away your sight, and seals up your hearts and stamps upon them, so that you understand no speech, perceive no proof, and comprehend no meaning, [[See the explanation of "sealing upon the heart" above, 1:258-262.]] what god other than Allah, to whom every worshipper's worship belongs, could return to you" — "could bring them back to you" — meaning: could restore to you what Allah has taken from you of hearing, sight and understanding, so that you would worship it or associate it with the worship of your Lord, who is able to take these away from you and to restore them to you whenever He wills?

This is from Allah, may He be exalted, teaching His Prophet the argument against the polytheists who associate others with Him. He says to him: Say to them: those whom you worship besides Allah do not possess for you any harm or benefit; worship is due from you only to the one in whose hand is harm and benefit, the restricting and the extending, the One Able to do whatever He wills, not the helpless who has power over nothing.

Then He, may He be exalted, said to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "Observe how We vary the signs" — meaning: observe how We continually send the proofs upon them, and strike for them the parables and lessons, so that they may take heed, remember, and turn back in repentance. [[See the explanation of "al-tasrif" above, 3:275-276.]] "Yet they turn away" — meaning: yet they, despite Our continual sending of proofs upon them and Our alerting them with lessons, turn away from remembrance and consideration.

* *

It is said of it: "Fulan turned away from me with his face (sadafa), so he turns away (yasdifu) with a turning away (sudufan) and a turning (sadafan)," meaning: he deviated and turned aside. From this is the saying of Ibn al-Raqa':

When they recount a tale, they say its best part, and they are, from every evil that is feared, turned away (sudufun).

[[I have not found this verse, nor identified the qasida it belongs to.]]

And Labid said:

They water the restive camels before night, turning away (sadifatan), like jinn-like figures, upon whom are fine garments and wrappers.

[[From his Diwan, qasida no. 12, verse 22. This verse is among verses in which he praises himself, and before it: "I do not say, when a calamity strikes, 'Woe to my soul for what fate has done'; nor do I go astray with companions I have guided, when the trodden path spreads out in the darkness; and I make trade profitable, if its wine is dear, until a companion returns sound with his company around him..." (the rest of the poem follows in the source, with the glosses).]]

But if someone says: How is it said, "a god other than Allah could bring it to you," with the pronoun singular, when the reference earlier was in the plural: "Have you considered if Allah takes away your hearing and your sight and seals your hearts?"

It is said: It is permissible that the pronoun refers back to "hearing," so it is singular to match the singular "hearing." And it is also permissible that it refers to: a god other than Allah who could bring you what was taken from you of hearing, sight and hearts, so it is singular to match "what" (ma). The Arabs do this: when they refer to actions, they use a singular pronoun, even if many things are referred to by it, as in their saying: "Your coming and your going please me." [[See al-Farra', Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:335.]]

* *

It has also been said that the pronoun in "bihi" refers back to "guidance." [[This too was mentioned by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:335.]]

* *

Consistent with what we have said in the interpretation of His words "yasdifun," the people of interpretation have spoken.

Those who said so:

13244 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words "yasdifun": he said: they turn away.

13245 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

13246 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words "yasdifun": he said: they deviate.

13247 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada regarding His words "We vary the signs, yet they turn away": he said: they turn away from them.

13248 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "yet they turn away": he said: they bar (others).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 47:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Say: Tell me, if the punishment of Allah should come upon you suddenly or openly, would any be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?﴾ (6:47)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these people who ascribe equals to their Lord, the idols, and who deny that you are a messenger to them: Tell me [[See the explanation of "arara'aytakum" (have you considered) above, pp. 351-353.]] "if the punishment of Allah comes upon you," and His retribution for what you associate with Him of idols and rivals, and your denial of me after you have witnessed the proof of the truth of my words, "suddenly," meaning: unexpectedly, while you are heedless [[See the explanation of "baghtah" (suddenly) above: 325, 360.]] "or openly," meaning: or the punishment of Allah comes upon you while you are watching it and looking at it, "would any be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?" meaning: Would Allah destroy any of us and you except those who worshipped other than the one who deserves worship from us, and abandoned the worship of the one who deserves worship from us?

We have already explained the meaning of "jahrah" (openly) in another place, sufficiently so that it need not be repeated: it derives from "ijhar," which is making a thing manifest to the eye, [[See the explanation of "jahrah" above: 2:80 / 9:358.]] as related:

13249 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "jahrah" — he said: "while they are looking on."

13250 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Say: Tell me, if the punishment of Allah comes upon you suddenly" — suddenly, while you are secure — "or openly," while they are looking on.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 48:

The explanation of His words: ﴿We send not the messengers except as bearers of good news and warners. So whoever believes and does righteousness, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We do not send Our messengers except with glad tidings for the people of obedience to Us of Paradise and the clear triumph on the Day of Resurrection, as a reward from Us for them for their obedience to Us [[See the explanation of "tabshir" (giving glad tidings) above, vol. 9, p. 318, footnote 2, and the references there.]] = and with warning to those who disobey Us and oppose Our command, of Our punishment for them for their disobedience to Us on the Day of Resurrection, as a recompense from Us for their disobedience, so that We may leave them without excuse, and that whoever perishes may perish with clear evidence [[See the explanation of "nadhir" (warner) above, vol. 10, p. 158.]]. ﴿So whoever believes and does righteousness﴾: that is, whoever affirms the warning that Our messengers gave him, accepts from them what they brought from God, and does righteous deeds in this world. ﴿Then there will be no fear for them﴾: upon their arrival before their Lord, from His punishment and chastisement which God has prepared for His enemies and the people of His disobedience. ﴿Nor will they grieve﴾: at that time, over what they left behind in the world. [[See the explanation of similar verses above, vol. 1, p. 551; vol. 2, pp. 150, 512, 513; vol. 5, p. 519; vol. 7, p. 396.]]

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Those who deny Our signs, the punishment will touch them for what they used to defiantly disobey﴾ (6:49)**

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His mention, means: As for those who denied the one to whom We sent Our messengers, opposed Our command and Our prohibition, and rejected Our proof, Our punishment and Our retribution will reach them for their denial of the proofs We sent [[See the explanation of "al-mass" (touching) above, p. 287, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿for what they used to defiantly disobey﴾, meaning: for what they used to deny.

* *

Ibn Zayd used to say: Every instance of "fisq" (defiant disobedience) in the Qur'an means lying. [[See what preceded shortly before, p. 206, note 2, and the references there. See also the two reports numbered 12103 and 12983.]]

13251 - Yunus narrated to me this, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, from him. [[At this point ends a section of the old division from which our copy was taken, and in it is the following text:

"Followed by the discussion of the interpretation of His saying ﴿Say: I do not tell you that I have the treasures of God, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me. Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal? Will you not reflect?﴾ And may God bless Muhammad the Prophet and his family abundantly and grant them peace," and then followed by the text: "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. My Lord, help me."]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 50:

The explanation of His words: ﴿Say: I do not tell you that with me are the treasuries of Allah, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me. Say: Are the blind and the seeing alike? Will you not then reflect?﴾ (50)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may He be exalted, says: Say to these deniers of your prophethood: I do not tell you that I am the Lord who possesses the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, and that I know the hidden unseen matters of things, which none knows except the Lord to whom nothing is hidden [see the explanation of "al-ghayb" (the unseen) above: 238, note 1, and the references there], so that you would disbelieve me in what I say of that. For it is not fitting that one be a lord except one who has dominion over everything, in whose hand is everything, and to whom no hidden thing is concealed, and that is Allah, there is no god but Him. ﴿Nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾, because it is not fitting for an angel to appear in his form to the eyes of mankind in this world, so that you would deny what I tell you of that [see the explanation of "malak" (angel) above 1: 444-447 / 4: 262, 263]. ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾, he says: Say to them: I follow in what I say to you and call you to only the revelation of Allah that He reveals to me, and His revelation that He sends down upon me [see the explanation of "al-wahy" (revelation) above: 290, note 1, and the references there], so I carry out His revelation and obey His command, and I have come to you with conclusive proofs from Allah as an excuse against you for the soundness of my words in that. What I say of that is not something strange to your minds nor impossible in its occurrence; rather, that, together with the existence of the proof of its reality, is perfect wisdom. So what is the basis of your denial of it?

This is an admonition from Allah, exalted is He, to His Prophet ﷺ regarding the place of his argument against the deniers of his prophethood among his people, the polytheists.

﴿Say: Are the blind and the seeing alike?﴾ He, may He be exalted, says: Say, O Muhammad, to them: Are the one blind to the truth and the one who sees it alike? ﴿The blind﴾ is the disbeliever who has become blind to the proofs of Allah, so he does not discern them and follow them; ﴿the seeing﴾ is the believer who has seen the signs and proofs of Allah, so he is guided by them and illuminated by their light [see the explanation of "al-a'má" (the blind) and "al-basir" (the seeing) above in the language indexes, under (ʿ-m-y) and (b-ṣ-r)]. ﴿Will you not then reflect?﴾ He says to those who denied the signs of Allah: Will you not reflect, O people, on what I argue against you with these proofs, so that you would know the soundness of what I say and call you to, and the corruption of what you persist in of associating idols and rivals with Allah your Lord, and your denial of me despite the manifestation of the proofs of my truthfulness before your eyes, so that you would abandon the disbelief in which you persist, for the faith to which I call you, by which you will succeed? [In the manuscript: "turn back" (taʿūdūn); the correct reading is that of the printed edition.]

* *

Similar to what we have said in the interpretation of this, a group of the people of interpretation said.

Mention of those who said that:

13252 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah, exalted is He: "Say: Are the blind and the seeing alike?" He said: The one astray and the one guided.

13253 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

13254 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: "Say: Are the blind and the seeing alike?" to the end of the verse, he said: "The blind" is the disbeliever who has become blind to the right of Allah, His command, and His blessings upon him; and "the seeing" is the believing servant who saw with beneficial sight, so he made Allah alone, worked in obedience to his Lord, and benefited by what Allah had given him.

**The Interpretation of His Words:** ﴿And warn with it those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having no protector or intercessor besides Him, so that they may be mindful of God.﴾ (6:51)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may He be exalted and remembered, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Warn, O Muhammad, with the Qur'an that We have sent down to you, the people who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, knowing that this will certainly happen. They believe in God's promise and threat, act in what pleases God, and are persistent in striving [[In the printed edition: "dāʼimūn fī al-saʻy" (those who are constant in striving), but the correct reading is what appears in the manuscript.]] for what will save them on their return from the punishment of God [[See the explanation of "al-indhār" (warning) above: 290, 369. And the explanation of "al-ḥashr" (gathering) above, pp. 346–349, note 1, and the references there.]]."

"﴿Having no protector besides Him﴾," meaning: they have no one to protect them from the punishment of God if He punishes them. "﴿Protector﴾," meaning one who helps them and rescues them from it [[See the explanation of "walī" in the linguistic indexes above, root (w-l-y).]]. "﴿Or intercessor﴾," meaning one who intercedes for them with God, may He be remembered and exalted, so that He frees them from His punishment [[See the explanation of "shafīʻ" above, 8:580, note 3, and the references there.]]. "﴿So that they may be mindful﴾," meaning: warn them so that they will be mindful of God regarding themselves, obey their Lord, work for their return, and beware of His wrath by avoiding His disobedience."

* *

It has been said: "﴿And warn with it those who fear that they will be gathered﴾" means: those who know that they will be gathered. The word "fear" is used in place of "knowledge," because their fear arose from their knowledge that this would occur and exist, without any doubt on their part about it [[See the explanation of "al-khawf" (fear) above: 4:550; 8:298, 299, 318; 9:123, 267. See also al-Farra's Maʻani al-Qur'an 1:336.]].

* *

This is a command from God, may He be exalted and remembered, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to teach his companions what God has sent down to him of His revelation, to remind them, and to turn toward them with warning, [and] [[In the printed edition: "wa-ṣadda ʻanhu al-mushrikūn bihi" (and the polytheists turned away from it), but the manuscript reads differently, and the printed version corrupts the meaning beyond acceptability.]] after giving them warning and after establishing proof against them, so that God alone is the Judge in their affair, deciding concerning them whatever judgment He wills.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 52 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance. Not at all is any of their reckoning upon you, nor is any of your reckoning upon them, that you should drive them away and thus be among the wrongdoers.﴾ (6:52)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), regarding a group of weak Muslims. The polytheists said to him: "If you were to drive these people away from you, we would sit with you and attend your gathering!"

The narration concerning this:

13255. Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, saying: Abu Zubayd narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Kurdus al-Tha'labi, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Prophet (ﷺ) while with him were Suhayb, Ammar, Bilal, Khabbab and others of the weak Muslims. They said: "O Muhammad, are you content with these people from your folk? These are the ones whom Allah has favoured from among us? Are we to be followers of these? Drive them away from you! Perhaps if you drive them away, we will follow you!" Then this verse was revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance﴾, down to ﴿And thus We have tried some of them through others﴾, to the end of the verse.

[[The narrator: "Abu Zubayd" is "Abthar ibn al-Qasim al-Zubaydi", a trustworthy transmitter, mentioned earlier under no. 12336 and 12402. In the printed edition it was "Abu Zayd", which contradicts the manuscript and is an error. "Ash'ath" is "Ash'ath ibn Sawwar", trustworthy, mentioned many times. "Kurdus al-Tha'labi" is "Kurdus ibn al-Abbas al-Tha'labi", a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i), listed in al-Tarikh al-Kabir 4/1/242-243 and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/175, where there is disagreement about his father's name and his nisba is given as "al-Taghlabi" with a ta' and a ghayn; the form "al-Tha'labi", as it appears in Abu Ja'far's narration, is the correct one.

This report was narrated by Abu Ja'far through three chains, this one and the two following it. . . Ahmad recorded it in his Musnad, no. 3985, through Asbat, from Ash'ath, from Kurdus, from Ibn Mas'ud, in a similar but abridged form. Al-Haythami cited it in Majma' al-Zawa'id and said: "Ahmad and al-Tabarani narrated it" (he mentioned al-Tabarani's addition, which agrees with what is in the tafsir), "and the narrators of Ahmad are the narrators of the Sahih, except Kurdus, who is trustworthy." Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:12, and attributed it additionally to Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya.]]

13256. ......Jarir narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Kurdus al-Tha'labi, from Abd Allah, who said: The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then he mentioned something similar.

[[Narration 13256: I have placed dots at the beginning of this chain, because Abu Ja'far could not have narrated directly from "Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Dabbi"; rather, his teachers narrated from him, such as "Muhammad ibn Humayd al-Razi", as in narration no. 10, and others.]]

13257. Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Kurdus, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A group of Quraysh's chiefs passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then he mentioned something similar.

[[Narration 13257: In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "from Kardas, from Ibn Abbas", which is an error beyond doubt. This report was not narrated except from Ibn Mas'ud, and Kurdus is not recorded as having narrated from Ibn Abbas. No one in the books attributes this report to anyone other than Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud. Kurdus is "Kurdus ibn Abbas al-Tha'labi", as previously mentioned in the note to no. 13255. In the manuscript, "an" ("from") has been written above, between "Kurdus ibn Abbas", so it appears to be an addition by the copyist. This report, as narrated by Abu Ja'far, is not traced back to Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, so I do not know whether the copyist made an error and omitted something, or whether the narration is like this.]]

13258. Al-Husayn ibn Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Sa'd al-Azdi, who was the reciter of the Azd, from Abu al-Kanud, from Khabbab, concerning the saying of Allah, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance﴾, to His words ﴿so that you would be among the wrongdoers﴾. He said: Al-Aqra' ibn Habis al-Tamimi and Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari came and found the Prophet (ﷺ) sitting with Bilal, Suhayb, Ammar and Khabbab, among some weak believers. [[In the printed edition: "from the weak believers", which differs from the manuscript.]] When they saw them around him, they looked down on them. They came to him and said: "We would like you to make for us a gathering with you, by which the Arabs will recognize our merit, for the delegations of the Arabs come to you, and we are ashamed that the Arabs should see us with these slaves. So when we come to you, remove them from us; and when we have finished, sit with them if you wish!" He said: "Yes!" They said: "Then write for us a document of your commitment to this." He said: So he called for the sheet, and called Ali to write. He said: We were sitting in a corner when Gabriel descended with this verse: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance. Not at all is any of their reckoning upon you, nor is any of your reckoning upon them, that you should drive them away and thus be among the wrongdoers﴾. Then he said: ﴿And thus We have tried some of them through others, that they might say, "Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ Then he said: ﴿And when those who believe in Our verses come to you, say, "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has decreed for Himself mercy."﴾ So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) threw the sheet from his hand, then called us, and we came to him while he was saying: "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has decreed for Himself mercy!" So we would sit with him, and whenever he wanted to rise, he rose and left us. Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance, and let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 28]. He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would sit with us, and when the hour came for him to rise, we rose and left him until he got up.

[[Narration 13258: "al-Husayn ibn Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqari" is weak and lenient. His father "Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqari" is trustworthy and acceptable in narration, mentioned under no. 6139. "Asbat" is "Asbat ibn Nasr al-Hamdani"; Ahmad declared him weak, but my brother preferred his trustworthiness, as passed in the note on narration no. 168. As for "al-Suddi", he is "Isma'il ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Karima al-Suddi", who is trustworthy, also mentioned under no. 168. "Abu Sa'id al-Azdi", the reciter of the Azd, is "Abu Sa'd al-Arhabi" or "Abu Sa'id al-Arhabi", as will come in the next narration. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat; he was mentioned under no. 8700. In the printed edition here it reads "Abu Sa'id", and I have adopted what is in the manuscript. "Abu al-Kanud al-Azdi" differs regarding his name: it is said "Abd Allah ibn Amir", and it is said "Abd Allah ibn Imran", and other things. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat, and among the authors of the six books only Ibn Majah narrated from him, and he narrated this very report to him. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib. This report was narrated by Ibn Majah through this same chain, with a slight addition in its wording, in his Sunan, p. 1382, no. 4127. In al-Zawa'id, it says: "Its chain is sound, and its narrators are trustworthy; Muslim, al-Nasa'i and the author narrated part of it from the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas..." As for Ibn Kathir, he said in his tafsir, having cited the report from Ibn Abi Hatim's tafsir through this same chain (3:315, 316): "This is a strange hadith, for this verse is Meccan, and al-Aqra' ibn Habis and Uyayna only embraced Islam long after the Hijra." This is the truth, if Allah wills.

Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:13, and attributed it additionally to Ibn Abi Shayba, Abu Ya'la, Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il.]]

13259. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Sa'id al-Azdi, from Abu al-Kanud, from Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, with a report similar to the hadith of al-Husayn ibn Amr, except that in his narration he said: "When they saw them around him, they drove them away (nafarruhum), so they came to him and sat privately with him." He also said: "and thus be among the wrongdoers", then he mentioned al-Aqra' and his companion, and said: ﴿And thus We have tried some of them through others﴾, the verse. He also said: "He called us, and we came to him while he was saying, 'Peace be upon you.' So we drew near to him that day until we placed our knees upon his knees", and the rest of the hadith is similar to it.

[[Narration 13259: "Abu Sa'id al-Azdi" is "Abu Sa'id al-Arhabi", the same as in the previous narration, where he is "Abu Sa'd". Both forms are correct, as I have mentioned.]]

13260. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada. And Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada and al-Kalbi, that some disbelievers of Quraysh said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "If it pleases you that we follow you, drive away from us so-and-so and so-and-so, some weak Muslims!" So Allah, exalted is His remembrance, said: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance﴾.

13261. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His words: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾, to His words ﴿And thus We have tried some of them through others﴾, the verse. He said: Some people said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "O Muhammad, if it pleases you that we follow you, then drive away from us so-and-so and so-and-so", referring to people who were beneath them in the world, whom the polytheists looked down upon. So Allah, exalted is His remembrance, revealed this verse to its end.

13262. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾: they were Bilal and Ibn Umm Abd (Ibn Mas'ud), who used to sit with Muhammad (ﷺ). Quraysh, belittling them, said: "Were it not for them and their like, we would have sat with him!" So he was forbidden to drive them away, up to His words ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾. He said: ﴿Say, "Peace be upon you"﴾, in what lies between that, in this (context).

13263. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh, from his father, who said: Sa'd said: "This verse was revealed concerning six of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), among them Ibn Mas'ud." He said: "We used to be ahead of others to the Prophet (ﷺ), draw near to him, and listen to him, so Quraysh said: 'These draw near to him ahead of us!'" Then this was revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾.

[[Narration 13263: "Sufyan" is al-Thawri. "al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh ibn Hani ibn Yazid al-Harithi" is trustworthy; he is mentioned in al-Tahdhib. His father "Shurayh ibn Hani ibn Yazid al-Harith" attained the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) but did not see him. He narrated from his father, Umar, Ali, Bilal, Sa'd, and Abu Hurayra. Ibn Sa'd mentioned him in the first class of the Successors of the people of Kufa. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib. "Sa'd" is "Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas", the Companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "Sa'id", which is an error. This report was narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, 15:187, through two routes: through Sufyan, from al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh; and through Isra'il, from al-Miqdam. Ibn Majah narrated it in his Sunan, p. 1383, no. 4128, through Qays ibn al-Rabi', from al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh, in a similar form but with different wording. Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:13, and attributed it additionally to Ahmad, al-Firyabi, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Nasa'i, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Hakim, Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il.]]

13264. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ikrima, concerning His words: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾, the verse. He said: Utba ibn Rabi'a, Shayba ibn Rabi'a, Mut'im ibn Adi, al-Harith ibn Nawfal, and Qarza ibn Abd Amr ibn Nawfal, along with nobles of the Banu Abd Manaf among the disbelievers, came to Abu Talib and said: "O Abu Talib, if your nephew would drive away from him our clients and allies, for they are only our slaves and hirelings, it would be greater in our hearts, more obedient to him among us, and closer to our following him and believing him!" He said: So Abu Talib came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him what they had said to him. Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "If you were to do that, wait to see what they want, and where their words will lead them!" So Allah, exalted is His remembrance, revealed this verse: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, for them there is no protector or intercessor besides Him, perhaps they will be mindful of Allah. And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance﴾, to His words ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾. He said: They were Bilal, Ammar ibn Yasir, Salim the client of Abu Hudhayfa, Subayh the client of Usayd [[In the printed edition: "Bilal... Salim... Subayh", in the accusative, as in al-Durr al-Manthur and Ibn Kathir; but what is in the manuscript is the better and sound reading. This is if this narration is indeed the correct version; otherwise, I found in al-Isaba, in the biography of this "Subayh", where it says: "from Hajjaj, from Ibn Jurayj", and in it: "They were three: Ammar ibn Yasir, Salim the client of Abu Hudhayfa, and Subayh." If this is correct, then the error is in the word "Bilal", and the correct reading is "three", but I cannot prefer that now.]] = and among the allies: Ibn Mas'ud, al-Miqdad ibn Amr, Mas'ud ibn al-Qari, Waqid ibn Abd Allah al-Handhali, Amr ibn Abd Amr Dhu al-Shimalayn, Murthid ibn Abi Murthid = Abu Murthid, of Ghani, the ally of Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib = and their likes among the allies. And there was revealed concerning the leaders of disbelief among Quraysh, the clients and allies: ﴿And thus We have tried some of them through others, that they might say, "Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?"﴾, the verse. When it was revealed, Umar ibn al-Khattab came and apologized for his statement, so Allah, exalted is His remembrance, revealed: ﴿And when those who believe in Our verses come to you, say, "Peace be upon you"﴾, the verse.

[[Narration 13264: "Mas'ud ibn al-Qari" is "Mas'ud ibn Rabi'a ibn Amr al-Qari", ascribed to "al-Qara", and he was an ally of the Banu Zuhra. "Waqid ibn Abd Allah al-Handhali al-Tamimi" was an ally of the Banu Adi ibn Ka'b. "Amr ibn Abd Amr ibn Fadla al-Khuza'i", "Dhu al-Shimalayn", was an ally of the Banu Zuhra. It has been reported that Ammar said: "There were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) three, all of them ambidextrous (adhbat): Dhu al-Shimalayn, Umar ibn al-Khattab, and Abu Layla." The "adhbat" is the one who works with both his hands.]]

13265. Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: A man said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "I am ashamed before Allah that He should see me with Salman, Bilal and their likes (dhawiyahum). So drive them away from you, and sit with so-and-so and so-and-so!" He said: Then the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance﴾. He recited until he reached ﴿and thus be among the wrongdoers﴾: "Between you and being among the wrongdoers there is nothing but that you drive them away." Then He said: ﴿And thus We have tried some of them through others, that they might say, "Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us? Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?"﴾ Then He said: "And these whom they have commanded you to drive away, convey to them my greeting, give them glad tidings, and inform them that I have forgiven them!" And he recited: ﴿And when those who believe in Our verses come to you, say, "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has decreed for Himself mercy"﴾, and he recited until he reached ﴿And thus We detail the verses, and that the way of the criminals may become clear﴾. He said: "That you may know it."

[[The phrase "dhawiyahum" means: their companions and their likes. I have already mentioned in Part 3, p. 261, note 2, that the grammarians have much to say, and the claim that the addition of "dhu" to a pronoun occurs only in the necessity of poetry. I said that it occurred in prose in ancient times, and this report is among the evidence for what I said.]]

* *

The interpreters differed concerning the supplication which those group, whom Allah forbade His Prophet (ﷺ) from driving away, used to make to their Lord.

Some of them said: It is the five obligatory prayers. [[In the printed edition: "the prescribed prayers", but I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]]

Those who said this:

13266. Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾, meaning: those who worship their Lord, "morning and evening", meaning: the prescribed prayers.

13267. Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Abu Hamza, from Ibrahim, concerning His words: ﴿Those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance﴾. He said: They are the five obligatory prayers. And if it were as the storytellers (al-qussas) say,

[[In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "wa-law kana yaqulu al-qussas", without "ma", which is an error.]]

"Al-qasas" is the plural of "qass" (storyteller), referring to one who stands up in a mosque or elsewhere, then begins to admonish people and remind them with the reports of past peoples. His narratives are liable to acquire additions and omissions, and for this reason a hadith says: "The storyteller awaits hatred." And there is the hadith: "When the Children of Israel told stories, they perished," meaning: when they added to the report and the narrative and lied. This is among the worst of deeds. But the Children of Israel fell into it, so God punished and destroyed them through it, and we entered into it too, eagerly, so God punished us with the scattering of our affairs, the weakness of our scholars, and the loss of our awe from the hearts of our enemies.
So, O God, guide us to the right path. Then see the following reports, numbers: 13270, and the reports: 13227, 13282. Those who did not sit with them perished.

13268 - Hanad ibn al-Sarri and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim: "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His face," he said: "It is the prayer."

13269 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening," the obligatory prayer, the dawn and the afternoon.

13270 - Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Kindi narrated to me, saying: Husayn al-Ju'fi narrated to us, saying: Hamza ibn al-Mughira informed me, from Hamza ibn Isa, who said: I entered upon al-Hasan and asked him, saying: "O Abu Sa'id, what do you say about the saying of God: 'And restrain yourself with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening' [Surah al-Kahf: 28]? Are these the storytellers?" He said: "No, rather they are those who guard the prayers in congregation."
[[Report 13270: "Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Kindi," a teacher of al-Tabari, I found no mention of him. In the printed edition here it was "Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Kindi," differing from the manuscript, with "Muhammad ibn" omitted; this is a blameworthy and ugly alteration. "Husayn al-Ju'fi" is "Husayn ibn Ali ibn al-Walid al-Ju'fi," which has passed many times; the printed edition had "Hasan al-Ju'fi," which is a pure error. "Hamza ibn al-Mughira ibn Nashit al-Makhzumi," the worshipper, has passed under number 184.
As for "Hamza ibn Isa," I did not find among the narrators anyone named thus, and I incline to think the copyist erred, rewriting "Hamza," so the name became confused; it cannot be corrected unless it is found elsewhere.]]

13271 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's saying: "Those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening," he said: the prescribed prayer.

13272 - It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: "call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening," he said: they worship their Lord "in the morning and the evening," meaning the prescribed prayer.

13273 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying: "And restrain yourself with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening" [Surah al-Kahf: 28], they are the two prayers: the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer.

13274 - Ibn al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ajlan narrated to us, from Nafi', from Abdullah ibn Umar, concerning this verse: "And restrain yourself with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening," the verse, that they are those who attend the prescribed prayers.
[[Report 13274: al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 4: 219, and attributed it additionally to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh. This chain is sound.]]

13275 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid and Ibrahim: "And restrain yourself with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening," they both said: the five prayers.

13276 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, the like of it.

13277 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening," he said: the believing worshippers who pray, Bilal and Ibn Umm Abd. Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah ibn Kathir informed me, from Mujahid, who said: I prayed the dawn prayer with Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, and when the imam finished the salam, the people rushed to the storyteller. Sa'id said: "How quickly they hasten to this assembly!" Mujahid said: I said, "They interpret what God, may He be mentioned, said." He said: "And what did He say?" I said: "'And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening.'" He said: "And is this about that? It is about the prayer from which we have just turned; it is about the prayer."
[[In the printed edition: "ma asra'uhum ila hadha al-majlis" ("how quick they are to this assembly"); in the manuscript: "ma asra' ila hadha al-majlis"; I judged the correct reading to be what I have adopted.]]

13278 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from his father, from Mansur, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Amra, who said: the prescribed prayer.
[[Report 13278: "Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Amra ibn Mihsan ibn Tha'laba al-Ansari," who narrated from his father, Uthman ibn Affan, and Ubada ibn al-Samit. Ibn Sa'd said: "He was trustworthy, abundant in narrations." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.
This matter will come at length under number 13282.]]

13279 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Amir, who said: it is the prayer.

13280 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from his father, from Isra'il, from Amir, who said: it is the prayer.

13281 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying: "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His face," he says: the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer.

13282 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Amra prayed in the Mosque of the Messenger; when he finished he stood and leaned against the chamber of the Prophet (ﷺ), and the people crowded around him. He said: "O people, to you!" It was said to him: "May God have mercy on you, they have come only seeking this verse: 'And restrain yourself with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening' [Surah al-Kahf: 28]." He said: "And this is what was meant by this! It is only about the prayer."
[[Report 13282 is the extended form of the report earlier numbered 13278. "The people crowded around him" (inthal): they followed one another and streamed in from every direction.
This report is evidence of the soundness of the knowledge of our earlier imams regarding the rights of their religion and of their Book sent down to them from their Lord. It is also evidence of the corruption into which our scholars and our writers fell, and of those among us who approached the Book of God with personal desire, so that this rejected interpretation, which the imams rejected, became a proof used by the ignorant among the Sufis and the people of trickery to support claims of saintly status and the assertion of wonders. O God, keep us far from ignorance, and carry us upon the right path.
* *
This, and these reports which he mentioned here, in which he explained the verse of Surah al-Kahf: 28, most of them are not narrated in the tafsir of "Surah al-Kahf," and this is one of the ways in which Abu Ja'far abridged this tafsir.]] Others said: it is the prayer, but the people did not ask the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to drive these weak ones away from his assembly, nor to delay them from his assembly; they only asked him to delay them from the first row, so that they would be behind them in the row.

Mention of those who said that:

13283 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying: "And thus We tried some of them with others" [Surah al-An'am: 53], the verse: they were people from the poor who were with the Prophet (ﷺ). Some people of the nobles said: "We will believe in you, but when we pray, delay these who are with you, so that they pray behind us!"
* *
Others said: rather the meaning of "their calling" was their remembrance of God, may He be mentioned.

Mention of those who said that:

13284 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us; and Hanad narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, concerning His saying: "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening," he said: the people of remembrance.

13285 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur: "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening," he said: they are the people of remembrance.

13286 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening," he said: do not drive them away from remembrance.
* *
Others said: rather that was their teaching of the Qur'an and its recitation.

Mention of those who said that:

13287 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far concerning His saying: "And restrain yourself with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening" [Surah al-Kahf: 28], he said: he used to teach them the Qur'an. Who is it that narrates to the Prophet (ﷺ)?!
[[In the printed edition: "qala kana yuqri'uhum al-Qur'an al-Nabi (ﷺ)," an addition absent from the manuscript. What I have adopted is: "min al-ladhi yaqussu ʿala" and then the sentence was joined, with error and corruption! These are two separate sentences: the first, "he used to teach them the Qur'an," and the second, the interrogative, "who is it that narrates to the Prophet (ﷺ)?" Both are a rebuttal of those who interpreted the verse as meaning the storytellers, that is the preachers, as is evident from reports 13267, 13270, 13277, 13282, and that the Prophet (ﷺ) was teaching these people the Qur'an, so he was commanded to restrain himself with them. Had the storytellers been meant by the verse, the Prophet (ﷺ) would have been commanded to restrain himself with those who sit and admonish and remind him of God, may my father and mother be sacrificed for him (ﷺ)! Therefore he said: "Who is it that narrates to the Prophet (ﷺ)?", that is: who is this who admonishes the Messenger of God and reminds him of God and of the days of God?!
This is a clear proof against those who interpreted the verse otherwise than the correct sense upon which the proof agreed.]]
* *
Others said: rather he meant by their calling their Lord, their worship of Him.

Mention of those who said that:

13288 - It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: "call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening," he said: he means: they worship, do you not see that He said: "Without doubt, that to which you call me has no claim" [Surah Ghafir: 43], meaning: you worship.
[[The verse is thus given in both the manuscript and the printed edition, and I am nearly certain that this is an error, from the lapse of a narrator or from Abu Ja'far himself; I incline to think he meant the verse of Surah Ghafir: 66: "Say: I have been forbidden to worship those whom you call upon besides God." The verse he substituted cannot be read with "calling" meaning "worship."]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter is to say: God, may He be mentioned, forbade His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to drive away a people who were calling upon their Lord in the morning and the evening. "Calling upon God" occurs through His remembrance, glorification and praise, by speech and words, and it may occur through acting for Him with the limbs, the deeds that were obligatory for them, and other supererogatory acts which please the Lord of the one who acts, toward the worshipper for what he does for Him. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "allati tarda 'an al-'amil lahu 'abidahu," which is not correct; the correct reading appears to be what I have adopted.]] It may also be that these people were combining all these meanings, so God described them as calling upon Him in the morning and the evening, because God has named "worship" as "calling," and He, may He be mentioned, said: "And your Lord said: Call upon Me, I will answer you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humbled" [Surah Ghafir: 60]. It may also be that this refers to a specific kind of calling.

There is no view more sound for this than describing the people by what God described them with: that they used to call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, so the description He gave of them applies generally, and none of it is restricted to one part over another.

The meaning of the speech therefore is: O Muhammad, warn with the Qur'an which I have sent down to you those who know that they will be gathered to their Lord. They, out of fear of coming before God, beside whom they have no intercessor and no helper, are persistent in acting for Him. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "da'imun", and I judge that what I have adopted is correct.]] When those among your people who disbelieve in God and the Last Day turn away from your warning and from listening to what God has sent down to you, out of arrogance toward God, do not drive them away and do not push them aside, lest you be among those who put exclusion in other than its place, excluding and driving away those whom it was not for him to drive away or exclude, and bringing near those whom it was not for him to advance by nearness and closeness. For those whom I forbade you to drive away are those who call upon their Lord, asking Him for His pardon and forgiveness through their righteous deeds, and fulfilling what He obligated upon them of His duties and their voluntary supererogations, and remembering Him with their tongues in the morning and the evening, seeking thereby nearness to God and closeness to His pleasure. "Upon you is nothing of their reckoning," meaning: upon you is nothing of the reckoning of what I have provided them of provision; and upon them is nothing of the reckoning of what I have provided you of provision; "so that you would drive them away," fearing my reckoning of you for what I have granted them of provision in the world.
* *
His saying "so that you would drive them away" is the answer to His saying: "Upon you is nothing of their reckoning, and upon them is nothing of your reckoning."
His saying "and thus you would be among the wrongdoers" is the answer to His saying: "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord."

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And thus We tested some of them by means of others, that they might say, "Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ [6:53]

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "And thus We tested some of them by means of others," may He be exalted, He means: And thus We tested and afflicted them, as in the following:

13289 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar. And al-Husayn ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding "And thus We tested some of them by means of others": he said, "We afflicted some of them by means of others."

* *

We have already shown earlier in this book the meaning of "fitnah" (trial), that it is testing and affliction, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary. [See the explanation of "fitnah" earlier, p. 297, note 2, and the references there.]

* *

Allah's testing of some of His creatures by means of others is His differentiating among them in what He has apportioned to them of provisions and dispositions. So He made some rich and some poor, some strong and some weak, and made some of them need others, as a test from Him for them through that.

* *

Scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) from a group said in agreement with what we have said.

Those who said that:

13290 - al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words "And thus We tested some of them by means of others": he means that He made some of them rich and some of them poor, so the rich said to the poor, "Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?" meaning: Allah has guided them. They only said that mockingly and derisively.

* *

As for His words "that they might say, 'Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?'" He, may He be exalted, says: We tested people with wealth and poverty, honour and humiliation, strength and weakness, guidance and misguidance, so that whoever Allah has misguided and blinded from the path of truth would say to those whom Allah has guided and granted success: "Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour" with guidance and right conduct, while they are poor, weak, and humble [See the explanation of "al-mann" (favour) earlier, 7:369 / 9:71] "from among us," while we are rich and strong? Mocking them and showing enmity to Islam and its people.

He, may He be exalted, says: "Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?" This is His response to those polytheists who denied that Allah guides the people of humility and weakness to the truth and leaves the rich among them without it, and it is an affirmation to them: I know best who among My creatures is grateful for My blessing and who is ungrateful for it. So My favour upon those whom I have favoured with guidance is a reward for their thankfulness to Me for My blessing, and My abandonment of those whom I have abandoned from the path of right guidance is a punishment for their ingratitude toward Me for My blessing, not because of the wealth of the rich among them nor the poverty of the poor, because reward and punishment are deserved by no one except as recompense for his own deeds which he has earned, not for his wealth or poverty, since wealth, poverty, weakness and strength are not among the actions of My creatures.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿When those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy: whoever of you does evil in ignorance, then repents after it and amends, then indeed He is Forgiving, Merciful﴾ [6:54].

Abu Ja'far said: The people of *ta'wil* (interpretation, the explanation of what a verse means) differed concerning those whom God, exalted is His remembrance, meant by this verse.

Some of them said: It means those whom God forbade His Prophet from driving away. The report with this has already passed from those who said it. [[See above, nos. 13258 and what follows.]]

Others said: It means a people who asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about great sins they had committed, and God did not make them despair of repentance.

Mention of those who said this:

13291 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mujammi', he said: I heard Mahan say: A people came to the Prophet (ﷺ) who had committed great sins. Mahan said: I do not think he replied to them with anything. He said: So God, exalted is His remembrance, revealed this verse: "When those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: Peace be upon you," to the end of the verse. [[The narrations 13291–13293: "Sufyan" is Ibn 'Uyayna. "Mujammi'" is Mujammi' ibn Sammaan Abu Hamza al-Tamimi, a reliable narrator, passed as no. 12710. "Mahan" al-Hanafi, Abu Salim al-A'war al-Abid, passed as no. 3226.]]

13292 - Hannad narrated to us, he said: Qabisa narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mujammi', from Mahan: that a people came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, we have committed great sins!" He said: I do not think he replied to them with anything. They departed, and God, exalted is His remembrance, revealed: "When those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy." He said: So he called them and recited it to them.

13293 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mujammi' al-Tamimi, he said: I heard Mahan say: and he mentioned something similar.

* * *

Others said: Rather, it refers to a group of believers who had advised the Prophet (ﷺ) to drive away the people whom God had forbidden him to drive away. This act of advising was a sin on their part, so God forgave them and pardoned them, and He commanded His Prophet (ﷺ), when they came to him, to give them the good news that their sin which had passed from them through their advice to the Prophet (ﷺ) to drive away those people had been forgiven. This is the view of Ikrima and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, and we have already mentioned the reports from them to this effect. [[See above, nos. 13264, 13265.]]

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these views, in my opinion, for the interpretation of the verse, is the view of those who said: those meant by "When those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: Peace be upon you" are not those whom God forbade the Prophet (ﷺ) from driving away. This is because His saying "When those who believe in Our signs come to you" is a new statement, following the completion of the report about those whom God forbade His Prophet (ﷺ) from driving away. Had they been the same people, it would have said: "When they come to you, say: Peace be upon you." The fact that God began a report about the story of these people, and did not connect the speech to the report about the earlier ones, indicates that they are other than them.

So the meaning of the speech, then, given that the matter is as we have described, is: "And when there come to you, O Muhammad, the people who affirm Our revelation, Our proofs and Our arguments, confirming that by word and deed, seeking your guidance about their sins which have passed from them between Me and them, whether there is repentance for them from these, then do not make them despair of it, and say to them: 'Peace be upon you,' a security from God for you regarding your sins, that He will not punish you for them after you repent of them." [[See the explanation of "peace" (salam) above, 10:145, and the root (s-l-m) in the language indexes.]] "Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy": that is, your Lord has decreed mercy for His creation. [[See the explanation of "prescribed" (kataba) above, p. 273, note 2, and the references there.]] "That whoever of you does evil in ignorance, then repents after it and amends, then indeed He is Forgiving, Merciful."

* * *

The readers differed in reading this:

The common reading of the Medinan readers (qurra' al-Madaniyyin) is ﴿أَنَّهُ مَنْ عَمِلَ مِنْكُمْ سُوءًا﴾, making "anna" (that) in the accusative, as an explanation of "mercy" (al-rahma), and ﴿ثُمَّ تَابَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ وَأَصْلَحَ فَإِنَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾, with "inna" (indeed) beginning a new sentence after the "fa" (then), so they read it with a kasra, making it a particle with no grammatical position, in the sense of: "then He is for him Forgiving and Merciful," or "then for him is forgiveness and mercy." [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 336, 337.]]

* * *

Some of the Kufan readers read both of them with a fatha on the hamza (alif) of both, in the sense of: "Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy" [that] "whoever of you does evil in ignorance"—then "fa-anna" (that indeed) is explained by the words "that whoever of you does evil in ignorance" as an explanation of "mercy," and ﴿فَأَنَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ is joined with the second "anna" to the first "anna," making both of them accusative nouns as I have explained. [[See what Abu Ja'far said in explaining this reading above, pp. 278–280.]]

* * *

Some of the Meccan readers and most of the readers of Iraq, from Kufa and Basra, read "inna" in "innahu" and "innahu" with a kasra on the hamza, as a beginning, and as particles with no grammatical position.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these readings in my opinion is the reading of those who read both with a kasra: ﴿كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ الرَّحْمَةَ إِنَّهُ﴾, as the beginning of speech, and that the report ended at His saying "Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy," and then a new report was begun about what He, exalted is His remembrance, does with those who do evil in ignorance, then repent and amend.

* * *

The meaning of His saying "that whoever of you does evil in ignorance" is: whoever among you commits a sin and does it in ignorance. [[See the explanation of "ignorance" (jahala) above, 8: 89–93, which is a very good explanation.]] "Then repents and amends," then "indeed He is Forgiving," for his sin, if he repents, returns to God, turns back to obedience to God and abandons returning to the like of it, together with remorse for what he has neglected. "Merciful" toward the penitent, that He will not punish him for his sin after his repentance from it.

Similar to what we have said on this was said by a group of the people of interpretation.

Mention of those who said that:

13294 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, he said: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from 'Uthman, from Mujahid: "whoever of you does evil in ignorance," he said: from ignorance: that he does not know the lawful from the unlawful, and from his ignorance he undertakes the matter.

13295 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, he said: Abu Khalid narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, the same.

13296 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid: "they do evil in ignorance," he said: whoever acts in disobedience to God, that is ignorance on his part until he returns.

13297 - al-Harith narrated to me, he said: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, he said: Bakr ibn Khunays narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid concerning His saying: "whoever of you does evil in ignorance," he said: everyone who commits a sin is ignorant of it. [[Report 13297: Bakr ibn Khunays al-Kufi, the worshipper, narrates from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad, Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, and 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah. Ibn 'Adi said: "He is among those whose hadith is written down, and he narrates strange hadiths from people who are not objectionable, and he himself is a righteous man, except that the righteous are confused about hadith, and they sometimes narrate by assumption. His hadith is among the weak narrations, and he is not one whose hadith is used as evidence," and things harsher than this have been said about him. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

13298 - al-Harith narrated to me, he said: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, he said: Khalid ibn Dinar Abu Khalda narrated to us, he said: When we entered upon Abu al-'Aliya, he would recite: "When those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy." [[Report 13298: Khalid ibn Dinar al-Tamimi al-Sa'di, Abu Khalda, a reliable narrator, passed as nos. 44 and 12239.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 55:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And thus do We detail the signs, that the way of the criminals may become clear﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying "And thus do We detail the signs," may He be exalted and remembered, He means: just as We have detailed for you in this surah, from its beginning and opening, O Muhammad, up to this point, Our proof against the polytheists who worship idols, and Our arguments, distinguishing them for you and clarifying them, so too do We detail for you Our signs and Our arguments concerning every truth that the people of falsehood deny, among all other religious communities (milal), so that We may make it clear to you, until you distinguish its truth from its falsehood, and its soundness from its unsoundness.

* *

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His saying: "and that the way of the criminals may become clear."

The majority of the readers of Medina recited it: ﴿وَلِتَسْتَبِينَ﴾ with a ta' (feminine prefix), and ﴿سَبِيلَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ with "the way" in the accusative, taking "tastabin" as addressed to the Prophet ﷺ, as if its meaning according to them is: "that you, O Muhammad, may make clear the way of the criminals."

* *

Ibn Zayd used to interpret it: "that you, O Muhammad, may make clear the way of the criminals, those who asked you to expel the group whom they asked you to expel from your companions."

13299 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding: "that the way of the criminals may become clear," (he said): those who command you to expel these people.

* *

Some Meccan and some Basran readers recited it: ﴿وَلِتَسْتَبِينَ﴾ with a ta', and ﴿سَبِيلُ الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ with "the way" in the nominative, the intent being the way, but they feminize it. The meaning of the speech according to them is: "And thus do We detail the signs, that the path of the criminals may become clear to you and to the believers."

* *

The majority of the readers of Kufa recited it: ﴿وَلِيَسْتَبِينَ﴾ with a ya' (masculine prefix), and ﴿سَبِيلُ الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ with "the way" in the nominative, the verb being attributed to the way, but they masculinize it. The meaning of these (readings) in this speech, and the meaning of whoever recites with a ta' in "tastabin" and the nominative "the way," is one; the difference between them is only in masculinizing or feminizing "the way."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings in my view regarding "the way" is the nominative, because God, may He be exalted and remembered, detailed His signs in His Book and revelation so that by them the truth may be distinguished from falsehood for all who are addressed by them, not some to the exclusion of others.

As for whoever reads "the way" in the accusative, he has confined the making clear of that to the Prophet ﷺ.

As for the recitation of His saying "wa-litastabin," whether it is read with a ta' or a ya', there is no difference, because among the Arabs some masculinize "the way" (they are Tamim and the people of Najd), and some feminize "the way" (they are the people of the Hijaz). These are two widely transmitted readings among the recitations of the metropolitan centres, and two well-known dialects among the dialects of the Arabs. There is no conflict in reciting it with one of them rather than the other, and no basis for preferring one over the other, once "the way" is in the nominative, for the reason we have mentioned.

* *

Scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said similarly regarding the interpretation of His saying "We detail the signs."

13300 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: "And thus do We detail the signs," (he said): We make the signs clear.

13301 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding: "We detail the signs," (he said): We make clear.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 56:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Say: Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides Allah. Say: I will not follow your desires; I would then have gone astray, and I would not be among the guided.﴾ (6:56)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists among your people, who ascribe to their Lord idols and rivals, and who invite you to agree with them in their religion and in the worship of idols: Indeed, Allah has forbidden me to worship those whom you invoke besides Him. So I will not follow you in what you call me to of that, nor will I agree with you concerning it, nor will I give you my love and your desire in it. And if I did that, I would have abandoned the path of truth and taken a course other than guidance, and I would become astray like you, without right direction. [[See the explanation of "al-dalal" (straying) in the earlier lexical indices, under (ḍ-l-l).]]

* *

The Arabs have two dialectal forms of "ḍalaltu" (I went astray): with the vowel of the "lam" open (fatḥ) and with it in the kasra (kasr). The eloquent and well-known form is with the open vowel, and it is by this that the majority of the readers of the great cities recited, and we recite by it because of its fame among the Arabs. As for the kasra, it is not the prevalent usage in their speech, and those who recite with it are few. Whoever says "ḍalaltu" says in the future "aḍillu," and whoever says "ḍaliltu" says in the future "aḍallu." And this is the reading we adopt throughout the Qur'an: ﴿And they say: When we have gone astray...﴾ (32:10), with the "lam" open.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 57:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Say: "Indeed, I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, but you have denied Him. I do not have what you are impatient for. The decision is only for Allah. He relates the truth, and He is the best of deciders."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet ﷺ: "Say", O Muhammad, to these who ascribe equals to their Lord and who call you to associate others with your Lord: "Indeed, I am upon clear evidence" (bayyinah), that is, indeed I am upon a clarity that I have made clear to myself, and a proof that has become evident to me, "from my Lord", meaning: from my monotheism and from what I am upon of sincere worship of Him, without associating anything with Him.

* *

Thus the Arabs say: "So-and-so is upon clear evidence concerning this matter" when he has clarity about it. Among that is the saying of the poet (I do not know who said it):

"Do you seek clear evidence after his confession, and after the saying of Suwayd, 'I have spared you Bishr'?"

[Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1: 193.]

* *

"But you have denied Him": meaning, you have denied your Lord. The "hu" in His saying "bihi" refers to the Lord, glorified and exalted. "I do not have what you are impatient for": meaning, the punishment and retribution of Allah that you are impatient for is not in my hand, and I am not capable of it. This is because when Allah sent His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ with His monotheism, and he called them to Allah and informed them that he was His messenger to them, they said: "This is none but a human like you. Will you then come to magic while you see?" [Al-Anbiya': 3]. And they said of the Qur'an: "It is a confusion of dreams." Some of them said: "Rather, it is a fabrication he has invented." Others said: "Rather, Muhammad is a poet; let him bring us a sign as the earlier ones were sent." So Allah said to His Prophet ﷺ: Answer them that the signs are in the hand of Allah, not in your hand; you are only a messenger, and upon you is only the delivery of what you were sent with. And that Allah will decide the truth concerning them and concerning you, and will separate by it between you and them, so that the truthful among you and the falsifier become distinct. [See the explanation of "al-fasl" earlier, 5: 338.] "And He is the best of deciders": meaning, He is the best of those who make clear and distinguish between the true and the false, and the most just of them, because there is no unfairness in His judgment and decree toward anyone, due to any means he has to Him, nor due to kinship or affinity, nor is there any tyranny in His decree, for He does not take bribes in rulings and so commit injustice. So He is the most just of judges and the best of deciders.

It has also been reported to us in the reading of Abdullah: ﴿وَهُو أَسْرَعُ الْفَاصِلِينَ﴾ ("and He is the swiftest of deciders").

13302 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: that he said: In the reading of Abdullah: ﴿يَقْضِي الْحَقَّ وَهُو أَسْرَعُ الْفَاصِلِينَ﴾.

* *

The readers differed concerning the reading of His saying "yaqussu al-haqq" (He relates the truth).

The majority of the readers of Hijaz and Madinah, and some of the readers of Kufa and Basra, read: "in al-hukmu illa lillahi yaqussu al-haqq", with the sad (ص), in the sense of "al-qasas" (narrating), and they interpreted in this the saying of Allah, may His remembrance be exalted: "We relate to you the best of narratives" [Yusuf: 3]. This was reported from Ibn 'Abbas.

13303 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "yaqussu al-haqq", and said: "We relate to you the best of narratives."

* *

And a group of the readers of Kufa and Basra read: "in al-hukmu illa lillahi yaqdi al-haqq" with the dad (ض), from "al-qada'" (judgment), in the sense of ruling and deciding by judgment, and they cited as evidence of its soundness His saying "and He is the best of deciders," and that "fasl" (deciding) between disputants is only through judgment, not through narration.

* *

This reading, in our view, is the more correct of the two readings, for the reason we have mentioned for its readers.

* *

So the meaning of the statement is: The decision regarding what you are impatient for, O polytheists, of the punishment of Allah, and regarding what is between me and you, is only for Allah, who does not act unjustly in His judgment, and in whose hand are the creation and the command. He decides the truth between me and you, and He is the best of those who decide between us by His judgment and decree.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 58:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Say: If I had what you are impatient for, the matter would have been decided between me and you. And Allah knows best the wrongdoers.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these who ascribe equals to their Lord, the gods and idols, who deny you in what you have brought them, and who ask you to bring them a sign, impatiently seeking the punishment: If what you are impatient for of the punishment were in my hand, "the matter would have been decided between me and you," and its judgment would have been carried out with the swiftest decision, by my hastening for you what you ask of me and are impatient for. But that is in the hand of Allah, who knows best the time of sending it upon the wrongdoers, those who place their worship, which should belong only to Allah, in other than its proper place, so they worship besides Him gods and idols. And He knows best the time of retribution against them and the moment of judgment between me and them.

* *

It has been said that the meaning of His words, "the matter would have been decided between me and you," is: the slaughter of death.
