Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, he said: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: It reached me concerning His words, "the matter would have been decided," he said: the slaughtering of death.

* *

I think that the one who said this drew it from His words: ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be decided, while they are in heedlessness﴾ [Surah Maryam: 39]. For there is reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning this a narration that indicates the meaning which this speaker said regarding "the decision of the matter." It is the report in which it is said that death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection like a white-speckled ram, and it will be made to stand between Paradise and Hell; then a caller will call out to the people of Paradise and the people of Hell, asking whether they recognize it. They will say: No! Then it will be said: This is Death. Then it will be taken and slaughtered, and a caller will call: O people of the Fire, eternity without death; and O people of Paradise, eternity without death.

But His words, "the matter would have been decided between me and you," have nothing to do with that. Rather, this is a command from Allah the Exalted to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to say to those who hasten him, the decision of judgment between him and them regarding the sign he would bring them: If the punishment and the signs were in my hand and in my possession, I would have hastened to you what you ask of me in that regard. But it is in the hand of One who knows better what sets right His creation, both me and all of His creation.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He. And He knows what is on the land and in the sea﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He means: With God are the keys of the unseen. [[In the printed edition: "He means: With Him are the keys of the unseen," but the correct reading is what is in the manuscript.]]

"Al-mafatih" is the plural of "mifta'," and it is said also "miftah." Whoever says "mifta'" makes its plural "mafatih," and whoever says "miftah" makes its plural "mafatih" as well, or "mafatih" from "mifta'"... [Note: the original reads: whoever says "miftah," its plural is "mafatih" ... ]

* *

By His words "And with Him are the keys of the unseen," He means the treasuries of the unseen, as in what was reported:

13305 — Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "And with Him are the keys of the unseen," he said: He means the treasuries of the unseen.

13306 — Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Mis'ar, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Abdullah ibn Salamah, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: Your Prophet (ﷺ) was given everything except the keys of the unseen. [[Report 13306: "Abdullah ibn Salamah al-Muradi" is a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i), one of the jurists of Kufa after the Companions. It has passed as no. 12398.

This report has a sound chain; Ahmad related it in his Musnad, no. 3659, see my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad's commentary on this report there.]]

13307 — al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas, regarding "And with Him are the keys of the unseen," he said: They are five: "Indeed, Allah has with Him the knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain..." up to "Indeed, Allah is Knowing, Aware" [Surah Luqman: 34].

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech is therefore: And Allah knows best the wrongdoers among His creation, and what they deserve and what He will do with them. For with Him is the knowledge of what is hidden from His creation, so they have not been informed of it nor perceived it, and they will never know it nor perceive it. [[In the printed edition: "and they did not know it, nor will they," but the manuscript reads "and they did not know it nor perceive it"; the context requires what I have adopted.]] "And He knows what is on the land and in the sea": He says: And with Him is also the knowledge of what is not hidden from you, because what is on the land and in the sea, being visible to the eye, is known to the servants. So the meaning of the speech is: With Allah is the knowledge of what is hidden from you, O people, which you do not know and will never know, that which He has kept to Himself; and He also knows everything that all of you know, nothing is hidden from Him, for there is nothing except what is hidden from people or what is not hidden from them. Thus God, may His remembrance be exalted, informs that with Him is the knowledge of everything that was and will be, and what is to come that has not yet been, and that is the unseen.

[[See the explanation of "the unseen" above, p. 371, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿And not a leaf falls but He knows it, nor a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything moist or dry, but it is in a clear Record﴾ (59)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: No leaf falls in the deserts and wastelands, nor in the cities and villages, but God knows it. "Nor a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything moist or dry, but it is in a clear Record": He says: Nor is anything at all, of what exists, or what will exist but has not yet existed, except that it is recorded in the Preserved Tablet, written therein, its number, extent, the time at which it will exist, and the state in which it will perish, all inscribed and drawn.

By His words "clear" (mubin) He means that it makes clear the truth of what is in it, by the existence of what was inscribed in it as it was inscribed. [[See the explanation of "mubin" above in the lexical indexes under (b-y-n).]]

* *

If someone says: What is the purpose of recording in the Preserved Tablet and the Clear Record that which is not hidden from Him, and which He knows in its entirety, and whose forgetting is not to be feared?

It is said to him: God, may His remembrance be exalted, does what He wills. It is possible that this was a trial from Him for His guardian angels, and a test for those charged with recording deeds, for they, as is reported, are commanded to record the deeds of the servants and then to present them against what God has recorded in the Preserved Tablet, until He records in it what He records each day. It is said that this is the meaning of His words: "Indeed, We were copying what you used to do" [Surah al-Jathiyah: 29]. It is also possible that it is for some other reason, known to Him, either as a proof He presents to some of His angels, or to the children of Adam, and so on. And:

13308 — Zayd ibn Yahya al-Hassani Abu al-Khattab related to me, saying: Malik ibn Su'ayr related to us, saying: al-A'mash related to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, who said: There is not a tree on the earth, nor anything the size of the point of a needle, but there is an angel assigned to it who brings God knowledge of it: its drying when it dries, and its moisture when it is moist. [[Report 13308: "Zayd ibn Yahya ibn Ziyad ibn Hassan al-Hassani al-Nakri," Abu al-Khattab, is trustworthy; the Six Books narrate from him. In the printed edition, "God comes to know its drying" appears, which is a mistake by the editor; I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is correct. The manuscript and Ibn Kathir's tafsir have "Zayd ibn Abdullah," which is clearly an error, since the one who narrates from Malik ibn Su'ayr is Zayd ibn Yahya. Malik ibn Su'ayr is described by Abu Zur'ah and Abu Hatim as "truthful," and Abu Dawud weakened him. Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad is the client of Abdullah ibn al-Harith, and Abdullah ibn al-Harith is trustworthy. This report was cited by Ibn Kathir through Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur, attributing it also to Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu al-Shaykh.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 60:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿It is He who takes your souls by night and knows what you have committed by day﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet ﷺ: Say to them, O Muhammad, and God knows best the wrongdoers: God is the One who takes your souls (arwah) by night, seizing them from your bodies, "and knows what you have committed (jaraḥtum) by day," meaning: and knows what deeds you have earned by day.

The meaning of "tawaffi" (taking in full, causing to die or sleep) in the speech of the Arabs is the completion of a number, [See the explanation of "tawaffi" above in 6:455-456, 8:73, 9:100, 11:239], as the poet said: [This is Manzur al-Wabari.]

"Indeed the Banu al-Adram are not of anyone, and Quraysh did not count them in the tally."

[Al-Lisan (w-f-y). It will come later in the tafsir, 21:61 (Bulaq). In the printed edition here it read "inna bani al-adam", and in al-Lisan "inna bani al-adrad", both of which are errors; the correct reading is what appears later in the tafsir. "Banu al-Adram" are the Banu Taym ibn Ghalib ibn Fihr ibn Malik, and they are of the "Quraysh al-Zawahir" (the outer Quraysh), not the "Quraysh al-Abatih" (the Quraysh of the valley-bottoms). This rajaz verse satirises them by saying that Quraysh, the people of the valley-bottoms, do not count the Banu al-Adram (who are of the outer Quraysh) as a complete part of their number, nor do they include them in their tally when they count.]

That is, Quraysh did not include them in the count.

* *

As for "al-ijtiraḥ" (jarḥ, "ijtirah") among the Arabs, it is a man's working with his hand, his foot or his mouth, and these are called "al-jawarih" (the limbs) among them, the limbs of the body, as is reported of them. Then every person who earns a deed is called "jarih", because the Arabs used this term for these limbs; then this usage became common in speech until it was said of anyone who earns something, with whatever part of his body he earns it: "mijtarih". [See the explanation of "al-jawarih" and "al-ijtiraḥ" above in 9:543-544.]

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

13309 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "It is He who takes your souls by night and knows what you have committed by day." As for "takes your souls by night," it is in sleep. As for "knows what you have committed by day," he says: what you have earned of sin.

13310 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas: "It is He who takes your souls by night and knows what you have committed by day," meaning: what you have earned of sin.

13311 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, saying: Ma'mar related to us, from Qatada: "what you have committed by day," he said: what you have done by day.

13312 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, the same.

13313 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, his saying: "It is He who takes your souls by night," meaning by that their sleep; "and knows what you have committed by day," that is: whatever sin you have committed, He knows it, nothing of that is hidden from Him.

13314 - al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "It is He who takes your souls by night and knows what you have committed by day," he said: As for His taking them at night, it is their sleep; and as for "what you have committed by day," he says: what you have earned by day.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Although this speech is a report from God, exalted is He, about His power and knowledge, it also contains an argument against the polytheists who denied His power to give them life after their death and to resurrect them after their annihilation. So He, may His remembrance be exalted, says arguing against them: "It is He who takes your souls by night and knows what you have committed by day, then He raises you up therein, that a specified term may be fulfilled," meaning: The One who seizes your souls by night and raises you in the day, so that you may reach a specified term, while you see that and know its truth, is not one who lacks power to seize your souls and annihilate you, then return them to your bodies and bring you into being after your deaths. For that is like what you witness and observe, and the one who is powerful over what you witness of that is not incapable of what you have not witnessed. What you have not seen or witnessed of that is like what you have seen and witnessed.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Then He raises you up therein, that a specified term may be fulfilled. Then to Him is your return. Then He will inform you of what you used to do﴾ (6:60)

[In the printed and manuscript editions, "thumma yab'athukum fihi" ("then He raises you up therein") has been dropped, though it is the text of the recitation.]

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: "Then He raises you up," rouses and wakes you from your sleep. [See the explanation of "al-ba'th" above in 2:84-85, 5:457, 10:229.] "Therein" means in the day, and the "ha'" in "fihi" refers back to "al-nahar" [In the printed and manuscript editions: "wal-ha' allati fihi raji'a," with "fi" dropped; the correct reading restores it.] "that a specified term may be fulfilled": that is, that God may fulfil the term He has appointed for your life, which is death, so that it reaches its duration and its end. [See the explanation of "ajal musamma" above in 6:43, 11:259.] "Then to Him is your return": that is, then to God is your ultimate return and destination. [See the explanation of "al-marji'" above in 6:464, 10:391, 11:154.] "Then He will inform you of what you used to do": that is, then He will tell you what you did in your life in this world, [See the explanation of "al-naba'" above, p. 335, note 2, and the references there,] then He will recompense you for that: good for good, and evil for evil.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

13315 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Then He raises you up therein," he said: in the day.

13316 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, saying: Ma'mar related to us, from Qatada: "Then He raises you up therein," in the day; "al-ba'th" is waking.

13317 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, the same.

13318 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "Then He raises you up therein," he said: by day.

13319 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj who said: Abd Allah ibn Kathir said: "Then He raises you up therein," he said: He raises you up in sleep.

* *

"That a specified term may be fulfilled," and that is death.

Mention of those who said this:

13320 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "That a specified term may be fulfilled," and it is death.

13321 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "That a specified term may be fulfilled," he said: it is the term of life until death.

13322 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj who said: Abd Allah ibn Kathir said: "That a specified term may be fulfilled," he said: their period.

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends over you guardians, until when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not neglect.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And He is the Subduer" (al-Qahir), meaning God is the Victor over His creation, exalted over them by His power, [see the explanation of "al-Qahir" above, p. 288] not subdued by their idols and images, nor humbled and overcome through their abasement. ["In the printed edition: 'al-maghlub 'alayhi li-dhullatihi' (overcome because of his humiliation), which is an error and mishandling; what is in the manuscript is correct."] "And He sends over you guardians," and these are His angels who follow one another over you by night and by day, guarding your deeds and recording them, and they do not neglect or fail in guarding and recording that. [see the explanation of "al-hifz" (guarding) in its meanings above: 5:167; 8:296, 297; 10:343, 562.]

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said.

Those who said so:

13323 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words "and He sends over you guardians": He said: They are the mu'aqqibat (successive angels) among the angels; they guard him and guard his deeds.

13324 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, who said: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words "And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends over you guardians, until when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not neglect": He said: Guardians, O son of Adam, guard over you your deeds, your provision and your term; when you die, that is taken and you are returned to your Lord. "Until when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not neglect" — He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Your Lord guards you through messengers who succeed one another; He sends them to you to guard you and guard your deeds, until death attends you and the command of God descends upon you. When that comes to one of you, Our angels entrusted with taking souls take him, and Our messengers sent with it [take him], "and they do not neglect," in that, so that they waste it.

[see the explanation of "al-tawaffi" (taking) above, p. 405 n. 1, and the references there.]

* *

If someone says: Is it not the one who takes souls the Angel of Death? So how is it said "Our messengers take him," when "messengers" is plural and he is one? Did He not say: "Say: The Angel of Death who has been entrusted with you will take you" [Surat al-Sajdah: 11]?

It is said: It is permissible that God, may His remembrance be exalted, aided the Angel of Death with helpers from Himself, who carry out that by the command of the Angel of Death, so the "taking" is attributed [mudafan] — although it is the act of the helpers of the Angel of Death — to the Angel of Death, since their doing of that is by his command, just as the killing of those killed by the agents of a ruler and the flogging of those flogged by his command is attributed to the ruler, even if the ruler did not carry it out himself nor his agent by his own hand.

* *

Some of the people of interpretation have also interpreted it this way.

13326 - Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, who said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah regarding His words "Our messengers take him, and they do not neglect": He said: Ibn 'Abbas was asked about it and said: The Angel of Death has helpers from among the angels.

13327 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, who said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah, from Ibrahim regarding His words "Our messengers take him, and they do not neglect": He said: They are the helpers of the Angel of Death.

13328 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, who said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: "Our messengers take him, and they do not neglect": He said: The messengers take the souls, and the Angel of Death takes them away.

13329 - Hannad narrated to us, who said: Hafs narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah, from Ibrahim, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Our messengers take him, and they do not neglect": the helpers of the Angel of Death from among the angels. [The report 13329: the interpretation of this verse in this report was: "He said: The messengers take the souls, and the Angel of Death takes them away," and this is wholly contrary to what is in the manuscript, so I have kept what is in it, and it is likely the correct reading, God willing.]

13330 - [Hannad narrated to us, who said: Hafs narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Our messengers take him, and they do not neglect." He said: The helpers of the Angel of Death from among the angels.] [The report 13330: this report is not in the manuscript, so I have placed it in brackets; my assessment is that it is a repetition introduced by a copyist, since its chain is that of the preceding one, except that it lacks "from Ibrahim" between "al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah" and "Ibn 'Abbas."]

13331 - Hannad narrated to us, who said: Qabisah narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah, from Ibrahim: "Our messengers take him": He said: They are the angels, the helpers of the Angel of Death.

13332 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, who said: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Qatadah: "Our messengers take him": He said: The Angel of Death has messengers; he sends them and the matter is raised to him. And al-Kalbi said: The Angel of Death himself undertakes that, and he hands it over, if the person is a believer, to the angels of mercy, and if he is a disbeliever, to the angels of punishment.

13333 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: "Our messengers take him": He said: Its taking falls to the messengers, then they hand it over to the Angel of Death.

13334 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: al-Thawri informed us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim regarding His words "Our messengers take him": He said: The messengers take him, then the Angel of Death takes the souls from them. Al-Thawri said: al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah informed me, from Ibrahim, who said: They are helpers of the Angel of Death. Al-Thawri said: A man informed me, from Mujahid, who said: The earth was made for the Angel of Death like a basin; he takes from wherever he wills, and he has helpers who take the souls, and then he takes them from them.

13335 - Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, who said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah, from Ibrahim, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words "Our messengers take him": He said: The helpers of the Angel of Death from among the angels.

13336 - Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, who said: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah, from Ibrahim who said: The angels are the helpers of the Angel of Death.

13337 - Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, who said: Qabisah narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: "Our messengers take him": He said: They take him, then hand him over to the Angel of Death.

13338 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Ishaq narrated to us, who said: Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, who said: I asked al-Rabi' ibn Anas about the Angel of Death, whether he alone takes the souls. He said: He is the one who is in charge of the souls, and he has helpers in that. Do you not hear the words of God, may His remembrance be exalted: "until when Our messengers come to them, taking them" [Surat al-A'raf: 37]? And He said: "Our messengers take him, and they do not neglect." Except that the Angel of Death is the one who travels every step from the east to the west. I said: Where are the souls of believers? He said: By the lote tree of the Garden.

13339 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Muslim informed us, from Ibrahim ibn Maysarah, from Mujahid, who said: There is no household of hair tents or clay houses but the Angel of Death visits them twice every day.

* *

We have already explained that the meaning of "tafrit" (neglect) is waste (al-tadyi'), as before. [see the explanation of "al-tafrit" above, pp. 345, 346.] And the interpreters likewise interpreted it so in this place.

13340 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, who said: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, who said: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words "and they do not neglect": He said: They do not waste.

13341 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "and they do not neglect": He said: They do not waste.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 62:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Then they are returned to Allah, their true Master. Unquestionably, judgment belongs to Him, and He is the swiftest of reckoners﴾ (6:62)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Then the angels who took their souls, seizing their selves and their spirits, are returned to Allah, their Lord and true Master (al-mawla, see the explanation of "al-mawla" in what has preceded, 6:141 and 7:278, and other lexical indices under the root w-l-y). ﴿Unquestionably, judgment belongs to Him﴾, meaning: unquestionably, the decision and the ruling belong to Him alone, apart from anyone else among all His creation (see the explanation of "al-hukm" in what has preceded, 9:175, 9:324, 9:462). ﴿And He is the swiftest of reckoners﴾, meaning: He is swifter than whoever counts your numbers, your deeds, your term of life and other of your affairs, O people, and takes account of them, and knows their measures and their extents (see the explanation of "al-hisab" in what has preceded, 6:207, 6:274, 6:275, and 6:279). This is because He does not reckon by counting on the fingers, but He knows all of that, and no hidden thing escapes Him, and there is not hidden from Him the weight of an atom's ounce in the heavens or on the earth, nor anything smaller than that or greater, except that it is in a clear Book. [This is an embedding of the verse of Surah Saba': 3.] [Surah Saba': 3]

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Say, "Who rescues you from the darknesses of the land and the sea, when you call upon Him in humility and in secret: 'If He rescues us from this, we will surely be among the thankful.'"﴾ (6:63)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these who ascribe equals to their Lord and who call to the worship of their idols: Who is it that rescues you "from the darknesses of the land," when you go astray in it and become bewildered, so that guidance and the right path become dark to you; and "from the darknesses of the sea," when you board it and miss the right course in it, so that the way becomes dark to you and you cannot find your direction? [It is] other than God, to whom you turn for refuge at that time by supplication, "in humility," from you toward Him, and submission, openly; "and in secret," meaning: and concealing the supplication at times, and at other times declaring and making it manifest. You say: "If You rescue us from this, O Lord," [[In the printed edition and the manuscript, the verse reads ﴿لَئِنْ أَنْجَيْتَنَا مِنْ هذِهِ﴾, which is the reading of the rest of the Seven; our reading in our codex is the reading of the Kufans. Abu Ja'far, in his commentary, followed the common reading and did not point to our reading, and in this way he treated the verse in his tafsir. Al-Qurtubi said: The Kufans read "la'in anjana" (with nun), while the consistency of the meaning with the taa' (anjayta) is as the people of Medina and Syria read. See also Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:338. I think Abu Ja'far abridged the tafsir at this point to a great extent, leaving out much that one would expect him to say.]] that is, from these darknesses in which we are; "we will surely be among the thankful," meaning: we will surely be among those who single You out with gratitude and devote worship to You alone, apart from those whom we used to associate with You in worship.

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

13342 - Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "Say, 'Who rescues you from the darknesses of the land and the sea, when you call upon Him in humility and in secret...'" He said: when a man loses his way, he calls upon God: "If You rescue us from this, we will surely be among the thankful." [[I have left out the report in the reading of the people, not our reading in our codex.]]

13343 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "Say, 'Who rescues you from the darknesses of the land and the sea,'" he said: from the distress of the land and the sea.

The discourse on the interpretation of His words: ﴿Say: "It is Allah who delivers you from them and from every distress; yet you still associate partners with Him."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say to those who equate others with their Lord, besides Him, among the gods, when you ask them about the one they call upon when distress comes upon them on land and sea: "Allah is the One able to relieve you when distress befalls you. He delivers you from the great calamity that has come upon you on land and sea, from the anxiety of misguidance and the fear of destruction, and from the distress of everything else besides that and the worry," not your gods which you associate with Him in worship, nor your idols which you worship besides Him, which have no power to bring you benefit or harm. Yet after He has favoured you by removing the calamity that has come upon you and repelling the great grief that has descended upon you, you set up your gods and idols as equals to Him, associating them in your worship of Him. This is from you ignorance of the right He is owed from you, and ingratitude for His favours upon you, and an exposure of yourselves to the hastening of His punishment upon you.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 6, Verse 65 (Part 1 of 3)**

**On the interpretation (ta'wil, meaning the explanation of the verse) of His saying: ﴿Say: He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet.﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet ﷺ: Say to these who ascribe equals to their Lord, such as the idols and images, O Muhammad: Indeed, the One who delivers you from the darkness of the land and the sea, and from every distress, and then you return to associating others with Him, is able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet, because of your polytheism, your claim of another god alongside Him, and your ingratitude for His blessings, despite His bestowing upon you His favours and bounties.

* * *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have differed concerning the meaning of the "punishment" with which God threatened these people, that He would send it upon them from above them or from beneath their feet.

Some of them said: As for the punishment with which He threatened them, that He would send it upon them from above them, it is stoning. And as for what He threatened them with, that He would send it upon them from beneath them, it is the sinking of the earth (khasf).

Those who said this:

13344. Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, both saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik: "a punishment from above you, or from beneath your feet," he said: It is the sinking of the earth. [[In the printed edition, it matches the wording of the verse; but I returned what is in the manuscript to its original form.]]

13345. Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from al-Ash'ja'i, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the like of it.

13346. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Salamah narrated to us, from Shibl, from Ibn Najih, from Mujahid: "Say: He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet," he said: The sinking of the earth.

13347. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Say: He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you," the punishment of the sky, "or from beneath your feet," so the earth will sink with you.

13348. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: "Say: He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet": Ibn Mas'ud used to cry out while he was in the assembly or upon the pulpit: "Ohh people, it has descended upon you! Indeed God says: 'Say: He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you,' if a punishment from the sky came upon you, not one of you would remain. 'Or from beneath your feet,' if the earth sank with you, it would destroy you, and not one of you would remain. 'Or cloak you in factions and make you taste the violence of one another.' Indeed, the worst of the three has descended upon you!" [[In the printed edition it differs from the manuscript, and the manuscript contains errors. In the manuscript: "...a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet, or a punishment came upon you from the sky," and also in it: "or from beneath your feet, the earth sinks with you," and the correct form of these two is what is in the printed edition. In the printed edition "one" was in the accusative in both places, and it also had: "destroyed you and did not leave" with a waw, but I have affirmed what is in the manuscript.]]

* * *

Others said: By the punishment from above you is meant the evil leaders, "or from beneath your feet" the servants and the base of the people.

Those who said this:

13349. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Khallad say: I heard Amir ibn Abd al-Rahman say: Ibn Abbas used to say concerning this: "Say: He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet." As for the punishment from above you, it is the evil leaders; and as for the punishment from beneath your feet, it is the evil servants. [[The report 13349: "Khallad" is Khallad ibn Sulayman al-Hadrami al-Misri, who was an illiterate tailor who could not write, and was among those who feared God. He narrated from him Ibn Wahb. Reliable. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/172, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/365.
As for "Amir ibn Abd al-Rahman," al-Bukhari and Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned him in the biography of Khallad, and mentioned that he heard from him. But I have not found a biography for him among the references available to me. And this is strange.]]

13350. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: "Say: He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you," meaning from your rulers, "or from beneath your feet," meaning: your lowest ones.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the two interpretations in my view is the statement of the one who said: By the punishment from above them is meant stoning, or the flood and what resembles it, which descends upon them from above their heads; and from beneath their feet is meant the sinking of the earth and what resembles it. This is because what is known in the speech of the Arabs regarding the meaning of "above" and "beneath" in relation to the feet is that, and not other than that. And although what has been related from Ibn Abbas on this has a sound aspect, when speech is disputed regarding its interpretation, carrying it upon its most prevalent and well-known meaning is more deserving and more fitting than other than it, so long as there is no conclusive proof preventing that which must be accepted.

* * *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿or cloak you in factions and make you taste the violence of one another﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: or He will mix you into "shi'a" (factions), divided groups, whose singular is "shi'ah."

* * *

As for His saying "yalbisakum" (cloak you), it comes from your saying "labastu 'alayhi al-amr" (I confused the matter for him), when you mix it, so "I confuse it" (fa-ana albisuhu). I have only said that this is so because there is no disagreement among the readers (qurra') in pronouncing the "ba'" with a kasra, so this is clear evidence that it is from "labisa yalbisu," and that is the meaning of mixing. What is meant by it is: or He will mix you with differing desires and scattered parties. [[See the explanation of "labisa" previously: 1:567, 568 / 6:503-505 / 11:270.]]

* * *

The people of interpretation agreed with what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

13351. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Shibl, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "or He will cloak you in factions," the scattered desires.

13352. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "or He will cloak you in factions," he said: He will divide you.

13353. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "or He will cloak you in factions," he said: what was among you of trials and discord. [[In the printed edition: "from division," and in the manuscript: "from the 'yr" without dots, and the correct reading of it is what I have affirmed.]]

13354. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: "or He will cloak you in factions," he said: That in which people are today of disagreement, and desires, and the shedding of one another's blood.

13355. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: "or He will cloak you in factions," he said: The desires and disagreement.

13356. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: "or He will cloak you in factions," meaning by the factions, the differing desires.

* * *

As for His saying: "and make you taste the violence of one another," it means: by the killing of some of you at the hand of others.

* * *

The Arabs say of a man who strikes another man with force and kills him with it: "So-and-so made so-and-so taste death" (adhaqa fulanun fulanan al-mawt), and "made him taste his violence" (adhaqahu ba'sahu). The origin of this is from "tasting food" (dhawq al-ta'am), when one feeds it. Then this was used for everything that reaches a man of pleasure and sweetness, or of bitterness, disliked matter and pain. [[See the explanation of "tasting" (dhawq) previously: 7:96, 446, 452 / 8:487 / 11:47, 324. But he did not explain it with a fully satisfying clarification in the previous passages, and here he clarified it with complete clarity; and this is a type of his abridgement in his tafsir.]]

* * *

I have previously explained the meaning of "ba's" (violence) in the speech of the Arabs in a way that suffices from repeating it in this place. [[See the explanation of "ba's" previously: 8:580 / 11:357.]]

* * *

The people of interpretation agreed with what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

13357. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "and make you taste the violence of one another," with swords.

13358. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Nu'man Arim narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Abu Harun al-Abdi, from Awf al-Bakali that he said concerning His saying: "and make you taste the violence of one another," he said: It is, by God, men with spears in their hands, stabbing at your sides.

13359. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: "and make you taste the violence of one another," he said: He will give some of you power over others by killing and punishment.

13360. Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: The punishment of this community is for the people of affirmation (ahl al-iqrar), by the sword: "or He will cloak you in factions and make you taste the violence of one another." And the punishment of the people of denial is the cry and the earthquake.

* * *

Then the people of interpretation differed concerning who is meant by this verse.

Some of them said: It is meant for the Muslims of the community of Muhammad ﷺ, and it was revealed concerning them.

Those who said this:

13361. Muhammad ibn Isa al-Damghani narrated to me, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, concerning His saying: "Say: He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you," to the end of the verse, he said: "They are four, and all of them are punishments; two of them came to a settled state" [[In the printed edition: "two of them came" (fa-ja'a minhunna ithnatan), which differs from the manuscript, and it is very clear in it, and it is also correct.]] twenty-five years after the death of the Messenger of God ﷺ. So they were cloaked in factions and made to taste the violence of one another. And two remained, and they are two that will certainly befall: that is, the sinking and the transformation (maskh).

[[The report 13361: "Muhammad ibn Isa al-Damghani," the teacher of Abu Ja'far, previously mentioned under number 3225.
And see the report of Abu al-Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, number 13380, and its takhrij (sourcing) there.]]

13362. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "from above you or from beneath your feet," for the community of Muhammad ﷺ, and He spared you from it; "or He will cloak you in factions," he said: what was among you of trials and discord.

13363. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

13364. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "Say: He is able to send upon you a punishment," to the end of the verse. It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of God ﷺ prayed the dawn prayer one day and lengthened it, and some of his family said to him: O Prophet of God, you have prayed a prayer that you did not used to pray? He said: "It is a prayer of desire and fear, and I asked my Lord three things in it: I asked Him not to give power over my community to an enemy from outside them, so that He would destroy them, and He gave it to me. And I asked Him not to give power over my community to drought (al-sanah), and He gave it to me. And I asked Him that He not cloak them in factions or make them taste the violence of one another, and He denied me it." It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God ﷺ used to say: "A group of my community will not cease fighting for the truth, prevailing, and whoever forsakes them will not harm them, until the command of God comes." [["Drought" (al-sanah): dearth and famine.]]

13365. Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Qurashi and Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' al-Razi narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr, who heard Jabir say: When God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed to the Prophet ﷺ: "Say: He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet," he said: "I seek refuge in Your Face"; "or He will cloak you in factions and make you taste the violence of one another," he said: "These two are easier"; or: "easier" (ahwan). [[The report 13365: "Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Qurashi," previously in number 1692: "Ahmad ibn al-Walid" without attribution, and my brother Sayyid Ahmad said there: "I did not know who he is." And I add that I found Abu Ja'far narrating in his history 1:167 from his teacher "Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Ramli," then naming him "Ahmad ibn al-Walid" without attribution, and he narrates in these chains from: "Ibrahim ibn Ziyad," "Ishaq ibn al-Mundhir," "Abd al-Malik ibn Yazid," "Amr ibn Awn," "Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah," and "Sa'dawayh." Then he narrated from him in al-Muntakhab min Dhayl al-Mudhayyal (his history 13:104), and "Ahmad ibn al-Walid" narrated in this chain from "al-Rabi' ibn Yahya." I have gathered this until I verify his identity and lineage; as for the takhrij of the report, it is in the following note.]]

13366. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr, from Jabir, who said: When it was revealed: "Say: He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet," he said: "We seek refuge in You, we seek refuge in You"; "or He will cloak you in factions," he said: "He is easier." [[The two reports 13365 and 13366: "Amr" is Amr ibn Dinar. Al-Bukhari (al-Fath 8:219) narrated it through Hammad ibn Zayd, from Amr ibn Dinar. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: "It occurs in al-I'tisam from another route, from Ibn Uyaynah, from Amr ibn Dinar, I heard Jabir," and likewise for al-Nasa'i through Ma'mar, from Amr ibn Dinar, and this means what al-Bukhari narrated (al-Fath 13, 329), and it will come through Ma'mar, from Amr ibn Dinar, in what follows as number 13372. And al-Tirmidhi narrated it in the Book of Tafsir of his Sunan, and said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."]]

13367. Zayad ibn Ubayd Allah al-Muzani narrated to me, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah al-Fazari narrated to us, saying: Abu Malik narrated to us, saying: Nafi' ibn Khalid al-Khuza'i narrated to me, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ prayed a light prayer, complete in its bowing and prostration, and he said: "It was a prayer of desire and fear, and I asked God three things in it. He gave me two, and one remained. I asked God that He not afflict you with a punishment with which He afflicted those before you, and He gave it to me. And I asked God that He not give power over you to an enemy who would violate your territory, and He gave it to me. And I asked Him that He not cloak you in factions or make you taste the violence of one another, and He denied me it." Abu Malik said: I said to him: Did your father hear this from the Messenger of God ﷺ? He said: Yes, I heard him narrate it to the people, that he heard it from the mouth of the Messenger of God ﷺ. [[The report 13367: "Zayad ibn Ubayd Allah al-Muzani": here it is "al-Muzani," and in number 8284: "Zayad ibn Ubayd Allah al-Mari," and my brother Sayyid Ahmad wrote about him previously, and said he did not know him, and said it is possible that he is "Zayad ibn Abd Allah ibn Khuza'i," because he also narrates from "Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah"; but his coming here also as "Zayad ibn Ubayd Allah" weakens this possibility.
And "Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah al-Fazari" is reliable, one of Ahmad's teachers. Previously in numbers 1222, 3322, 3842, 7685.
And "Abu Malik" is "al-Ash'ja'i," whose name is "Sa'd ibn Tariq ibn Ushaym"; he narrated from his father, Anas, Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, Rib'i ibn Hirash, and others; Ahmad declared him reliable. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/2/59, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/86.
And "Nafi' ibn Khalid al-Khuza'i," narrated from his father; Abu Malik al-Ash'ja'i, Sa'd ibn Tariq, narrated from him. He is biographed in Lisan al-Mizan 6:145, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 4/2/85, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/457. Neither al-Bukhari nor Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned any criticism of him, but al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar made a grievous error in Lisan al-Mizan, saying: "Ibn Abi Hatim said, from his father, in his biography: he and Nafi' are both unknown," and this is a serious oversight, for the one whom Ibn Abi Hatim said this about is another Khalid, and he is in his book 1/2/362, number 1643, as follows: "Khalid, narrated from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ; narrated from him his son Muhammad. I heard my father say that, and he said: they are both unknown." As for "Khalid al-Khuza'i," he said about him: "His son Nafi' narrated from him; he is counted among the Kufans; I heard my father say that," and it is found before that biography, number 1642. This is a grievous oversight which should be corrected. And his father: "Khalid al-Khuza'i al-Azdi," whose lineage is not clarified, was biographed by al-Bukhari in al-Kabir 2/1/127, and he said: "He is counted among the Kufans." Ibn Abi Hatim said, 1/2/362: "He has companionship (suhbah); his son Nafi' narrated from him," as I mentioned before. And al-Hafiz biographed him in al-Isabah.
And this report's narrators are reliable, as al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Isabah in his biography. And al-Bukhari also pointed to this report in his history 2/1/127, through Ibn Abi Za'idah, from Sa'd ibn Tariq, from Nafi' ibn Khalid al-Khuza'i, who said: "My father told me, and he was among the companions of the tree (ashab al-shajarah): that the Prophet ﷺ, when he prayed while people were watching, prayed a light prayer, complete in its bowing and prostration." Al-Hafiz also pointed to it in al-Fath (8:221). As for al-Isabah, he said: "Al-Hasan ibn Sufyan, Abu Ya'la, al-Tabarani in his tafsir, and others, narrated through Abu Malik..." and then he mentioned the report and said: "its narrators are reliable."]]

Al-Haythami cited it in Majma' al-Zawa'id (7:222), with a similar wording, and then said: "al-Tabarani narrated it through several chains; some of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih, except Nafi' ibn Khalid. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned him and no one criticized him. It was also narrated by al-Bazzar." Ibn Kathir cited it in his Tafsir (3:329) from the narration of the hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh, from Abdullah ibn Isma'il ibn Ibrahim al-Hashimi and Maymun ibn Ishaq ibn al-Hasan al-Hanafi, both from Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from Abu Malik al-Ashja'i, in an extended form. As-Suyuti cited it in ad-Durr al-Manthur (3:19), attributing it to Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh, and added nothing. al-Tirmidhi, in the Book of Trials (al-Fitan), narrated from the hadith of Khabbab ibn al-Arat something similar, as will come at no. 13370.

As for his saying "yastabih baydatahum" (he will destroy their egg), he means: their community, their origin and gathering, the seat of their authority, and the place where their call is established. He says: do not give an enemy power over them to uproot and destroy them all. They said: this is because when the root of the egg is destroyed, all that is in it of food or chicks is destroyed; and when the root of the egg is not destroyed, some of its chicks may survive. Others said: "al-baydah" is the open courtyard of the people and the main part of their dwelling. This is closer to me.

**13368** – Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu al-Ash'ath, from Abu Asma' al-Rahbi, from Shaddad ibn Aws, who raised it to the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Allah gathered the earth for me until I saw its easts and its wests, and the dominion of my community will reach what was gathered for me of it. I have been given the two treasures, the red and the white. I asked my Lord that He not destroy my people by a general famine, and that He not clothe them in factions, nor let some of them taste the violence of others. He said: 'O Muhammad, when I decree a decree, it is not turned back. I have given you for your community that I will not destroy them by a general famine, nor give power over them to an enemy from outside them who will destroy them entirely, until some of them destroy others, some kill others, and some take others captive.'" The Prophet ﷺ then said: "I fear for my community the misleading leaders. When the sword is placed among my community, it will not be lifted from them until the Day of Resurrection."

[Note in the printed edition: In the printed edition: "fa-yuhlikahum", and in the manuscript: "fa-yuhlikuhum hum", confused in writing; the correct reading is from the Musnad.]

[Commentary on the report 13268: Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani is Shurahbil ibn Adah, of Sanaa of al-Sham, a reliable Successor (tabi'i); he is in al-Tahdhib. Abu Asma' al-Rahbi is Amr ibn Murthad, a reliable Successor, passed at no. 4844. Shaddad ibn Aws ibn Thabit al-Ansari is a Companion; Ubadah ibn al-Samit said: "Shaddad ibn Aws, of those who were given knowledge and forbearance, and among people, one was given one of them." This report was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (4:123), through the route of Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, with the same wording as Abu Ja'far's narration. Its narration from the hadith of Shaddad was pointed out by al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar in al-Fath (8:221), who said: "al-Tabari narrated from the hadith of Shaddad something similar, with a sound chain," meaning: similar to the hadith of Thawban, as I will point out later. Ibn Kathir cited it in his Tafsir (3:328, 329) from the Musnad of Ahmad, and said: "It is not in any of the six books, and its chain is good and strong. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Zayd, Abbad ibn Mansur, and Qatadah, all three from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Asma', from Thawban, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in similar form, and Allah knows best." This report was also narrated with nearly this wording through the route of Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Asma', from Thawban, with nearly this wording. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih (18:12, 14), and Abu Dawud in his Sunan (4:138), in extended form. As-Suyuti cited it from Thawban in ad-Durr al-Manthur (3:17), saying: "Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, al-Bazzar, Ibn Hibban, and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, with his wording, and Ibn Mardawayh" then he quoted al-Hakim's wording in al-Mustadrak, in extended form. His saying "zawa li al-ard": he gathered it and drew it together until he saw it all together. And "al-sanah": drought. An-Nawawi said in his commentary on Muslim: "This hadith contains manifest miracles, all of which occurred, praise be to Allah, as the Prophet ﷺ informed. The scholars said: what is meant by the two treasures is gold and silver, and what is meant is the treasures of Kisra and Caesar, the kingdoms of Iraq and al-Sham. It contains an indication that the dominion of this community will be greatest in extent to the east and the west. And so it happened. As for the south and north, it is little compared with east and west. May the blessings and peace of Allah be upon His Messenger, the truthful, who does not speak from desire; it is only a revelation that is revealed."]

**13369** – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: Ayyub informed me, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu al-Ash'ath, from Abu Asma' al-Rahbi, from Shaddad ibn Aws, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, and mentioned something similar, except that he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "I do not fear for my community except the misleading leaders." [Commentary: see the note on the earlier report. Through this route too, Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (4:123), in the same form as Abu Ja'far mentioned.]

**13370** – Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Khabbab ibn al-Arat, who was at Badr, watched the Prophet ﷺ while he prayed, until he finished, and it was at dawn. He said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, I saw you pray a prayer such as I have never seen you pray before." He said: "Indeed, it is a prayer of raghab and rahab. I asked my Lord for three qualities; He gave me two and withheld one from me. I asked Him not to destroy us with what He destroyed the nations with, and He gave it. I asked Him not to give an enemy power over us, and He gave it. I asked Him not to clothe us in factions, and He withheld it from me."

[Commentary: This report was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (5:108), and al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Trials, connected, through the route of al-Zuhri, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal, from Abdullah ibn Khabbab ibn al-Arat, from Khabbab ibn al-Arat, client of the Banu Zuhrah. Ibn Kathir cited it in his Tafsir (3:328) from the Musnad of Ahmad, then said: "al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah, from al-Zuhri, with it, and by another route. Ibn Hibban in his Sahih through both chains from Salih ibn Kaysan. And al-Tirmidhi in the Trials from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Rashid, all of them from al-Zuhri, with it, and he said: hasan sahih." As-Suyuti cited it in ad-Durr al-Manthur (3:18), saying: "Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi who authenticated it, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Khabbab ibn al-Arat," and quoted the report. His saying "raghab wa rahab": both are with two fathas, i.e., desire and fear.]

**13371** – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, regarding His saying: "or clothe you in factions," he said: Khabbab ibn al-Arat, who was at Badr, watched the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and mentioned something similar, except that he said: "three qualities." [Commentary: see the note on the earlier report.]

**13372** – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Amr ibn Dinar, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: When the verse was revealed upon the Prophet ﷺ: "Say: He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you," the Prophet ﷺ said: "I seek refuge in Your face" ["or from beneath your feet"], the Prophet ﷺ said: "I seek refuge in Your face" ["or clothe you in factions"], he said: "This is easier." [Commentary: see the note on the two earlier reports, nos. 13365 and 13366; this is another route.]

**13373** – Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "I asked my Lord for four things; three were given to me and one was withheld. I asked Him not to give power over my community to an enemy from other than them, who would destroy their egg, nor to let hunger afflict them, nor to unite them upon misguidance; and they were given to me. And I asked Him not to clothe them in factions, and to let some of them taste the violence of others; and it was withheld."

**13374** – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I asked my Lord for several things; He gave me three and withheld one. I asked Him that my community not be destroyed in one single transaction, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to let an enemy from other than them prevail over them, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to punish them with what He punished the nations before them with, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to make their violence among themselves, and it was withheld from me."

**13375** – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr, from al-Hasan, who said: When this verse was revealed, His saying: "and let some of you taste the violence of others," al-Hasan said: Then He said to Muhammad ﷺ, while He made him witness over them: "Look how We vary the signs that they may understand." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood and performed ablution, and asked his Lord not to send upon them a punishment from above them or from beneath their feet, nor to clothe his community in factions and let some of them taste the violence of others as He made the Children of Israel taste it. Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, descended to him and said: "O Muhammad, you asked your Lord for four things; He gave you two and withheld two: no punishment will come to them from above them, nor from beneath their feet, to uproot them, for these two are punishments for every nation that united in denying its prophet and rejecting the Book of its Lord; but He will clothe them in factions and let some of them taste the violence of others [In the printed edition and the manuscript: "but He will clothe them..." which is permissible, and the better reading is "but He will clothe them," and I fear that what is in the copies is the copyist's error], and these two are punishments for the people of acknowledgment of the Book and belief in the Prophets, but they are punished for their sins." And it was revealed to him: "So whether We take you away, indeed We will take vengeance upon them" [i.e., of your community] "or We show you what We promised them" [i.e., of punishment while you are alive], "indeed We are Able over them" [Az-Zukhruf 41-42]. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ stood and returned to his Lord, saying: "What calamity is greater than that I see my community punish one another!" And it was revealed to him: "Alif, Lam, Mim. Do people think that they will be left to say 'We believe' and they will not be tested? And We certainly tested those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful and will surely make evident the liars" [Al-Ankabut 1-3]. He informed him that his community was not singled out among the nations for trials, and that it would be tested as the nations were tested. Then He sent down upon him: "Say: My Lord, if You show me what they are promised, My Lord, do not place me among the wrongdoing people" [Al-Mu'minun 93-94]. The Prophet of Allah sought refuge, and Allah granted him refuge, and he saw from his community only unity, harmony, and obedience. Then He sent down upon him a verse warning his companions of trial, and He informed him that it would afflict some of them specifically rather than others. He said: "And beware of a trial which will not strike those among you who have wronged in particular; and know that Allah is severe in punishment" [Al-Anfal 25]. So it struck specific groups among the companions of Muhammad ﷺ after him, and it preserved other groups.

**13376** – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, who said: When Gabriel came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of what would happen in his community of division and disagreement, it grieved him, then he supplicated and said: "O Allah, make the best of them prevail over them, the remnant." [In the printed edition: "afdalahum taqiyyah," and the correct reading seems to be what is established here, since in the manuscript it is undotted. His saying "baqiyyah" means: sparing of whoever is made to prevail over and be victorious.]

**13377** – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Aswad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Lahi'ah informed us, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Abu al-Zubayr, who said: When this verse was revealed: "Say: He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you," the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I seek refuge with Allah from that!" [He said: "or from beneath your feet"], he said: "I seek refuge with Allah from that" [He said: "or clothe you in factions"], he said: "This is easier!" And if he had sought refuge from it, He would have granted it. [Commentary: "Khalid ibn Yazid" is al-Jumahi, al-Misri, passed at nos. 3965, 5465, 9185, 9507, 12283. "Abu al-Zubayr" is Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Makki, passed many times.]

**13378** – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'ammal al-Basri narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub ibn Isma'il ibn Yasar al-Madini informed us, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to us, who said: When it was revealed: "Say: He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet or clothe you in factions and let some of you taste the violence of others," the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not return after me as disbelievers, striking each other's necks with swords!" They said: "And we bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that you are the Messenger of Allah!" He said: "Yes!" Then some people said: "This will never happen!" So Allah revealed: "Look how We vary the signs that they may understand. Yet your people denied it, though it is the truth. Say: I am not a guardian over you. For every news there is a fixed time, and you will come to know" [Al-An'am 65-67]. [Commentary: "al-Mu'ammal al-Basri" is Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il al-Basri, who has passed several times, at nos. 2057, 3337, 5728, 8356, 8367. As for "Ya'qub ibn Isma'il ibn Yasar al-Madini," I have found no mention of him in the books of biography, and this is strange.]

* *

Others said: by some of it He meant the people of polytheism, and by some of it the people of Islam.

Those who said that:

**13379** – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Harun ibn Musa, from Hafs ibn Sulayman, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: "Say: He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet," he said: this is for the polytheists; "or clothe you in factions and let some of you taste the violence of others," he said: this is for the Muslims.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view in my opinion is that it should be said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, addressed through this verse the people of polytheism who worship idols, and it was to them that it was addressed, because it lies between a report about them and an address to them. This is because it follows His saying: "Say: It is He who delivers you from the darkness of land and sea, when you call upon Him humbly and secretly: If He delivers us from this, we will surely be among the thankful. Say: Allah delivers you from it and from every distress; then you associate others with Him" and is followed by His saying: "Yet your people denied it, though it is the truth." It is not permissible that the believers were the ones who denied it; and since that is not permissible, and this verse lies between these two verses, it becomes clear that this is a warning to those whose polytheism was mentioned before, and whose denial was reported afterwards, and not to those who had not been mentioned. However, although that is so, its warning has generally included everyone who follows their path among those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, and deny the signs of Allah, from this and other than this.

As for the reports narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "I asked my Lord three things, and He gave me two and withheld one," it is possible that this verse was revealed at that time as a warning to the polytheists I have mentioned, and to those who were on their way, opposing their Lord; so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked his Lord to protect his community from what the nations afflicted by it had been afflicted with, those who had merited from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, these punishments because of their disobedience to Him. So He protected them through his supplication and his desire for Him, from the sins for which they would deserve the most severe of these four kinds of punishment; and He did not protect them from what would make them deserve two of them.

As for those who interpreted that all of what is in this verse refers to this community, I see that they interpreted that in this community there will be those who will come to disobey Allah and commit what displeases Allah, like what those before them committed of the past nations, from opposing and disbelieving in Him; so there will befall them the like of what befell those before them of the punishments and retributions. Likewise said Abu al-Aliyah and whoever said with his saying: "Two of them came after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ twenty-five years later, and two remained: the sinking and the transformation." That is because it was narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "There will be in this community sinking, transformation, and hurling," [This is the hadith of Aisha, narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the Trials with its chain, and its text:

= and that a people of his community will spend the night in amusement and play, then wake up as monkeys and pigs. [[Al-Bukhari (al-Fath 10: 47-49) narrated from Abu Malik and Abu 'Amir al-Ash'ari, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'There will certainly be people among my community who make lawful the adultery (al-hirr, i.e., fornication), silk, wine, and musical instruments. And some people will be led astray beside a mountain-path (alam), with a herd grazing for them. A man will come to them for some need, and they will say: Come back to us tomorrow! God will then destroy them by night and cast down the mountain upon them, and He will transform others into monkeys and pigs until the Day of Resurrection.'"]] That, when it occurs, is undoubtedly similar to what happened to the peoples who transgressed against their Lord in denying and rejecting His signs. It has also been related something similar to what was related from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy.

13380 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, and Sufyan narrated to us, saying: My father informed us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, regarding the verse ﴿Say: He is able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet, or to confuse you into sects﴾. He said: Four characteristics, all of them punishment, and all of them will occur before the Day of Resurrection. Two of them passed after the death of the Prophet (ﷺ) by twenty-five years: they were confused into sects, and some of them were made to taste the violence of others. And two will certainly occur: the sinking (of the earth) and stoning. [[The report: 13380 - its isnad is sound. Ahmad related it in his Musnad 5: 134, 135, through Waki', from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, similarly.
Al-Haythami cited it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 7: 21, then said: "Ahmad related it, and its narrators are trustworthy. I say: It appears that from his words 'two passed' onward is the statement of Rafi' (meaning Abu al-'Aliyah), for Ubayy ibn Ka'b did not live until the time of the trial." Ibn Hajar also mentioned a similar objection to this report in al-Fath (8: 220), then said: "It is also criticized as contradicting the hadith of Jabir and others. It is answered that the way to reconcile them is that the protection mentioned in the hadith of Jabir and others is restricted to a specific time, namely the presence of the Companions and the virtuous generations; after that, it is possible that it occurs among them. Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi related from the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was asked about this verse, 'Say: He is able...' to its end, and he said: 'Indeed, it will happen, and its fulfilment has not yet come.' This may be understood as not contradicting the hadith of Jabir, since what is meant by its fulfilment is what relates to trials and the like." The discussion of the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Observe how We vary the signs, that they may understand (65)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Observe, O Muhammad, with the eye of your heart, how We repeat Our proofs to these people who deny their Lord and reject His blessings, and how We turn them about among them [[See the tafsir (exegesis) of "taṣrif al-ayat" above: 365]], ﴿that they may understand﴾, meaning: that they may comprehend that and take heed, and be admonished and restrain themselves from what they persist in, of what displeases God among them, such as worshipping idols and images, and denying the Book of God, Exalted is He, and His Messenger (ﷺ). [[See the tafsir of "fiqh" above: 8: 557 / 11: 307]]

**The interpretation of His words:** ﴿Your people have denied it, though it is the truth. Say: I am not a guardian over you.﴾ (6:66) ﴿For every news there is a fixed time, and you will come to know.﴾ (6:67)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may He be exalted, says: Your people have denied, O Muhammad, what you tell them and inform them of and threaten them with, of threats, ﴿though it is the truth﴾. That is, the threat that We have warned them of, for their persistence in their polytheism, namely that He will send punishment upon them from above them, or from beneath their feet, or that He will confuse them into factions and make some of them taste the violence of others, ﴿is the truth﴾ that there is no doubt it will befall them if they do not repent and turn back from what they persist in, namely disobedience to God and associating others with Him, to obedience to God and belief in Him. ﴿Say: I am not a guardian over you﴾, that is: Say to them, O Muhammad, I am not a keeper or watcher over you, but I am only a messenger who conveys to you what I have been sent with to you.¹ ﴿For every news there is a fixed time﴾, that is: for every report there is a fixed time, meaning a settled place where it comes to rest and an end to which it arrives, whereby its truth and veracity become clear, and the one who denied it and its falsehood are distinguished. ﴿And you will come to know﴾, that is: And you will come to know, O you who deny the truth of what I inform you of, the threat of God against you, O you polytheists, its reality, when His punishment descends upon you. Then you will see it and witness it, and He will kill them that day by the hands of His allies among the believers.

And the people of ta'wil (interpretation)² have said what we have said regarding the interpretation of this.

**Those who said this:**

13381 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Your people denied it, though it is the truth﴾ – he said: The Quraysh denied the Qur'an, though it is the truth. As for ﴿guardian﴾, it means keeper. As for ﴿For every news there is a fixed time﴾, the news of the Qur'an became settled on the day of Badr through what He had promised them of punishment.

13382 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿For every news there is a fixed time﴾ – for every news there is a reality, either in this world or in the Hereafter. ﴿And you will come to know﴾ – what was in this world, you will surely see it, and what was in the Hereafter, it will surely become manifest to you.

13383 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, from Mu'awiya, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿For every news there is a fixed time﴾ – he said: a reality.

13384 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿For every news there is a fixed time, and you will come to know﴾ – he said: an act and a reality, whatever of it was in this world and whatever of it was in the Hereafter.

al-Hasan used to interpret it as referring to the strife that occurred among the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ.

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His words: ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our signs, turn away from them until they engage in another discourse. And if Satan causes you to forget, do not sit, after the remembrance, with the wrongdoing folk﴾ [6:68]

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And when you see, O Muhammad, the polytheists who engage in vain talk concerning Our signs, which We have sent down to you and the revelation We have revealed to you," = their "engaging in it" (khawd) was their mocking of them, their reviling of the one who sent them down and recited them, and their denial of them. [[See the explanation of "khawd" (engaging in vain talk) above, 9:320.]] "Then turn away from them," meaning: turn your face away from them, rise from them, and do not sit with them. [[See the explanation of "i'rad" (turning away) above, p. 337, note 1, and all the references there.]] "Until they engage in another discourse," meaning: until they begin speaking of something other than mocking the signs of God in their conversation among themselves. "And if Satan causes you to forget," meaning: if Satan makes you forget, We have forbidden you to sit with them and to turn away from them while they engage in vain talk concerning Our signs; then, once you remember, rise from them, and do not sit, after your remembrance, with the wrongdoing folk who engaged in what was not theirs to engage in, with the engagement they engaged in. This is the meaning of "their wrongdoing" in this place. [[See the explanation of "zulm" (wrongdoing) in the lexical indexes above, under (z-l-m).]]

* *

What we have said concerning this is also what the people of ta'wil have said.

Those who said this:

13386. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: "And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our signs, turn away from them until they engage in another discourse," he said: God forbade him to sit with those who engage in vain talk concerning the signs of God, denying them. If he forgets, then he should not sit, after the remembrance, with the wrongdoing folk. [[In the printed edition: "after the remembrance (dhikra)"; I have adopted what is in the manuscript, which is pure correctness, as you will see in the tafsir, p. 439.]]

13387. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, similarly.

13388. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His words: "And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our signs," he said: those who deny Our signs.

13389. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our signs, turn away from them until they engage in another discourse. And if Satan causes you to forget, do not sit, after the remembrance, with the wrongdoing folk." He said: When the polytheists sat with the believers, they would fall upon the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Qur'an, reviling him and mocking him. So God commanded them not to sit with them until they engaged in another discourse. As for His words "And if Satan causes you to forget," he means: Our prohibition, so that you sit with them.
