The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners in regard to you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to those who ascribe equals to their Lord on the Day of Resurrection: We do not see with you your intercessors whom you used to claim in the world would intercede for you with your Lord on the Day of Resurrection. [See the explanation of "the intercessor" above, p. 446, note 5, and the references there.]

* *

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, because he said: Al-Lat and al-ʿUzza will intercede for him with Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

* *

It was also said: That was the saying of all idol-worshippers.

Those who said so:

13572 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: As for His saying, "And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners in regard to you," the polytheists used to claim that they worshipped the gods because they were intercessors who would intercede for them with Allah, and that these gods were partners of Allah.

13573 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Al-Hakam ibn Aban informed me, from ʿIkrimah, who said: al-Nadr ibn al-Harith said: "Al-Lat and al-ʿUzza will surely intercede for me!" Then this verse was revealed: "And you have certainly come to Us alone, as We created you the first time," until His saying: "partners."

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Certainly has been severed between you, and lost from you is what you used to claim﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says, reporting what He will say on the Day of Resurrection to these polytheists who ascribe equals to Him: "Certainly has been severed between you," meaning the mutual connection that existed between them in the world has ended that Day, so there is no connection among them, no affection, and no support. In the world they used to connect and support one another, but all of that was dissolved in the Hereafter, so none of them helps his companion or connects with him. [See the explanation of "al-bayn" above, 8: 319.]

* *

The scholars of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

13575 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Certainly has been severed between you," he said: their connection in the world.

13576 - Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah: "Certainly has been severed between you," he said: your ties.

13577 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: "Certainly has been severed between you," he said: what was between you of connection.

13578 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "Certainly has been severed between you and lost from you is what you used to claim," meaning the kinship ties and dwellings.

13580 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash said: "Certainly has been severed between you," the connection in the world. [Report 13580: This is a broken chain, as I pointed out earlier, nos. 1246, 2150. "Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash ibn Salim al-Asadi," trustworthy and well known, mentioned under nos. 1246, 2150, 3000, 5725, 8098.]

* *

The readers differed regarding the reading of His saying "baynakum."

The majority of the readers of Medina read it in the accusative, meaning: "Certainly has been severed what is between you."

* *

The majority of the readers of Mecca and Iraq read: ﴿Certainly has been severed your connection﴾ in the nominative, meaning: "Certainly has been severed your ties."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view in my opinion regarding this is that it should be said: these are two well-known readings with the same meaning, so whichever of them the reciter recites, he is correct.

This is because the Arabs sometimes put "bayn" in the accusative in the position of a noun. They cite as attested usage: "He came to me nahwaka, dunaka, and sawaaka," in the accusative in place of the nominative. It is also reported from them as attested usage the nominative of "bayn" when the verb belongs to it and it is treated as a noun, and the verse of Muhalhil is recited:

As if their spears were ropes of a well... far, bayn its sides, deep-bottomed

[Amali al-Qali 2: 132, and Lisan (b-y-n), and others, from his famous ode composed when he avenged his brother Kulayb Wa'il. Before it: "Ransom for the Banu al-Shaqiqa, the day they came... like lions of the thicket, roaring in their roar..."

"Al-ashtan" are very tightly twisted ropes with which water is drawn, singular "shatn." "Al-jal" and "al-jawl" (with a damma on the jim) are the side of the well and its edge and what holds back the water from it. "Jarur" is an epithet of a well of deep bottom, because its bucket is dragged over its lip due to its depth. He describes the length of their spears and the movement of their hands in striking with them, then pulling them out of the body of whoever was struck.]
with "bayn" in the nominative, since it was a noun, though the more common usage among them in speech is the accusative in both cases, whether it is an epithet or a noun.

* *

As for His saying: "And lost from you is what you used to claim," He says: And strayed from your path and your method is what you used to claim among your gods, that it is a partner of your Lord, and that it is your intercessor with your Lord, so it will not intercede for you today. [See the explanation of "al-dalal" above in the vocabulary indexes (d-l-l).]

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: This is a reminder from Allah, may His praise be exalted, to those who equate others with Him, the gods and idols, concerning the place of His proof against them, and an informing from Him to them of the error of what they persist in, namely associating idols with their worship of Him. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, the One who deserves worship, O people, to the exclusion of all that you worship of gods and idols, is Allah, who splits the grain (*al-habb*), meaning He splits the grain of every plant that grows, bringing forth from it crops, ﴿and the date-stone﴾, from everything planted that has a stone, bringing forth from it trees.

* *

*Al-habb* is the plural of *al-habbah*, and *al-nawa* is the plural of *al-nawāh*.

* *

Several people of *ta'wil* (interpretation of the Qur'an) said in agreement with what we have said.

Those who said that:

13581 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾: as for ﴿the splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾, it is the splitter of the grain from the ear of wheat, and the splitter of the date-stone from the date palm.

13582 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿the splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾, he said: He splits the grain and the date-stone to bring forth plants.

13583 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words ﴿the splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾: Allah is the splitter of that. He splits it and causes to grow from it what He causes to grow. He split the date-stone and brought forth the growth of a date palm, and He split the grain and brought forth the growth of what He created.

* *

Others said: The meaning of *fāliq* is *khāliq* (Creator).

Those who said that:

13584 - Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾, he said: the creator of the grain and the date-stone.

13585 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, the same.

13586 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾, he said: the creator of the grain and the date-stone.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is that He split the cleft that is in the grain and the date-stone.

Those who said that:

13587 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿the splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾, he said: the two halves that are in them.

13588 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

13589 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Mu'alla ibn Asad narrated to us, saying: Khalid narrated to us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾, he said: the cleft that is in the date-stone and in the wheat.

13590 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasah, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Mujahid: ﴿the splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾, he said: the two halves that are in them.

13591 - It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to me, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words: ﴿the splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾: he says: the creator of the grain and the date-stone, meaning every grain.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings in my view is what we have already mentioned. That is because Allah, may His praise be exalted, followed that with His informing about His bringing forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living. Thus it was known by that that He only meant, by informing about Himself, that He is the splitter of the grain for the plants, and of the date-stone for the saplings and trees, just as He is the one who brings forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living.

* *

As for the saying related from al-Dahhak concerning the meaning of *fāliq* as *khāliq*, it is a view, if he did not mean by it that He creates from it the plants and saplings by splitting it, which I do not know a meaning for, because it is not known in the language of the Arabs that "Allah split the thing" in the sense of "created."

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿He brings forth the living from the dead, and brings forth the dead from the living. That is Allah, so how are you deluded?﴾ (95)

Abu Ja'far said: His, may His remembrance be exalted, words mean: He brings forth the living ear of grain from the dead grain, and brings forth the dead grain from the living ear, and the living tree from the dead date-stone, and the dead date-stone from the living tree.

* *

A tree, as long as it stands on its roots and has not dried up, and a plant on its stalk has not withered, the Arabs call it "living." When it dries out or is cut from its root, they call it "dead."

* *

Several people of *ta'wil* said in agreement with what we have said.

Those who said that:

13592 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: As for ﴿He brings forth the living from the dead﴾, He brings forth the living ear from the dead grain, and brings forth the dead grain from the living ear, and brings forth the living date palm from the dead date-stone, and brings forth the dead date-stone from the living date palm.

13593 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik: ﴿He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living﴾, he said: the date palm from the date-stone, and the date-stone from the date palm, and the grain from the ear, and the ear from the grain.

* *

Others said:

13594 - al-Muthanna narrated to me this, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the splitter of the grain and the date-stone. He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living﴾, he said: He brings forth the dead drop from the living, then from the drop He brings forth a living human.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We have chosen the interpretation we have chosen in this matter because it follows His words: "Indeed, Allah is the splitter of the grain and the date-stone," so that His words "He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living," although it is an informing from Allah about His bringing forth the ear from the grain and the grain from the ear, is included in the generality of what was related from Ibn Abbas in its interpretation. Every dead thing Allah brings forth from a living body, and every living thing Allah brings forth from a dead body.

* *

As for His words, "That is Allah," it means: the doer of all that is Allah, may His majesty be exalted. ﴿So how are you deluded?﴾ means: By what manner of turning away from the truth, O ignorant ones, do you turn away from the right course and get diverted? [[See the explanation of *al-afk* (deluding/turning away) above, 10: 485, 486.]] Do you not reflect and know that it is not fitting to make a partner in worship, one who neither harms nor benefits, nor hears nor sees, with Him who has bestowed upon you the splitting of the grain and the date-stone, bringing forth for you from dry grain and date-stone crops, tilled fields, and fruits, of which you eat some and enjoy some?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 96:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿He is the Splitter of the daybreak, and He has made the night for rest﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying "Splitter of the daybreak," He means the One who cleaves the pillar of dawn out of the darkness and blackness of the night. [[See the explanation of "al-falaq" (splitting) above, shortly before p. 550.]]

* *

"Al-isbah" (daybreak) is a verbal noun from the speaker's saying: "asbahna isbahan" (we entered the morning).

* *

The majority of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

13595 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "Splitter of the daybreak" – he said: the brightening of the dawn.

13596 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Splitter of the daybreak" – he said: the brightening of the dawn.

13597 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

13598 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "Splitter of the daybreak" – he said: the splitter of the dawn.

13599 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "Splitter of the daybreak" – he means by "al-isbah" the light of the sun by day and the light of the moon by night.

13600 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, saying: Anbasah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Mujahid: "Splitter of the daybreak" – he said: the splitter of the dawn.

13601 - Ibn Humayd narrated it to us once more with this chain, from Mujahid, and he said regarding His saying: "Splitter of the daybreak" – he said: the brightening of the dawn.

13602 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "Splitter of the daybreak" – he said: the cleaving of the dawn from the night.

13603 - It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: "Splitter of the daybreak" – he says: the Creator of light, the light of day.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: the Creator of night and day.

Those who said that:

13604 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Splitter of the daybreak and the One who made the night for rest﴾, [[This is the reading of the people of the Hijaz, as will be mentioned later; I have left it in their reading in this report.]] he says: He created the night and the day.

* *

It is reported from al-Hasan al-Basri that he used to read: ﴿Faliq al-asbah﴾, with an open alif, as if he interpreted it as the plural of "subh" (dawn), as though he meant the dawn of each day, making it "asbah." No one other than him is known to have read it thus to us. The reading which we do not permit to be departed from is with a kasra on the alif: [[In the printed edition: "which we do not permit other than it," the manuscript's wording, which is clearly correct, is preserved.]] ﴿Faliq al-isbah﴾, because of the consensus of the authoritative transmitters of readings and the people of interpretation on its correctness and the rejection of its opposite.

* *

As for His saying: "and the One who made the night for rest," the readers differed regarding its recitation.

The majority of the readers of the Hijaz and Medina, and some of the Basrans, [[In the printed edition: "the majority of the readers of the Hijaz," and I have restored the manuscript's wording.]] read: ﴿wa-ja'ili al-layl﴾ with an alif, in the form of the noun, and in the nominative, coordinated with "Faliq"; the "al-layl" is in the genitive by the annexation of "jA'il" to it; and "al-shams wa-al-qamar" in the accusative, coordinated with the position of "al-layl," because "al-layl," although genitive in form, is in the accusative position, as it is the object of "jA'il." This coordination with the meaning of "al-layl" rather than its form is acceptable because "sakanan" intervenes between them. The poet said: [[It is al-Farazdaq.]]

Sitting at the doors, seekers of need, a need that is a repeated one, or a need that is a fresh one.

[[The verse, its takhrij and explanation were mentioned earlier, 2:195; I add here Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu Ubaydah 1:201, and it is narrated there as "qu'ud" in the nominative, as I pointed out there.]]

So he put the second "al-hajah" in the accusative, coordinating it with the meaning of the first "al-hajah" rather than its form, because its meaning is accusative, although in form it is genitive. Such a construction may also occur, with the second coordinated to the meaning of what precedes it rather than its form, even when nothing intervenes between them, as one of them said: [[By a man of Qays Aylan, and it is also attributed to Nusayb.]]

While we were watching him, there came to us one carrying a waterskin and the flint of a shepherd.

[[Sibawayh 1:87, Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:346, al-Sahibi: 118, Sharh Shawahid al-Mughni: 270; what is here is the narration of al-Farra' and Ibn Faris. Sibawayh's narration is "bayna nahnu natlubuhu," and in his commentary "narqubuhu," and his narration also has "mu'allaq wa-wifdah." In the printed edition here it read "fa-baynana" with an fa', and I have restored the manuscript's reading. In the printed edition: "shilwhu," which is an error. "Nanzuruhu": we watch and await him. "Al-shakwah": a container like a bucket or a small vessel in which water is cooled and milk is kept. As for "al-wifdah," it is a pouch like a quiver in which the shepherd carries his provisions and food.

I have not found the rest of the verse.]]

* *

And the readers of the Kufans, the majority of them, read: ﴿wa-ja'ala al-layla sakanan wa-al-shamsa﴾, with "ja'ala" in the past tense, and "al-layl" in the accusative.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is to say that both are widely transmitted recitations among the readers of the regions, agreeing in meaning and not differing in it; so whichever of the two a reader recites, he is correct both in grammatical parsing and in meaning.

* *

He, may His praise be exalted, informed that He made the night for rest, because every thing that moves by day is at rest in it, and is still in it, settling in its dwelling and refuge.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿and the sun and the moon as a reckoning﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed regarding this:

Some of them said: The meaning of that is: He made the sun and the moon run in their orbits according to a reckoning.

Those who said that:

13605 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: "and the sun and the moon as a reckoning" – he means: the number of days, months and years.

13606 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "and the sun and the moon as a reckoning" – he said: they run until a term appointed for them.

13607 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "and the sun and the moon as a reckoning" – he says: by a reckoning.

13608 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His saying: "and the sun and the moon as a reckoning" – he said: the sun and the moon are in a reckoning; when their days are finished, that is the end of time and the beginning of the Great Terror, "that is the decree of the Mighty, the Knowing."

13609 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "and the sun and the moon as a reckoning" – he said: they revolve in a reckoning.

13610 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "and the sun and the moon as a reckoning" – he said it is like His saying: "each in an orbit they swim" [Surah Ya-Sin: 40], and like His saying: "The sun and the moon by a reckoning" [Surah al-Rahman: 5].

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: He made the sun and the moon a light.

Those who said that:

13611 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "and the sun and the moon as a reckoning" – meaning, a light.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more preferable of the two views in the interpretation of this, in my opinion, is the interpretation of the one who interpreted it: He made the sun and the moon run by reckoning and number, for the arrival of their command and the end of their terms, and revolve for the benefits of creation for which they were made.

We say this is the more preferable of the two interpretations of the verse because God, may His remembrance be exalted, mentioned before it His favours toward His creation and the greatness of His dominion, by splitting the dawn for them and bringing forth plants and orchards from grain and date-stones, and followed that by mentioning the creation of the stars to guide them on land and sea. So describing His running of the sun and moon for their benefit is more fitting in this place than mentioning their giving light, since He had already described that earlier with His saying "Splitter of the daybreak," and there is no point in repeating it a second time in one verse without purpose.

* *

"Al-husban" in the speech of the Arabs is the plural of "hisab" (reckoning), as "al-shuhban" is the plural of "shihab." [[See Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu Ubaydah 1:201.]] It has also been said that "al-husban" in this place is a verbal noun from the speaker's saying: "hasabtu al-hisab ahsubuhu hisaban wa-husbanan" (I counted the reckoning). It is related from the Arabs: "ala Allah husban fulan wa-hisbatuhu," meaning his reckoning.

* *

I suppose Qatadah, in interpreting it as meaning light, went to something narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "and He sends upon it a reckoning from the sky" [Surah al-Kahf: 40]. He said: fire. So he directed the interpretation of "and the sun and the moon as a reckoning" toward that meaning. But this is not at all the meaning here.

* *

As for "al-hisban" with a kasra on the "ha'", it is the plural of "al-hisbanah," [[Abu Ja'far here said "with a kasra on the ha'," whereas the lexicographical books unanimously agree that it is with a damma on the ha', and they did not note a kasra in this word.]] which is a small cushion; and it has nothing to do with the first meaning either. One says: "hassabtuhu," meaning I seated him upon it.

* *

The accusative of His saying "husbanan" is governed by "wa-ja'ala."

* *

Some of the Basran grammarians used to say: its meaning is: "and the sun and the moon as a reckoning," i.e., by reckoning, so the preposition "bi" was omitted, as it was omitted in His saying: "He knows best who strays from His way" [Surah al-An'am: 117], i.e., He knows best of who strays from His way. [[The speaker of this is al-Akhfash, as is clear in Lisan al-Arab (h-s-b).]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿That is the decree of the Mighty, the Knowing﴾ (96)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: This act which He described as having done, namely the splitting of the dawn, the making of the night for rest, and the sun and the moon as a reckoning, is the decree of the One whose authority is mighty, who cannot be overcome by anyone who intends harm to Him, punishment, or vengeance, from whom none can prevent Him; "the Knowing," of the interests of His creation and their management. It is not the decree of idols and images, which do not hear or see, do not understand or perceive anything, neither harm nor benefit, and if they were intended with harm they would not be able to prevent whoever intended it. [[See the explanation of "al-Aziz" and "al-Alim" above in the indexes of language.]] He, may He be exalted, says: So devote your worship, O ignorant ones, to the Doer of these things, and do not associate anything else with Him in worship.

**The commentary on His words (ta'wil):** ﴿It is He who has placed for you the stars so that you may be guided by them in the darkness of the land and the sea. We have detailed the signs for a people who know.﴾ (6:97)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His mention, says: And God, who has placed the stars for you, O people, as guides on land and sea when you go astray on the road, or become bewildered and are not guided, so that at night you may find your way by them to the right path and the correct course, and thus be guided by them to the road and the course, follow it, and be saved by them from the darkness of that. As His praise declares: ﴿And landmarks; and by the star they are guided﴾ (16:16), meaning: from losing the way on land and sea. By "darkness" He means the darkness of the night, the darkness of error and straying, and the darkness of the land or the water.

* *

As for His words, "We have detailed the signs for a people who know," meaning: We have distinguished the proofs and separated the arguments among you and explained them, O people, [[See the explanation of "fasala" (detailed) in what has passed, pp. 394–396.]] so that those among you who possess knowledge of God may reflect upon them, and those among you who have understanding may comprehend them, and so that they may turn back from their ignorance in which they persist, and refrain from the error of their deeds in which they remain steadfast, and not persist in obstinacy against God, [while knowing that what they persist in is error] in their deviation. [[In the printed edition: "wa la yatamadaw fi 'inad Allah" ("and do not persist in opposition to God"), with an extra "fi" which corrupts the meaning utterly. The sentence structure is "wa la yatamadaw 'inadan li-Allah... fi ghayyihim," and the intervening clause is set off between two lines.]]

* *

Similar to what we have said on this matter, a group of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said:

Mentioned by those who said this:

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 6, Verse 98 (Part 1 of 2)**

On the interpretation (*ta'wil*) of His saying: ﴿It is He who produced you from a single soul, then there is a resting place and a place of storage. We have made the signs clear for a people who understand.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And your God, O you who ascribe equals to God, is "the One who produced you," meaning: the One who originated your creation from nothing, bringing you into existence after you had not been anything [[See the explanation of "anshaa" (produced) above: 263, 264.]]. "From a single soul," meaning: from Adam, as:

13613 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "from a single soul," he said: Adam, peace be upon him.

13614 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "It is He who produced you from a single soul," (he said): from Adam, peace be upon him.

* *

As for His saying: "a resting place and a place of storage," the people of *ta'wil* differ in its interpretation.

Some of them said: The meaning of that is: "It is He who produced you from a single soul; so among you is one who rests in the womb, and among you is one who is stored in the grave until God resurrects him for the scattering (*nashr*) of the Resurrection."

13616 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Ibrahim, from Abd Allah, that he said: "The place of storage" is where one dies, and "the resting place" is what is in the womb.
