[[In the printed edition: "ma kana fihi mustawda'an" (ما كان فيه مستودعًا), which differs from the manuscript without any benefit.]]

13653 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: "The resting place" is in the womb, and "the place of storage" is in the loins.

13654 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Ibn Abbas: "a resting place and a place of storage." He said: "A resting place" is in the womb, and "a place of storage" is in the loins.

13655 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "a resting place and a place of storage." He said: "A resting place" is in the womb, and "a place of storage" is in the loins.

13656 - I was told from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Dahhak: "a resting place and a place of storage." As for "a resting place," it is what has come to rest in the womb; and as for "a place of storage," it is what has been stored in the loins.

13657 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "a resting place and a place of storage": "A resting place" is in the wombs, and "a place of storage" is in the loins.

13658 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and from Abu Hamzah, from Ibrahim, both said: "A resting place and a place of storage": "The resting place" is in the womb, and "the place of storage" is in the loins.

* *

And others said: "The resting place" is in the grave, and "the place of storage" is in this world.

---

Narrator said: Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, he said: Yazid ibn Zurai' related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan used to say: "mustaqarr" refers to the grave, and "mustawda'" refers to the world, and it is about to join its companion.

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The most correct of these interpretations, in my view, is to say that Allah, may His praise be exalted, by His words "fa-mustaqarrun wa-mustawda'un" (﴿So there is one who settles and one who is entrusted﴾) included all His creatures whom He brought into being from a single soul, as settled and as entrusted, and He did not restrict it to one meaning over another. There is no doubt that among the children of Adam there is one who is settled in the womb and entrusted in the loins, and among them one who is settled on the surface or in the belly of the earth and entrusted in the loins of men, and among them one who is settled in the grave and entrusted on the surface of the earth. So every "settled" or "entrusted" in any of these senses is included in the generality of His words "fa-mustaqarrun wa-mustawda'un" and is intended by it, unless a report comes that must be accepted as specifying one meaning over another, and a particular over a general.

* *

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words "fa-mustaqarrun wa-mustawda'un".

The majority of the readers of Madinah and Kufah recited it: ﴿فَمُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمُسْتَوْدَعٌ﴾ (fa-mustaqarrun wa-mustawda'un, with fatha on the "qaf"), meaning: among them is one whom Allah has caused to settle in his place, so he is settled (mustaqarr), and among them is one whom Allah has entrusted in what He entrusted him to, so he is entrusted in it (mustawda').

* *

Some of the readers of Madinah and some of the readers of Basrah recited it: ﴿فَمُسْتَقِرٌّ﴾ (fa-mustaqirrun, with kasrah on the "qaf"), meaning: among them is one who has settled in his place, so he is one who settles (mustaqirr) in it.

* *

The more correct of the two recitations in my view, although both have a sound meaning in my view, is ﴿فَمُسْتَقَرٌّ﴾ (fa-mustaqarrun), meaning: Allah has caused him to settle in his place of settlement, so that the meaning is harmonized concerning it and concerning "mustawda'" (entrusted), in that each of them is in the passive form without naming its doer, and in attributing the report of that to Allah, as being the One who causes this one to settle and this one to be entrusted. This is because all agree on the recitation of His words "wa-mustawda'" with fatha on the "dal" in the passive form without naming its doer, so conforming the first, that is His words "fa-mustaqarr", to it is more fitting than deviating from it.

* *

As for His words "Qad fassalna al-ayat li-qawmin yafqahun" (We have detailed the signs for a people who understand), He, may He be exalted, says: We have clarified the proofs, distinguished the evidences and signs, and made them firm, ("li-qawmin yafqahun") for a people who understand the placements of proofs and the sites of lessons, and comprehend the signs and the reminder, for when they take heed from what I have alerted them to, namely My bringing them into being from a single soul, what they witnessed of humankind, and what I created from it of wondrous colors and forms, they will know that this is the act of one who has no like nor partner, so that they would not associate others with him in their worship of Him, as:

١٣٦٦٠ - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: "Qad fassalna al-ayat li-qawmin yafqahun," he said: We have clarified the signs for a people who understand.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 99 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And it is He who sends down water from the sky, and by it We bring forth the vegetation of every thing, and from it We bring forth green [growth], from which We bring forth grains piled up﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And Allah, to whom worship is exclusively due with no partner in it for anything besides Him, [[In the printed edition: "لا شركة فيها لشيء سواء" ("no partnership in it for anything besides Him"), which differs from what is in the manuscript, through poor judgment!!]] is the God who sent down water from the sky. ="So We brought forth thereby the vegetation of every thing," meaning, We brought forth by the water which We sent down from the sky the nourishment of livestock, beasts, birds and wild animals, and the provisions and sustenance of the children of Adam, what they feed on and eat, so that they grow upon it and thrive. The meaning of His saying "So We brought forth thereby the vegetation of every thing" is: We brought forth thereby that by which every thing grows and thrives upon and is set right.
* *
And if it were said: its meaning is, "So We brought forth thereby the vegetation of all kinds of plants," so that "every thing" means the kinds of plants, that would be a [valid] view, although the correct interpretation is the first statement.
* *
And His saying: "So We brought forth from it green [growth]," means: "So We brought forth from it," i.e., from the water which We sent down from the sky, "green [growth]," meaning moist crops.
* *
"Al-khidr" is "al-akhdar" (the green), like the saying of the Arabs: "Arinīhā namirah, urkihā maṭirah" (show me her [a cloud] speckled, make her rainy). [[This is a proverb, which the author of Lisan al-Arab attributes in (n-m-r) to Abu Dhu'ayb al-Hudhali, but he does not attribute it in (kh-d-r). Al-Maydani in al-Amthal 1:258 and Abu Hilal in Jamharat al-Amthal: 14 narrate it without attributing it to him. I recall having read its story, then lost track of it and have not found it now. Its "namirah" means a cloud, which is one having blackness, whiteness and speckling; it is struck as a proverb for the soundness of the presumption about a thing and the soundness of the indication of it. That is when you see the sign of a thing, you know what follows it.]] It is said: "The earth became green, khadaran, and khadarah." [["Al-khadarah" is a verbal noun, like "al-ghadarah," not mentioned under its root in the lexicon books.] And "al-khidr" is the moist herbs. It is said: "a date palm khudayrah," when it sheds its unripe dates green before they ripen. And "the man was struck green" (ukhtudira) and "ughtudira," when he dies young in good health. And it is said: "It is yours, khadiran madiran," i.e., wholesome and agreeable. [[Mentioned by the author of Lisan al-Arab under (kh-d-r), and not mentioned under (m-d-r). "Al-madir" is the tender, fresh.]]
* *
His saying: "We bring forth from it grains piled up," means: We bring forth from the green [growth] grain, i.e., what is in the ear of grain: the ears of wheat, barley and rice, [[See the explanation of "al-habb" above, p. 550.]] and similar ears whose grains are piled upon one another.
* *
And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, a group of the people of interpretation said.
Those who said that:
13661 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: "green [growth], from which We bring forth grains piled up": this is the ear of grain.
* *
Interpretation of His saying: ﴿And from the palm trees, from their spathes, are clustered dates hanging low﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And from the palm trees, from their spathes, [are] clusters, its clusters hanging low, [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "ومن النخل من طلعها قنوان دانية" which is the text of the verse, and it is an explanation that does not stand; the correct version is what I have set down, which I deduced from al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Quran 1:347.]] = therefore "al-qinwan" is in the nominative.
* *
"Al-qinwan" is the plural of "qinw," as "al-sinwan" is the plural of "sinw," and it is the bunch (al-idhq), [["Al-idhq" (with a kasra and sukun): the cluster of dates and its stalks.]] one says for the singular: "qinw," "qunw," and "qana"; its dual is "qinwan," and its plural is "qinwan" and "qunwan." [[See Majaz al-Quran by Abu 'Ubaydah 1:202.]] They said, for its small plural: "three aqna'." And "al-qinwan" is from the dialect of the Hijaz, and "al-qunwan" is from the dialect of Qays, and Imru' al-Qays said:
"Its tops bent, and its roots were pressed, and there inclined a cluster of unripe dates, reddened."
[[His Diwan: 67, and al-Lisan (q-n-a), and many others. From his well-known ode, and it is from its beginning, describing the travelling of the tribe, likening them to palms; he says before it: ... (the rest of the poem is given in the original).]]
And "qinyan," all of them, and another said: [[I do not know who said it.]]
"She has a tail like a cluster, which has become still due to it, and blackened for the mounting after the swishing."
[[Abu Zayd narrated it in his Nawadir: 182, as a single verse, and he said in its explanation: "al-tashadhdhur," when the she-camel is in heat she raises her tail and sets it on her rump, that is the tashadhdhur. "Al-madhal" (with two fathas): that it does not move its tail. I do not know a meaning for his saying "asham" in this verse, and Abu Zayd's narration is "wa-asmah," which I think is the correct meaning. "Al-takhtar" is the verbal noun of "khatara al-fahl bi-dhanbihi," raising it again and again and striking his two haunches with it. This verbal noun is not mentioned in any lexicon. The meaning is that she set her tail, then its swaying after its liveliness and strutting relaxed. Thus I thought its meaning.]]
And the Tamim say: "qinyan" with a ya'.
* *
By His saying "dāniyah" he means near, hanging low.
* *
And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation said.
Those who said that:
13662 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "qinwan dāniyah," he means by "the hanging clusters," the short palms, whose clusters stick to the ground.
13663 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "from its spathes are clusters hanging low": he said: clusters drooping.
13664 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "qinwan daniyah," he says: drooping.
13665 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' regarding His saying: "qinwan daniyah," he said: near.
13666 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib: "qinwan daniyah," he said: near.
13667 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: "And from the palm trees, from their spathes, are clusters hanging low": he said: the hanging ones, due to the drooping of the clusters from the spathes.
13668 - Narrated from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: "And from the palm trees, from their spathes, are clusters hanging low": he means the short palms clinging to the ground, and "al-qinwan" is its spathe.
* *
Interpretation of His saying: ﴿And gardens of grapes, and the olive and the pomegranate, similar and dissimilar﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And We also brought forth gardens of grapes = meaning orchards of grapes. [[See the explanation of "al-jannat" above in the lexical indexes (j-n-n).]]
* *
The reciters differed in the reading of this.
The majority of reciters read: ﴿wa-jannātin﴾ in the accusative, except that the "ta'" was given a kasra, because it is the feminine plural "ta'," which takes the genitive in the accusative position. [[In the printed edition, "fi" was dropped from the sentence by mistake.]]
* *
And:
13669 - al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam narrated to us, from al-Kisa'i, saying: Hamzah informed us, from al-A'mash that he read: ﴿wa-jannātun min a'nāb﴾ (nominative).
* *
= with the nominative, so "jannāt" is in the nominative by following "qinwān" in its case, even though it is not of its kind, as the poet said:
"And you saw your husband in the battle, girded with a sword and a spear."
[[The verse has passed and its takhrij several times.]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The reading which I do not permit anyone to read except with it is the accusative: ﴿wa-jannātin min a'nāb﴾, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on its correctness and their recitation with it, and their rejecting what differs from it, and the distance of the meaning of that from correctness if it is read in the nominative.
* *
His saying "and the olive and the pomegranate" is a conjunction with "al-zaytun" to "al-jannat," meaning: and We brought forth the olive and the pomegranate, similar and dissimilar.
* *
And Qatadah used to say regarding the meaning of "mushtabihan wa-ghayra mutashabih":
13670 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "gardens of grapes and the olive and the pomegranate, similar and dissimilar": he said: similar in their leaves, differing in their fruit.
* *
It is possible that what is intended is: similar in form, differing in taste. [[See the explanation of "mutashabih" above 1:385-394 / 6:173.]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech is: and [the trees of] the olive and the pomegranate; he suffices with mention of the fruit for mention of the trees, as it is said: ﴿and ask the town﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 82], suffices with mention of "the town" for mention of "its people," because the addressees know its meaning.
* *
Interpretation of His saying: ﴿Look at its fruit when it bears fruit and [at] its ripening﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed in the reading of this.
The majority of the reciters of Madinah and some of the reciters of Basrah read: ﴿unẓurū ilā thamarihi﴾, with a fatha on the "tha'" and the "mim".
* *
And some reciters of Makkah and the majority of the reciters of Kufah read: ﴿ilā thumurihi﴾, with a damma on the "tha'" and the "mim".
* *
= So whoever read the "tha'" and "mim" with a fatha directed the meaning of the speech: look at the fruit of these trees that we named from the palm, the grapes, the olive and the pomegranate when they bear fruit; and that "thamar" is the plural of "thamarah," as "qasab" is the plural of "qasabah" and "khashab" is the plural of "khashabah."
* *
= And whoever read the "tha'" and "mim" with a damma directed it to it being the plural of "thimar," as "al-humur" is the plural of "himar" and "al-jurub" is the plural of "jirab," and:
13671 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad narrated to us, from Ibn Idris, from al-A'mash, from Yahya ibn Wathhab: that he used to read: ﴿ilā thumurihi﴾, he says: it means kinds of property.
13672 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Hammad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Qays ibn Sa'd, from Mujahid, he said: "al-thumur" is property, and "al-thamar" is the dates of the palm. [[It is narrated from Mujahid more clearly than this, when he said: "it is gold and silver," as al-Farisi related from him.]]
* *
The more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of the one who read: ﴿unẓurū ilā thumurihi﴾ with a damma on the "tha'" and "mim," because Allah, exalted is His praise, described kinds of property, as Yahya ibn Wathhab said, and likewise the grain of sown crops piled up, the hanging clusters of palms, and the gardens of grapes, olives and pomegranates; so these were kinds of fruit, so "thamarah" was made plural as "thamar," then "thamar" was made plural as "thimar," then that was made plural and it was said: ﴿unẓurū ilā thumurihi﴾, so that was the plural of "thimar," and "thimar" is the plural of "thamar" = and "ithmāruh" is the gathering of the fruit.
* *
As for His saying "wa-yan'ihi," it is its ripening and its reaching maturity when it attains it.
* *
And some scholars of the Arabic language from Basrah used to say regarding "yan'ihi" when its ya' is given a fatha, it is the plural of "yani'," as "al-tajr" is the plural of "tajir" and "al-sahb" is the plural of "sahib." [[This is Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Quran 1:202, and it is also attributed to Ibn Kaysan, as came in Lisan al-Arab (y-n-'.)]]
* *
And some of the people of Kufah used to deny that and held that it is a verbal noun from their saying: "al-thamar yani'a fa-huwa yay'a yan'an," and they relate three dialects for its verbal noun from the Arabs: "yan'" (yan'), "yun'" and "yana'," and likewise for "al-nadaj," "al-nudj" and "al-nadaj." [[Abu Ja'far mentions a third verbal noun for "yan'a" and "nadaja" other than what the lexicographers mentioned; the lexicographers limited themselves in (y-n-') to a fatha on the ya' with a sukun on the nun, and a damma with a sukun on the nun; and in (n-d-j) to a fatha on the nun with a sukun on the dad, and a damma with a sukun on the dad. As for this third verbal noun which Abu Ja'far narrated and did not vowel, I have not found it in any lexicon; it is something to be added to them, except that I deduce its vowels in the two roots as a fatha on the ya' and nun in "yan'a," and a fatha on the nun and dad in "nadaja." Abu Ja'far will mention another verbal noun shortly, which is "yunu'."]]
* *
As for the reading of the one who reads: ﴿wa-yāni'ihi﴾, he means by it: its ripening and its reaching maturity.
* *
The verbal noun of it may be "yunu'an," and it is heard from the Arabs: "ayna'at al-thamarah tunīʻu iynā'an," and from the dialect of those who said "yana'," the saying of the poet: [[This is a poem disputed as to its attribution, from the poetry of Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah; al-Mubarrad attributed it to al-Ahwas, al-Jahiz attributed it to Abu Dahbal, and it is wrongly attributed to al-Akhtal.]]
"In domes near a dasker, around which the olive has ripened."
[[Al-Hayawan 4:10, al-Kamil 1:226, Ansab al-Ashraf 4/2/2, Majaz al-Quran of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:202, Tarikh Ibn Kathir 8:234, Tarikh al-Khulafa of al-Suyuti: 140, Mu'jam Yaqut ("al-Matarun"); al-Khizanah 3:279, al-'Ayni (margin of al-Khizanah 1:149), and al-Lisan (y-n-') and others. From poetry which it is said Yazid said concerning a Christian nun who became a recluse in a ruined monastery near al-Matarun, a place in al-Sham. This is the poem, with variations in the narration: ... (the rest of the poem is given in the original).]]
* *
And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation said.
Those who said that:
13763 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "wa-yan'ahu," meaning: when it ripens.
13674 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: "Look at its fruit when it bears fruit and its ripening": he said: "yan'ahu," its ripening.
13675 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "Look at its fruit when it bears fruit and its ripening," that is its ripening.
13676 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "wa-yan'ahu," he said: its ripening.
13677 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "wa-yan'ahu," he says: and its ripening.
13678 - Narrated from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: "wa-yan'ahu," he said: meaning its ripening.

[1367 9] Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said regarding "wani'ahu" (its ripening): "its ripening" (nadjhu).

* *

Discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ (99)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Indeed, in God's sending down water from the sky, by which He brings forth the vegetation of every thing, and the green [growth] from which He brings forth the piled-up grain, and the rest of the varieties of His creation that He enumerated in this verse, are "signs." He says: in that, O people, when you look at its fruit at the time its fruit forms, and at its ripening and maturity, and you observe the variation of its conditions and its development in growth and increase, you will know that it has a Manager, there is nothing like Him, and worship is fitting only for Him, not for the deities and rivals. And in this there are proofs, evidence, and clarification, ﴿for a people who believe﴾, meaning: for a people who affirm the Oneness of God and His power over whatever He wills.

God, may He be exalted and remembered, singled out for this those who believe, because they are the ones who benefit from God's proofs and take lessons from them, unlike those whom God has sealed upon their hearts, so that they do not recognize truth from falsehood nor distinguish guidance from error.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 100:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And they made the jinn partners with Allah, though He created them, and they invented for Him sons and daughters without knowledge.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: these who ascribe equals to their Lord, the idols and rivals, made the jinn partners with Allah, as He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿And they have made between Him and the jinn a kinship﴾ [Surah al-Saffat: 158].

* *

Regarding "the jinn" there are two possible readings of the accusative.

One: that it is an explanation (tafsir) of "partners." [[- "Tafsir" here is the badal (apposition).]]

The other: that the meaning of the sentence is: "and they made the jinn partners to Allah, while He is their Creator."

* *

They differed over the reading of His saying "wa-khalaqahum" (and He created them).

The readers of the major cities (qurra' al-amsar) read it as ﴿wa-khalaqahum﴾, meaning that Allah created them, singling Himself out as their creator. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 348.]]

* *

It is related from Yahya ibn Ya'mar that:

13680 - Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim ibn Salam narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, from Wasil, mawla of Abu 'Uyayna, from Yahya ibn 'Aqil, from Yahya ibn Ya'mar, that he said: "shuraka'a al-jinn wa-khalaqahum" (with the lam of "wa-khalaqahum" vowelled with a jazm).

The meaning of this is that they said: the jinn are partners of Allah in His creating us.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings is the reading of those who read ﴿wa-khalaqahum﴾, because the consensus of the authoritative reciters (al-hujja min al-qurra') is upon it.

* *

As for His saying ﴿wa-kharaqu lahu banina wa-banatin bi-ghayri 'ilm﴾, by "kharaqu" He means "iktalaqu" (they fabricated).

* *

It is said: "Fulan ikhtalaqa 'ala Fulan kadhiban" and "ikhtaraqahu", when he fabricated and invented it.

[[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 348, and Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubayda 1: 203.]]

* *

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:

13681 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: "wa-ja'alu lillahi shuraka'a al-jinn wa-Allahu khalaqahum" and "wa-kharaqu lahu banina wa-banatin", meaning that they made things up (takharraṣu).

13682 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying "wa-kharaqu lahu banina wa-banatin bi-ghayri 'ilm", he said: they made for Him sons and daughters without knowledge.

13683 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "wa-kharaqu lahu banina wa-banatin bi-ghayri 'ilm", he said: they lied.

13684 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

13685 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His saying: "wa-ja'alu lillahi shuraka'a al-jinn" they lied, "subhanahu wa-ta'ala 'amma yasifun", (meaning) "of what they lie." As for the Arabs, they made for Him daughters, and for themselves what they desire of boys; and as for the Jews, they made a kinship between Him and the jinn, "and the jinn have certainly known that they will be brought forth [for punishment]" [Surah al-Saffat: 158]. [[Read the verse of Surah al-Saffat: 158.]]

13686 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: "wa-kharaqu lahu banina wa-banatin bi-ghayri 'ilm", he said: they conjectured for Him sons and daughters.

13687 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufadhdhal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "wa-kharaqu lahu banina wa-banatin bi-ghayri 'ilm", he says: they cut out for Him sons and daughters. [[This is how it appears in the manuscript and the printed edition: "qatta'u" (they cut), in the sense of "ikhtalaqu," "da'au," and "nasabu" (fabricated, claimed, attributed). I have not found this metaphorical usage in any lexicographical work. If it is correct, and I find it close to correct, then it bears the meaning you mentioned. Unless it is a corruption of something I have not identified.]] The Arabs said: the angels are daughters of Allah; and the Jews and Christians said: the Messiah and 'Uzayr are sons of Allah.

13688 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "wa-kharaqu lahu banina wa-banatin bi-ghayri 'ilm", he said: "kharaqu" means they lied; Allah has no sons or daughters. The Christians said: the Messiah is the son of Allah; and the polytheists said: the angels are daughters of Allah. So all of them "kharaqu" the lie, and "kharaqu" means "ikhtaraqu."

13689 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj regarding His saying: "wa-ja'alu lillahi shuraka'a al-jinn", he said: the saying of the zanadiqa (heretics); "wa-kharaqu lahu". Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: "kharaqu" means they lied.

13690 - Ibn Wakî' narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "wa-kharaqu lahu banina wa-banatin", he said: they described Him.

13691 - 'Imran ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, from Abu 'Amr: "wa-kharaqu lahu banina wa-banatin", he said: its explanation is: they lied.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the speech therefore is: they made the jinn partners to Allah in their worship of Him, while He alone created them with no partner, helper or supporter; "and they invented for Him sons and daughters", meaning: they conjured up lies about Allah, and fabricated for Him sons and daughters without knowledge on their part of the reality of what they say, but out of ignorance of Allah and of His greatness, and that it is not fitting for one who is a god to have sons, daughters or a consort, nor for anyone to share with Him in His creation.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Glorified and exalted is He above what they describe﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 100]

Abu Ja'far said: His remembrance, may He be exalted, says: Allah is exalted and высоко raised far above what these ignorant people among His creation attribute to Him, in their claim that He has partners among the jinn and in their invention of sons and daughters for Him. That is not befitting for Him, because that is a quality of His creatures, from whom come the intercourse that produces children, and whom weakness drives by desires to take a consort for the satisfaction of pleasures. Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, is not incapable so that something compels Him to something, nor weak and needy so that His need for women drives Him to take a consort for pleasure.

* *

His saying "ta'ala": it is a form ("tafa'ala") from "al-'uluw" (elevation) and "al-irtifa'" (rising). [[See the explanation of "al-'uluw" above, 5: 405.]]

* *

It is related from Qatada regarding the interpretation of His saying "'amma yasifun" that it means: "they lie."

13692 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "subhanahu wa-ta'ala 'amma yasifun", (meaning) "of what they lie."

* *

I think Qatada intended by his interpretation this: that they lie in their description of Allah with what they used to ascribe to Him, namely their claim that He has sons and daughters; not that he directed the interpretation of "wasf" (description) to mean lying.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 101:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a son when He has no consort?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, mighty is His remembrance, says: He is the One who made these disbelievers associate the jinn with Him as partners, and who attributed to Him sons and daughters without knowledge. ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: the Innovator of them, the One who brought them into being and created them after they were not. [[See the explanation of "badi'" (originator) in what has preceded, 2:540.]] As related:

13693. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "Originator of the heavens and the earth," he said: He is the One who originated their creation, majestic is His majesty; He created them when they were nothing before Him.

* *

﴿How could He have a son when He has no consort?﴾ A son only comes from a male and a female, and it is not fitting for Allah, glorified is He, to have a consort so that He would have a son. That is because He is the One who created everything. He says: since nothing exists except what Allah created, how could Allah have a son when He has no consort from whom He would have a son?

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And He created all things, and He is Knowing of all things (101)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, mighty is His remembrance, says: Allah created all things, and there is no creator besides Him. And everything you invoke, O you who ascribe equals to Allah, the idols apart from Him, is His creation and His servants, whether it is a possessed thing, which you call a lord and claim that He has a son, or a jinn or a human. ﴿And He is Knowing of all things﴾ means: Allah, who created all things, nothing of what He created is hidden from Him, nor any part of it, and the weight of an atom in the earth or in the heavens does not escape Him. He knows your number and your deeds, and the deeds of those you have invoked as lords or claimed to be sons of Allah, and He keeps account of them against you and against them, until He recompenses each for his deeds. [[See the explanation of "'alim" (knowing) in the preceding lexical indexes, under ('-l-m).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 102:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; there is no deity except Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him. And He is Disposer of all things.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, the Exalted, says: The One who created all things and who has knowledge of all things, He is Allah, your Lord, O you who ascribe to Allah deities and idols, and who make the jinn partners with Him, and your gods, which possess no benefit or harm and do not do good or evil: ﴿there is no deity except Him.﴾

This is a refutation from Allah, may His praise be exalted, of those who claimed that the jinn are partners of Allah. He, may His praise be exalted, says to them: O ignorant ones, there is nothing that has divinity and worship except the One who created all things, and who has knowledge of all things. Indeed, it is not fitting that your worship and the worship of all who are in the heavens and the earth be directed to anyone but Him, sincerely, without any partner you associate with Him in it, for He is the Creator of all things, their Originator and their Fashioner, and it is right that the created thing single out its Fashioner for worship. ﴿So worship Him﴾: that is, humble yourselves before Him in obedience, worship and service, and submit to Him in that. [[See the explanation of "worship" (ʿibadah) in the preceding lexical indexes under the root ʿ-b-d.]]

﴿And He is Disposer of all things﴾: that is, Allah is a watchful Guardian and Protector over everything He has created; He sustains all of it with its provisions and sustenance, and manages, directs and disposes of it by His power. [[See the explanation of "wakil" (disposer/trustee) earlier, vol. 11, p. 434, note 1; refer back there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 103 (part 1 of 2):

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿No vision comprehends Him, but He comprehends vision; and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾ [6:103]

Abu Ja'far said: The exegetes differed concerning the interpretation of His words: "No vision comprehends Him, but He comprehends vision."

Some of them said: its meaning is: no vision encompasses Him, but He encompasses vision.

Mention of those who said this:

13694 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: "No vision comprehends Him, but He comprehends vision," he said: no one's sight encompasses the King.

13695 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "No vision comprehends Him, but He comprehends vision," (he said): He is greater than that vision should comprehend Him.

13696 - Sa'd ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam related to me, saying: Khalid ibn Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Abu Arfajah related to us, from Atiyyah al-Awfi, concerning His words: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾ [75:22-23], he said: they will look upon God, and their sight will not encompass Him because of His greatness, while His sight encompasses them. This is His saying: "No vision comprehends Him," and so on. [[The report 13696: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam al-Misri is trustworthy; he was previously related from at no. 436. In the manuscript and printed edition here it reads "Yunus ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Hakam," which is an error; the correct form is as it appears later in the tafsir 29:120 (Bulaq), where this same report is narrated with its chain from "Sa'd ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam."

Khalid ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Khurasani al-Marwazi: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam and his brother Sa'd related from him. Abu Hatim said: "a shaykh, there is nothing wrong with him." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and in Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/341. As for Abu Arfajah, I do not know who he is.

Atiyyah al-Awfi is Atiyyah ibn Sa'd ibn Janadah al-Awfi, and he is weak; he has passed many times, and my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad has fully discussed him at no. 305. Abu Ja'far will relate this report again in the tafsir 29:120 (Bulaq).]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Those who held this view argued for their position by saying: God said: "Until, when drowning overtook him, he said, 'I believe'" [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "falamma adraka-hu al-gharq" (when drowning overtook him), which is a mistake; the text of the recitation is as I have established it.]] [10:90]. They said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, described drowning as having "overtaken" Pharaoh, and there is no doubt that drowning is not described as seeing anything, nor is it something that may be described as seeing something. They said: thus the meaning of His words "no vision comprehends Him" as "no vision sees Him" is far-fetched, because a thing may overtake a thing without seeing it, as He, majestic is His praise, related about the words of Moses' companions to Moses when Pharaoh's companions drew near them: ﴿When the two hosts saw each other, the companions of Moses said: "We are surely overtaken."﴾ [26:61], because God had promised His prophet Moses that they would not be overtaken, as in His words: ﴿And We revealed to Moses: "Travel by night with My servants and strike for them a dry path in the sea, not fearing being overtaken, nor being afraid."﴾ [20:77].

They said: if a thing may see a thing without overtaking it, and overtake it without seeing it, then it is known from this that His words "no vision comprehends Him" are far from meaning "no vision sees Him," and that its meaning is: no vision encompasses Him, because encompassing Him is not permissible.

They said: thus the believers and the people of Paradise see their Lord with their eyes, yet their eyes do not comprehend Him, meaning that they do not encompass Him, since it is impermissible to describe God as having something encompass Him.

They said: and the parallel to the permissibility of describing Him as seen but not comprehended is the permissibility of describing Him as known but not encompassed in knowledge, [[In the printed edition: "wa la yuhaatu bihi" (and is not encompassed by it); the context requires what I have established.]] as He, majestic is His praise, said: ﴿And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills﴾ [2:255]. They said: thus He, majestic is His praise, negated that His creatures encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills. They said: the word "knowledge" in this place means "the known." They said: so His negating that His creatures encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills was not a negation of their knowing it. They said: so if negating encompassment of a thing is not a negation of knowing it, then likewise, negating comprehension of God by vision is not a negation of seeing Him. They said: just as it is permissible for creatures to know things without encompassing them in knowledge, so too it is permissible that they see their Lord with their eyes without comprehending Him with their eyes, since the meaning of "seeing" is other than the meaning of "comprehending," and the meaning of "comprehending" is other than the meaning of "seeing," and the meaning of "comprehending" is only encompassment, as Ibn Abbas said in the report we mentioned earlier.

They said: if someone says to us: what made you deny that the meaning of His words "no vision comprehends Him" is "no vision sees Him"?

We say to him: we denied that, because God, may His majesty be exalted, informed in His Book that faces on the Day of Resurrection will be looking toward Him, [[He means the two verses of Surat al-Qiyamah: 22, 23.]] and that the Messenger of God ﷺ informed his community that they will see their Lord on the Day of Resurrection, as the moon is seen on the night of the full moon, and as you see the sun with no cloud between it and you. [[In the manuscript, "al-badr" (the full moon) is omitted; its inclusion is correct.]] They said: since God has informed in His Book of what He informed, and the reports of the Messenger of God ﷺ have been confirmed by what we have mentioned from him, ﷺ, namely his saying: the interpretation of His words, ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾ [75:22-23], is that it is the looking of eyes toward God, majestic is His majesty, [[See the sound hadiths on the vision of our Lord, glorified is He, on the Day of Resurrection in Sahih al-Bukhari (al-Fath 13:356 and following) and Sahih Muslim 3:25 and following. The two reports which Abu Ja'far mentioned are both sound reports.]] and God's Book confirms one part of it by another part, and it was at the same time impermissible that one of these two reports abrogate the other, since abrogation is impermissible in reports, as we have explained in our book "Kitab Latif al-Bayan 'an Usul al-Ahkam" and elsewhere, [[His words "'alima" (he knew) is the answer to his earlier words: "since God has informed in His Book..."]] he knew that the meaning of His words "no vision comprehends Him" is other than the meaning of His words: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾ [75:22-23]. The people of Paradise look with their eyes on the Day of Resurrection toward God, and do not comprehend Him with them, affirming God in both reports, and submitting to what His revelation brought in both surahs.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: no vision sees Him, and He sees vision.

Mention of those who said this:

13697 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "no vision comprehends Him": nothing sees Him, and He sees the creatures.

13698 - Hannad related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Amir, from Masruq, from Aishah, who said: whoever tells you that the Messenger of God ﷺ saw his Lord has lied! "No vision comprehends Him, but He comprehends vision" [6:103], and "It is not for any human that God should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil" [42:51]. But he did see Gabriel in his form twice.

13699 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Amir, from Masruq, who said: I said to Aishah: O Mother of the Believers, did Muhammad see his Lord? She said: Glory be to God, my hair stood on end at what you said! Then she recited: "No vision comprehends Him, but He comprehends vision; and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware."

[[The reports 13698 and 13699: the hadith of Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid from al-Sha'bi is related by Muslim in his Sahih 3:10, abridged. "Qaffa sha'ri": his hair stood up from fright.]]

13700 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Abd al-A'la and Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from Aishah, similarly. [[The report 13700: the hadith of Dawud from al-Sha'bi is related by Muslim in full 3:8-10; part of this lengthy report has passed earlier at nos. 12280-12283. See its takhrij there.]]

13701 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Aishah said: whoever says that anyone saw his Lord has greatly slandered God! God said: "No vision comprehends Him, but He comprehends vision."

* *

Those who held this view said: the meaning of "comprehension" in this place is seeing; and they denied that God is seen with the eyes in this world or the next; and they interpreted His words ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾ [75:22-23] as meaning their waiting for God's mercy and reward.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: some of them interpreted the reports related from the Messenger of God ﷺ that confirm the view of the people of Paradise seeing their Lord on the Day of Resurrection with various interpretations, and some denied their authenticity, and disputed that this was the saying of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and referred the matter back to their own intellects, claiming that their intellects judge the vision of God, majestic is He, with the eyes to be impossible, and they brought in this regard various kinds of confusions, and multiplied the discussion of it by way of deductions.

Among the most important of what they claimed they knew by evidence the soundness of their position is that they found their eyes see only what is separate from them, not what adjoins them, for they do not see what adjoins them. They said: so what is separate from the eyes, when they perceive it, there is between it and them an空 space and gap. They said: if the eyes see their Lord on the Day of Resurrection in the manner they see bodies today, then it must be that the Creator is bounded. They said: and whoever describes Him with that has described Him with the attributes of bodies, which admit increase and decrease.

They said: and another point: it is the nature of eyes to perceive colors, as it is the nature of ears to perceive sounds, and the nature of one who smells to perceive scents. They said: just as it is impermissible for hearing to be fulfilled without perceiving sounds, or for smelling to be fulfilled without perceiving scents, it is likewise impermissible for sight to be fulfilled except by perceiving colors. They said: and since it is impermissible that God, may His remembrance be exalted, be described as having a color, it is established that it is impermissible for Him to be described as visible.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: the eyes of creatures do not perceive Him in this world, but in the next they will perceive Him. The people of this view said: "comprehension" in this place means seeing.

The people of this view argued for their position by saying: "comprehension," although in some states it may have a meaning other than seeing, seeing is one of its meanings. That is because it is impermissible for sight to reach a thing and see it, while not comprehending it when it has seen and perceived it, even if it does not encompass all its parts by sight. They said: so seeing what the seer perceives is comprehension of it, as opposed to not seeing it. They said: God has informed that faces on the Day of Resurrection will be looking toward Him. They said: then it is impossible that they be looking toward Him while they do not comprehend Him by sight. They said: and if that is so, and it is impermissible that there be contradiction and conflict in God's reports, then it is required and correct that His words "no vision comprehends Him" are specific, not general, and that its meaning is: no vision comprehends Him in this world, while He comprehends vision in this world and the next, since God excepted what He excepted from it by His words: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾ [75:22-23].

* *

Others among the people of this view said: the verse is specific, but it is permissible that its meaning be: the eyes of the wrongdoers do not comprehend Him in this world and the next, while the eyes of the believers and God's friends do comprehend Him. They said: it is also permissible that its meaning be: no vision comprehends Him by way of ultimate limit and encompassment, but as for seeing, yes. [[The use of "bala" (yes) with a non-negation has been explained earlier with its evidence at 2:280, 2:510, and 10:98, note 4.]] They said: it is also permissible that its meaning be: no vision comprehends Him in this world, but it comprehends Him in the next; and it is also permissible that its meaning be: no vision of one who sees Him in the sense by which the Eternal perceives the vision of His creatures comprehends Him, so that what He negated of His creatures' perception of Him is what He affirmed for Himself, since their eyes are weak and penetrate only what He, majestic is His praise, strengthened them to penetrate, while all things are manifest to His sight, and nothing is hidden from Him of them. They said: there is no doubt about the specificity of His words "no vision comprehends Him," and that God's friends will see Him on the Day of Resurrection with their eyes; but we do not know which of the four meanings of specificity is intended by the verse. They argued for the soundness of the view that God is seen in the next world with arguments similar to those of the people we mentioned earlier.

* *

Others said: the verse is general, and no vision of anyone will comprehend God in this world or the next; but God will create for His friends on the Day of Resurrection a sixth sense beyond their five senses, and they will see Him with it.

They argued for their view by saying that God, may His remembrance be exalted, negated that vision comprehends Him, without any indication in it or in another verse of its specificity. They said: likewise He informed in another verse that faces will be looking toward Him on the Day of Resurrection. They said: so God's reports do not contradict or conflict, [[In the printed edition: "la tatabayan" (do not differ); I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is the correct reading of it.]] and both reports are sound in meaning as the revelation brought them. They also argued on rational grounds, saying: if it is possible that we see Him in the next world with these eyes of ours even if their strength is increased, then it must be that we see Him in this world even if they are weak, because every sense was created to perceive some meaning, and even if it is extremely weak, it may perceive with its weakness what it was created to perceive, even if its perception of it is weak, so long as it has not been destroyed. They said: so if sight were capable of perceiving its Creator in some state or at some time and seeing Him, it would have to perceive Him in this world and see Him in it, even if its perception of Him were weak. They said: since that is not found in our eyes in this world, it is impermissible that it be in the next except in its state of this world, in that it perceives only what is its nature to perceive in this world. They said: since that is so, and God, may His remembrance be exalted, has informed that faces in the next world will see Him, it is known that they see Him without the sense of sight, since it is impermissible that His report be other than true.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: the correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is what the reports from the Messenger of God ﷺ have consistently affirmed, that he said: "Indeed you will see your Lord on the Day of Resurrection as you see the moon on the night of the full moon," and "as you see the sun with no cloud beneath it." [[See p. 16, note 1.]] So the believers will see Him, and the disbelievers on that day will be veiled from Him, as He, majestic is His praise, said: ﴿No indeed! Surely they will be veiled from their Lord that Day﴾ [83:15].

As for what those who deny the vision of God with the eyes on the Day of Resurrection argued, namely that eyes see only what is separate from them, and that between them and Him there is space and a gap, and that it was therefore impermissible in their view that the vision of God be with the eyes in this manner, because that would imply a limit and an ending for Him, and so the permissibility of the vision of Him was rejected by them: it is said to them: [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "wa innahu yuqalu lahum" with a waw; the context requires what I have established.]] Have you known anything described with management other than your Creator, except as touching you or separate from you?

If they claim that they know that, they are obligated to explain it, and there is no way to that.

If they say: we do not know that.

It is said to them: Have you not known Him, neither touching you nor separate from you, while He is described with management and action, and was it not necessary for you, since you have not known anything described with management and action other than Him except as touching you or separate from you, that knowledge of Him be impossible while He is described with management and action, being neither touching nor separate?

If they say: it is so.

They were told: "What is it that you find objectionable about the eyes being like this, that they perceive only what is separate from them and with a gap between them and it, while one may see something that is neither separate from them nor with a gap or space between them and it? Just as the hearts do not know something described as governing except when it is in contact with them or separate from them, yet, according to you, they know it otherwise. Or is there, between you and one who denies that something described as governing and acting can be known without being in contact with the knower or separate from him, while he permits that it be described as seen by the eyes without being in contact with them or separate from them, a difference?"

Then they are asked to explain the difference between these. Whatever they say about any of these matters, they will be bound to the same thing in the other.

They are likewise questioned concerning what they rely on in this matter: that it is the nature of the eyes to perceive colours, just as it is the nature of the ears to perceive sounds, and the nature of the sense of smell to perceive odours. Therefore, by the same reasoning by which it is invalid to assign to hearing a perception other than the perception of sounds, it is invalid to assign to the eyes a perception other than the perception of colours. [[In the printed edition: "that hearing should require other than..." and "that the eyes should require other than..." In the manuscript: "that hearing should decree..." and "that it should decree for the eyes..." The correct reading is what has been adopted.]]

So it is said to them: Have you not, in what you have witnessed and observed, found nothing described as governing and acting except as coloured, while you have known it to be described as governing without being coloured?

If they say, "Yes," they have no way out of acknowledging this, unless they lie and claim that they have seen and observed something described as governing and acting that is not coloured, in which case they are required to demonstrate this, and there is no way to do so. [[In the printed edition: "they are required to demonstrate" ; in the manuscript: "fadalqu" which is illegible; the correct reading is likely what has been adopted.]]

So it is said to them: Since this is so, what prevents you from denying that the eyes, in what you have witnessed and observed, perceive only colours, just as you have not found yourselves knowing anything described as governing except as coloured, while you have found yourselves knowing it as described as governing and not coloured? Then they are asked to explain the difference between these, and whatever they say about one of them, they will be bound to the same thing in the other.

The proponents of this view have questions containing deception, which we disliked to mention, and to lengthen the book with them and with the answers to them, since our aim in this book is not to expose their deceptions but to explain the interpretation of the verses of the Criterion. Yet we have mentioned the measure we have mentioned so that the reader of this book may know that they return from their statement only to what Satan has confused for them, which it is easy for the people of truth to explain the corruption of, and that they do not, in their statement, return to any clear verse of revelation, nor to any sound or weak report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They grope in darkness and wander in blindness. We seek refuge in Allah from bewilderment and misguidance.

* *

As for His saying, "And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware," He means: Allah, mentioned be He, is the one who is able to perceive by sight, and the one who is able to encompass it, the sight being unable to perceive Him or encompass Him, and He is "the All-Aware," meaning: the Knower of His creation and their sight, and of the cause by which it is impossible for sight to perceive Him; He is subtle by His power, so He made the sights of His creation in a state that does not perceive Him, and He is aware by His knowledge of how their arrangement and affairs are managed and what is most beneficial for His creation. [[See the explanation of "al-Khabir" in the earlier linguistic indices (kh-b-r).]] Such as what has been related:

13702- Hannad related to us, saying: Waki' related to us; and Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, concerning His saying, "the Subtle, the All-Aware," he said: "Subtle" means by extracting them, and "All-Aware" means by their place.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 104:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed there has come to you insights from your Lord. So whoever sees, it is for his own soul; and whoever is blind, it is against it. And I am not over you a guardian.﴾ (6:104)

Abu Ja'far said: This is a command from Allah, majestic is His praise, to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to say to those whom He admonished with these verses from His saying: [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "li-hadhihi al-ayat" with a lam, but the context requires what has been established.]] "Indeed, Allah is the splitter of the grain and the date-stone" up to His saying: "And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware" as proofs against them, and against the rest of His creation along with them, [[In the printed edition: "wa-ala tabyin khalqihi ma'ahum", which is meaningless; in the manuscript the writing is poor, and the correct reading is what has been established. The phrase "wa-ala sa'ir khalqihi ma'ahum" is conjoined to "alayhim" before it.

And His saying "ala hujajihi" — the context: "an yaqula li-ha'ula'i alladhina nabbahahum bi-hadhihi al-ayat ... ala hujajihi alayhim".

And His saying after it: "al-'adilina bihi al-awthan" is an attribute of the earlier phrase "an yaqula li-ha'ula'i alladhina nabbahahum bi-hadhihi al-ayat..."]] those who make equals to Him idols and rivals, and who deny Allah and His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ and what has come to them from Allah. Say to them, O Muhammad: "There has come to you," O you who make equals to Allah and who deny His Messenger, "insights from your Lord," meaning: that by which you see guidance from error, and faith from disbelief.

* *

= It is the plural of "basirah," and from it is the saying of the poet: [[He is al-Asar al-Ja'fi.]]

They carried their insights upon their shoulders... and my insight is borne by a swift, sturdy steed

[[Al-Asma'iyyat: 23 (and the Ma'arif edition: 157), al-Wahshiyyat no. 58, al-Makhsas 1:160, Lisan (basar) (ataad) (wa'y). And elsewhere, many. It is from a qasidah in which he taunts his paternal brothers, because his father was killed when he was a youth, and his paternal brothers took the blood-money and consumed it. When al-Asar grew up, he sought vengeance for his father, and before it he said:

Indeed I know, despite my bearing of destruction, that fortresses are horses, not the clods of villages.

The lexicographers explained "basirah" here as the blood not yet spilled, meaning: their blood within their bodies, taunting his brothers. Others said: "al-basa'ir" is the blood of their father; he says: they left their father's blood behind them and did not avenge it, and I sought it. "Ataad" (with fatha on the ayn, and fatha or kasra on the ta'): the strong, complete-formed horse, swift in its leap, prepared for running, with no unsteadiness or looseness in it. "Al-wa'y" is the swift, long, capable-built horse.]]

He means by "basirah": the clear, manifest proof, [[See Majaz al-Quran of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:203]] as:

13703 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "There has come to you insights from your Lord," he said: "The insights" are guidance, insights in their hearts for their religion, and not insights of the heads. And he recited: ﴿For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 46], and said: Indeed the religion, its sight and its hearing are in this heart. [[ "Al-din" (with shaddah on the ya and kasra): the one who is religious, the possessor of religion.]]

13704 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "There has come to you insights from your Lord," meaning: clear evidence.

As for His saying: "So whoever sees, it is for his own soul," he says: whoever distinguishes the proofs of Allah, recognizes them, acknowledges them, and believes in what they indicate of the oneness of Allah, the confirmation of His Messenger, and what he brought, then he has attained the share of his own soul, and for his soul is the reward, and it is for it that good is sought. "And whoever is blind, it is against it," he says: whoever does not take guidance from them, and does not confirm what they indicate of faith in Allah and His Messenger and His revelation, but is blind to their indication by which they point, he says: then he has harmed his own soul, and it is to it that he has done evil, not to anything else.

* *

As for His saying: "And I am not over you a guardian," he says: I am not over you a watcher who counts your deeds and actions; I am only a messenger who conveys to you what I was sent with to you, and Allah is the Guardian over you, to whom nothing of your deeds is hidden. [[See the explanation of "al-Hafiz" previously: 8:562.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 105:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Thus do We vary the verses, so that they may say, "You have studied," and that We may make it clear to a people who know﴾.

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Just as We have varied for you, O people, the signs and proofs in this surah, and made them clear, so that you have come to know them, [[See the explanation of "variation of the verses" in what has preceded, 11:433:1, and the references there.]] concerning My oneness and the confirmation of My messenger and My Book, and caused you to stand upon them, [[In the printed edition: "wassaytukum 'alayha" (and I bequeathed them to you), which has no meaning; the correct reading is in the manuscript, although its writing is poor.]] thus I make clear to you My signs and proofs in everything of My command and prohibition that you have been ignorant of and not known, as:

13705 - My father related to me, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Thus do We vary the verses", for those who ascribe equals to their Lord, as We varied them in this surah, and so that they will not say: "You have studied."

* *

The reciters differed regarding the reading of this.

The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa recited: ﴿wa-liyaqulu darasta﴾, meaning: you have read, you, O Muhammad, without an "alif".

* *

A group of the early authorities, among them Ibn Abbas, with differing reports from him, and others, and a group of the Successors, and it is the reading of some reciters of Basra, recited: "wa-liyaqulu darasta", with an alif, meaning: you have studied together (with others) and learned from the People of the Book.

* *

It is related from Qatada that he used to recite it: "durisat", meaning: it was recited and recounted. [[In the printed edition: "qara'at wa-tuliyat" (they were recited and recited), which is an error; the correct reading is in the manuscript. See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:349.]]

* *

From al-Hasan that he used to recite it: "darasat", meaning: it was effaced. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:349, where he explained it by saying: "it has grown old, that is, this which you recite to us is something that has lengthened and passed by us."]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most preferred of these readings in my view as correct is the reading of the one who recited: ﴿wa-liyaqulu darasta﴾, with the interpretation: you read and you learned; because the polytheists used to say this to the Prophet (ﷺ), and God has informed of their saying in His words: ﴿And We certainly know that they say, "Only a human teaches him." The tongue of the one they point to is foreign, while this is clear Arabic tongue﴾ [Surah al-Nahl: 103]. This is a report from God informing about them that they used to say: Muhammad learns what he brings you from someone else. Since this is so, the reading ﴿wa-liyaqulu darasta﴾, O Muhammad, meaning: you learned from the People of the Book, is more akin to the truth and more fitting to the correct meaning than the reading of the one who recited "darasta" meaning: you read with them and disputed with them, and other readings.

* *

The people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of this, in accordance with the difference of the reciters in its recitation. [[See the explanation of "al-dars" in what has preceded, 6:544-546.]]

Mention of those who recited it: ﴿wa-liyaqulu darasta﴾, from the early authorities, and its interpretation as: you learned and read.

13707 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, he said: Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid: ﴿wa-liyaqulu darasta﴾, he said: you read and you learned.

13708 - Hannad narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us = and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, who agreed with him, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Taymi, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿wa-liyaqulu darasta﴾, he said: you read and you learned.

13709 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿wa-liyaqulu darasta﴾, he says: you read the books.

13712 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Taymi, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.

13720 - Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, both said: Sufyan ibn Uyayna narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Amr ibn Kaysan, who said: Ibn Abbas, concerning "darasta", said: you recited, you disputed, you argued.

13721 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning this verse: "wa-liyaqulu darasta", he said: you recited.

13722 - Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Adam narrated to us, he said: Shu'ba narrated to us, he said: Abu Bishr narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he recited: "darasta", also with an alif, the ta' with a fatha, and said: you recited.

13723 - Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Al-Hajjaj narrated to us, he said: Abu Awana narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he recited: "darasta", i.e.: you copied.

13725 - Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "wa-liyaqulu darasta", he said: you recited, you recited to the Jews, and they recited to you.

13727 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, he said: Ibn Uyayna narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "darasta", he said: you recited to the Jews, and they recited to you.

Mention of those who recited it: "darasat", meaning: it was recited and read, [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "nubbi'at" (it was reported), which is a plain error; the correct reading is what is given here, as above, p. 26 line 9.]] in the passive form.

Mention of those who said: "darasat", meaning: it was effaced and became old, i.e., this which you recite to us has passed by us long ago, and its duration has lengthened. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:349.]]

13734 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: al-Hasan said: "wa-liyaqulu darasat": he means: it became old and was effaced.

* *

Others recited it: "darasa", from "darasa al-shay'", meaning: he recited it.

13735 - Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Tha'labi related to me, he said: Abu Ubayda narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, who said: It is in the codex of Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Ibn Mas'ud: "wa-liyaqulu darasa", he said: meaning the Prophet (ﷺ) recited.

* *

It is permissible to say at one time "darasta" and at another "darasa", addressing in one case and reporting in another, on account of the saying.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We have already explained which of these readings is the correct one in our view, and the evidence for the soundness of what we have chosen among them.

* *

As for the interpretation of His saying: "wa-linubayyinahu li-qawmin ya'lamun", He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Just as We have varied the signs, lessons and proofs in this surah for those who ascribe equals and rivals to their Lord, so We vary the signs for them in other places, lest they say to Our messenger whom We have sent to them: "You only learned what you bring us, which you recite to us from the People of the Book," and so they desist from denying him and from fabricating against him falsehood and lies; and that by Our varying of the signs We may make the truth clear to a people who know the truth when it becomes clear to them, so they follow it and accept it, and are not like those who, when it is made clear to them, become blind to it and do not understand it, and grow further from comprehending it. [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "min al-fahm bihi" (from understanding it); the context requires what is given here.]]

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: "Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord; there is no deity except Him, and turn away from the polytheists" (6:106).

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Follow, O Muhammad, what your Lord has commanded you in the revelation He has revealed to you, so act upon it, and refrain from what He has forbidden you from therein, and leave aside what the polytheists of your people invite you to, namely the worship of idols and images, for there is no deity except Him. That is, there is no object of worship deserving of your sincere devotion except Allah, who is the Cleaver of the grain and the date-stone, the Cleaver of the dawn, the One who made the night a time of rest, and the sun and the moon a reckoning (6:96). "And turn away from the polytheists" means: leave aside their disputation and their contention. [See the explanation of "turn away" in what has preceded, vol. 11, p. 436, note 2, and the references there.] Then His Majesty abrogated that with His words in Bara'ah (Surah al-Tawbah): "Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them" (9:5), the verse. As follows:

13736 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: As for His words, "And turn away from the polytheists" and similar, in which Allah commanded the believers to pardon the polytheists, it was abrogated by His words: "Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them."

* *

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: "Had Allah willed, they would not have associated others with Him, and We have not made you a watcher over them, nor are you a guardian over them" (6:107).

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His remembrance says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Turn away from these polytheists who associate others with Allah, and leave aside their disputation, their contention and their reviling. "Had Allah willed, they would not have associated others with Him": that is, had your Lord willed to guide them and rescue them from their misguidance, He would have shown them kindness through His granting them success, so they would not have associated anything with Him, and they would have believed in you, followed you, and affirmed what you brought them of the truth from your Lord. "We have not made you a watcher over them": Exalted is His remembrance says: Rather, I sent you to them only as a conveying messenger, and We did not send you as a guardian over them concerning what they do, to reckon it against them; for that is up to Us, not you. [See the explanation of "watcher" in what has preceded, p. 25, note 1, and the references there.] "Nor are you a guardian over them": that is, you are not a keeper who takes charge of their provision and sustenance, nor of their protection; so what has not been placed in your charge concerning their affairs, you are not responsible for its preservation. [See the explanation of "guardian" in what has preceded, p. 13, note 2, and the references there.]

* *

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said on this matter.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 108:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not revile those whom they invoke besides Allah, lest they revile Allah in enmity without knowledge﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and to the believers in him: Do not revile those whom the polytheists invoke besides Allah, of the deities and rivals, lest the polytheists revile Allah out of ignorance of their Lord and transgression without knowledge, as:

13738: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: (And do not revile those whom they invoke besides Allah, lest they revile Allah in enmity without knowledge). He said: They said: "O Muhammad, you must cease reviling our gods, or we will certainly satirize your Lord!" So Allah forbade them from reviling their idols, lest they revile Allah in enmity without knowledge.

13739: Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His saying: ﴿And do not revile those whom they invoke besides Allah, lest they revile Allah in enmity without knowledge﴾. The Muslims used to revile the idols of the disbelievers, and they would return that upon them, so Allah forbade them to expose their Lord to reviling (istasabba li-rabbihim). [[(Istasabba lahu) means: to expose him to being reviled and to draw it toward him. In the hadith of Abu Hurayra: "Do not walk in front of your father, do not sit before him, do not call him by his name, and do not expose him to reviling (wa la tastasibba lahu)," meaning: do not expose him to being reviled and draw it toward him, by reviling another's father so that he revenges by reviling yours. This is a courtesy that people are losing day by day.]] for they are an ignorant people with no knowledge of Allah.

13740: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And do not revile those whom they invoke besides Allah, lest they revile Allah in enmity without knowledge﴾. He said: When death came to Abu Talib, Quraysh said: "Come, let us go to this man and order him to forbid his nephew from us, for we are ashamed to kill him after his death, and the Arabs will say: 'He used to protect him, and when he died they killed him!'" So Abu Sufyan, Abu Jahl, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Umayya and Ubayy, the two sons of Khalaf, Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt, Amr ibn al-'As, and al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib set out, and they sent a man among them called "al-Mutallib," saying: "Ask permission to enter upon Abu Talib!" So he came to Abu Talib and said: "These are the elders of your people, who wish to enter upon you!" So he permitted them, and they entered upon him and said: "O Abu Talib, you are our greatest and our lord, and Muhammad has harmed us and harmed our gods, so we want you to summon him and forbid him from mentioning our gods, and we will leave him and his god!" So he summoned him, and the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) came, and Abu Talib said to him: "These are your people and the sons of your paternal uncle!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What do you want?" They said: "We want you to leave us and our gods, and we will leave you and your god!" Abu Talib said to him: "Your people have been fair to you, so accept from them!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do you see, if I give you this, will you give me one word which, if you speak it, you will rule the Arabs, and the non-Arabs will submit to you and pay you tribute?" Abu Jahl said: "Yes, by your father, we will give it to you and ten times its like. What is it?" He said: "Say: 'There is no god but Allah!'" They refused and recoiled. Abu Talib said: "Nephew, say something else, for your people have been alarmed by it!" He said: "O uncle, I will not say anything else even if they bring me the sun and place it in my hands; even if they brought me the sun and placed it in my hands, I would not say anything other than it!" intending to despair them. They became angry and said: "You must cease reviling our gods, or we will certainly revile you and revile whoever commands you." That is His saying: ﴿lest they revile Allah in enmity without knowledge﴾.

13741: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada who said: The Muslims used to revile the idols of the disbelievers, so the disbelievers would revile Allah in enmity without knowledge, and Allah revealed: ﴿And do not revile those whom they invoke besides Allah, lest they revile Allah in enmity without knowledge﴾.

13742: Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿lest they revile Allah in enmity without knowledge﴾: If you revile their god, they will revile your God, so do not revile their gods.

* * *
