Abu Ja'far said: The reciters of the cities unanimously agreed upon the recitation: ﴿فَيَسُبُّوا اللَّهَ عَدْوًا بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾, with the 'ayn vowelled with a fatha, the dal sukun, and the waw lightened in His saying ﴿عدوًا﴾, as a verbal noun from the speaker's saying "'adā fulān 'alā fulān" when he wronged him and transgressed against him: "ya'du 'adwan wa 'udwan wa 'udwanan." And "al-i'tida'" is merely its "ifti'al" form.

* * *

It is narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri that he used to recite it: "'udwan" with the waw doubled.

13743: Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to me with this, saying: al-Qasim ibn Salam narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, from Uthman ibn Sa'd: ﴿فَيَسُبُّوا اللَّهَ عُدُوًّا﴾, with the 'ayn dammed and doubled.

* * *

It has been mentioned that some Basrans recited it: "fa-yasubbu Allaha 'aduwwan," directing its interpretation to them being a group, as He, mighty is His praise, said: ﴿For indeed they are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds﴾, and as He said: ﴿Do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾. The accusative of "'aduww" would then be a circumstantial state (hal) referring to the "polytheists" in His saying ﴿fa-yasubbu﴾, so the meaning of the statement would be: "Do not revile, O believers, those whom the polytheists invoke besides Allah, lest the polytheists revile Allah, [being] enemies of Allah, without knowledge." And if the interpretation is thus, then "'aduww" is a description and attribute of the "polytheists," as if it were said: "the polytheists revile the enemies of Allah without knowledge." But since "'aduww" takes the form of an indefinite noun while being an attribute of a definite noun, it is put in the accusative as a state.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in my view is the recitation of the one who read with a fatha on the 'ayn and a lightened waw, due to the consensus of the authorities among the reciters upon reciting it thus, and it is not permissible to oppose what they have unanimously agreed upon.

* * *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Thus We have made attractive to every community its deeds; then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them of what they used to do﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Just as We made attractive to those who equate others with their Lord the idols and statues, the worship of idols and obedience to Satan, by abandoning them from obeying the Merciful, so too We made attractive to every group that has united upon a deed of the deeds, of obedience to Allah or disobedience, their deed upon which they are united; then their return and their destination after that is to their Lord, "then He will inform them of what they used to do." He says: He will make them stand and inform them of their deeds which they used to do in the world, then He will recompense them for them: if it is good, then good, and if it is evil, then evil, or He will pardon by His bounty, so long as it is not association or disbelief.

* * *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths that if a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it. Say: "Signs are only with Allah." And what will make you know that when they come, they will not believe?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And these equaling ones with Allah swore by Allah with the utmost of their oaths, and that is the most emphatic and hardest and most severe of the oaths they were able to make [[See "aqsama" and "jahd aymanihim" previously at 10:407-409, where he did not explain them.]] = (if a sign came to them), he says: They said: We swear by Allah that if a sign came to us confirming what you say, O Muhammad, like that which came to the nations before us, ﴿they would surely believe in it﴾, he says: They said: We will certainly affirm its coming with you, and that you are a Messenger sent by Allah, and that what you brought us is the truth from Allah.

It is said: "layu'minunna bi-ha" (they would believe in it), so the report was directed toward "the sign," while the meaning is toward the coming of the sign.

He says to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Say: "Signs are only with Allah"﴾, He being the one capable of bringing them to you above anyone of His creation = ﴿And what will make you know﴾, he says: And what will inform you [[See the explanation of "ash'ara" previously at 11:316, note 2, and references there. See also Abu Ubayda's Majaz al-Qur'an 1:204.]] = ﴿that when they come, they will not believe?﴾

* * *

It is mentioned that those among his people who asked him for the sign were those whom Allah made the Prophet despair of their belief among the polytheists of his people.

* * *

And the people of interpretation said similarly to what we have said regarding that.

Those who said that:

13744: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding Allah's saying: ﴿If a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it﴾, up to His saying: ﴿they are ignorant﴾: Quraysh asked Muhammad to bring them a sign, and made them swear that they would surely believe in it.

13745: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih: ﴿If a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it﴾, then he mentioned the like.

13746: Hannad narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke with Quraysh, and they said: "O Muhammad, you inform us that Musa had with him a staff with which he struck the rock, and twelve springs gushed from it; and you inform us that Isa used to give life to the dead; and you inform us that Thamud had a she-camel. So bring us some of the signs so that we may believe you!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "What is it that you wish I would bring you?" They said: "Make al-Safa gold for us." He said to them: "If I do so, will you believe me?" They said: "Yes, by Allah, if you do it, we will surely follow you all!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood to supplicate, and Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him and said: "For you is what you wish. If you wish, it will become gold in the morning, but if He sends a sign and they do not believe at that point, We will surely punish them. And if you wish, then grant them respite until whoever among them repents may repent." He said: "Rather, let whoever among them repents repent." So Allah, exalted, revealed: ﴿And they swore by Allah﴾ up to His saying: ﴿they are ignorant﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 109:

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And what will make you realize that when they come they will not believe?ﴩ

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding those addressed by His words: ﴿And what will make you realize that when they come they will not believe?ﴩ

Some of them said: The address in His words ﴿And what will make you realize﴾ was to the polytheists who swore by God that if a sign came to them they would surely believe. The report ends at His words ﴿And what will make you realize﴾, and then the judgment that they will not believe when it comes is resumed as a fresh, independent statement.

* *

Those who said this:

13747 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's words: ﴿And what will make you realize﴾, he said: "What will make you know." He said: Then He informed about them that they will not believe.

13748 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And what will make you realize﴾, and what will make you know "that when they come", he said: He made it obligatory upon them that when they come they will not believe.

13749 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: I heard Abdullah ibn Zayd say: "The signs are only with God," then he resumes and says: that when they come, they will not believe.

13750 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿The signs are only with God, and what will make you realize﴾, and what will make you know that you will believe when they come. Then he resumed informing about them, saying: when they come, they will not believe.

* *

On this interpretation is the reading of those who read "innaha" with a kasra on the alif, so that His words "innaha idha ja'at la yu'minun" are a new statement, separated from the first.

* *

Among those who read it thus were some of the readers of Mecca and Basra.

* *

Others said: Rather, that is an address from God to His Prophet ﷺ and his companions. They said: The reason is that those who asked the Messenger of God ﷺ to bring a sign were believers in him. They said: The cause of their asking him for this was that the polytheists swore that if the sign came they would believe and follow the Messenger of God ﷺ. So the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Ask your Lord for that, O Messenger of God!" He asked, and God revealed concerning them and their asking Him for it: "Say" to those who believe in you, O Muhammad, ﴿The signs are only with God, and what will make you realize﴾, O believers, that when the signs come to these polytheists, they will not believe in Him. So they opened the alif of "anna".

* *

Those who read it thus were the majority of the readers of Medina and Kufa, and they said: The "la" in His words ﴿they will not believe﴾ is superfluous (silah), [[(silah): an added or redundant particle; see the glossary of terms.]] just as it is inserted in His words ﴿What prevented you from prostrating?﴾ [Surat al-A'raf: 12], and in His words ﴿And it is forbidden to a town which We have destroyed that they will not return﴾ [Surat al-Anbiya': 95]. The meaning is: "It is forbidden for them to return," and "What prevented you from prostrating."

* *

Some who read it with the fatha on the alif of ﴿anna﴾ interpreted it to mean "la'alla" (perhaps). They mentioned that this is how it is in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b.

* *

It has been reported from the Arabs, as something heard from them: "Go to the market, perhaps (annaka) you will buy something for me," meaning: "perhaps you will buy." [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 349-350, and Abu 'Ubaydah's Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 204.]]

It has also been said that the verse of 'Adi ibn Zayd al-'Ibadi:

"O blamer, what will make you know that my death is at an hour in the day or in the morning of tomorrow?"

means: "perhaps my death." [[Jamharat ash-Ash'ar al-'Arab 103; Lisan al-'Arab (anna); and others. From his wise poem, in which he says before it: ...]]

And they recited in the verse of Duraid ibn al-Simmah: [[In the printed edition: "and they recited to me", and I have confirmed what is in the manuscript.]]

"Leave me to wander through the lands, for I see what you see, or a miser made immortal"

[[This line is as it appears in the manuscript and the printed edition, and it is an error by Abu Ja'far or by al-Farra, without doubt, for the last hemistich of this poem belongs to the poetry of Hata'it ibn Ya'fur... The correct verse of Duraid ibn al-Simmah, which is indisputable, is: "Leave me to wander through the lands, perhaps I will meet a band of Muharib..." ...]]

meaning: "perhaps I." And what our companions related to me from al-Farra is: "Perhaps I see what you see." And the verse of Tawbah ibn al-Humayyir was also recited:

"Perhaps, O billy-goat that mounted a sturdy rope, the tormentor of Layla, that you will see me visiting her" [[From a poem, as collected from his poetry; and Sibawayh 1: 312. He says this to the husband of Layla al-Akhiliyyah, his beloved, threatening him for preventing him from visiting her, and torturing him on account of her, and likening him to a billy-goat mounting in its rope. "Mirrah" is a tightly twisted rope.]]

"Lahannaka ya taysan" means "li'annaka," which is in the sense of "la'allaka." And the verse of Abu al-Najm al-'Ijli was recited:

"I said to Shayban, come close to his encounter, that we may feed the people from its roast" [[Al-Ma'ani al-Kabir of Ibn Qutaybah 393; al-Khizanah 3: 591. The poem's version reads "kama nughaddi"...]]

meaning: "perhaps we feed the people."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these interpretations, concerning the sense of the verse, is the saying of those who said: That is an address from God to those who believe in Him among the companions of His Messenger — I mean His words: ﴿And what will make you realize that when they come they will not believe?﴾ — and that His words "anna" mean "la'alla" (perhaps).

This is the most correct interpretation because of the widespread reading among the readers of the cities with the ya' in His words ﴿they will not believe﴾ (yu'minun).

Had His words ﴿And what will make you realize﴾ been addressed to the polytheists, the reading of ﴿they will not believe﴾ would be with the ta' (tu'minun). That reading, though some readers of Mecca read it so, is a reading departing from what the readers of the cities hold, and their unanimous opposition to it is sufficient proof of its abandonment and anomaly. [[His words "dhahabuha" mean its destruction and corruption.]]

* *

The meaning of the speech is: "And what will make you realize, O believers, perhaps when the signs come to these polytheists they will not believe, so that they are hastened with vengeance and punishment at that time and are not delayed."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 110:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their eyes away, just as they did not believe in it the first time﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: The meaning is: even if We brought them a sign as they asked, they would not believe, just as they did not believe in what came before it the first time, because God had placed a barrier between them and that.

Mention of those who said this:

13751 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their eyes away, just as they did not believe in it the first time﴾, the verse. He said: When the polytheists denied what God had sent down, their hearts did not remain steadfast upon anything, and they were turned away from every matter.

13752 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their eyes away﴾, he said: We prevent them from that, just as We did to them the first time. And he recited: ﴿just as they did not believe in it the first time﴾.

13753 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their eyes away﴾, he said: We come between them and faith, so that even if every sign came to them, they would not believe, just as We came between them and faith the first time.

* *

Others said: The meaning is: And We turn their hearts and their eyes away if they were returned from the Hereafter to the world, so that they would not believe, just as We did to them that, and they did not believe in the world. They said: This is like His saying: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾ [Surat al-An'am: 28].

Mention of those who said this:

13754 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: God informed of what the servants would say before they said it, and of their deeds before they did them. He said: And none informs you like the One who is All-Aware: ﴿Lest a soul should say: "Alas for my regret over what I neglected concerning God, and indeed I was among the mockers." Or lest it say: "If only God had guided me, I would have been among the righteous." Or lest it say when it sees the punishment: "If only I had a return, so I could be among the good-doers"﴾ [Surat al-Zumar: 56-58], meaning: among the guided. So God informed that if they were returned [to the world, they would not remain] upon guidance, and [He said]: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾. [In the printed edition: "So God informed that if they were returned they would return to what they were forbidden..." some of the manuscript text was omitted. In the manuscript: "So God informed that if they were returned upon guidance, and He said: If they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden..." I have adopted the manuscript text and added what I added between the brackets to make the sentence coherent.] And He said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their eyes away, just as they did not believe in it the first time﴾. He said: If they were returned to the world, they would be prevented from guidance, just as We prevented them from it the first time while they were in the world.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the interpretations in my view is that it should be said: God, may His praise be majestic, informed about those who swore by God with their most emphatic oaths that if a sign came to them they would surely believe in it: that He turns their hearts and their eyes and directs them as He wills, that this is in His hand, He makes them upright when He wills and makes them deviate when He desires; and that His saying ﴿just as they did not believe in it the first time﴾ indicates an omitted element of the speech; and that His saying "just as" (kama) is a comparison of what follows it to something before it.

Since that is so, the meaning of the speech must be: And We turn their hearts, so We make them deviate from faith, and their eyes from seeing the truth and recognizing the place of proof, and even if the sign they asked for came to them, they would not believe in God and His Messenger and what he brought from God, just as they did not believe when We turned them before its coming, once before that.

* *

Since that is its interpretation, the "ha'" in His saying ﴿just as they did not believe in it﴾ refers back to the "turning" (taqlib).

* *

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ (110)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His mention be exalted, says: And We leave these polytheists, who swore by God with their most emphatic oaths that if a sign came to them they would surely believe in it when it came [see the explanation of "yadhar" above, 11:529, note 2, and the references there] — in their rebellion against God and their transgression of His limits [see the explanation of "tughyan" above, 10:475, note 2, and the references there] — wandering back and forth, not guided to the truth, nor seeing what is right [see the explanation of "'ama" above, 1:309-311]. Abandonment has overcome them, and Satan has taken possession of them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 111:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels, and the dead had spoken to them, and We had gathered against them every thing before them, they would not have believed, unless Allah willed. But most of them are ignorant.﴾ (6:111)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): O Muhammad, despair of the success of these people who ascribe equals to their Lord, worshipping idols and images, and who say to you: "If you bring us a sign, we will surely believe in you." Indeed, even if We sent down to them the angels so that they saw them with their own eyes, and the dead spoke to them by Our reviving them, as a proof for you and an indication of your prophethood, and they informed them that you are right in what you say, and that what you have brought them is the truth from Allah, and We gathered against them every thing so that We made them face you, they still would not have believed, nor believed you, nor followed you, unless Allah willed that for whomever of them He wills. ﴿But most of them are ignorant﴾ means: but most of these polytheists are ignorant that this is so; they think that faith is in their hands and disbelief is in their hands, that whenever they wish they believe, and whenever they wish they disbelieve. That is not so. That is in My hand; none of them believes except the one whom I guide and enable, and none disbelieves except the one whom I forsake from rightness and cause to go astray.

* *

It was said: this was revealed concerning the mockers of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and of what he brought from Allah, from among the polytheists of Quraysh.

Mention of those who said this:

13755 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: It was revealed concerning the mockers who asked the Prophet (ﷺ) for the sign, the verse: "Say, O Muhammad, 'Signs are only with Allah, and what will make you perceive that when they come they will not believe?'" And there was revealed concerning them: ﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels, and the dead had spoken to them, and We had gathered against them every thing before them.﴾

* *

Others said: What is meant by His saying ﴿they would not have believed﴾ is the people of wretchedness, and His saying ﴿unless Allah willed﴾ is an exception from His saying ﴿to believe﴾, meaning the people of faith and felicity.

Mention of those who said this:

13756 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels, and the dead had spoken to them, and We had gathered against them every thing before them, they would not have believed﴾, and they are the people of wretchedness. Then He said: ﴿unless Allah willed﴾, and they are the people of felicity who had already been decreed in His knowledge to enter into faith.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two views in this matter is the view of Ibn Abbas, because Allah, mighty is His praise, by His saying ﴿they would not have believed﴾ encompassed the people whose mention preceded in His saying: ﴿And they swore by Allah their most emphatic oaths that if a sign came to them they would surely believe in it.﴾

It is possible that those who asked for the sign were the mockers whom Ibn Jurayj said were meant by this verse, but there is no indication in the apparent wording of the revelation for that, nor any report establishing it as proof. The statement from Allah comes in the form of generality, so the view that what is meant is the people of wretchedness among them is more appropriate, for the reason we have described.

* *

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His saying: ﴿and We had gathered against them every thing "qubulan"﴾.

The reciters of Medina recited it as "qiblan" (قِبَلا), with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the ba', meaning: face to face, from the saying of the speaker: "I met him qiblan," meaning face to face and openly.

* *

The majority of the readers of Kufa and Basra recited it: ﴿قُبُلا﴾, with a damma on the qaf and the ba'.

When it is recited thus, it has three possible interpretations:

The first is that "qubul" is the plural of "qabil" (قبيل), like "rughuf" which is the plural of "raghif," and "qudub" which is the plural of "qadib," and "qubul" would mean guarantors and sureties. If that is its meaning, the sense of the speech is: We gathered against them every thing as sureties who guarantee to them that We will punish them for their faith in Allah if they believe, or threaten them for their disbelief in Allah if they die in their disbelief, yet they would not have believed unless Allah willed.

The second is that "qubul" means confrontation and facing, from the speaker's saying: "I came to you qubulan, not dubura," meaning he came to him from the front of his face.

The third is that its meaning is: We gathered against them every thing tribe by tribe, category by category, group by group, so "qubul" then is the plural of "qabil," which is the plural of "qabila," so "qubul" is the plural of a plural.

* *

Some interpreters have said all of these.

Mention of those who said the meaning is: face to face.

13757 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and We had gathered against them every thing qubulan﴾, he said: face to face.

13758 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and We had gathered against them every thing qubulan﴾, until they see it face to face, ﴿they would not have believed unless Allah willed﴾.

* *

Mention of those who said the meaning is: tribe by tribe, category by category.

13759 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us: whoever recites ﴿qubulan﴾, its meaning is: tribe by tribe.

13760 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said: ﴿qubulan﴾, in groups, tribe by tribe.

13761 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Abu Khaythamah, who said: Aban ibn Taghlib narrated to us, who said: Talhah narrated to me that Mujahid recited in "al-An'am": ﴿every thing qubulan﴾, and said: tribes, tribe after tribe, and tribe after tribe.

* *

Mention of those who said the meaning is: facing.

13762 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "And even if We had sent down to them the angels, and the dead had spoken to them, and We had gathered against them every thing qubulan," he said: if all of that confronted them, they would not have believed unless Allah willed.

13763 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿and We had gathered against them every thing qubulan﴾, he said: they were gathered to them all together, and they faced them and confronted them.

13764 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us: Isa recited ﴿qubulan﴾, and its meaning is: openly, before their eyes.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two recitations in our view is the recitation of the one who recited ﴿وَحَشَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ قُبُلا﴾ with a damma on the qaf and the ba', because of the possible meanings we have mentioned, and because the meaning of "qibal" (with a kasra) is included within it, while the meanings of "qibal" are not the only ones that it includes.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and We had gathered against them﴾, its meaning is: We assembled against them and drove them toward them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 112:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy—devils of mankind and jinn, inspiring one another with decorated speech as deception.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, exalted is His mention, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), consoling him with this for what he suffered from the disbelievers of his people for the sake of Allah, and urging him to be patient over what he endured in it: ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy﴾, meaning: just as We have tested you, O Muhammad, by appointing for you enemies among the polytheists of your people, devils who inspire one another with decorated speech, so that by disputing with you they may turn them away from following you and believing in you and in what you brought them from your Lord, so We tested those before you among the prophets and messengers, by appointing for them enemies from their people who harmed them with disputation and quarrels. He means: this with which I have tried you, I have not singled you out from among them alone; rather I have made them all share it with you, in order to try them and test them, although I am able to prevent those who harmed them from harming them. I did not do this except to know the people of steadfast resolve among them from others. He means: so be patient, just as the people of steadfast resolve among the messengers were patient.

* *

As for "devils of mankind and jinn," they are their rebellious ones (marada). We have already explained the verb from which this name is derived, in a way that suffices without repeating it. [See the explanation of "shaytan" earlier: 1:111, 112, 296.]

* *

The accusative of "enemy" (ʿaduwwan) and "devils" (shayatin) is governed by His saying "We have appointed" (jaʿalna). [See Maʿani al-Qur'an 1:351.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿inspiring one another with decorated speech as deception﴾, it means that one of them casts to his companion a speech which he has adorned and made attractive with falsehood, so that whoever hears it may be deceived by it and go astray from the way of Allah. [See the explanation of "wahy" (inspiration) earlier in the lexical indexes, under (w-h-y).]

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of His saying: ﴿devils of mankind and jinn﴾.

Some of them said: its meaning is: the devils of mankind who are with mankind, and the devils of the jinn who are with the jinn; and mankind has no devils.

Those who said this:

13765 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy, devils of mankind and jinn, inspiring one another with decorated speech as deception, and had your Lord willed, they would not have done it." As for "devils of mankind," they are the devils who lead mankind astray; and "devils of the jinn" are those who lead the jinn astray. They meet, and each one of them says: "I have misled my companion with such-and-such, and you have misled your companion with such-and-such," and so they inform one another.

13766 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, who said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, from Shurayk, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, from Ikrimah: "devils of mankind and jinn." He said: there are no devils among mankind; rather the devils of the jinn inspire the devils of mankind, and the devils of mankind inspire the devils of the jinn.

13767 - al-Harith narrated to me, who said: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, who said: Isra'il narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His saying: "inspiring one another with decorated speech as deception." He said: For mankind there is a devil, and for the jinn there is a devil; the devil of mankind meets the devil of the jinn, and they inspire one another with decorated speech as deception.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Ikrimah and al-Suddi, in this interpretation of theirs that I have mentioned from them, made the enemies of the prophets whom Allah mentioned in His saying "And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy" to be the sons of Iblis, and not the sons of Adam nor the jinn; and they made those described as inspiring one another with decorated speech as deception to be the sons of Iblis, and that whoever is with the son of Adam of the sons of Iblis inspires whoever is with the jinn of his offspring with decorated speech as deception.

This interpretation has no intelligible basis, because Allah made Iblis and his offspring enemies of the son of Adam, so all his offspring are enemies to all of his offspring. In this verse, Allah specifically reports about the prophets that He appointed for them enemies from the devils. If what was meant by that were the devils that al-Suddi mentioned, who are the sons of Iblis, there would be no point in specifically reporting about the prophets that He appointed devils as enemies for them. He has appointed the like of what He appointed for them for His greatest enemy. Rather, it is as we have said: what is meant is that He appointed the rebellious ones of mankind and jinn as an enemy for every prophet, inspiring one another with speech by which they harm them.

* *

The report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has come in a manner similar to what we have said.

13768 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, who said: Hammad narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, who said: a man of the people of Damascus narrated to me, from Awf ibn Malik, from Abu Dharr: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Dharr, have you sought refuge in Allah from the evil of the devils of mankind and jinn?" He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, do mankind have devils?" He said: "Yes!"

13769 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Abu Salih narrated to us, who said: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ayyub and others among the shaykhs, from Ibn A'idh, from Abu Dharr, that he said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in a gathering in which he had prolonged sitting. He said: "O Abu Dharr, have you prayed?" I said: "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Rise and pray two rak'ahs." He said: then I came and sat with him, and he said: "O Abu Dharr, have you sought refuge in Allah from the evil of the devils of mankind and jinn?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, do mankind have devils?" He said: "Yes, the evil of them is worse than the devils of the jinn!"

13770 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: It reached me that Abu Dharr once stood praying, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Seek refuge, O Abu Dharr, from the devils of mankind and jinn." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, do mankind have devils?" He said: "Yes!"

* *

Others said, in a manner similar to what we have said: that this is a report from Allah that the devils of mankind and jinn inspire one another.

Those who said this:

13771 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: "devils of mankind and jinn." He said: among the jinn there are devils, and among mankind there are devils, who inspire one another. Qatadah said: It reached me that Abu Dharr was once praying, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Seek refuge, O Abu Dharr, from the devils of mankind and jinn." He said: "O Prophet of Allah, do mankind have devils?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Yes!"

13772 - Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: "And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy, devils of mankind and jinn," the verse. It was mentioned to us that Abu Dharr once stood praying, and the Prophet of Allah said to him: "Seek refuge in Allah from the devils of the jinn and mankind." He said: "O Prophet of Allah, do mankind have devils like the devils of the jinn?" He said: "Yes, did I lie about him?"

13773 - al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said: "And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy, devils of mankind and jinn," and he said: the disbelieving jinn are devils, who inspire the devils of mankind, the disbelieving mankind, with decorated speech as deception.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿decorated speech as deception﴾, it means what is adorned with falsehood, as I described before. It is said of it: "he embellished his speech and his testimony," when he makes it attractive with falsehood and embroiders it, as:

13774 - Sufyan ibn Waki narrated to us, who said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, from Shurayk, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, from Ikrimah concerning His saying: "decorated speech as deception." He said: the adornment of falsehood with tongues.

13775 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: As for "zukhruf," they embellished it, they made it beautiful.

13776 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, who said: Abu Asim narrated to us, who said: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "decorated speech as deception," he said: the adornment of falsehood with tongues.

13777 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, who said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

13778 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, who said: my uncle narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying: "decorated speech as deception," he says: some of them made speech attractive to others, so that they would follow them in their trial.

13779 - Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: "decorated speech as deception": "al-zukhruf" is what is adorned, insofar as it adorned this deception for them, just as Iblis adorned for Adam what he brought him, and swore to him that he was surely among the sincere advisers. And he recited: "And We appointed for them companions who made their deeds seem fair to them" [Fussilat: 25]. He said: that is the zukhruf.

* *

As for "ghurur" (deception), it is that which deceives a person and deludes him, turning him from the right to the wrong and from the truth to the falsehood [See the explanation of "ghurur" earlier: 7:453 / 9:224]. It is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "I deceived so-and-so with such-and-such, so I deceive him, deception and delusion," like what was reported:

13780 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "ghurur," he said: they deceive people and jinn with it.

* *

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And had your Lord willed, they would not have done it; so leave them and what they fabricate﴾ (112)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, exalted is His mention, says: Had you willed, O Muhammad, that those who were enemies of My prophets from the devils of mankind and jinn believe, their plotting would not have touched them, and they would have been safe from their harms and their injury, I would have done so. But I did not will that, in order to test some of them by means of others, so that each group deserves what has preceded for it in the previous Book. ﴿So leave them﴾, meaning: leave them [See the explanation of "dhara" earlier, p. 46, note 1, and the references there] — meaning the devils who dispute with you in falsehood from the polytheists of your people and argue with you with what their allies among the devils of mankind and jinn inspire to them — ﴿and what they fabricate﴾, meaning: what they invent of lies and falsehood. [See the explanation of "iftira'" earlier: 11:533, note 1, and the references there.]

He says to him (ﷺ): be patient with them, for I am behind their punishment for their fabrication against Allah and their inventing of falsehood and lies against Him.

* *

The explanation of His saying: ﴿and that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it, and that they may be pleased with it﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, exalted is His mention, says: ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy, devils of mankind and jinn, inspiring one another with decorated speech as deception﴾ — ﴿and that it may incline to it﴾, His majesty says: some of these devils inspire to others the speech adorned with falsehood, so that they may deceive with it the believers among the followers of the prophets and turn them away from their religion — ﴿and that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it﴾, meaning: and that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline toward it.

* *

It is from "sagha yasgha and yasghu" (to incline), and the Revelation came with "yasgha," "sagwan and suguwwan." Some Arabs say "saghiya," with a yā', it is related from some of the Banu Asad: "saghiya ila hadithihi, fa-ana asgha sughiyyan" with a yā', and that is when one inclines. It is said: "sagwi ma'aka" (my inclination is with you) when your desire and your leaning are with him, like their saying "dhili'i ma'aka" (my side is with you). And it is said: "asghaytu al-inai" (I tilted the vessel) when you tilt it so that what is in it gathers, and from it is the saying of the poet: [I do not know who said it.]

You see the foolish one, away from every firm verse, is in deviation, and in him is an inclination toward the likeness.

[Al-Lisan (sagha); also in Abu Hayyan's Tafsir 4:205, and al-Qurtubi 7:69; in al-Lisan and al-Qurtubi it reads "from every honored [thing]," but the correct reading appears to be that of Ibn Jarir's Tafsir and Abu Hayyan's, and the poet apparently means those who follow what is ambiguous (mutashabih) among the verses of Allah's Book and turn away from its clear (muhkam) verses.]

It is said of the moon when it inclines toward the hidden things: "sagha" and "asgha."

* *

The people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said.

Those who said this:

13781 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, who said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas: "and that the hearts may incline to it," he says: the hearts may swerve toward it.

13782 - al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said concerning His saying: "and that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it," he said: "to incline."

13783 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "and that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it," he says: the hearts of the disbelievers incline to it, and love it, and are pleased with it.

13784 - Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: "and that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it," he said: "and that it may incline," and that they may desire that and be pleased with it. He said: a man says to a woman: "I have inclined to her," meaning I have desired her.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 113:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And that they may commit [of sins] what they are committing﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, exalted is His mention, means: "And that they may earn from deeds what they are earning."

* *

It is related from the Arabs, by hearing from them: "He went out to iqtarafa (to earn/provide) for his family," meaning he earns for them. And from this it is said: "So-and-so committed (qarafa) this matter," when he engaged in it and did it.

Some of them said: it means accusation and claim. It is said to a man: "You have accused me (qarafta-ni)," meaning you accused me. And it is said: "What an evil thing you have earned (iqtarafta) for yourself." Ru'ba said:

"The committing of the committed lie has wearied... the piety of the pious and the chastity of the chaste." [Not found in his Diwan; they are in Majaz al-Qur'an 1:205.]

* *

Those who interpreted the exegesis said the same as what we have said concerning His saying: ﴿And that they may commit﴾.

Those who said that:

13785 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And that they may commit what they are committing﴾, and that they may earn what they are earning.

13786 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And that they may commit what they are committing﴾, he said: that they may do what they are doing.

13787 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿And that they may commit what they are committing﴾, he said: that they may do what they are doing.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 114:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Shall I seek a judge other than Allah, when it is He who has sent down to you the Book, fully detailed?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say to those who ascribe equals to Allah, the idols and images, who say to you, "Desist from our gods, and we will desist from your God": Indeed Allah has judged concerning my mentioning your gods in a way that would turn people away from worshipping them. ﴿Shall I seek a judge other than Allah?﴾ That is, say: then it is not for me to transgress His judgment or go beyond it, for there is no judge more just than Him, and no speaker more truthful than Him [[See the explanation of "al-hukm" (judgment) in the earlier lexical indexes, under the root (ḥ-k-m).]]. ﴿And it is He who has sent down to you the Book, fully detailed﴾, meaning the Qur'an, "fully detailed," meaning: clarifying therein the judgment concerning what you dispute about, regarding my affair and yours.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "tafsil" (detailing) earlier [[See the explanation of "al-tafsil" in the earlier volume 11: 394.]].

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And those to whom We have given the Book know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth, so do not be among the doubters﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: If those who ascribe equals to Allah, the idols, among your people deny the Oneness of Allah, associate rivals with Him, reject what We have sent down to you, and deny that it is true and call it a lie, then ﴿those to whom We have given the Book﴾, namely the Torah and the Gospel, from the Children of Israel, ﴿know that it is sent down from your Lord﴾, meaning the Qur'an and what it contains. ﴿In truth﴾ means: as a decisive distinction between the people of truth and the people of falsehood, indicating the truthfulness of the truthful in the knowledge of Allah and the falsehood of the liar who fabricates against Him. ﴿So do not be among the doubters﴾ means: so do not be, O Muhammad, among those who doubt the reality of the reports that came to you from Allah in this Book and other things it contains, because those to whom We have given the Book know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth.

* *

We have already explained earlier the meaning of His saying ﴿so do not be among the doubters﴾, in a way that suffices without repetition, along with the narration transmitted concerning it [[See the explanation of "al-imtira'" in the earlier volumes 3: 190–192 / 6: 472, 473 / 11: 260.]], and indeed:

13788- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His saying ﴿so do not be among the doubters﴾: he says, "Do not be in doubt about what We have related to you."

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice; there is none who can alter His words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ (6:115).

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: "And the word of your Lord was perfected," meaning the Qur'an.

* *

He called it "word" just as the Arabs call a poem that a poet recites "this is the word of so-and-so." [[See the explanation of "word" (al-kalimah) above: 3:7-17 / 6:371, 410-412 / 8:432 / 9:410 / 10:129, 313]]

* *

﴿In truth and justice﴾: he says, the word of your Lord was perfected in truth and justice.

* *

"Truth" and "justice" are in the accusative as a specification (tafsir) of the word, just as one says, "I have twenty dirhams." [[The "tafsir" here is the "tamyiz" (specification), see the glossary of terms above.]]

= ﴿There is none who can alter His words﴾: he says, there is none who changes what He informed in His books that would occur, from its happening at its appointed time and its term, which Allah informed would take place in it. [[See the explanation of "tabdil" (alteration) above: 11:335, and the indices of language, root b-d-l.]] This is like His, exalted is His praise, saying: ﴿They wish to change the words of Allah. Say: You will not follow us; thus has Allah said before﴾ [Surah al-Fath: 15]. Their wish to change the words of Allah was their request of the Prophet of Allah that he let them attend the battle with him, and their saying to him and to those who were with him of the believers: ﴿Let us follow you﴾, after the report which Allah, exalted is His mention, had informed them of in His Book by His saying: ﴿So if Allah returns you to a group of them and they ask your permission to go out, say: You will never go out with me, and you will never fight an enemy with me...﴾ up to the end of the verse [Surah al-Tawbah: 83]. So they attempted to change the words and report of Allah, that they would never go out with the Prophet of Allah on a raid, nor fight an enemy with him, by their saying to them: ﴿Let us follow you.﴾ Then Allah, exalted is His mention, said to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "They wish to change" — by their request of that — the words and report of Allah: ﴿Say: You will not follow us; thus has Allah said before.﴾ Likewise the meaning of His saying: ﴿There is none who can alter His words﴾ is only: there is none who changes what He reported as something that will occur, so that its coming, its existence and its occurrence as He, exalted is His praise, reported would be nullified, because the distorters do not add to or subtract from the books of Allah. This is because the Jews and Christians are, without doubt, the people of the books of Allah which He sent down to His prophets, and He, exalted is His praise, has informed that they distort what He reported cannot be altered.

* *

Those who held this view and the people of interpretation said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

13789- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice; there is none who can alter His words﴾, he says: truth and justice in what He judged.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾, its meaning is: and Allah is "the All-Hearing" of what these who ascribe equals to Allah say, those who swear by Allah with their most solemn oaths: "If a sign comes to them, they will surely believe in it," and other speech of His creation; "the All-Knowing" of what their oaths will lead to of righteousness, truth, falsehood and breaking, and other matters of His servants. [[See the explanation of "al-Sami'" (the All-Hearing) and "al-Alim" (the All-Knowing) above in the indices of language, roots s-m-' and '-l-m.]]

* *

At this point ends a part of the old division from which our copy was transcribed, and in it is the text: "Followed by the discussion of the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will mislead you from the way of Allah. They follow not except assumption, and they are not but guessing﴾, and may Allah bless Muhammad, his family and companions abundantly."

Then follows what reads: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. My Lord, grant success and help."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 116:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will mislead you from the way of Allah. They follow not except assumption, and they are not but guessing.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Do not obey these who ascribe equals to Allah, O Muhammad, in what they have invited you to, namely eating what they slaughter for their idols and what they dedicate to other than their Lord, and their likes from among the people of deviation and error. Indeed, if you obey most of those on earth, they will mislead you from the religion of Allah and the clear path of truth and correctness, and they will turn you away from that.

Allah said to His Prophet, ﴿if you obey most of those on earth﴾, from among the children of Adam, because they were at that time disbelievers in error. So He, mighty is His praise, said to him: Do not obey them in what they invite you to, for if you obey them you will be misled by their misguidance and you would be like them, since they do not invite you to guidance while they have missed it. Then He, mighty is His praise, informed about the condition of those whom He forbade His Prophet to obey in what they invited him to, regarding themselves, saying: ﴿They follow not except assumption﴾. So He, mighty is His praise, informed that concerning their affair they are upon assumption in their own selves, and conjecture about the soundness of a resolve they hold to, [[Thus it is in the printed edition and the manuscript, and I am in doubt about its correctness.]] though it is in reality an error. ﴿And they are not but guessing﴾, meaning: they are none other than conjecturers, who assume and utter conjecture, not certain knowledge.

[[See Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubayda, 1: 206.]]

* *

It is said of it: "kharasa yakhrusu kharsan wa kharusan" [[In the printed edition: "kharsan wa kharsan". I have adopted what is in the manuscript; I did not find "kharusan" as a verbal noun of this verb in any of the lexicons available to me, but Abu Hayyan also mentioned it in his tafsir, 4: 205.]]

meaning he lied; and "takharrasa bi-zann" (he conjectured by assumption), and "takharrasa bi-kadhib" (he fabricated with a lie), and "kharastu al-nakhl akhrusuhu" (I estimated the palm trees), and "kharisat ibiluka" (your camels were struck by cold and hunger).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 117:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His way, and He is most knowing of those who are guided.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: God, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): O Muhammad, indeed your Lord, who forbade you to obey those who associate idols with God, lest they lead you astray from His way, is more knowing than you and than all of His creation as to which of His creatures strays from His way through the deceptive speech that the devils inspire in one another, so that they turn others away from obeying Him and following what He has commanded. ﴿And He is most knowing of those who are guided﴾: He says, and He is also more knowing than you and them of those who were upright and rightly guided, nothing about them being hidden from Him. He says: So follow, O Muhammad, what I have commanded you, and refrain from what I have forbidden you, namely obeying those whose obedience I have forbidden you, for I am more knowing than you of the guide and the misguided among My creatures.

* *

The scholars of Arabic grammar differed regarding the position (i'rab) of "man" (مَن) in His words: ﴿Indeed your Lord is most knowing of who strays﴾.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: its position is genitive (khafd), with an implied "bi" (ba', the preposition "with/about"). He said: the meaning of the statement is: indeed your Lord is most knowing of whoever strays. [See what has preceded in vol. 11, p. 560, note 1, that its speaker is al-Akhfash.]

* *

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: its position is nominative (raf'), because it carries the meaning of "ayyu" (whichever), and what makes it nominative is "yadillu" (strays). [See the detailed explanation in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an, vol. 1, p. 352; this is al-Farra's view.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this is that it is nominative by "yadillu," and it carries the meaning of "ayyu." There is no known instance in Arabic speech of a noun in the genitive without a governing particle, so that this could have a parallel.

* *

Some have claimed that His words ﴿a'lam﴾ (most knowing) in this position mean "ya'lam" (knows), citing the verse of Hatim al-Ta'i:

"So Tayyi' allied themselves apart from us in a pact, and God knows that we did not forsake them."

[The verse is not in the Diwan of Hatim; it is in the Tafsir of al-Qurtubi, vol. 7, p. 72, quoting this passage of Abu Ja'far's tafsir: his words "half" are with a kasra on the ha' and lam; the kasra of the ha' made the lam carry a kasra for the necessity of poetry. Had he said "hilfan" (with fatha on the lam), being the verbal noun of "halafa yahlifu," like "al-half" (with kasra then sukun), it would have been correct, because "al-half," meaning the covenant, was called "halfan" from the verbal noun of "halafa" in the sense of "swore," since a covenant is secured by oath.]

And by the saying of al-Khansa':

"The people know that his fire-pit, when lit, runs at the morning of the windy cold, or travels by night."

[From her Diwan, p. 104, in lamenting her brother Sakhr; after it: "When it lights up and its cauldron boils, how excellent is the lord of fire and pot." Her words "tagdu" mean it goes forth to his people and guests. "Ghadat al-rih" means a morning in winter, in a time of drought and scarcity of milk. "Tasra" means at night. Her words "adaa" mean he kindled his fire so the pots could be set on it and the guests could see it.]

Yet what the speaker of this interpretation said, although it is permissible in Arabic speech, is not the meaning of God's words, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿Indeed your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His way﴾. This is because He joined to it His words ﴿and He is most knowing of those who are guided﴾, and by the entry of the "bi" into "al-muhtadin" He made clear that "a'lam" does not mean "ya'lam," since when it means "yaf'alu," it is not connected with "bi," just as one does not say "he knows with Zayd," meaning "he knows Zayd."

The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿So eat of that over which the name of God has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and to His servants who believe in Him and in His signs: "So eat," O believers, "of what you have slaughtered by your own means of slaughter, and which you have slaughtered in the manner that I have made clear to you makes the animal lawful for you. That is what is slaughtered by those among the people of your religion, the religion of truth, who believe in Me, or what is slaughtered by those among the People of the Book who profess the monotheism I teach, as opposed to what is slaughtered by the idolaters and by those who have no scripture, such as the Magians." ﴿If you are believers in His signs﴾ means: if you are believers, in the proofs of God that have come to you and His indications, in the permissibility of what I have made lawful for you and the prohibition of what I have forbidden you of foods and victuals, affirming them as true. And leave aside the adornment of what the devils inspire to one another of ornamented speech directed at you, and the confusion they bring to your religion, as deception.

* *

Atâ used to say concerning this:

13790. Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: I said to 'Ata', regarding His words: ﴿So eat of that over which the name of God has been mentioned﴾. He said: He commands the mention of His name over drink, food, and slaughter, and everything that indicates the remembrance of Him, He commands it.

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, while He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you, except what you are compelled to?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The scholars of the Arabic language differed concerning the interpretation of His words: ﴿Wa ma lakum an la ta'kulu﴾ (And what is [the matter] with you that you do not eat).

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The meaning of that is: "And what [benefit] is there for you in not eating?" He said: This is similar to His words: ﴿And what is [the matter] with us that we should not fight﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 246]. It means: "What is there for us in abandoning fighting?" He said: And if "la" were superfluous, the verb would not take effect. [Note: "la yaqa' al-fi'l" means it would not be transitive; "al-wuqu'" means transitivity.] And if it were in the sense of "wa ma lana wa kadha," it would be: "And what is [the matter] with us and that we do not fight."

* *

Others said: "La" was introduced for prohibition, because the meaning of "ma laka" and "ma mana'aka" is one. "Ma mana'aka la taf'alu dhalika" and "ma laka la taf'alu" are one and the same. Therefore "la" was introduced. He said: In this construction "la" may occur, and "an" may occur, like His words: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 176], and "an la tadillu" (lest you go astray), which restrains you from going astray through clarification. [Abu Ja'far has thoroughly examined this matter previously (5: 300–305), and al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (1: 163–166); Abu Ja'far did not refer to that here, as is his custom in earlier passages.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two opinions in my view is the statement of the one who said: the meaning of His words ﴿wa ma lakum﴾ in this place is: "And what prevents you from eating of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned?" This is because Allah, exalted is His mention, had previously addressed the believers with the permissibility of what the name of Allah has been mentioned over, and the permission to eat what was slaughtered in His religion or the religion of those who adhered to some of the known laws of His books, and the prohibition of what was dedicated to other than Him among animals; and He warned them against listening to what the devils inspire to one another of ornate speech concerning carrion, the strangled, the fallen, and the rest of what Allah has forbidden of foods. Then He said: And what prevents you from eating what was slaughtered by My religion which I have approved, when I have detailed for you the lawful from the unlawful in what you eat, and made it clear to you by My word: ﴿Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah﴾, up to His words: ﴿But whoever is compelled by hunger, without inclination to sin﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 3]. So there is no confusion for you regarding the unlawful from the lawful, such that you would refrain from eating the lawful out of fear of falling into the unlawful.

Since this is its meaning, there is no basis for the view of those who interpret it as "And what [benefit] is there for you in not eating," because that is said only of one who has refrained from eating in hope of reward for abstaining from it, and that occurs only from one who believed and so refrained, following Allah's command and submitting to His judgment. We know of no one from the early generations of this nation who refrained from eating the slaughtered animals that Allah had made lawful, hoping for Allah's reward for leaving it, and believing that Allah had forbidden it to him. It is therefore clear, since the matter is as we have described, that the more correct of the two interpretations is what we have said.

* *

We have already explained earlier that the meaning of His words "fassala," "fassalna," and "fussila" is "bayyana" or "bu'ayyina" (made clear), which suffices without repeating it here [see the explanation of "al-tafsil" earlier, p. 60, note 2, and its references; and see the language indexes under (fassala)]. As follows:

13791 — Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And He has detailed for you what He has forbidden to you﴾, he said: "He has made clear to you what He has forbidden to you."

13792 — Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Ibn Zayd, similarly.

* *

The readers differed concerning the recitation of Allah's words, exalted is His mention: ﴿wa qad fassala lakum ma harrama 'alaykum﴾.

Some of them read the first letters of "fassala" and "harrama" with a fatha, meaning: He detailed what He forbade of your foods, and made it clear to you.

* *

The common readers of the Kufans read ﴿wa qad fassala﴾ with a fatha on the fa' of "fassala" and shaddah on its sad, and "ma hurrima" with a damma on its ha' and shaddah on its ra', meaning: And Allah has detailed for you what is forbidden to you of your foods.

* *

Some of the Makkans and some of the Basrans read: "wa qad fussila lakum," with a damma on its fa' and shaddah on its sad, and "ma hurrima 'alaykum," with a damma on its ha' and shaddah on its ra', in the passive form in both letters.

* *

It is related from 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi that he used to read it: "wa qad fasala," with lightening of the sad and a fatha on the fa', meaning: the judgment of Allah concerning what He has forbidden to you has come to you.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct position in this matter, in our view, is to say that all these three readings we have mentioned, apart from the reading we attributed to 'Atiyyah, are well-known, widely transmitted readings in the cities' recitation, and their meanings agree and do not differ. Thus whichever of them the reciter recites, he is correct in it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿illa ma idturirtum ilayh﴾ (except what you are compelled to), He, exalted is His mention, means: that what we are compelled to of the forbidden foods, whose prohibition He has made clear to us outside the state of necessity, is lawful for us in what we are compelled to, until the necessity passes [see the explanation of "idturra" earlier, 3: 56, 322 / 9: 532]. As follows:

13793 — Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿except what you are compelled to﴾, of the carrion.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And indeed, many [of them] lead [others] astray by their desires without knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of the transgressors﴾ (119)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: And indeed many of the people [who] dispute with you concerning eating what Allah has forbidden to you, O believers in Allah, namely carrion, lead their followers astray by their desires, without knowledge on their part of the soundness of what they say, nor any proof they have for what they dispute about, except that they ride upon their desires and follow the promptings of their souls, transgressing and opposing the command and prohibition of Allah, and obeying the devils [see the explanation of "al-ahwa'" earlier in the language indexes under (hawa), and "al-dalal" under (dalla)]. ﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of the transgressors﴾ — He says: Indeed your Lord, O Muhammad, who made lawful for you what He made lawful and forbade you what He forbade, is most knowing of those who transgress His limits, going beyond them to their opposite, and He is watching them closely [see the explanation of "al-i'tida'" earlier in the language indexes under (ada)].

* *

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words: ﴿liyudillun﴾.

The common people of Kufa read it: ﴿liyudillun﴾, meaning: they lead others astray.

* *

Some of the Basrans and Hijazis read it: "liyadillun," meaning: they themselves go astray from the truth and deviate from it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings in this matter is the reading of the one who reads: ﴿wa inna kathiran liyudillun bi-ahwa'ihim﴾, meaning: they lead others astray. This is because Allah, exalted is His mention, informed His Prophet ﷺ about their misleading of those who followed them, and forbade him from obeying and following them in what they called to, saying: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will mislead you from the way of Allah﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 116]. Then He informed his companions about them with the like of what He had informed him, and forbade them from accepting their speech with the like of what He had forbidden him, saying to them: And indeed many of them mislead you by their desires without knowledge — like His words to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will mislead you from the way of Allah﴾.

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿And leave the outward and the inward of sin﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: His mention, exalted is He, says: "And leave, O people, the open [[See the explanation of ((dh-r)) above, p. 57, note 1, and the references there.]] sin, which is its outward, and its secret, which is its inward." As follows:

13794. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And leave the outward and the inward of sin﴾: that is, its little and its much, and its secret and its open.

13795. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And leave the outward and the inward of sin﴾: he said, its secret and its open.

13796. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding His saying ﴿And leave the outward and the inward of sin﴾, he said: its secret and its open. And His saying ﴿what is apparent of them and what is hidden﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 33], he said: its secret and its open.

13797. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding His saying ﴿And leave the outward and the inward of sin﴾, he said: Allah forbade the outward of sin and its inward, that it be done in secret or in the open, and that is its outward and its inward.

13798. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And leave the outward and the inward of sin﴾: disobedience to Allah in secret and in the open.

13799. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And leave the outward and the inward of sin﴾, he said: it is what one intends while doing it.

* *

Then the people of interpretation (ta'wil) [[Ta'wil: interpretation or explanation of the meaning of the Qur'an.]] differed concerning what is meant by the outward and the inward of sin in this place.

Some of them said: "The outward of it" is what He, exalted is His mention, forbade by His saying ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 23], and His saying ﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers﴾, to the end of the verse. And "the inward of it" is fornication.

Those who said this:

13800. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying ﴿And leave the outward and the inward of sin﴾, he said: The outward of it: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women, except what has already passed﴾, and the mothers, the daughters, and the sisters. "And the inward": fornication.

* *

Others said: "The outward" is the prostitutes who hoisted banners [[((Ulat al-rayat)): the prostitutes of the pre-Islamic period, who would set up banners at their tents or houses by which they were recognized.]], and "the inward" is those who take secret lovers.

Those who said this:

13801. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And leave the outward and the inward of sin﴾: As for "its outward", it is the prostitutes in the shops; and as for "its inward", it is the female friend whom a man takes and visits secretly.

13802. al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj narrated to me, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to me, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿And do not approach indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 151]: The people of the Jahiliyyah would conceal fornication, and they considered it lawful so long as it was secret. So Allah forbade both its secret and its open. "What is apparent of them" means the open, "and what is hidden" means the secret.

13803. Ibn Wakf'i narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Abu Makin and his father, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And do not approach indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden﴾, he said: "What is apparent of them": the combining of two sisters, and a man's marrying his father's wife after him. "And what is hidden": fornication.

* *

Others said: "The outward" is nakedness and stripping off clothing, and what covers the private parts during circumambulation (tawaf), and "the inward" is fornication.

Those who said this:

13804. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And do not approach indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden﴾: its outward is the nakedness (al-'urya) [[((al-'urya)) (with a vowel on the ʿayn and a sukun on the rāʾ) is a verbal noun from ((ʿarā min thawbihi yaʿrā ʿaryan wa ʿuryatan)), meaning he was stripped of his garment. It is said: ((jāriya ḥasanat al-ʿurya, wa ḥasanat al-maʿrā wa al-maʿrāh)), meaning a girl who is beautiful when stripped of her clothing.]] in which they would act while circumambulating the House, and its inward is fornication.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that it should be said: Allah, exalted is His mention, has directed His creatures to leave the outward of sin and its inward, that is, its secret and its open. And "sin" (al-ithm) is everything by which Allah is disobeyed in what He has forbidden. It may include in that the secret of fornication and its open, fornicating with the women of banners and those who take secret lovers among them, marrying the wives of fathers, mothers, and daughters, circumambulating the House naked, and every act of disobedience to Allah, whether apparent or hidden. Since this is so, and all of that is "sin", and Allah has generalized by His saying ﴿And leave the outward and the inward of sin﴾ all that is apparent of sin and all that is hidden, no one may single out any part of it over another except with a clear proof of excuse.

However, if it were permissible to direct this to a particular meaning without evidence, then directing it to mean, in this place, the outward and the inward of sin as what Allah forbade of foods and eatables, such as carrion and blood, and what Allah explained as forbidden in His saying ﴿Forbidden to you is carrion﴾ to the end of the verse, would be more appropriate, since the beginning of the verses before it dealt with the prohibition of that, and this verse is within its context. Yet it is not objectionable that it means that, and that it includes the command to avoid everything similar to it of the acts of disobedience to Allah, so the command becomes general in prohibiting all that is apparent or hidden of sin.

* *

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, those who earn sin will be recompensed for what they used to commit﴾ (120)**

Abu Ja'far said: His mention, exalted is He, says: Indeed, those who act upon what Allah has forbidden them, and commit the acts of disobedience to Allah, and do what Allah has prohibited: ﴿will be recompensed﴾, meaning: Allah will reward them on the Day of Resurrection for the acts of His disobedience they used to do in the world. [[See the explanation of ((kasab)) above in the linguistic indices (kasab); and the explanation of ((al-jaza')) above in the indices (jazā); and the explanation of ((iqtarafa)) above, pp. 59–60.]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 121 (part 1 of 2):**

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed it is defiantly disobedient. And indeed, the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you. And if you obey them, indeed you are associators [with Allah].﴾ (6:121)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾, He means: Do not eat, O believers, of that which has died without your slaughtering it, or without its being slaughtered by a monotheist who submits to Allah in the laws He prescribed for him in a revealed Book, for it is forbidden to you. Nor [do not eat] of that over which other than Allah has been invoked, which the polytheists slaughtered for their idols. ﴿For indeed, it is "fisq"﴾, meaning: disobedience, [i.e.,] unbelief. [[See the explanation of "al-fisq" above, 11:370; note 2 and the references there.]]

* *

So by His words "wa-innahu" ("and indeed it"), He refers to "the eating" [al-akl], but He mentioned the verb [i.e., the verbal noun]. [[The "verb" here is the verbal noun (al-masdar).]] As in His words: ﴿Those to whom the people said, "Indeed the people have gathered against you, so fear them," but it increased them in faith﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:173]. What is meant is: their saying that increased them in faith. So He refers to "the saying" [al-qawl], though its mention came with a verb. [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:352.]]

= ﴿And indeed, the devils inspire their allies﴾. [[See the explanation of "al-wahy" (inspiration) in the earlier language indices (w-h-y).]]

The interpreters differed regarding who is meant by His words ﴿And indeed, the devils inspire their allies﴾. Some of them said: He means the devils of Persia and those who follow their religion of the Magians. ﴿To their allies﴾ means the rebellious leaders of the polytheists of Quraysh, who inspire to them ornate speech, to dispute with the Prophet of Allah and his Companions over eating carrion. [[In the printed edition: "they inspire to them ornate speech so that it reaches the Prophet of Allah and his Companions concerning eating carrion." The editor did not read the manuscript well, and made an effort that corrupted the sentence beyond any sense. In the manuscript it was: "... ornate speech yahudd ila Nabi Allah" (unpointed), and this is the correct reading.]]

Those who said this:

13805 – Ibn Bashshar ... (narrated to me) ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Bishr ibn al-Hakam al-Nisaburi said: Musa ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz al-Qanbari said: al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from Ikrimah: When this verse was revealed, prohibiting carrion, he said: Persia inspired to its allies among Quraysh that they should dispute with Muhammad — and they had been their allies in the pre-Islamic era [[i.e., Quraysh were the allies and supporters of Persia in the pre-Islamic era; this is a parenthetical clause which I have placed between two lines.]] — and say to him: "Is what you slaughter lawful, while what Allah slaughters [is forbidden]?"
