[[In the printed and manuscript editions: "that what you slaughter" — as if it were a statement; it is in fact a question and an expression of astonishment that the slaughter of creatures be lawful while the slaughter of Allah — by their claim, which is carrion — be forbidden.]] Ibn ʿAbbas said: "With a golden shamshar" [[The word "shamshar" in Ibn Kathir's Tafsir 3:389 is "shamshir"; its explanation in another report indicates that "al-shamshar" or "al-shamshir" is a knife or blade; see report 13806. It seems this was among the beliefs of the Magians, that carrion is the slaughter of Allah, slaughtered with a golden shamshar!!]] = so it is forbidden!! Then Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And indeed, the devils inspire their allies﴾. He said: The devils are Persia, and their allies are Quraysh.

[[The report 13805: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Bishr ibn al-Hakam al-ʿAbdi al-Nisaburi: trustworthy, truthful, among the teachers of al-Bukhari and Abu Hatim. Biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/215.
Musa ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz al-Yamani al-ʿAdani al-Qanbari: "la ba's bihi" (no harm in him), but spoken about. Biographed in al-Tahdhib, and al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 4/1/292, where he mentions no criticism of him, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/151.
"Al-Qanbari" is a nisba to "al-qanbar," which is ropes twisted from the fiber of the coconut palm tree, called the Indian nut; ships are towed with qanbar ropes because of their strength.]]

13806 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, said: al-Husayn narrated to us, said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ʿAmr ibn Dinar said, from Ikrimah: The polytheists of Quraysh corresponded with Persia against Rome, and Persia corresponded with them. Persia wrote to the polytheists of Quraysh: "Muhammad and his Companions claim that they follow the command of Allah. So what Allah slaughters with a golden knife, Muhammad and his Companions will not eat it = [this is] carrion = but what they slaughter themselves, they eat!" The polytheists wrote this to the Companions of Muhammad, peace be upon him. Some of the Muslims were troubled in their souls by this, so there was revealed: ﴿And indeed it is fisq, and indeed the devils inspire﴾, the verse; and there was revealed: ﴿They inspire to one another ornate speech as deception﴾ [al-An'am 6:112].

* *

Others said: The devils who deceive the children of Adam are meant; they inspired to their allies from Quraysh.

Those who said this:

13807 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, said: Hakkam narrated to us, from ʿAnbasa, from Simak, from Ikrimah, who said: Among what the devils inspired to their allies from mankind was: "How do you worship something that you do not eat of what it has killed, while you eat what you yourselves have killed?" So it was related until it reached the Prophet ﷺ, and there was revealed: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾.

13808 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, said: al-Husayn narrated to us, said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: His words ﴿And indeed, the devils inspire their allies﴾ — he said: It is Iblis, who inspires to the polytheists of Quraysh. Ibn Jurayj said, from ʿAta' al-Khurasani, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The devils of the jinn inspire to the devils of mankind: "They inspire to their allies to dispute with you." Ibn Jurayj said, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Kathir, who said: I heard that the devils inspire to the people of polytheism, ordering them to say: "What dies and what you slaughter are no different!" They order them to dispute with this against Muhammad ﷺ = ﴿And if you obey them, indeed you are associators﴾. He said: The saying of the polytheists: "As for what Allah slaughters, [it is] carrion, so you do not eat it; but what you slaughter with your hands is lawful!"

13809 – Muhammad ibn ʿAmmar al-Razi narrated to us, said: Saʿid ibn Sulayman narrated to us, said: Sharik narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Ikrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas: The polytheists said to the Muslims: "What your Lord kills, you do not eat; what you kill yourselves, you eat!" So Allah revealed to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾. [[The report 13809: Muhammad ibn ʿAmmar ibn al-Harith al-Razi, Abu Ja'far; he narrated from Ishaq ibn Sulayman, al-Sindi ibn ʿAbdawayh, and Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il; Ibn Abi Hatim wrote from him and said: "He is truthful and trustworthy." Biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/43.
"Sa'id ibn Sulayman": I do not know who among those named thus this is, and I fear that the correct reading is "Ishaq ibn Sulayman al-Razi," whom Ibn Hibban mentioned that "Muhammad ibn ʿAmmar narrates from him."]]

13810 – Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, said: My father narrated to me, said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When Allah prohibited carrion, the devil ordered his allies, saying to them: "What Allah kills for you is better than what you slaughter with your knives!" Then Allah said: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾.

13811 – Yahya ibn Dawud al-Wasiti narrated to us, said: Ishaq ibn Yusuf al-Azraq narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Harun ibn ʿAntara, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The polytheists disputed with the Muslims, saying: "What is the matter with what Allah kills, that you do not eat it, while what you kill yourselves, you eat it! And you follow the command of Allah!" So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, and indeed it is fisq﴾, to the end of the verse.

13812 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, said: ʿUbayd Allah narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿And indeed, the devils inspire their allies﴾: They say: "What Allah slaughters, do not eat; what you slaughter yourselves, eat!" So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾.

13813 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, said: al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Yazid, from Ikrimah: Some polytheists entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Tell us about the sheep when it dies: who killed it?" He said: "Allah killed it." They said: "You claim that what you and your Companions kill is lawful, and what Allah kills is forbidden!" So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾.

13814 – Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-A'la narrated to us, said: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, from al-Hadrami: Some polytheists said: "As for what the falcon and the dog kill, you eat it; but what Allah kills, you do not eat!"

13815 – Al-Muthanna narrated to us, said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, said: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words: ﴿So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs﴾ [6:118]. He said: They said: "O Muhammad, as for what you kill and slaughter, you eat it; but what your Lord kills, you forbid!" So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, and indeed it is fisq, and indeed the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you, and if you obey them, indeed you are associators﴾ — that is, if you obey them in eating what I have forbidden you, then indeed you would be associators.

13816 – Al-Muthanna narrated to us, said: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, said: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: The polytheists said: "What you kill, you eat; and what your Lord kills, you do not eat!" So it was revealed: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾.

13817 – Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, said: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And if you obey them, indeed you are associators﴾: the saying of the polytheists: "As for what Allah slaughters = [i.e., carrion] = do not eat of it; but what you slaughter with your hands is lawful!"

13818 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, said: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

13819 – Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-A'la narrated to us, said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And indeed, the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you﴾, he said: The polytheists disputed with them concerning the slaughtered animal, saying: "What you kill with your hands, you eat; but what Allah kills, you do not eat!" They meant "carrion." So this was their disputation with them.

13820 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, said: Yazid narrated to us, said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, and indeed it is fisq﴾, the verse: meaning the enemy of Allah, Iblis, inspired to his allies from the people of misguidance, saying to them: "Dispute with the Companions of Muhammad concerning carrion, and say: 'What you slaughter and kill, you eat; but what Allah kills, you do not eat, while you claim that you follow the command of Allah!'" So Allah revealed to His Prophet: ﴿And if you obey them, indeed you are associators﴾. And by Allah, we do not know that there was ever shirk except in one of three ways: that one calls upon another god with Allah, or prostrates to other than Allah, or names the slaughtered animals for other than Allah.

13821 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾: The polytheists said to the Muslims: "How do you claim that you seek the pleasure of Allah, while what Allah slaughters you do not eat, and what you slaughter, you eat?" So Allah said: "If you obey them and eat carrion, indeed you are associators."

13822 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, said: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words: ﴿And indeed, the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you﴾, he said: They used to say: "What has the name of Allah been mentioned over and what you slaughter, eat!" So it was revealed: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, and indeed it is fisq, and indeed the devils inspire their allies﴾.

13823 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, said: Jarir narrated to us, from ʿAta', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾, to His words ﴿to dispute with you﴾, he said: He says: the devils inspire their allies: "You eat what you kill, and you do not eat what Allah kills!" He said: "Indeed what you kill has had the name of Allah mentioned over it, and what has died has not had the name of Allah mentioned over it."

13824 – It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak regarding His words: ﴿And indeed, the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you﴾: This concerns the matter of the slaughtered animal. He said: The polytheists said to the Muslims: "You claim that Allah has forbidden you carrion, and made lawful for you what you slaughter with your own hands, and forbidden you what He Himself slaughters for you? How is this, when you worship Him!" So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾, to His words ﴿are indeed associators﴾.

* *

Others said: Those who disputed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning this were a people from the Jews.

Those who said this:

13825 – Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-A'la and Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, both saying: ʿImran ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, from ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas. Ibn ʿAbd al-A'la said: "The Jews disputed with the Prophet ﷺ." Ibn Waki' said: "The Jews came to the Prophet ﷺ," and they said: "We eat what we kill, and we do not eat what Allah kills!" So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, and indeed it is fisq﴾.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings, in what is nearest to the truth, is to say: Allah informed that the devils inspire their allies to dispute with the believers concerning their prohibition of eating carrion, by what we have mentioned of their disputation with them. It is permissible that the inspirers were devils of mankind inspiring to their allies among them; and it is permissible that they were devils of the jinn who inspired to their allies from mankind; and it is permissible that both kinds cooperated in this, as Allah informed about both in another verse in which He says: ﴿And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy — devils of mankind and jinn, inspiring to one another ornate speech as deception﴾ [al-An'am 6:112]. Rather, that is the more predominant interpretation of it in my view, because Allah informed His Prophet that He had made for him enemies from the devils of the jinn and mankind, just as He had made for His prophets before him, some of them inspiring to others the adorned false sayings; then He informed him that those devils inspire to their allies from mankind to dispute with him and with those believers who followed him concerning what Allah has forbidden them of carrion.

* *

The interpreters differed concerning what Allah, may His praise be exalted, meant by His prohibition of eating that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned.

Some of them said: It is the slaughtered animals which the Arabs slaughtered for their gods.

Those who said this:

13826 – Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, both saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, who said: I said to ʿAta': What is His saying: ﴿So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned﴾? He said: He orders the mention of His name over drink, food, and slaughter. I said to ʿAta': Then what is His saying: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾? He said: He forbids the slaughtered animals which were in the pre-Islamic era offered to idols, which the Arabs and Quraysh used to slaughter.

* *

Others said: It is carrion. [[This heading, "Others said: It is carrion," is not in the manuscript, but its inclusion as in the printed edition is correct, God willing.]]

Those who said this:

13827 – Ibn Humayd and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾, he said: Carrion.

* *

Others said: Rather, what is meant by that is every slaughtered animal over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned.

Those who said this:

13828. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us: Abū Usāma narrated to us, from Jahīr ibn Yazīd, who said: Al-Ḥasan was asked. A man said to him: "I was brought a bird, a karā (a kind of bird)" [[In the printed edition it reads "bi-ṭayr kadhā", which is certainly an error. In the manuscript it reads "bi-ṭayr kadā" with a dāl, which has no meaning. The correct reading is what I have established: "karā" (with two fatḥas), the plural of "al-karawān", a bird between a hen and a pigeon, pleasant in voice, whose meat is eaten. The author of Lisān al-ʿArab mentions that it is called al-ḥajal and al-qabīḥ, but the correct view is that it is a kind of bird similar to it. When hunting it, one says to it: "Uṭruq karā, uṭruq karā, inna al-niʿām fī al-qurā", so it cowers and presses itself to the ground, and a garment is thrown over it and it is caught.]] Some of them were slaughtered with the name of God mentioned over them, and some of them were slaughtered without the name of God being mentioned over them, and the birds became mixed together. Al-Ḥasan said: "Eat it, eat it!" He said: And I asked Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, and he said: God says: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of God has not been mentioned﴾.
[[The report: Jahīr ibn Yazīd al-ʿAbdī narrated from Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra and Ibn Sīrīn; Abū Usāma, Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl and al-Qaʿnabī narrated from him. Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn and Ibn Ḥibbān and others deemed him reliable, and al-Bukhārī mentioned no criticism of him. He is biographed in Taʿjīl al-Manfaʿa: 74, al-Kabīr 1/2/253, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim 1/1/547. Ibn Ḥajar said: "Jahīr, in the diminutive form; it is said also to be on the pattern of ʿaẓīm."]]

13829. Al-Muthannā narrated to me: al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us: Ḥammād narrated to us, from Ayyūb and Hishām, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd al-Khaṭmī, who said: "Eat of the slaughter of the People of the Book and of the Muslims, but do not eat of that over which the name of God has not been mentioned."

13830. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, from Ashʿath, from Ibn Sīrīn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd, who said: "I used to sit with him in a circle, and there would sit in it some men of the Anṣār, of whom he was the head. Whenever a questioner came, he would ask him, and they would remain silent." He said: A man came to him and asked him, saying: "A man slaughtered and forgot to pronounce the name of God?" So he recited this verse: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of God has not been mentioned﴾, until he finished it.

* *

Abū Jaʿfar said: The correct statement on this matter is that it should be said: God meant by this that which is slaughtered for idols and deities, and that which dies, or which is slaughtered by one whose slaughter is not lawful.

As for the one who said: "He meant by this: what a Muslim slaughters, forgetting to mention the name of God," this is a view far from the truth, because of its rarity and its departure from what the proof has established by consensus as lawful, and this suffices as evidence of its corruption. We have already shown its corruption on the basis of analogy in our book entitled "Laṭīf al-Qawl fī Aḥkām Sharāʾiʿ al-Dīn," so that is sufficient and there is no need to repeat it here.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And indeed it is fisq﴾, it means: and indeed eating that over which the name of God has not been mentioned, and that which is dedicated to other than God, is fisq.

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of "fisq" in this place. [[See the explanation of "fisq" in the preceding linguistic indices, under (f-s-q).]]
Some of them said: its meaning is: disobedience.
So the interpretation of the statement according to this is: indeed eating that over which the name of God has not been mentioned is disobedience to God and sin.
Those who said this:
13831. Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me: my father narrated to me: my paternal uncle narrated to me: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed it is fisq﴾, he said: "fisq" is disobedience.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: disbelief.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire to their allies﴾, we have already mentioned the disagreement of those who differed concerning the referent of His saying: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire﴾, and the correct statement about it. As for their inspiring to their allies, it is their hinting to them at what they indicated to them, whether by speech, or by message, or by writing.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "wahy" (inspiration) earlier, in a way that suffices without repeating it here. [[See the explanation of "wahy" in the preceding volume 9: 399, note 3, and the references there.]]

And:
13832. Al-Muthannā narrated to me: Abū Ḥudhayfa narrated to us: ʿIkrima narrated to us, from Abū Zumayl, who said: "I was sitting with Ibn ʿAbbās when a man of his companions came to him and said: 'O Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Isḥāq claims that it was revealed to him last night!' — meaning al-Mukhtār ibn Abī ʿUbayd — so Ibn ʿAbbās said: 'He speaks the truth!' I was startled and said: 'Ibn ʿAbbās says "he speaks the truth"!' Ibn ʿAbbās said: 'There are two inspirations: the inspiration of God, and the inspiration of Satan. The inspiration of God came to Muḥammad, and the inspiration of the devils comes to their allies.' Then he recited: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire to their allies﴾."
[[The report: Abū Zumayl is Simāk ibn al-Walīd al-Ḥanafī; he narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, Mālik ibn Murthad and ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr. Shuʿba, Musʿar and ʿIkrima ibn ʿAmmār narrated from him. He is reliable; see Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr 2/2/174, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim 2/1/280.
Al-Mukhtār ibn Abī ʿUbayd ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī was a liar, a wicked pretender to prophethood, whom God killed at the hand of Muṣʿab ibn al-Zubayr and his companions in the year 67 AH. He has a long account containing his lies and what he did, and what people did to him.]]

* *

As for "the allies" (al-awliyāʾ), they are the helpers and supporters in this place. [[See the explanation of "walī" in the preceding volume 10: 497, note 5, and the references there.]]

* *

By His saying: ﴿to dispute with you﴾, He means: to argue with you, in the sense already mentioned earlier. [[See the explanation of "jidāl" in the preceding linguistic indices, under (j-d-l).]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if you obey them, indeed you are polytheists﴾, it means: if you obey them in eating carrion and what your Lord has forbidden to you; as:
13833. Al-Muthannā narrated to me: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us: Muʿāwiya narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿And if you obey them﴾, he says: if you obey them in eating what I have forbidden you.
13834. Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to me: Aḥmad ibn Mufaḍḍal narrated to us: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī: ﴿And if you obey them﴾, that is, you eat carrion.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿indeed you are polytheists﴾, it means: indeed you are then like them, since these people would eat carrion considering it lawful. So if you eat it in the same way, you have become like them, polytheists.

* *

Abū Jaʿfar said: The scholars differed concerning this verse: was any part of its ruling abrogated or not? Some of them said: nothing of it was abrogated, and it is muḥkam (unabrogated) regarding what it addresses. This is the view of the majority of scholars. [[See "al-Nāsikh wa'l-Mansūkh" by Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās (may God have mercy on him): 144, where he said: "In this surah, meaning Surat al-Anʿām, there is something that some people mentioned, which is apart from abrogation, but we mention it so that the book may be of general benefit..." Then he mentioned the verse and what was said about it, up to p. 146.]]

* *

It is related from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and ʿIkrima that:
13835. Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us: Yaḥyā ibn Wāḍiḥ narrated to us, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid, from Yazīd, from ʿIkrima and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, both said: ﴿So eat of that over which the name of God has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs. And do not eat of that over which the name of God has not been mentioned, and indeed it is fisq﴾, and it was abrogated, and an exception was made from this, when He said: ﴿The food of those who were given the Book is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them﴾ [Sūrat al-Mā'ida: 5].

* *

Abū Jaʿfar said: The correct statement on this matter in our view is that this verse is muḥkam in what it was revealed for, and nothing of it has been abrogated, and that the food of the People of the Book is lawful, and their slaughtered animals are dhakī (validly slaughtered). This is unconnected to what God forbade the believers to eat by His saying: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of God has not been mentioned﴾. For God only forbade us by this verse carrion and what is dedicated to the tyrants (ṭawāghīt), while the slaughtered animals of the People of the Book are dhakī, whether they mentioned God's name over them or not, because they are people of monotheism and possessors of Books of God, following their rulings, slaughtering animals according to their religions, just as a Muslim slaughters according to his religion, whether he mentions God's name over his slaughter or not. The exception is if the one who omitted mention of God's name over his slaughter does so out of adherence to a creed of denial or of worshipping something other than God; then his slaughter is forbidden, whether God's name was mentioned over it or not.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 122:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one whose likeness is in darkness, never to emerge from it?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This statement from Allah, majestic is His praise, indicates His prohibition to the believers in His Messenger at that time from obeying some of the polytheists who argued with them about eating carrion, based on what we have mentioned of their argument with them, and His command to them to obey a believer among them who had been an unbeliever, whom Allah, majestic is His praise, guided to his right course and granted success in faith. So He said to them: Is the obedience of one who was dead, meaning one who was an unbeliever, [to be preferred]? Allah, majestic is His praise, made him, by his turning away from obedience to Him, his ignorance of His oneness and the laws of His religion, and his abandonment of taking his share of work for Allah that would lead to his salvation, like the "dead" who benefits himself with no benefit and repels from himself no harm that befalls him. ﴿And We gave him life﴾, meaning: We guided him to Islam and revived him, so he came to know what harms and benefits himself, and works for his deliverance from the wrath and punishment of Allah in the Hereafter. Thus His seeing the truth, may He be exalted, after his blindness to it, and his knowledge of His oneness and the laws of His religion after his ignorance of that, became a life and a light by which he is guided, so that he walks on the straight path and the clear way among the people. ﴿Like one whose likeness is in darkness﴾, who does not know how to head or which path to take, because of the severe darkness of the night and the loss of the way. So likewise is this unbelieving, misguided person in the darknesses of disbelief, who sees no right guidance and knows no truth, meaning in the darknesses of disbelief. He says: Is the obedience of this one whom We have guided to the truth and granted insight into right guidance like the obedience of one whose likeness is that of someone who is in darkness, wandering, not knowing the way out of it, calling this one to forbid what Allah has forbidden and to permit what He has permitted, and to permit what Allah has forbidden and forbid what He has permitted?

* *

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning two specific men who were well known: one a believer and the other an unbeliever.

Then the people of interpretation differed concerning them.

Some of them said: As for the one who was dead and whom Allah gave life, it is Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him. And as for the one whose likeness is in darkness and never emerges from it, it is Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.

Mention of those who said this:

13836. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Abi Hawdhah informed us, from Shu'ayb al-Sarraj, from Abu Sinan, from al-Dahhak, concerning His saying: ﴿Or one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people﴾, he said: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him. ﴿Like one whose likeness is in darkness﴾, he said: Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.

[Note: Report 13836. Sulayman ibn Abi Hawdhah narrated from Hammad ibn Salamah, Abu Hilal al-Rasibi, and Amr ibn Abi Qays. Al-Bukhari mentioned no criticism of him, and Abu Zur'ah said: "Truthful, there is no harm in him." He is biographed in al-Kabir 2/2/42 and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/148. As for Shu'ayb al-Sarraj, I have not found any mention of him in the books available to me.]

* *

Others said: Rather, the dead one whom Allah gave life is Ammar ibn Yasir, may Allah have mercy on him. And as for the one whose likeness is in darkness and never emerges from it, it is Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.

Mention of those who said this:

13837. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Bishr ibn Tayym, from a man, from Ikrimah, concerning: ﴿Or one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning Ammar ibn Yasir.

[Note: Reports 13837 and 13838. Bishr ibn Tayym ibn Murrah, also said to be Bishir ibn Tayym ibn Murrah. He is in the first chain, between him and Ikrimah is "from a man." Al-Bukhari said in al-Kabir 1/2/96: "Bishir ibn Tayym ibn Murrah, from Ikrimah, related to us by al-Humaydi, from Ibn Uyaynah," a mursal report, and he mentioned no criticism of him, and he made him "Bishir." As for Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/372, he biographed him under "Bishir," as al-Bukhari said, and did not mention "Bishr," but he biographed him earlier at 1/1/352 under "Bishr ibn Tayym" and said: "Makki, narrated from him Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Uyaynah. I heard my father say that." Ibn Uyaynah says "Bishir." But here in the manuscript, in both places, it is "Bishr ibn Tayym," and in Ibn Uyaynah's narration it says "says," so I left what was in the manuscript as it stands, lest it appear to be a disagreement regarding Ibn Uyaynah.]

13838. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Ibn Uyaynah, from Bishr, from Tayym, from Ikrimah, concerning: ﴿Or one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people﴾: Ammar ibn Yasir. ﴿Like one whose likeness is in darkness﴾: Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.

[Note: Reports 13837 and 13838, the same note as above.]

* *

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said concerning the verse.

Mention of those who said this:

13839. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿Or one who was dead and We gave him life﴾, he said: astray, and We guided him. ﴿And made for him a light by which he walks among the people﴾, he said: guidance. ﴿Like one whose likeness is in darkness, never to emerge from it﴾, he said: in error forever.

13840. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Or one who was dead and We gave him life﴾, We guided him. ﴿And made for him a light by which he walks among the people, like one whose likeness is in darkness﴾, in error forever.

13841. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Mujahid: ﴿Or one who was dead and We gave him life﴾, he said: astray, and We guided him.

13842. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Or one who was dead and We gave him life﴾, meaning: one who was an unbeliever and We guided him. ﴿And made for him a light by which he walks among the people﴾, meaning by the light, the Qur'an, for whoever believes in it and acts upon it. ﴿Like one whose likeness is in darkness﴾, meaning by the darknesses, disbelief and error.

13843. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Or one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people﴾, he says: the guidance. "By which he walks among the people": he says: so he is the unbeliever whom Allah guides to Islam. He says: He was a polytheist and We guided him. ﴿Like one whose likeness is in darkness, never to emerge from it﴾.

13844. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Or one who was dead and We gave him life﴾, this is the believer who has with him from Allah a light and a clear proof, by which he acts and takes, and to which he returns: the Book of Allah. ﴿Like one whose likeness is in darkness, never to emerge from it﴾, and this is the likeness of the unbeliever in error, bewildered in it and wandering, finding no exit and no outlet.

13845. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Or one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people﴾, he says: whoever was an unbeliever, We made him a Muslim, and made for him a light by which he walks among the people, which is Islam. He says: this is like one who is in darkness, meaning: polytheism.

13846. Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿And made for him a light by which he walks among the people﴾: it is Islam to which Allah guided him. ﴿Like one whose likeness is in darkness﴾: he is not of the people of Islam. And he recited: ﴿Allah is the Guardian of those who believe; He brings them out of darknesses into light﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 257]. He said: The light by which one is illuminated in his house and sees, likewise the one to whom Allah has given this light, is illuminated by it in his religion and acts by its light, as the owner of this lamp is illuminated. He said: ﴿Like one whose likeness is in darkness﴾, he does not know what will come or what will befall him.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Thus has been made attractive to the disbelievers what they used to do﴾ [6:122].

Abu Ja'far said: His statement, may His remembrance be exalted, means: Just as I forsook this unbeliever who argues with you, O believers in Allah and His Messenger, concerning eating what I have forbidden you of foods, away from the truth, and made his evil deed seem good to him so that he saw it as good, so that he might deserve what I have prepared for him of painful punishment, likewise I made attractive to others of those who were upon the same disbelief in Allah and His signs what they used to do of disobedience to Allah, so that by their deeds they might deserve what they have with their Lord of retribution. [Note: For the explanation of "tazyin" (making attractive), see earlier: p. 37, note p. 1, and the references there.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: In this is the clearest proof against the claim of those who assert that Allah delegated affairs to His creatures in their actions, so that He has no hand in their deeds, [Note: "Al-Tafwid" (delegation) is the claim of the Qadariyyah, the Mu'tazilah, and the Imamiyyah among the sects, that the matter has been delegated to the servant, so that his will suffices to bring about his act, whether obedience or disobedience, and that he creates his acts. They are the ones who deny that the acts of servants are of Allah's creation. See what preceded at 1:162 note 3, and 11:340 note 2, and see what will come at p. 108 note 1.] and that He has equated all of them in the causes by which they reach obedience and disobedience. For if that were as they claim, He would have made attractive to His prophets and friends misguidance and disbelief, similar to what He made attractive to His enemies and the people of disbelief in Him, and made attractive to the people of disbelief in Him faith in Him, similar to what He made attractive to His prophets and friends. And in His informing, may He be exalted, that He made attractive to every doer among them his deed, there is an indication of the making attractive of disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience. He singled out His enemies and the people of disbelief with the making attractive of disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience to them, and made faith in Him and obedience hateful to them.

The commentary on the words of God, the Exalted: ﴿And thus We placed in every city its greatest criminals, so that they might scheme therein. Yet they scheme only against themselves, and they do not perceive.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His saying, glorified is His remembrance, means: Just as We made the disbelievers' deeds appear pleasing to them, so We have placed in every city its great ones, its criminals, meaning the people of associating partners with God and of disobedience to Him, ﴿so that they might scheme therein﴾, through deceptive speech or false action, against the religion of God and His prophets. ﴿Yet they scheme only against themselves﴾: that is, the evil of their scheming returns only upon themselves, because God, mighty and majestic, is behind their punishment for turning people away from His path. ﴿And they do not perceive﴾ means they do not know what painful punishment God has prepared for them, so they persist in their error and their defiance against God.

* *

The people of ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) have said similarly to what we have said on this.

Whoever said this:

13847: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿its greatest criminals﴾, he said: its great ones.

13848: al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

13849: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿its greatest criminals﴾, he said: its great ones.

13850: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Ikrimah: It was revealed concerning the mockers. Ibn Juraij said, from Amr, from Ata', from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿its greatest criminals﴾, up to His saying ﴿because of what they used to scheme﴾: against the religion of God, and against His Prophet, peace be upon him (ﷺ), and his believing servants.

* *

Al-akabir (the greatest ones) is the plural of akbar, just as al-afadil is the plural of afdal. If it were said that it is the plural of kabir, with akabir as its plural, that would be correct, because it may be said akbar, as in His saying: ﴿Say: Shall we inform you of the greatest losers in their deeds?﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 103], whose singular is al-khasir, it would be sound. It is reported from the Arabs by transmission that they say al-akabirah and al-asaghirah, and al-akabir and al-asaghir without the ta' marbutah, intending them as adjectives, as one says: "He is better than you" (afdal minka). The Arabs do the same with adjectives that come in the form af'al when they use them as nouns, such as their pluralizing of al-ahmar (the red) and al-aswad (the black) as al-ahamir and al-ahamirah, and al-asawid and al-asawidah. From this is the saying of the poet:

Indeed, the three reds have destroyed my wealth,
and I was formerly devoted to them.
Wine, and fat meat is their condiment,
and saffron. I will not go out (to my wife) except perfumed with saffron-stains.

[Footnote: This is al-A'sha. Its verses appear in his Diwan, pages 247 and 248, and they are in my photographed copy of the Diwan of al-A'sha, number 29, and in Lisan al-Arab (h-m-r), and it is the beginning of the poem. In the printed edition here it read: "al-samin adimuhu" and "fa-lan azal mubaqqa'an", and I have adopted what is in the manuscript and in the manuscript of al-A'sha: "al-samin, wa-utli bi'l-za'faran wa-qad urawwih mubaqqa'an".

Thus it came in the manuscript: "al-samin idamuhu". Al-idam is what one eats with bread, whatever it may be.

The attribution of idam to meat is strange. It is also narrated as "adimuhu", vocalized in Lisan with an initial fatha on the alif, and that is not accepted; rather the correct reading, God willing, is "adimuhu", from "adama al-shay'", when one prolongs its duration and continues with it.

Abu Ja'far's version here is "fa-lan urawwih mubaqqa'an", and the version in the manuscript of his Diwan is "wa-qad urawwih mubaqqa'an", which is the better of the two. Al-mubaqqa' is one in whom there is a color different from his own, or the color of what water or saffron or similar things have touched. The meaning is that he uses a great deal of saffron until it leaves a sheen on his skin. The Arabs used saffron most in their weddings: when a man married, he would apply saffron. So this was used as a metaphor for the frequency of his marriages.

There are other versions of this verse; consult them in the margins of his Diwan, in its appendix.]

* *

As for al-makr (scheming), it is deception and trickery against the one deceived, through treachery, so that the schemer may bring upon him some hateful matter.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿When a sign comes to them, they say: "We will not believe until we are given the like of what was given to the messengers of God. God knows best where to place His message."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: When these polytheists, who dispute with the believers using ornamented speech concerning what God has forbidden them, in order to turn people away from the path of God, are presented with ﴿a sign﴾, meaning a proof from God for the truth of what Muhammad brought from God and its reality [[See the explanation of "āyah" (sign) in the earlier language indices, under (ʾ-y-y).]], they say to the Prophet of God and his companions: ﴿We will not believe﴾, meaning they say: "We will not accept what Muhammad ﷺ calls us to believe in, nor what he brought of forbidding what he claims God has forbidden us." ﴿Until we are given﴾, meaning: they say, "until God gives us miracles like those He gave Moses, such as splitting the sea, and Jesus, such as raising the dead and healing the blind and the leper." [[See the explanation of "al-ītāʾ" (giving) in the earlier language indices, under (ʾ-t-y).]] God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿God knows best where to place His message﴾, meaning by this, may His praise be exalted, that the signs of the prophets and messengers will not be given except to a sent messenger from among mankind, and those who equate their Lord with idols and images are not among them, so they would be given them. He, may His praise be exalted, says: "I know best the places of My messages and who is fit for them. So it is not for you, O polytheists, to choose this over Me, for choosing the messenger is the affair of the One who sends, not of the one to whom he is sent, and God knows best where to place His messages when He sends one."

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Those who committed crimes will suffer humiliation before God and a severe punishment for what they used to scheme﴾ (124).

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, teaching him what He will do to these rebels against him: "will befall", O Muhammad [[See the explanation of "al-iṣābah" (befalling) in the earlier volume, 11:170, note 2, and the references there.]], those who earned sin by associating others with God and worshipping other than Him. ﴿Humiliation﴾, meaning abasement and disgrace, as related:

13851- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿will befall those who committed crimes, humiliation before God﴾, he said: "Al-ṣighār" is abasement.

* *

It is a verbal noun from the speaker's saying: "ṣaghira yaṣghar ṣaghāran wa ṣagha√an," and it is the most intense form of humiliation.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿humiliation before God﴾, its meaning is: humiliation from God will befall them, like the speaker's saying: "My provision will come to me from God," meaning: from God, intending by it: what is mine with God will come to me. It is not permissible for one who says "humiliation from God will befall them" to say "I came before ʿAbd Allāh" meaning "I came from ʿAbd Allāh," because the meaning of "humiliation will befall them before God" is: what is with God of abasement will befall them, because of their denial of His messenger. So that is not analogous to "I came from ʿAbd Allāh." [[See al-Farrāʾ's Maʿānī al-Qurʾān 1:253; and the explanation of "ʿinda" (before/with) in the earlier volumes: 2:501, 7:490, 8:555.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and a severe punishment for what they used to scheme﴾, it means: these deniers of God and His messenger, who consider lawful what God forbade them, such as carrion, will suffer, alongside the humiliation, a severe punishment, for what they used to plot against Islam and its people through disputing with falsehood and ornamented speech, deceiving the people of God's religion and obedience to Him. [[See the explanation of "al-makr" (scheming) earlier, p. 95.]]

* *

At this point ends a section of the old division from which our copy was transcribed, and in it there is what follows:

"Followed by the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Whomever God wills to guide, He opens his breast to Islam﴾."

May God bless Muhammad the Prophet, and his family and companions, abundantly. Then there follows the text: "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. My Lord, make it easy" (*rabbi yassir*).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 125 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Allah, may He be remembered, says: Whomever Allah wills to guide, that he believe in Him, in His Messenger, and in what he brought from his Lord, and grant him success in it [[See the explanation of "guidance" (al-huda) in the earlier word index of the language (h-d-y).]] = ﴿He expands his breast to Islam﴾. He means: He widens his breast for that, makes it easy for him, and facilitates it for him, by His kindness and His help, until Islam shines in his heart, illuminates for him, and his breast becomes wide to accept it. This is like the report transmitted from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which is:

13852 - Sawwar ibn Abd Allah al-Anbari told us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman told us, saying: I heard my father narrate, from Abd Allah ibn Murra, from Abu Ja'far, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾, they said: How is the breast expanded? He said: When light descends into the heart, the breast expands and widens. They said: Is there a sign by which one may know it? He said: Yes, turning to the abode of eternity, withdrawing from the abode of delusion, and preparing for death before it overtakes you. [[The report 13852: "Abd Allah ibn Murra" is so written in the manuscript, the printed edition, and the Tafsir of Ibn Kathir, but I find it unlikely for several reasons.
First, I find it unlikely that he is "Abd Allah ibn Murra al-Kharifi," who narrates from Ibn Umar, Masruq, and Abu Kathif, and from whom al-A'mash and Mansur narrate. He is biographically recorded in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/165, and he is trustworthy.
Second, al-Tabari transmitted this report through several chains, numbered 13853 and 13854, and they all revolve around "Amr ibn Murra."
Third, it will become clear later who "Abu Ja'far" is who transmitted this report, and it is mentioned there that "Amr ibn Murra" narrated from him, without mentioning "Abd Allah ibn Murra."
For this reason I incline to think the correct form is "Abu Abd Allah ibn Murra" or "Abu Abd Allah Amr ibn Murra," and it fell out through the copyists.
As for "Abu Ja'far," around whom this report revolves, he is described in report 13854 as "a man called Abu Ja'far, who used to live in al-Mada'in." Then another description appears in al-Suyuti's takhrij of this report in al-Durr al-Manthur, where he said: "a man from the Banu Hashim, and he is not Muhammad ibn Ali," meaning al-Baqir.
I first paused at this "Abu Ja'far" and thought he was unknown, because I found no mention of him in anything before me among the books. But when I came to report 13856, narrated through "Khalid ibn Abi Karima, from Abd Allah ibn al-Musawwar," it became clear to me with certainty that this "Abu Ja'far" who lived in al-Mada'in, and who was from the Banu Hashim, is himself "Abd Allah ibn al-Musawwar," from whom report 13856 is narrated.
Thus, he is "Abu Ja'far": "Abd Allah ibn al-Musawwar ibn Awn ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Talib," "Abu Ja'far al-Hashimi al-Mada'ini." Amr ibn Murra and Khalid ibn Abi Karima narrated from him. He is biographically recorded in Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/169, Tarikh Baghdad 10:17, Mizan al-I'tidal of al-Dhahabi 2:78, and Lisan al-Mizan 3:360. Al-Khatib said: "He lived in al-Mada'in and narrated there from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya," and he mentioned in some of the chains he cited for his reports: "from Khalid ibn Abi Karima (who is the one coming in report 13856), from Abu Ja'far, who is Abd Allah ibn al-Musawwar, a man from the Banu Hashim, who lived in al-Mada'in."
And "Abu Ja'far," "Abd Allah ibn al-Musawwar," is weak and a liar. Jarir ibn Ruqba said: "Abu Ja'far al-Hashimi al-Mada'ini used to fabricate sayings that were true words from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they got mixed with the hadiths of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and people accepted them." And from Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal: "My father said: Abu Ja'far al-Mada'ini, his name is Abd Allah ibn al-Musawwar ibn Awn ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Talib. My father said: Strike out his hadith; he used to fabricate hadith and lie, and I have abandoned his hadith. And Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi would not narrate from him to us." Ibn Abi Hatim said: "I asked my father about Ja'far al-Hashimi, and he said: The Hashimis do not know him, and he is weak in hadith; he narrates mursal reports for which no origin is found among the hadiths of the trustworthy."
Thus, the reports from 13852 to 13854, and 13856, are defective, weak, and feeble reports, as you see.
These three reports, 13852 to 13854, are mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 3:394, 395, and al-Suyuti takhrraj them in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:44, and attributed the report to Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd, Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shayba, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat.
Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir 3:395, after mentioning these reports and the report of Mas'ud that Abu Ja'far narrated as 13855 and 13857: "These are chains for this hadith, mursal and muttasil, which strengthen one another, and Allah knows best."
The hafiz erred greatly, as you see, for the hadith of Abu Ja'far al-Hashimi is the hadith of a liar and fabricator that strengthens nothing and is not strengthened by anything!! Written by Mahmud Muhammad Shakir.]]

13853 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Amr ibn Qays, from Amr ibn Murra, from Abu Ja'far, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: Which of the believers is most intelligent? He said: The one who remembers death most, and is best prepared for what comes after it. He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about this verse: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾. They said: How is his breast expanded, O Messenger of Allah? He said: A light is cast into it, so it expands and widens. They said: Is there any sign by which it is known? He said: "Turning to the abode of eternity, withdrawing from the abode of delusion, and preparing for death before death."

13854 - Hannad told us, saying: Qabisa told us, from Sufyan, from Amr ibn Murra, from a man called "Abu Ja'far," who used to live in al-Mada'in, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about his saying: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾. He said: A light is cast into the heart, so it expands and widens. They said: O Messenger of Allah, is there a sign by which it is known? = Then he mentioned the rest of the hadith similarly. [[The two reports 13853 and 13854 are two weak hadiths, as was previously explained in the note on the earlier report.
And "Amr ibn Murra al-Muradi" is trustworthy and reliable. He has passed many times, the last being number 12396.]]

13855 - Hilal ibn al-Ala' told me, saying: Sa'id ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Waqid al-Harrani told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salama told us, from Abu Abd al-Rahim, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa, from Amr ibn Murra, from Abu Ubayda, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: It was said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when this verse was revealed: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾: He said: When the light enters the heart, it expands and widens. They said: Is there any sign by which it is known? He said: Turning to the abode of eternity, withdrawing from the abode of delusion, and preparing for death before death. [[The report 13855: "Hilal ibn al-Ala' ibn Hilal al-Bahili al-Raqqi," the teacher of Abu Ja'far, has passed under number 4964, and he is truthful, though spoken of.
In the printed edition it appears as "Muhammad ibn al-Ala'," which has no basis here. In the manuscript it reads "li'alli ibn al-Ala'," undotted, as if it were read "Ya'la ibn al-Ala'," but I did not find anyone by that name among Abu Ja'far's teachers or among the narrators. I saw Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 3:395 quoting this place from Ibn Jarir as saying: "Hilal ibn al-Ala' told me, Sa'id ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Waqid told us," which supports that the manuscript's reading is probably a distortion, and therefore I have adopted what is in Ibn Kathir: "Hilal ibn al-Ala'."
"Sa'id ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Waqid al-Harrani": weak; Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Daraqutni weakened him, and al-Daraqutni said: "He is not to be used as proof." Abu Hatim said: "They speak of him; it is said that he took books of Muhammad ibn Salama and narrated from them. I saw in what he narrated falsehoods; he lied." Biographically recorded in Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/45, Mizan al-I'tidal 1:387, and Lisan al-Mizan 3:37.
"Muhammad ibn Salama al-Harrani": trustworthy, passed under number 175.
"Abu Abd al-Rahim" is "Khalid ibn Abi Yazid al-Harrani," whose nephew "Muhammad ibn Salama al-Harrani" narrated from him; he is good in hadith and precise. His mention has passed in the note on report number 8396.
"Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa al-Jazari": trustworthy, passed under numbers 4964 and 8396.
"Amr ibn Murra al-Muradi": has passed just above under numbers 13853 and 13854.
"Abu Ubayda" is "Abu Ubayda ibn Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud," who has passed many, many times, and he did not hear from his father, as has been explained many times before.
This is also a weak report, due to the weakness of the hadiths of "Sa'id ibn Waqid al-Harrani" from "Muhammad ibn Salama," as Abu Hatim mentioned.
Then, because Abu Ubayda did not hear from his father Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud. The report of Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud will come under number 13857 by another route. So it is strange of Ibn Kathir: how can these be connected hadiths, and then how do the reports of a liar and fabricator strengthen them? See what I have already set forth in the note on number 13852.]]

13856 - Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' al-Razi told me, saying: Sufyan ibn Uyayna told us, from Khalid ibn Abi Karima, from Abd Allah ibn al-Musawwar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾, then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: When the light enters the heart, it expands and widens. They said: O Messenger of Allah, is there any sign by which it is recognized? He said: Yes, turning to the abode of eternity, withdrawing from the abode of delusion, and preparing for death before the arrival of death. [[The report 13856: "Khalid ibn Abi Karima al-Asbahani" and "Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Iskaf" was declared trustworthy by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and Abu Hatim, and Ibn Hibban said "he errs," and Ibn Ma'in weakened him. Biographically recorded in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/154, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/349. Al-Bukhari said: "From Mu'awiya ibn Qurra, and Abu Ja'far Abd Allah ibn Maswar al-Maswari," and he did not mention any criticism of him.
"Abd Allah ibn Maswar ibn Awn ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Talib al-Hashimi al-Mada'ini" has passed under number 13852, and that he is the "Abu Ja'far" al-Mada'ini, and that he is a liar and fabricator. See the takhrij of the report and the commentary on it there.]]

13857 - Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz told me, saying: Mahbub ibn al-Hasan al-Hashimi told us, from Yunus, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Utba, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾. They said: O Messenger of Allah, how is his breast expanded? He said: The light enters into it and it widens. They said: Is there any sign of that, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Withdrawing from the abode of delusion, turning to the abode of eternity, and preparing for death before death comes down. [[The report 13857: "Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz," the teacher of al-Tabari, is "Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz," passed under numbers 157, 1999, 2056, 5419, 6822.
"Mahbub ibn al-Hasan al-Hashimi al-Basri": "Mahbub" is a nickname, by which he is better known, and his name is "Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Hilal ibn Abi Zaynab Fayruz al-Qurashi," a client of the Banu Hashim. Trustworthy, though some weakened him. Biographically recorded in al-Tahdhib and al-Kabir 1/1/67, under "Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Basri," and Ibn Abi Hatim under "Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Basri" 3/2/228, then under "Mahbub ibn al-Hasan ibn Hilal" 4/1/388, and he did not indicate that his name is "Muhammad ibn al-Hasan."
"Yunus" is "Yunus ibn Ubayd ibn Dinar al-Abdi," trustworthy, passed under numbers 2616, 4931, 10574.
"Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Utba": this is a very serious difficulty, for "Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Utba ibn Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud" is very late; he narrated from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i and his generation, and died in the year 160 or 165. And "Yunus ibn Ubayd" is of a higher generation than him; he narrated from Ibrahim al-Taymi, al-Hasan al-Basri, and Ibn Sirin, and died in the year 140, so he is in the generation of his teachers. So if Yunus had narrated from him, he would have mentioned such in the biography of "Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Utba."
I incline to think the correct chain is: "from Yunus, from Abu Abd al-Rahman Abd Allah ibn Utba."
That is "Abd Allah ibn Utba ibn Mas'ud al-Hudhali," whose kunya is "Abu Abd al-Rahman," who narrates from his paternal uncle "Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud," and was born in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) and saw him, and died in the year 74. He is the one most fitting for Yunus ibn Ubayd to narrate from.
This is also a weak report, due to the weakness of "Mahbub ibn al-Hasan," and so everything the hafiz Ibn Kathir said, that these reports came with chains mursal and muttasil strengthening one another, is a statement negated by the analysis of these chains as you have seen. And Allah is the one who grants success to the truth. Written by Mahmud Muhammad Shakir.]]

And the people of interpretation have said in accordance with what we have said regarding that.

Mention of those who said that:

13859 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾: As for "He expands his breast to Islam," He widens his breast for Islam. [[In the numbering I skipped number 13858: an error.]]

13860 - al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾: with "There is no god but Allah."

13861 - al-Muthanna told me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, a reading: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾: with "There is no god but Allah," He makes for it in his breast a spaciousness.

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And whomever He wills to lead astray, He makes his breast constricted, tight﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may He be remembered, says: Whomever Allah wills to lead astray from the path of guidance, He occupies him with his disbelief and turns him away from His path, and makes his breast, by His forsaking him and the domination of disbelief over him, [[In the printed edition: "to occupy him with his disbelief ... makes his breast," the latter without a waw; in the manuscript as I have recorded it, and without a waw before "makes his breast," and the context requires what I have recorded.]] tight. [[See the explanation of "misguidance" (al-idlal) in the earlier word index of the language (d-l-l).]]

* *

And "al-haraj" is the utmost constriction, the kind that cannot penetrate, from the intensity of its tightness, [[In the printed edition: "does not penetrate," and I have kept what is in the manuscript. That is the correct reading.]] and here it is the breast to which admonition does not reach, and into which the light of faith does not enter, because of the rust of polytheism upon it. Its origin is from "al-haraj," and "al-haraj" is the plural of "haraja," which is a tree intertwined by trees, into whose midst nothing can enter because of the intensity of its interlacing, [[See the explanation of "al-haraj" in the earlier part, 8:518 / 10:85.]] as:

13862 - al-Muthanna told me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal told us, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Ammar, a man from the people of Yemen, told us, from Abu al-Salt al-Thaqafi: that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah have mercy on him, recited this verse: ﴿And whomever He wills to lead astray, He makes his breast constricted, tight﴾ with the "ra'" vowelled with a fatha. He said: And some of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who were with him recited: "dayyiqan harijan" with a kasra. Safwan said: Then Umar said: Find me a man from Kinana and make him a shepherd, [[His saying: "make him a shepherd," meaning seek him out, and let him be a shepherd, not in the sense of "making" as "appointing." This is an ancient Arabic usage of "ja'ala," but they did not mention it in the dictionaries; it is common in the speech of the Arabs, and this is one of its witnesses, so let it be noted in its place in the books of Arabic.]] and let him be from the Mudlij. [[Mudlij is a tribe from the Banu Murra ibn Abd Manat ibn Kinana, and they are the famous "qafa" (trackers). This report indicates that their pasture land was abundant in trees.]] He said: So they brought him to him. Umar said to him: O young man, what is the "haraja"? He said: The "haraja," among us, is a tree that is among trees, which neither a shepherdess nor a wild animal nor anything can reach. He said: Umar said: Thus is the heart of the hypocrite, to which nothing of good reaches. [[The report 13862: "Abd Allah ibn Ammar al-Yamami," Ibn Abi Hatim said: "unknown," and Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy. Biographically recorded in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/129.]]

And Abu al-Salt al-Thaqafi transmitted from Umar, and Abdullah ibn Ammar al-Yamami transmitted this report from him. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, in al-Bukhari's al-Kuna (no. 44), and in Ibn Abi Hatim (4/2/394).

This is a very rare report, concerning the transmission and explanation of lexical usage, and the questioning of Bedouins and herdsmen about it.

13863. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And whoever Allah wills to lead astray, He makes his breast constricted and tight﴾: he said: whoever Allah wills to lead astray, his breast is constricted for him until Islam becomes tight upon him, though Islam is spacious. This is what He means when He says: ﴿And He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾ [al-Hajj 22:78], meaning: He has not placed upon you any constriction in Islam.

* * *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: its meaning is "doubting."
Those who said this:

13864. Imran ibn Musa related to us, saying: Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id related to us, saying: Humayd related to us, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿constricted and tight﴾: he said: doubting.

13865. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿constricted and tight﴾: as for "tight," it means doubting.

* * *

Others said: its meaning is "entangled/confused" (multabisan).
Those who said this:

13866. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿makes his breast constricted and tight﴾: he said: constricted, entangled.

13867. Abd al-Warith ibn Abd al-Samad related to us, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from al-Hasan, from Qatadah, that he used to read ﴿đayyiqan harajan﴾ and say: entangled.

* * *

Others said: its meaning is that, because of the extreme constriction, faith cannot reach him.
Those who said this:

13868. Ibn Wakie related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Habib ibn Abi Amra, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿makes his breast constricted and tight﴾: he said: he finds no path except that which is steep (ṣu'udan).

13869. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Ata al-Khurasani, regarding ﴿constricted and tight﴾: he said: there is no outlet for good in it.

13870. al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ma'mar, from Ata al-Khurasani, the like of it.

13871. al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, his statement: ﴿And whoever Allah wills to lead astray, He makes his breast constricted and tight﴾, [so that] "There is no god but Allah" finds no place to enter his breast.

13872. al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, in a reading, regarding His statement: ﴿And whoever Allah wills to lead astray, He makes his breast constricted﴾, [so that] "There is no god but Allah" — until you cannot make it enter.

* * *

The readers (al-qurra') differed regarding the reading of this.

Some of them read: ﴿đayyiqan harajan﴾, with a fatha on the ḥā' and the rā' in ﴿ḥarajan﴾, and this is the reading of most of the Meccans and Iraqis, meaning the plural of "ḥarajah," as I have described. [See pp. 103, 104.]

* * *

And the majority of the readers of Medina read: "ḍayyiqan ḥarijan," with a fatha on the ḥā' and a kasra on the rā'.

* * *

Then those who read it differed about its meaning.

Some of them said: it has the meaning of "al-ḥaraj" [the same]. They said: "al-ḥaraj" with fatha on the ḥā' and rā', and "al-ḥarij" with fatha on the ḥā' and kasra on the rā', have one meaning, and they are two well-known dialects, like "al-danaf" and "al-danif," "al-waḥad" and "al-waḥid," "al-fard" and "al-farid."

* * *

Others among them said: rather, it means sin (al-ithm), from their saying: "So-and-so is sinful and ḥarij," and it is reported from the Arabs by hearing from them: "ḥarij 'alayka ẓulmī" [my wrongdoing is a burden upon you], meaning: constriction and sin. [See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 353, 354.]

Abu Ja'far said: my view on this is that they are two well-known readings and two widely attested dialects with one meaning, and whichever of them the reader recites, he is correct, because their meanings agree. This is like what we have mentioned from the reports from the Arabs regarding "al-waḥad" and "al-fard," with fatha on the ḥā' of "al-waḥad" and the rā' of "al-fard," and with kasra on them, with one meaning.

* * *

As for "al-ḍayyiq," most readers have a fatha on its ḍād and a shadda on its yā', except that some Meccans read it as "ḍayqan," with a fatha on the ḍād and a sukun on the yā', without the shadda.

For this sukun there are two possible explanations:
One: that he made it sukun while intending the sense of vocalization and gemination, as it is said: "hayn layn," meaning: hayyin layyin [easy, gentle].
The other: that he made it sukun in the form of the verbal noun (maṣdar), from their saying: "This matter became tight (ḍāqa) and constricted (yaḍīqu) ḍayqan," as Ru'ba said:

"We have known, at every tight, hard situation, with a face of the matter, or constricted."

And from this is the saying of God: ﴿And do not be in constriction because of what they plot﴾ [al-Nahl 16:127]. Ru'ba also said: "And the drought (al-lawḥ) wasted her with a hardship that is tight (ḍayq)," meaning: constricted. It is reported from al-Kisa'i that he used to say: "al-ḍayq" with a kasra, in livelihood and in place, and in the matter, "al-ḍayq" [with fatha].

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: in this verse there is the clearest of clarifications for whoever is granted success in understanding it, that the cause by which one arrives at faith and obedience is other than the cause by which one arrives at disbelief and disobedience, and that both causes are from Allah. [This is a refutation of the Mu'tazilah; see what has passed, p. 92, note 3, and it is among the best refutations of the Mu'tazilite claim.] That is because Allah, majestic is His praise, informed about Himself that He expands the breast of whomever He wills to guide to Islam, and makes the breast of whomever He wills to lead astray constricted from Islam, tight, as if he were climbing into the sky. It is known that expanding the breast for faith is the opposite of constricting it, and that if arrival at faith were caused by constriction of the breast from faith, there would be no difference between constricting it from faith and expanding it for faith, and whoever had his breast constricted from faith would have had it expanded for it, and whoever had it expanded for it would have been constricted from it, since each of the constriction and the expansion — I mean constriction and expansion — would be connected to what the other is connected to. If that were so, it would necessarily follow that Allah expanded Abu Jahl's breast for belief in Him, and constricted the breast of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from it. This view is among the greatest disbelief in Allah. In the corruption of this being so is clear evidence that the cause by which the believers believed in Allah and His messengers, and by which the obedient obeyed Him, is other than the cause by which the disbelievers disbelieved in Allah and the disobedient disobeyed Him, and that both causes are from Allah and in His hand, because He, majestic is His praise, informed that He is the one who expands the breast of this believer for faith when He wills his guidance, and constricts the breast of this disbeliever from it when He wills his misguidance.

* * *

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His statement: ﴿As if he were climbing up into the sky﴾

Abu Ja'far said: this is a parable from Allah, dhikruh exalted, struck for the heart of this disbeliever in the extremity of its constriction, [making it impossible] for it to reach it, like his refusal to ascend into the sky and his inability to do so, because that is not within his capacity.

* * *

Those of the people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.
Those who said this:

13873. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Ata al-Khurasani, regarding ﴿as if he were climbing up into the sky﴾: he says: his likeness is like that of one who cannot climb into the sky.

13874. al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ma'mar, from Ata al-Khurasani, the like of it.

13875. And with this same chain: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, in a reading: "makes his breast constricted and tight," [so that] "There is no god but Allah" — until you cannot make it enter, "as if he were climbing up into the sky," from the extremity of that upon him.

13876. al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, the like of it.

13877. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿as if he were climbing up into the sky﴾: from the constriction of his breast.

* * *

The readers differed regarding the reading of this.

The majority of the readers of Medina and Iraq read: ﴿ka-annamā yaṣṣaʿʿadu﴾, meaning "yataṣaʿʿadu" [he is making himself climb], and they assimilated the tā' into the ṣād, which is why they doubled the ṣād.

* * *

Some Kufans read it: "yaṣṣāʿadu," meaning "yataṣāʿadu" [he is making himself climb], and assimilated the tā' into the ṣād and made it a doubled ṣād.

* * *

Some Meccan readers read it: "ka-annamā yaṣʿadu," from "ṣaʿida yaṣʿadu" [he climbs].

* * *

All these readings are close in meaning, and whichever of them the reader recites, he is correct. However, I prefer the reading of those who read ﴿ka-annamā yaṣṣaʿʿadu﴾, with the ṣād doubled and without an alif, meaning "yataṣaʿʿadu" [he is making himself climb], because of the large number of readers who recite it thus, [see the explanation of "al-ṣuʿūd" in what has passed, vols. 7: 299-302,] and because of the saying of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him: "Nothing has made me climb (taṣaʿʿadanī) as the wedding sermon has made me climb (taṣaʿʿadatnī)."

* * *

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His statement: ﴿Thus Allah places filth upon those who do not believe﴾ [al-An'am 6:125]

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, dhikruh exalted, says: just as Allah makes the breast of the one He wills to lead astray constricted and tight, as if he were climbing into the sky because of his constriction from faith, so He recompenses him for that. Likewise, Allah empowers Satan over him and over those like him who refuse faith in Allah and His messenger, so he misleads him and turns him away from the path of truth.

* * *

The people of interpretation have differed regarding the meaning of "al-rijs" [filth].

Some of them said: it is everything that has no good in it.
Those who said this:

13878. Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "al-rijs" is what has no good in it.

13879. al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shabl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Allah places the filth upon those who do not believe﴾: he said: what has no good in it.

* * *

Others said: "al-rijs" is the punishment.
Those who said this:

13880. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding ﴿Thus Allah places the filth upon those who do not believe﴾: he said: "al-rijs" is the punishment of Allah.

* * *

Others said: "al-rijs" is Satan.
Those who said this:

13881. al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, his statement: ﴿al-rijs﴾ — he said: Satan.

* * *

Some of the Kufan scholars of Arabic dialects used to say: "al-rijs" and "al-najs" are two dialects, and it is reported from the Arabs that they say: "mā kāna rijsan" [it was not filth], and "laqad rajusa rajāsatan" and "najusa najāsatan" [he became filthy].

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: "al-rijs" and "al-rijz" are the same, and both mean punishment. [See Abu Ubaydah's Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 206, for this is his statement.]

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: the correct view on this, in my opinion, is what Ibn Abbas said, and whoever says that "al-rijs" and "al-najs" are one and the same is supported by the report transmitted from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he used to say when entering the privy: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the filthy, the impure, the wicked, the evil one, the accursed Satan." [Abu Ubayd said: "al-khabīth" is one who is wicked in himself, and "al-mukhbith" (with kasra on the bā') is one whose companions and helpers are wicked. It is like their saying: "So-and-so is weak (ḍaʿīf) and makes others weak (muḍʿif), and strong (qawī) and makes others strong (muqwī)": the strong one is strong in his body, and the one made strong is one whose animal is strong. He means: it is the one who teaches them wickedness and brings them into it.]

13882. Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Bakhtari al-Ta'i related this to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi related to us, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, from al-Hasan and Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ. [The report 13882: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Bakhtari al-Ta'i is a teacher of Abu Ja'far, and I have found no mention of him in the books available to me, and I fear there may be an error in his name. Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi has passed many times, the last being no. 10339. Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Makki al-Basri has passed as nos. 5417 and 8811. This chain is sound, but I have not found this report in the hadith of Anas, in the Musnad or elsewhere, and I found it in this wording in the hadith of Abu Umamah with a weak chain, through Yahya ibn Ayyub, from Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr, from Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah; Ibn Majah related it in his Sunan, p. 109, no. 299. Ibn Hibban said: "When a chain contains Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr and Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, that is among what their hands have produced!"]

* * *

This report makes clear that "al-rijs" is "al-najs," the filth that has no good in it, and that it is a quality of Satan.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 6, Verse 126**

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And this is the path of your Lord, straight. We have detailed the verses for a people who remember.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "This which We have made clear to you, O Muhammad, in this surah and in other surahs of the Qur'an, is the path of your Lord," meaning: the way of your Lord and His religion, which He has approved for Himself as a religion and made straight, with no crookedness in it. [[See the explanation of "al-Sirat al-Mustaqim" (the straight path) in what has preceded, 10:146, note 2, and the references there.]] So persist in it, forbid what He has forbidden you, and permit what He has permitted you, for We have made clear the signs and proofs of the truth and soundness of that. [[See the explanation of "fassala" (to detail) in what has preceded, p. 69, note 2, and the references there. And the explanation of "ayah" (sign) in what has preceded, in the language indexes (ayy).]] ﴿for a people who remember﴾ means: for those who remember the signs and lessons by which God has argued against them, so that they take heed by them. [[See the explanation of "al-tadhakkur" (remembrance) in what has preceded, in the language indexes (dhakar).]] He specified "those who remember" because they are the people of discernment and understanding, and the possessors of intellect and virtue. It was also said: "yadhdhakarun" ........................ [[In the printed edition it reads "fa-qila yadhdhakarun" (then it was said: yadhdhakarun), and in the manuscript: "wa-qila yadhdhakarun" (and it was said: yadhdhakarun), as if he intended to write something and then broke off.
