Perhaps he intended to indicate the assimilation of the taa' into the dhaal in "yatadhakkarun," and then it dropped out from him or from the copyist, so dots were placed for it, although its omission does no harm.]]

* *

Those of interpretation said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

13883. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And this is the path of your Lord, straight﴾, he meant by it Islam.

**The discussion on the interpretation of His words: ﴿For them is the Abode of Peace with their Lord, and He is their Protector because of what they used to do﴾ (6:127)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words "for them" (*lahum*), may His remembrance be exalted, He means the people who call to mind the signs of God and take lessons from them, and who are certain of their indication of what they point to: the oneness of God, the prophethood of His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and other things. They affirm what they have reached knowledge of through them.

* *

As for "the Abode of Peace" (*dar al-salam*), it is the abode of God which He has prepared for His friends (*awliya'*) in the Hereafter, as a recompense for what they endured in this world for the sake of God. It is His Garden. And "al-Salam" is one of the names of God, the Exalted [see the explanation of "al-Salam" in what has preceded, 10:145 / 11:392], as al-Suddi said:

13884 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿For them is the Abode of Peace with their Lord﴾: God is al-Salam, and the Abode is the Garden.

* *

As for His words ﴿and He is their Protector﴾, He means: God is the helper of these people who call to mind the signs of God [see the explanation of "wali" in what has preceded in the language indexes, root w-l-y]. ﴿because of what they used to do﴾ means: as a recompense for what they used to do of obedience to God, seeking His good pleasure.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 128:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, ﴿And the day He gathers them all, [saying], "O company of jinn, you have taken much of mankind"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, ﴿And the day He gathers them all﴾, may He be exalted in remembrance, He means: and the day He gathers these who associate others with God, [worshipping] idols and statues and others among the polytheists, together with their allies among the devils, who used to inspire to them ornate speech as deception, to dispute by it with the believers; so He gathers them all together at the standing place of the Resurrection [[See the explanation of "gathering" (al-hashr) above, p. 50, note 1, and the references there.]] — He says to the jinn: ﴿O company of jinn, you have taken much of mankind﴾. The words "He says to the jinn" have been omitted from the speech, being sufficiently indicated by what appears of the speech.

* *

By His saying, ﴿You have taken much of mankind﴾, He means: you have taken much of them by misguiding and seducing them, as:

13885 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And the day He gathers them all, [saying], "O company of jinn, you have taken much of mankind"﴾, meaning: you have misled many of them.

13886 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿O company of jinn, you have taken much of mankind﴾, he said: You have misled many of mankind.

13887 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding the saying of God: ﴿You have taken much of mankind﴾, he said: Those whom you have led astray have increased.

13888 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

13889 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Abu Sufyan related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan: ﴿You have taken much of mankind﴾, he says: You have misled many of mankind.

* *

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And their allies from mankind will say, "Our Lord, some of us have enjoyed others"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May He be exalted in remembrance, says: So the allies of the jinn from mankind will answer and say: "Our Lord, some of us have enjoyed others" in the world. [[See the explanation of "enjoyment" (al-istimta') above, vol. 8, p. 175, note 1, and the references there.]] As for the enjoyment of mankind from the jinn, it was as follows:

13890 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj regarding His saying: ﴿Our Lord, some of us have enjoyed others﴾, he said: A man in the Jahiliyyah would alight in a land and say: "I seek refuge with the chief of this valley," and that was their enjoyment; so they will make excuses on the Day of Resurrection.

* *

= As for the enjoyment of the jinn from mankind, it was, as has been mentioned, what the jinn gained from mankind of their exalting them in seeking refuge with them, so they would say: "We have become masters of the jinn and the Hinn" [[In the printed edition: "We have become masters of the jinn and the mankind", differing from what is in the manuscript, which its editor misread because it is undotted. I have adopted what is in the manuscript. "Al-Hinn" (with a kasra on the ha') is a tribe among the tribes of the jinn; its explanation has been given earlier in vol. 1, p. 455, note 1, so refer to it there. See also al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 354, which agrees with the printed text.]]

* *

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And we have reached our term which You appointed for us﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May He be exalted in remembrance, says: They said: We have reached the time which You appointed for our death. [[See the explanation of "term" (al-ajal) above, vol. 11, p. 259, note 1, and the references there.]] By this, may His majesty be praised, He means only that they said: some of us enjoyed others during the days of our life until the state of our death. As:

13891 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: As for His saying: ﴿And we have reached our term which You appointed for us﴾, it is death.

* *

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying: ﴿He will say, "The Fire is your abode, wherein you will abide eternally, except what God wills. Indeed your Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing"﴾ (128)

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from God, may He be exalted in remembrance, of what He will say to those whom He gathers on the Day of Resurrection from among those who associated others with Him in the world, idols, and their jinn companions. He expressed the report of what will occur in the form of a report of what had occurred, because the preceding speech had the same meaning and intent. So He said: God said to the allies of the jinn from mankind, whose report has already preceded concerning them: ﴿The Fire is your abode﴾, meaning the Fire of Hell, ="your abode", where you will dwell, i.e., remain.

* *

"Al-mathwa" is the "maf'al" form from their saying, "Such-and-such a person dwelt (thawa) in such-and-such a place," when he remained in it. [[See the explanation of "al-mathwa" above, vol. 7, p. 279.]]

= ﴿Abiding therein eternally﴾, i.e., remaining therein. = ﴿Except what God wills﴾, meaning except what God wills of the length of the period between their being raised from their graves and their going to Hell; that is the period which God excepted from their eternal abiding in the Fire. = ﴿Indeed your Lord is All-Wise﴾, in His management of His creation, and in His turning them from state to state according to His will, and other of His acts. = ﴿All-Knowing﴾, of the outcomes of His management of them, and what their affair will come to, of good and evil. [[See the explanation of "All-Wise" and "All-Knowing" above, in the glossaries of language under (ḥ-k-m) and (ʿ-l-m).]]

* *

It has been related from Ibn 'Abbas that he would interpret this exception as meaning that God placed the matter of these people, in the extent of His punishment of them, under His will.

13892 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿He will say, "The Fire is your abode, wherein you will abide eternally, except what God wills. Indeed your Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing"﴾, he said: This verse is a verse which it is not fitting for anyone to pass judgment upon God in His creation, that He does not cause them to descend into Paradise or into Fire. [[In the printed edition: "that He does not cause them to descend" with an added "that", which corrupts the meaning until it contradicts itself. Rather, his words "does not cause them to descend into Paradise or Fire" are a prohibition to people from saying "So-and-so is in Paradise" or "So-and-so is in the Fire." "Yunzilahum" is jussive in the lam, by the prohibitive particle.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 129:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others, because of what they used to earn﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters differed regarding the interpretation of ﴿nuwalli﴾.

Some of them said: its meaning is: We make some of them allies (waliyy) of others, in disbelief in God.

Those who said this:

13893. Yunus related to us, saying: Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others, because of what they used to earn﴾. Indeed, God makes people allies of one another according to their deeds: the believer is the ally (waliyy) of the believer wherever he is and wherever he may be, and the disbeliever is the ally of the disbeliever wherever he is and wherever he may be. Faith is not by wishful thinking nor by adornment.

* *

Others said: its meaning is: We cause some of them to follow others in the Fire, from "al-muwalah" (following), which is the continuation between one thing and another, from the saying of the speaker: "I made one thing follow another (walaytu bayna kadha wa kadha)," when I made them follow one another.

Those who said this:

13894. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others﴾, in the Fire, they follow one another. [See the explanation of "wala" in the earlier indexes of linguistic terms, under (w-l-y).]

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: We give some of the oppressors power over others.

Those who said this:

13895. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others﴾, he said: the wrongdoers among the jinn and the wrongdoers among mankind. And he recited: ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is his companion﴾ [Surah al-Zukhruf: 36]. He said: We empower the oppressive jinn over the oppressive humans.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions regarding the interpretation of that is the saying of the one who said: its meaning is: "And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others." This is because God mentioned before this verse what the polytheists said, when He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿And their allies from among mankind will say: Our Lord, we enjoyed one another﴾. He, may His praise be exalted, informed that some of them are allies of others, then followed that report with His report that their alliance with one another is by His making them allies, so He said: Just as We made some of these polytheists, from the jinn and mankind, allies of others, enjoying one another, so likewise We make some of them allies of others in all matters, "because of what they used to earn," from the disobedience to God and what they practice. [See the explanation of "al-kasb" (earning) in the earlier passages: 11:448, note 1, and the references there.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 130:

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿O assembly of jinn and humankind! Did there not come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My signs and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is information from God, may His praise be mentioned, about what He will say on the Day of Resurrection to those among the polytheists of humankind and jinn who associated others with Him. He informs that He, may His remembrance be exalted, will say to them on that day: ﴿O assembly of jinn and humankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you relating to you My signs?﴾ meaning: they will inform you of what was revealed to them of My admonishing you concerning the places of My proofs, My making known to you My evidences for My oneness, the confirmation of My prophets, acting upon My command, and ceasing at My limits. ﴿And warning you of the meeting of this your day﴾ meaning: they will warn you of the encounter with My punishment on this your day, and of My retribution for your disobedience to Me, so that you would desist from My disobedience. [See the explanation of "warning" (al-indhar) in the earlier indexes of linguistic terms, under (n-dh-r).]

This is a rebuke and reproach from God, may His praise be mentioned, to these disbelievers for the sinful deeds and disobedience they committed in the world. Its meaning: Messengers from among you have already come to you, drawing your attention to the error of what you were upon, establishing the conclusive proofs, and warning you of God's threat for your persistence in what you were persisting upon. Yet you did not accept that, you did not remember, and you did not take heed.

* *

The interpreters differed over "the jinn": whether messengers were sent to them from among themselves or not.

Some of them said: Messengers were indeed sent to them, just as messengers were sent to humankind from among them.

Those who said this:

13896 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: al-Dahhak was asked about the jinn: Was there a prophet among them before the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent? He said: Have you not heard God's saying: ﴿O assembly of jinn and humankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you relating to you My signs?﴾ Does He mean by this: messengers from humankind and messengers from the jinn? They said: Yes!

* *

Others said: No messenger was sent to them from among the jinn, and there was never a sent messenger from the jinn at all; the messengers are from humankind only, while from the jinn there are only warners (nudhur). They said: God said, "Did there not come to you messengers from among you," and messengers are from one of the two groups, as He said: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting together﴾ [Surah al-Rahman: 19], then said: ﴿from them come forth the pearl and the coral﴾ [Surah al-Rahman: 22]. Pearl and coral only come out of the salt water, not the fresh of the two; the meaning is: they come forth from one of them, or from one of them only. [This is the view of al-Farra', see Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 354, and it is evident that what follows is also from al-Farra' but from another place than this one.] He said: This is like the speaker saying to a group of houses, "Indeed in these houses is evil," though the evil is in only one of them; the report is made about all of them while it is meant about some of them. And like saying, "I ate bread and milk," when they are mixed; if one said, "I ate milk," the speech would be wrong, because milk is drunk and not eaten.

Those who said this:

13897 - al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj concerning His saying: ﴿O assembly of jinn and humankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you﴾, he said: He gathered them together as He gathered in His saying: ﴿and from both you eat tender flesh and extract ornaments you wear﴾ [Surah Fatir: 12], while ornaments are not extracted from the rivers. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: They are the jinn who met their people, and they were messengers to their people.

* *

According to this saying of Ibn Abbas, that among the jinn there were messengers to their people, the interpretation of the verse on this interpretation which Ibn Abbas adopted is: Did there not come to you, O jinn and humankind, messengers from among you? As for the messengers of humankind, they are messengers from God to them; and as for the messengers of the jinn, they are messengers of God's messengers from the sons of Adam, and they are those who, when they heard the Qur'an, turned back to their people as warners. [Read the verses of Surah al-Ahqaf: 29–32.]

* *

As for those who held the view of al-Dahhak, they said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, informed that among the jinn there were messengers sent to them, just as He informed that among humankind there were messengers sent to them. They said: If it were permissible for His report concerning the messengers of the jinn to mean that they were messengers of humankind, it would be permissible for His report concerning the messengers of humankind to mean that they were messengers of the jinn. [He means by this that the warners who went back to their people, if it were permissible for them to be called "messengers" sent by humankind to the jinn, it would be permissible to call "messengers of humankind" — who are God's messengers to humankind and the jinn — "messengers of the jinn," sent by the jinn to humankind. This is evidently false.] They said: In the corruption of this meaning there is evidence that both reports mean that they are messengers of God, because that is what is well known in address, and not otherwise.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿They will say: We bear witness against ourselves, and the life of this world deceived them, and they will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers﴾ (130)

Abu Ja'far said: This is information from God, may His praise be mentioned, about the saying of the polytheists of the jinn and humankind when He rebukes them with His saying to them: ﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among you relating to you My signs and warning you of the meeting of this your day?﴾ that they will say it: ﴿We bear witness against ourselves﴾ that Your messengers came to us with Your signs, and warned us of the meeting of this our day, but we denied them and rejected their message, and we did not follow Your signs nor believe in them.

God said, as a report beginning: The idols and images, and their allies among the jinn, deceived these people who associated others with God — ﴿the life of the world﴾, meaning: the adornment of the life of the world, and the seeking of leadership in it and rivalry over it, so that they would not submit to God's command to obey His messengers in it. So they were arrogant, and they were a haughty people. He suffices by mentioning "the life of the world" from mentioning the other meanings by which they were deceived and beguiled, since mention of it suffices in place of mention of others, the context indicating what has been omitted. God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And they bear witness against themselves﴾, meaning: these associators on the Day of Resurrection, that they were disbelievers in Him and His messengers in the world, so that God's proof against them is complete by their acknowledgment against themselves of what necessitates His punishment and His painful torment.

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying: ﴿That is because your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly while their people are unaware﴾ (131)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿That is because your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly﴾, meaning: We sent the messengers, O Muhammad, to those whose condition I have described and whose news I have informed you of, from among the polytheists of mankind and jinn, reciting My verses to them and warning them of the meeting of their return to Me, because your Lord would not destroy the towns unjustly.

* *

In the interpretation of His saying "unjustly," two meanings are possible:

The first: ﴿That is because your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly﴾, meaning: by the polytheism of those who associated partners with Allah, and the disbelief of those among their people who disbelieved, as Luqman said: ﴿Indeed, associating others with Allah is a great injustice﴾ [Surah Luqman: 13]. ﴿And their people are unaware﴾, meaning: He would not punish them suddenly until He sent to them messengers to alert them to the proofs of Allah against them, and to warn them of the punishment of Allah on the Day of their return to Him, and He would not seize them while heedless, so that they could say: "No bringer of good news or warner came to us."

* *

The second: ﴿That is because your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly﴾, meaning: He would not destroy them without alerting and reminding them through messengers, signs and lessons, thereby wronging them, and Allah is not unjust to His servants.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the two views in my opinion is the first: that its meaning is that He would not destroy them for their polytheism without sending messengers to them and establishing the proof between Him and them. This is because His saying ﴿That is because your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly﴾ follows His saying ﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among you, reciting to you My verses?﴾, and so this is clear evidence that the sense of His saying ﴿That is because your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly﴾ is: We did that because We do not destroy towns without reminder and warning. [See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:355; this is a refutation of al-Farra', who holds the second view.]

* *

As for His saying ﴿That﴾, it may be in the accusative, meaning: We did that; and it may be in the nominative, as a beginning (mubtada'), as if he said: "That is so."

* *

As for "an" (that), it is in the accusative position, meaning: We did that because your Lord would not destroy the towns. When the preposition that governed it is removed, the verb attached to it takes the accusative. [See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:355.]

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿And for each there are degrees according to what they have done, and your Lord is not unaware of what they do﴾ (6:132).

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: For every doer, whether in obedience to God or in disobedience, there are ranks and levels according to his deed, which God will cause him to attain and reward him with: if it is good, then good, and if it is evil, then evil. [[See the explanation of "darajah" (degree) above: 11:505, note 1, and the references there.]] = ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what they do﴾. He, exalted is His praise, says: All of that of their deeds, O Muhammad, is with knowledge from your Lord, who counts it and records it for them with Him, so that He may recompense them for it when they meet Him and return to Him.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And your Lord is the Self-Sufficient, the Possessor of mercy. If He wills, He can eliminate you and replace you with whom He wills after you, just as He produced you from the descendants of another people.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, says: "And your Lord" — O Muhammad — who commanded His servants with what He commanded them, forbade them from what He forbade them, rewarded them for obedience, and punished them for disobedience, "is the Self-Sufficient" (al-Ghani), free of His servants whom He commanded with what He commanded and forbade from what He forbade, and free of their deeds and their worship of Him, while they are the ones in need of Him, for in His hand is their life and death, their provision and sustenance, their benefit and harm. [[See the explanation of "al-Ghina" (self-sufficiency) above: 5:521, 570 / 9:296.]] He, dhikruhu be exalted, says: I did not create them, O Muhammad, nor did I command them with what I commanded you, nor forbid them from what I forbade you, out of any need I have for them or for their deeds, but so that I may bestow favor upon them by My mercy and reward them for their good deeds if they do good, for I am the Possessor of compassion and mercy. [[See the explanation of "al-Rahma" (mercy) in the preceding lexical indexes (r-h-m).]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿If He wills, He can eliminate you and replace you with whom He wills after you﴾, He says: If your Lord, O Muhammad, who created His creation without any need for them or for their obedience to Him, wills — ﴿He can eliminate you﴾, meaning: He can destroy these creatures of His whom He created from the offspring of Adam [[See the explanation of "al-Idhhab" (eliminating) above: 9:298.]] — ﴿and replace you with whom He wills after you﴾, meaning: and bring others besides you, and peoples other than you, who will succeed you on the earth — ﴿after you﴾, meaning: after your passing away and your destruction — ﴿just as He produced you from the descendants of another people﴾, meaning: just as He brought you into being and originated you after other creatures who were before you.

* *

The meaning of "min" (from) in this place is that of substitution, as one says in speech: "I gave you a garment from your dinar," meaning: a garment in place of the dinar, not that the garment is a part of the dinar. Likewise, those addressed by His saying ﴿just as He produced you﴾ — this report does not mean that they were produced from the loins of another people; rather, the meaning is what we have mentioned: that they were brought into being in place of a creation that succeeded another people who had perished before them.

* *

And "al-dhurriyya" is on the pattern "fu'lliyya," from the saying of the speaker: "dhara'a Allah al-khalq" (God created the creation), meaning He created them; "fahuwa yadhrauhum." Then the hamza was dropped and it was said "dhara Allah," then the form "fu'lliyya" was derived without hamza, on the pattern of "al-'ubbiyya." [[In the printed edition: "al-'ulliyya," which is an error, since this is with a kasra on the ayn. In the manuscript: "al-'ulmah," undotted, and I have read it as such. In a hadith: "Indeed God has removed from you the 'ubbiyya of the Jahiliyya and its pride in ancestors," and "al-'ubbiyya" is the boastfulness and arrogance and conceit of the Jahiliyya. It is said to derive from "al-ta'biyya," and some said it is on the pattern "fu'ulla," and it is permissible that it be "fi'lliyya," as this speaker said regarding "dhurriyya." See the root ('-b-b) in Lisan al-'Arab.]]

* *

It has been related from some of the earlier scholars that he used to recite: "min dhurrai'ati qawmin akharin" on the pattern of "fu'ayyila." [[In the manuscript: "min dhurriyya," as the previous recitation, but it is evident that what is in the printed edition is correct, because "dhurriyya" originally was "dhurri'a," from "dhara'a Allah al-khalq," so it should have been hamzated; it became frequent, so the hamza was dropped, and the Arabs left off its hamza. See Lisan al-'Arab (dh-r-'a).]]

* *

And from another that he used to recite: "wa-min dhirriyyati," on the pattern of "'iliyya."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The reading upon which the reciters in the cities agree is ﴿dhurriyyati﴾ with a damma on the dhal and a shadda on the ya, on the pattern of "'ubbiyya." [[See the preceding note No. 1. In the printed edition here too it reads "'iliyya," and likewise in the manuscript; the preferred correct reading is what I have established.]]

* *

We have already explained its derivation earlier, in a manner sufficient to avoid repeating it here. [[See the explanation of "al-dhurriyya" above: 3:19, 73 / 5:543 / 6:327; he did not explain it in these places, then explained it at 6:362 / 8:19 / 11:507.]]

* *

The root of "al-inshā'" (producing/bringing into being) is "al-ihdath" (originating). It is said: "So-and-so began (anshaa) to speak to the people," meaning he started and took up in it. [[See the explanation of "al-inshā'" above: 11:263, 264, 562.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 134:

The explanation of His words: ﴿Indeed, what you are promised is coming, and you cannot escape it.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He who mentions this to the polytheists: O you who ascribe equals to God, the idols and the images, indeed what your Lord promises you of His punishment, because of your persistence in your disbelief, will befall you, and ﴿you cannot escape it﴾. That is, you will not be able to frustrate your Lord by fleeing from Him on the earth so as to escape Him, for wherever you are, you are in His grip, and He is able to punish you for your disobedience to Him. That is to say: so beware of Him, and turn in repentance to His obedience, before the calamity descends upon you.

* *

The explanation of His words: ﴿Say: O my people, act according to your standing; indeed I am acting, so you will come to know.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His mention, speaking to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Say," O Muhammad, to your people from Quraysh who set up another god alongside God: ﴿Act according to your standing﴾, that is, act according to your position and your situation. As related:

13898 - Ali ibn Dawud related to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿O my people, act according to your standing﴾, meaning: according to your situation.

* *

It is said of it: "He acts according to his standing (makanah) and his position (makinah)."

* *

Some of the Kufans recited it as "ʿalā makānātikum" (ﻋَﻠَﻰ مَكَانَاتِكُمْ), as the plural of "makānah."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: And the reading upon which the readers of the major cities agree is ﴿ʿalā makānatikum﴾, in the singular.

* *

= ﴿Indeed I am acting﴾, He, exalted be His praise, says to His Prophet: Say to them: Act as you are acting, for I am acting what I am commanded to do by my Lord = ﴿so you will come to know﴾, that is: you will come to know, when the vengeance of God descends upon you, which of us was in the right in his action and upon the path of right guidance, I or you.

His words, exalted is His mention, to His Prophet: Say to your people: ﴿O my people, act according to your standing﴾, are a command from Him to him to threaten and warn them, not a permission for them to do whatever acts of disobedience to God they wish.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 135:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Whoever will have the good outcome of the abode. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, ﴿Whoever will have the good outcome of the abode﴾, and ﴿so you will soon know﴾, O disbelievers in God, at the moment you witness the punishment, who among us and among you will have the good outcome of the abode. [[See the explanation of "al-'aqibah" (outcome) in what has passed, 11:272, 273.]] He means: who is it whose worldly life brings him, in consequence, something better or worse than it, according to the good or evil deeds he sent ahead in it. [[In the printed edition: "who is it whose worldly life brings (yu'qibu) him," and what is in the manuscript is the correct reading.]]

Then, may His praise be exalted, He began the statement, saying: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾. He means: indeed, whoever acts contrary to what God commanded him to do in the world does not prosper nor win his need with God. [[See the explanation of "al-falah" (success) in what has passed, 11:296, note 5, and the references there.]] This is the meaning of "the wrongdoer does wrong" (zulm al-zalim) in this place. [[See the explanation of "al-zulm" (wrongdoing) in what has passed in the language indices, under (z-l-m).]]

* *

As for the "man" (min) in His saying ﴿Whoever will have﴾, it has two grammatical possibilities (i'rab):

= The nominative (raf'), as the subject of a new clause (ibtida', the inchoative).

= The accusative (nasb), governed by His saying ﴿you will know﴾, the verb "knowing" ('ilm) operating on it.

The nominative is better, because its meaning is: "so you will soon know which of us will have the good outcome of the abode?" Thus treating "man" as the subject of a new clause is more sound and more eloquent than having "knowing" govern it. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:355.]]

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And they assign to God a share of what He has created of the tilth and the cattle, and they say, "This is for God," by their claim, and "This is for our associates." So what is for their associates does not reach God, but what is for God reaches their associates. Evil is what they judge.﴾ (6:136)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: And those who equate their Lord with others have assigned to their Lord the idols and images — ﴿of what He has created﴾, meaning, of what He has created of the tilth and the cattle.

* *

It is said of this: "God created the creatures, He creates them (yadhra'uhum) in creation (dhar'an), and (dharwan)," [[The manuscript also has "wa-dharwan," as if it means the softening of the hamza. I have not found this mentioned in the sources of this verb, and I do not think he intended "wa-dhar'an," since no one has mentioned that.]] when He created them.

* *

"A share" (nasiban) means a portion and a part. [[See the explanation of "nasib" above, 9:324, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed concerning the nature of the share that they assigned to God, and that which they assigned to their associates, the idols and the devil.

Some of them said: That was a part of their tilth and cattle which they set apart (yufrizunahu) for this, [[In the printed edition: "yaqrunahu"; in the manuscript: "yafarrirun," not fully pointed, and the correct reading is what I have established. "Farraztu al-shay'" and "afraztuhu" mean that I separated it from other things and distinguished it. "Al-firz" (with a kasra and a sukun): the share set apart for its owner, whether one or two.]] and another part for this.

Mention of those who said that:

13899 - Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Habib ibn al-Shahid narrated to me, saying: Attab ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Khusayf, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿So what is for their associates does not reach God﴾, the verse. He said: When they brought in the food and made it into sheaves, they set aside for God a portion and a portion for their gods. When the wind blew from the direction of what they had set aside for their gods toward what they had set aside for God, they returned it to what they had set aside for their gods. And when the wind blew from the direction of what they had set aside for God toward what they had set aside for their gods, they left it and did not return it. That is His saying: ﴿Evil is what they judge.﴾

13900 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And they assign to God of what He has created of the tilth and the cattle a share, and they say, "This is for God, by their claim, and this is for our associates."﴾ He said: They assigned to God a share of their produce and their property, and to the devil and the idols a share. If something fell from the produce of what they assigned to God into the share of the devil, they left it. And if something fell from what they assigned to the devil into the share of God, they gathered it, preserved it, and returned it to the share of the devil. If the water burst from the irrigation (siqy) of what they assigned to God into the share of the devil, they left it. [[Al-siqy (with a kasra and a sukun in the sin, and a qaf): drinking, and al-shirb (with a kasra and a sukun): the watering place like a channel, by which the crops are irrigated.]] And if the water burst from the irrigation of what they assigned to the devil into the share of God, they blocked it. This is what they assigned from the tilth and irrigation. As for what they assigned to the devil from the cattle, it is the saying of God: ﴿God did not ordain any baheerah, sa'ibah, wasilah, or ham﴾ [Surat al-Ma'idah: 103].

13901 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And they assign to God of what He has created of the tilth and the cattle a share, and they say, "This is for God, by their claim,"﴾ the verse. That was because the enemies of God, when they cultivated a field, or had produce, set aside for God a part of it and for the idol a part. What was of field, produce, or any share of the idols, they guarded and counted. If something fell from it into what was named for God, they returned it to what they had set aside for the idol. If the water overtook them to what they had set aside for the idol and irrigated something they had set aside for God, they made that for the idol. And if something of the field and produce that they had set aside for God fell and mixed with what they had set aside for the idol, they said, "This is poor," and did not return it to what they had set aside for God. And if the water that they had set aside for God overtook what was named for the idol, they left it for the idol. They used to forbid from their cattle the baheerah, the sa'ibah, the wasilah, and the ham, and they would assign them to the idols, while claiming that they forbade them for God. So God said concerning that: ﴿And they assign to God of what He has created of the tilth and the cattle a share﴾, the verse.

13902 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning the saying of God: ﴿And they assign to God of the tilth and the cattle a share﴾. He said: They designate for God a part of the field, and for their associates and idols a part. What the wind carries away of what they designated for God into the part of their idols, they leave. And what goes from the part of their idols into the part of God, they return, saying, "God is free of this!" And "the cattle" are the sa'ibah and the baheerah that they named.

13903 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

13904 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: ﴿And they assign to God of what He has created of the tilth and the cattle a share﴾, the verse. Some people of misguidance deliberately set aside for God a part of their fields and livestock, and a part for their associates. When something of what they set aside for God mixed with what they set aside for their associates, they left it. But when something of what they set aside for their associates mixed with what they set aside for God, they returned it to their associates. And when a year of drought struck them, they used what they had set aside for God and left what they had set aside for their associates. God said: ﴿Evil is what they judge.﴾

13905 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And they assign to God of what He has created of the tilth and the cattle a share﴾. He said: They used to set aside a portion of their wealth, saying, "This is for God, and this is for the idols" which they worship. When a camel of what they had set aside for their associates went missing and mixed with what they had set aside for God, they returned it. And if something of what they had set aside for God went missing and mixed with something of what they had set aside for their associates, they left it. And if a year of drought struck them, they ate what they had set aside for God and left what they had set aside for their associates. So God said: ﴿Evil is what they judge.﴾

13906 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And they assign to God of what He has created of the tilth and the cattle a share﴾ to ﴿they judge﴾. He said: They used to apportion a portion of their wealth and designate it for God, and sow a crop and designate it for God, and they designated for their gods the like of that. What came out for the gods they spent on them, and what came out for God they gave in charity. When what they did for their associates perished and what was for God increased, they said, "Our gods must have provision," and they took what was for God and spent it on their gods. And when what was for God became barren and what was for their gods increased, they said, "If He wished, He would have purified what is His!" And they did not return anything of what was for the gods. God said: "Even if they were truthful in what they apportioned, it would be a terrible judgment for them to take from Me and not give Me." That is when He says: ﴿Evil is what they judge.﴾

* *

Others said: The "share" that they used to assign to God, from which something reached their associates, was that they would not eat what they slaughtered for God until they mentioned the names of the gods, and what they slaughtered for the gods they would eat without mentioning God's name over it.

Mention of those who said that:

13907 - Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿And they assign to God of what He has created of the tilth and the cattle a share﴾, until: ﴿And what is for God reaches their associates﴾. He said: Everything they assigned to God of slaughter that they slaughtered [[Al-dhibh (with a kasra and a sukun): it is the slaughtered animal, and al-madhbuh, and it is everything prepared for slaughter of sacrificial animals and other animals.]] they would never eat until they mentioned the names of the gods with it. And what was for the gods, they did not mention God's name with it. And he recited the verse until: ﴿Evil is what they judge.﴾

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two interpretations of the verse is what Ibn Abbas said and whoever said the like of his saying on that, because God, exalted is His praise, informed that they had assigned to God a determined portion of their tilth and cattle, and said, "This is for God," and assigned its like to their associates, who are their idols, by consensus of the people of interpretation, and said, "This is for our associates." And the share of their associates does not reach God, meaning: it does not reach the share of God, and what is for God reaches the share of their associates. For if the arrival of that were by naming and by leaving the naming, then the very things which God informed did not arrive would be permissible to have arrived, and what He informed had arrived would not have arrived. And that contradicts what the apparent meaning of the speech indicates, because of two slaughtered animals, one is slaughtered for God and the other for the gods; it is permissible that their meats had mixed, and they mixed them, since what was hateful to them was mentioning God's name over what was slaughtered for the gods, not the mixing of the bodies and their joining to one another.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, it is an informing by God, exalted is His praise, about the deed of these polytheists whose attribute He described. He, exalted is His praise, says: They have indeed done evil in their judgment, [[See the explanation of "sa'a" above in the indexes of language (s-w-')—and the explanation of "yahkum" above in the indexes of language (h-k-m).]] in that they took from my share for their associates, and did not give me from the share of their associates. He, exalted is His mention, meant by this an informing of their ignorance and misguidance, and their departure from the path of truth, in that they were not content to equate with the One who created them and provided for them, and bestowed upon them blessings that cannot be counted, that which neither harms them nor benefits them, until they preferred it in their divisions in their own estimation by apportioning to it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 137:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And thus their partners have made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children, to ruin them and to confuse them regarding their religion. And had Allah willed, they would not have done so. So leave them and what they invent.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: Just as the partners of these people who equate others with their Lord, the idols and images, made attractive to them what they made attractive, namely their assigning to their Lord a portion of their wealth, by their claim, and their leaving what reached the portion they had designated for Allah to go to the portion of their partners in their division, and their returning what reached the portion they had designated for their partners to the portion of Allah's share, to the portion of their partners— ﴿thus their partners have made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children﴾, from among the devils, so they made attractive to them the burying of daughters alive [[See the explanation of "zayyana" (made attractive) earlier, p. 92, note 2, and the references there.]] — ﴿to ruin them﴾, meaning: to destroy them — ﴿and to confuse them regarding their religion﴾, they did that to them, to mix up their religion for them so that it becomes confused, so they go astray and perish, by their act of doing what Allah has forbidden them [[See the explanation of "al-labs" (confusion) earlier, vol. 11, p. 492, note 1, and the references there.]] — ﴿And had Allah willed that they not do what they were doing of killing them, they would not have done it,﴾ by His guiding them to the truth and granting them success in rectitude, so they would not kill them. But Allah forsook them from right guidance, so they killed their children and obeyed the devils who misled them.

Allah says to His Prophet, threatening them for their grave fabrication against their Lord concerning what they used to say about the shares they allotted, "This is for Allah and this is for our partners," and concerning their killing of their children: ﴿So leave them﴾, O Muhammad, [[See the explanation of "dhar" (leave) earlier, p. 72, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿and what they invent﴾, what they fabricate against Me of lies and falsehood [[See the explanation of "al-iftira'" (fabrication) earlier, p. 57, note 2, and the references there.]], for I am lying in wait for them, and behind them is the punishment and retribution.

* *

And the people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

13908- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿And thus their partners have made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children, to ruin them﴾, they made attractive to them the killing of their children.

13909- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding the words of Allah: ﴿the killing of their children, their partners﴾, their devils, who command them to bury their children alive for fear of poverty. [[al-'Ayla (with fatha and sukun), poverty and severe need.]]

13910- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

13911- Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿And thus their partners have made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children﴾, the verse, he said: Their partners made that attractive to them = ﴿And had your Lord willed, they would not have done it, so leave them and what they invent.﴾

13912- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿And thus their partners have made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children﴾, he said: Their devils whom they worshipped made attractive to them the killing of their children.

13913- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufadal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And thus their partners have made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children, to ruin them﴾, the devils commanded them to kill the daughters. As for ﴿to ruin them﴾, it means: to destroy them. As for ﴿to confuse them regarding their religion﴾, it means: to mix up their religion for them.

* *

The readers differed regarding the recitation of this.

The reciters of the Hijaz and Iraq recited it: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ زَيَّنَ لِكَثِيرٍ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ قَتْلَ أَوْلادِهِمْ شُرَكَاؤُهُمْ﴾, with fatha on the zay of "zayyana", "qatla" in the accusative, and "shuraka'uhum" in the nominative, meaning that the partners of these polytheists, who made attractive to them the killing of their children, are the ones who made it attractive; so they make "the partners" nominative as the agent of their verb, and make "the killing" accusative because it is the object.

* *

Some of the reciters of the people of Syria recited it: "وَكَذَلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِكَثِيرٍ مِنَ المُشْرِكِينَ قَتْلُ أَوْلادَهُمْ شُرَكَائِهِمْ" with damma on the zay, "qatlu" in the nominative, "awladahum" in the accusative, and "shuraka'ihim" in the genitive, meaning: and thus was made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children by their partners. They separated the governing word from the governed by what the noun governs. In the speech of the Arabs this is ugly and not eloquent. A line of poetry has been transmitted from some people of the Hijaz supporting the reading of those who recite as the people of Syria did, but the transmitters of poetry and the scholars of Arabic from Iraq deny it, being the saying of their poet:

"fazajjatuhu mutamakkinan ... zajja al-qalusi abi mazadah" [[Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:358; al-Insaf 179; al-Khizanah 2:251; al-'Ayni (in the margin of al-Khizanah) 3:468; and many others. "Zajja": pushed with the zajj, which is the iron at the lower end of the spear. "Al-qalus": the young she-camel. "Abu Mazadah": the name of a man. This line is evidence for the view of the Kufans that it is permissible to separate the genitive construct from its second term by other than an adverb or a preposition, out of poetic necessity. The estimate is: "zajja Abi Mazadah al-qalus," so he separated the construct from its second term with "al-qalus," which is an object, and it is neither an adverb nor a preposition. Although this is the saying of the Kufans, al-Farra' rejected it in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:358, and said it is "not a thing."]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The reading I do not permit other than is: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ زَيَّنَ لِكَثِيرٍ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ قَتْلَ أَوْلادِهِمْ شُرَكَاؤُهُمْ﴾, with fatha on the zay of "zayyana", the accusative of "qatla" by the falling of "zayyana" upon it, the genitive of "awladihim" by the construct of "qatla" to them, and the nominative of "shuraka'" by their verb, because they are the ones who made attractive to the polytheists the killing of their children, according to the interpretation I have mentioned.

I only said "I do not permit a reading other than it" because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it, and because the interpretation of the people of interpretation came in accordance with it; and in that is the clearest explanation of the corruption of what opposes it in recitation.

* *

Had it not been that the interpretation of all the people of interpretation came in accordance with it, and then a reader recited: "وَكَذَلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِكَثِيرٍ مِنَ المُشْرِكِينَ قَتْلُ أَوْلادَهُمْ شُرَكَائِهِمْ", with damma on the zay of "zuyyina", "qatlu" in the nominative, and "awlad" and "shurakai" in the genitive, on the basis that "the partners" are in the genitive by being a substitute (badal) for "the children", on the grounds that "the children" are partners of their fathers in lineage and inheritance, it would have been permissible.

* *

And if a reader recited it thus but made "the partners" nominative and "the children" genitive, as one says: "ḍuriba 'Abdullahi akhūka" so that the agent appears after the report has been stated with the passive form, it would have been correct and permissible in Arabic.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 6, Verse 138:

The explanation of His words, ﴿And they say: These are cattle and tilth, forbidden (ḥijr); none may eat of them except whom we will, by their claim.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is an account from God, may His remembrance be exalted, about these ignorant polytheists, that they used to forbid and permit from themselves, without God having authorised them to do any of that.

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: These polytheists who equate their Lord with others said, out of ignorance, concerning their cattle and tilth: "These are cattle, and this is tilth, forbidden (ḥijr)." By "the cattle" and "the tilth" they mean what they had designated for God and their gods, which was mentioned in the verse before this one.

* *

It has been said: "The cattle" refers to the sā’ibah, the wasīlah and the baḥīrah, which they named. [[See the explanation of "al-an‘ām" above, 6:257 / 9:457, and the explanation of "al-ḥarth" above, 4:240–243, 397 / 6:257 / 7:134.]]

13914. Muhammad ibn ‘Amr told me this, saying: Abu ‘Asim told us, saying: ‘Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "The cattle" are the sā’ibah and the baḥīrah, which they named.

* *

And "al-ḥijr" in the speech of the Arabs means "the forbidden." [[The manuscript does not contain "al-ḥarām" (the forbidden); its addition in the printed edition is correct and agrees with what is in Majaz al-Qur’an of Abu ‘Ubaydah, 1:207.]] It is said: "I forbade so-and-so such-and-such" (ḥajartu ‘alā fulān kadhā), meaning I made it unlawful for him. From this is God's word: ﴿And they will say: a forbidding forbidden (ḥijran maḥjūran)﴾ [Surah al-Furqan: 22]. From it is also the verse of al-Mutalammis:

*They longed toward the far palm, so I said to her: "Forbidden, forbidden, is there anything but the Dahārīs?"* [[From his Diwan, qasidah 4; Mukhtarat Ibn al-Shajari: 32; Majaz al-Qur’an 1:207; it will come in the explanation at 19:302 (Bulaq edition); al-Lisan (d-h-r-s); Mu‘jam Isti‘jam: 1304; and Mu‘jam Yaqut (the far palm; he attributed it to Jarir, but it is al-Mutalammis, Jarir ibn ‘Abd al-Masih, from his qasidah which he composed when fleeing to al-Sham from ‘Amr ibn Hind; the story of al-Mutalammis and Tarafah and ‘Amr ibn Hind is well known). Thus "al-nakhlah al-quswa" (the far palm) appears here, and it is one transmission; the other transmission is "nakhlah al-quswa" without the definite article, as will come in the narration of Abu Ja‘far in the explanation at 19:302 (Bulaq edition). They have mentioned that the "nakhlah al-quswa" mentioned here is "nakhlat al-Yamaniyyah," which is a valley descending from the bottom of Qarn al-Manazil, the road from Yemen to Makkah. The apparent sense of this poetry, as far as my own reasoning leads me, indicates that "nakhlah al-quswa" is in the land of Iraq, leading to al-Hirah, the abode of ‘Amr ibn Hind, for he said this poetry when ‘Amr ibn Hind had forbidden him the land of Iraq, so his she-camel longed for its homeland in Iraq, and he said to her: "How have you become restless, when you were not blamed for restlessness, and between you and your beloved are desolate wastes that are dangerous?" He means: how do you long for a land in which is my destruction? Then he returned, saying: I do not blame you for the longing that stirred your yearning, for whoever is separated from his beloved by deserts must yearn. Then he explained the reason for his disapproval of her yearning, saying to her, as if addressing himself and apologising to her for blaming this wretched one: *They longed toward the far palm, so I said to her: "Unlawful for you, is it not those Dahārīs?"* ("Basl ‘alayki" means "forbidden to you," and this is another transmission.) "Al-Dahārīs" means calamities. He means: I do not blame her for longing for her beloved, but I blame her for longing for the land in which is my destruction. He said to her: the far palm toward which you yearn is forbidden to you, for in it are calamities and dangers. Thus it is shown that he means the abode of ‘Amr ibn Hind, from whom he fled; then he said to her after that: *My mother is Shamiyyah, since we have no Iraq, a people we love, while our people are hostile-eyed (shūs).* He means: aim for the palm of al-Shamiyyah, for Iraq has been forbidden to us, and in al-Sham are our beloved and the people of our affection, while our people in Iraq look at us with eyes full of hostility. Thus by his saying "since we have no Iraq" it is established that "nakhlat al-quswa" is in the land of Iraq. In this is sufficiency for verifying the place, God willing.]] And the saying of Ru’bah, [al-‘Ajjaj]: [[Here it is attributed to "Ru’bah," but the correct attribution is that it is by his father al-‘Ajjaj, without doubt; for this reason I have placed it between brackets, and it seems to be an error by the copyist or by Abu Ja‘far.]]

*And the neighbour of the House, for her is ḥujriyy*  [[Diwan al-‘Ajjaj: 68; al-Lisan (ḥ-j-r), from a long, well-known rajaz in which he described himself as chaste and protected, saying: "I am a man who is restrained concerning his neighbour, abstaining from harm, for harm is hated; and restrained from pursuing her secret." Then after some verses he said: "And the neighbour of the House, for her is ḥujriyy, and prohibitions whose violation is forbidden (bujriyy)." The author of al-Lisan explained it as: "for her, especially."]]

meaning the forbidden (al-muḥarram). From it is also the saying of another:

*So I spent the night reclining, and the eye is wakeful, as if my sleep upon the night is forbidden (maḥjūr).* [[Attributed to A‘sha Bahilah, Ibn Bari attributed it in al-Lisan (r-f-q); I have not found it elsewhere. "Murtafiqan" means leaning on the elbow of one's hand.]]

That is, forbidden. It is said "ḥijr" and "ḥujr," with the ḥā’ vowelled with kasrah or ḍammah.

* *

And it was read with ḍammah, as has been mentioned, by al-Hasan and Qatadah. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "al-Husayn," which is an error; the correct form is "al-Hasan," meaning al-Basri.]]

13915. ‘Abd al-Warith ibn ‘Abd al-Samad told me, saying: My father [said, my paternal uncle told me] told me, saying: My father told me, from al-Husayn, from Qatadah, that he used to read it: "wa-ḥarthun ḥujrun" (and tilth, ḥujr), saying: forbidden, with the ḥā’ vowelled with ḍammah. [[The report 13915: this chain of narration has a difficulty. ‘Abd al-Warith ibn ‘Abd al-Samad ibn ‘Abd al-Warith Sa‘id ibn Dhakwan al-Tamimi al-‘Anbari has passed several times; he narrates from his father, ‘Abd al-Samad ibn ‘Abd al-Warith ibn Sa‘id ibn Dhakwan; and his father, ‘Abd al-Samad ibn ‘Abd al-Warith, narrates from his father, ‘Abd al-Warith ibn Sa‘id ibn Dhakwan, and ‘Abd al-Warith ibn Sa‘id ibn Dhakwan narrates from Husayn al-Mu‘allim, who is Husayn ibn Dhakwan al-‘Awdhi; and Husayn al-Mu‘allim narrates from Qatadah. Therefore the more probable form of the chain is: "‘Abd al-Warith ibn ‘Abd al-Samad told me, saying: my father told me, saying: my father told me, from al-Husayn, from Qatadah," with the omission of "my paternal uncle told me," which I placed between brackets; by this the chain becomes sound, for I have not found "‘Abd al-Samad ibn ‘Abd al-Warith" narrating from "his paternal uncle," nor have I found anyone narrating from him. Moreover, his saying "my paternal uncle told me" requires that Sa‘id ibn Dhakwan, their grandfather, be the narrator from Husayn al-Mu‘allim, yet no narration from Sa‘id ibn Dhakwan has ever been mentioned, nor is he mentioned in the books of biographers. It is therefore established that the correct reading is to omit what I placed between the brackets. I also note that this chain has passed before as I have recorded it, but I was unable to locate it again. The addition, God willing, is an error by the copyist, and the chain of "Muhammad ibn Sa‘ad from his father, from his paternal uncle..." (no. 305) became confused for him, so he hastened and added: "my paternal uncle told me."]]

* *

As for the readers of al-Hijaz, Iraq and al-Sham, they read it with kasrah. This is the reading which I do not permit opposing, because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it, and because it is the most eloquent (al-lughah al-judhā) of the dialects of the Arabs. [[al-Judha (the most eloquent) is the feminine of al-ajwad; it is rarely used after the printed edition of Abu Ja‘far, as I mentioned in the note on its first use before, 6:437, note 1; and this is the second time Abu Ja‘far has used it.]]

* *

And it is related from Ibn ‘Abbas that he used to read it: "wa-ḥarthun ḥirjun," with the rā’ before the jīm.

13916. Al-Harith told me this, saying: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz told me, saying: Ibn ‘Uyaynah told us, from ‘Amr, from Ibn ‘Abbas, that he used to read it so.

* *

This is a third dialect, whose meaning and the meaning of "ḥijr" are one. This is like their saying "jadhb" and "jabdh," and "nā’" and "nā’a." 

So in "ḥijr" there are then three dialects: "ḥijr," with kasrah on the ḥā’ and the jīm before the rā’; "ḥujr," with ḍammah on the ḥā’ and the jīm before the rā’; and "ḥirj," with kasrah on the ḥā’ and the rā’ before the jīm.

* *

And the people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said concerning the interpretation of ḥijr.

Those who said that:

13917. ‘Imran ibn Musa al-Qazzaz told me, saying: ‘Abd al-Warith told us, from Humayd, from Mujahid and Abu ‘Amr: ﴿wa-ḥarthun ḥijr﴾ , he says: forbidden.

13918. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: ‘Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, saying: Mu‘awiyah told me, from ‘Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, his words: ﴿wa-ḥarthun ḥijr﴾ , "al-ḥijr" is what they forbade from the wasīlah, and the forbidding of what they forbade.

13919. Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-A‘la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma‘mar, from Qatadah: ﴿wa-ḥarthun ḥijr﴾ , he said: forbidden.

13920. Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa‘id told us, from Qatadah, his words: ﴿These are cattle and tilth, forbidden﴾ , to the end of the verse: it was a prohibition upon them from the devils concerning their wealth, and a severity and stringency. That was from the devils, and was not from God.

13921. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: as for His words: ﴿And they say: these are cattle and tilth, forbidden﴾ , they say: forbidden, that we feed none except whom we wish.

13922. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿These are cattle and tilth, forbidden﴾ , "we seclude it for whom we wish and from whom we wish, none may eat of it except whom we will, by their claim." He said: They only secluded that for their gods, and they said: none may eat of it except whom we will, by their claim; they said: we seclude it from the women, and we make it for the men.

13923. It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu‘adh say, saying: ‘Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: ﴿cattle and tilth, forbidden﴾ , as for "ḥijr," he says: prohibited. That is because they used to do things in the Jahiliyyah which God had not commanded: they forbade some of their cattle, things which they did not eat, and they set aside a known portion of their tilth for their gods, and they said: what we have named for our gods is not lawful for us.

13924. Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿cattle and tilth, forbidden﴾ , what they made for God and for their associates.

13925. Muhammad ibn ‘Amr told me, saying: Abu ‘Asim told us, saying: ‘Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

The explanation of His words: ﴿And cattle whose backs are forbidden, and cattle over which they do not mention the name of God, a fabrication against Him; He will recompense them for what they used to fabricate﴾ (138)

Abu Ja‘far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: These ignorant polytheists forbade the backs of some of their cattle, so they do not ride upon their backs, though they benefit from their milk (rusl), their offspring (nitāj) and all other things from them except riding their backs. [[al-Rusl (with kasrah then sukun): milk. And al-Nitaj (with kasrah on the nūn): what she gives birth to of her young.]] And they forbade from their cattle other cattle, so they do not perform the Hajj upon them, and they do not mention the name of God over them, whether they ride them in any way, nor when they milk them, nor when they carry loads upon them.

* *

And the people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said concerning that.

Those who said that:

13926. Sufyan told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn ‘Ayyash told us, from ‘Asim, who said: Abu Wa’il said to me: Do you know what "cattle over which they do not mention the name of God" is? I said: No! He said: They are cattle upon which they do not perform the Hajj.

13927. Muhammad ibn ‘Abbad ibn Musa told us, saying: Shadhan told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn ‘Ayyash told us, from ‘Asim, who said: Abu Wa’il said to me: Do you know what His saying is: "whose backs are forbidden, and cattle over which they do not mention the name of God"? I said: No! He said: It is the baḥīrah, upon which they did not perform the Hajj. [[The report 13927: Muhammad ibn ‘Abbad ibn Musa al-Khutali has passed as no. 11318; there I cited from Ibn Abi Hatim (4/1/15) that he narrated from Hisham ibn Muhammad al-Kalbi and al-Walid ibn Salih, and that Abu Bakr Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated from him. Then I stopped at this brief biography mentioned by Ibn Abi Hatim, and doubted the correctness of what is in it, for Abu Bakr Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrates only from his father, ‘Abbad ibn Musa al-Khutali. I do not know whether he narrated from his son, Muhammad ibn ‘Abbad, or did not narrate from him, for they did not mention that in the biography of Abu Bakr Ibn Abi al-Dunya. And "Shadhan" is: al-Aswad ibn ‘Amir, a trustworthy and truthful narrator, whose biography is in al-Tahdhib.]]

13928. Ahmad ibn ‘Amr al-Basri told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sa‘id al-Shahid told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn ‘Ayyash told us, from ‘Asim, from Abu Wa’il: ﴿and cattle over which they do not mention the name of God﴾ , he said: they do not perform the Hajj upon them. [[The report 13928: Ahmad ibn ‘Amr al-Basri, what I said about him has passed as no. 9875. And Muhammad ibn Sa‘id al-Shahid, I do not know who he is, and I have not found any mention of him.]]

13929. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, as for: ﴿cattle whose backs are forbidden﴾ , they are the baḥīrah, the sā’ibah and the ḥām. As for "the cattle over which they do not mention the name of God," he said: when they make them bear young (idha awladūhā) [[Perhaps the correct reading is: "not when they make them bear young" (lā in awladūhā).]], nor when they slaughter them.

13930. Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, his words: ﴿and cattle over which they do not mention the name of God﴾ , he said: among their camels there was a group over which they did not mention the name of God, nor in any matter concerning them, neither when they rode them, nor when they milked, nor when they carried loads, nor when they lent them, nor when they did anything.

13931. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿and cattle whose backs are forbidden﴾ , he said: no one rides them; ﴿and cattle over which they do not mention the name of God﴾ .

* *

As for His words: ﴿a fabrication against God﴾ , He says: these polytheists did what they did of forbidding what they forbade, and said what they said of that, as a lie against God and a false invention upon Him; for they attributed what they used to forbid of that, as He described it of them, may He be exalted, in His Book, to God as the one who forbade it. God denied that about Himself, refuted them, and informed His Prophet and the believers that they are liars in what they claim. [[See the explanation of "al-iftira’" (fabrication) above, p. 136, note 4, and the sources cited there.]]

* *

Then He, may His might be mentioned, said: ﴿He will recompense them﴾ , He says: their Lord will reward them for what they used to fabricate the lie against God, and He will give them their recompense for that. [[See the explanation of "al-jaza’" (recompense) above in the language indexes (j-z-y).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 139:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And they say, "What is in the wombs of these livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives; but if it is stillborn, then they are partners in it."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The commentators differed concerning what is meant by His saying: ﴿what is in the wombs of these livestock﴾.

Some of them said: It means milk.

Those who said this:

13932. Abu Kurayb related to us, who said: Ibn 'Atiyyah related to us, who said: Isra'il related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And they say, what is in the wombs of these livestock is exclusively for our males﴾: "It is milk." [Note on the report: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl al-'Anazi, Abu al-Mughira, a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i). He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and in Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/196, where the nisba is given as "al-'Anbari"; I do not know which of the two is correct.]

13933. Ibn WakI' related to us, who said: Yahya related to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

13934. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And they say, what is in the wombs of these livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives﴾: "The milk of the baheers was for the males, not the females; and if it was stillborn, their males and females shared in it."

13935. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives﴾, he said: "What is in the wombs of the baheers, meaning their milk, they used to assign it to the men, not the women."

13936. al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: 'Isa ibn Yunus related to us, from Zakariya, from 'Amir, who said: "The baheera: only men would drink its milk; and if any of it died, men and women would eat it."

13937. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, who said: My father related to me, who said: My paternal uncle related to me, who said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And they say, what is in the wombs of these livestock is exclusively for our males﴾, to the end of the verse: it is milk. They forbade it to their females, while their males drank it. When a ewe gave birth to a male, they slaughtered it, and it was for the men, not the women. If it was female, it was ridden and not slaughtered. If it was stillborn, "they are partners in it." Thereupon God forbade that.

* * *

Others said: Rather, it means what is in the wombs of the baheers and the sawa'ib, of the embryos.

Those who said this:

13938. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, who said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And they say, what is in the wombs of these livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives; but if it is stillborn, then they are partners in it.﴾ As for these livestock, what is born of them alive is exclusively for the men and not the women; but what is born dead, men and women eat it.

13939. Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿what is in the wombs of these livestock is exclusively for our males﴾: the sa'iba and the baheera.

13940. al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, who said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings regarding its interpretation is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, reported about these disbelievers that they said, concerning particular livestock: "What is in the wombs of these livestock is exclusively for our males, to the exclusion of our females." Milk is what is in their wombs, and likewise their embryos. God did not specify in His report about them that they said that some of it was forbidden to the women and not to others.

Since that is so, it is necessary to say that they said: what is in the wombs of those livestock, of milk and embryos, is lawful for their males, exclusively, to the exclusion of their females; and that they used to give preference to their men with it, except that if what is in their wombs of embryos is dead, then men and women share in eating it at that point.

* * *

The grammarians differed concerning the reason for which "al-khāliṣa" (exclusive) was made feminine.

Some grammarians of Basra and some Kufans said: it was made feminine to emphasize "exclusivity" (al-khulūṣ); as if, when it established exclusivity for them, it resembled abundance, so it took the pattern of "rāwiya" (one who transmits much) and "nassāba" (one who traces genealogies much).

* * *

Some grammarians of Kufa said: it was made feminine to match the feminine "al-an'ām" (livestock), since "mā fī buṭūnihā" (what is in their wombs) is like it, so it was made feminine to match it. And whoever made it masculine did so to agree with "mā" (what). He said: in the reading of 'Abd Allah it is "khāliṣun" (masculine). He said: "al-khāliṣa" may also, in its feminine form, be a verbal noun (maṣdar), as you say "al-'āfiya" and "al-'āqiba," and this is like His saying: ﴿Indeed We purified them with a pure quality﴾ [Surah Sad: 46]. [See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 358, 359.]

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is to say: what is intended by it is emphasis on the exclusivity of what is in the wombs of the livestock whose embryos they had forbidden to their wives, exclusively for their males to the exclusion of their females, just as this is done with "al-rāwiya," "al-nassāba," and "al-'allāma," when emphasis is intended in describing one who has that attribute, as it is said: "So-and-so is the exclusive one of so-and-so, and his select companions." [See the explanation of "al-khāliṣa" above 2: 365, 366. See the rest of Abu Ja'far's argument on this a few lines later.]

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿and forbidden to our wives﴾, the commentators differed concerning what is meant by "al-azwāj" (the wives).

Some of them said: it means women.

Those who said this:

13941. al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿and forbidden to our wives﴾, he said: the women.

* * *

Others said: rather, by "al-azwāj" is meant the daughters.

Those who said this:

13942. Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿and forbidden to our wives﴾, he said: "The wives" are the daughters. And they said: the daughters have no share of it.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view in this matter is to say: God informed us that these polytheists used to say of what is in the wombs of these livestock, meaning their livestock: "This is forbidden to our wives," and "al-azwāj" in their speech means only their women, and they are without doubt the daughters of those who are their offspring, and the lawful wives of those who are their husbands. [See the explanation of "al-zawj" above 1: 514 / 2: 446.]

In the saying of God Mighty and Majestic: ﴿and forbidden to our wives﴾ there is clear evidence that the feminine form of "al-khāliṣa" was because of the emphasis I described regarding the attribution of exclusivity to the males in what is in the wombs of the livestock; for if it were because of the feminine gender of the livestock, it would have been said: "and forbidden [feminine] to our wives." But since the feminine form in "al-khāliṣa" is for the reason I mentioned, and then the same emphasis was not intended in "al-muḥarram" (the forbidden), it reverted to the masculine of "mā," using the form that is more appropriate to its attribute.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿but if it is stillborn, then they are partners in it﴾, the readers differed in their recitation of it.

Yazid ibn al-Qa'qa' and Talha ibn Musarrif, along with others, read: "wa-in takun maytatun" with a "t" on "takun" and "maytatun" in the nominative, except that Yazid used to stress the yā' in "mayyita" while Talha lightened it.

13943. al-Muthanna related to me this, who said: Ishaq related to us, who said: Ibn Abi Hammad related to us, who said: 'Isa related to us, from Talha ibn Musarrif.

13944. And Ahmad ibn Yusuf related to us, from al-Qasim, and Isma'il ibn Ja'far, from Yazid.

* * *

Some readers of Medina, Kufa and Basra read: ﴿wa-in yakun maytatan﴾ with a "y" and "maytatan" in the accusative, with the yā' lightened.

* * *

It seems that whoever read ﴿wa-in yakun﴾ with "y" and ﴿maytatan﴾ in the accusative intended: "And if what is in the wombs of those livestock be dead." So he used the masculine "yakun" to agree with the masculine "mā," and put "al-maytatu" in the accusative because it is the predicate of "yakun."

As for whoever read "wa-in takun maytatun," he intended, God willing: "And if what is in their wombs be stillborn," so he made "takun" feminine to agree with the feminine "maytatun."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿then they are partners in it﴾, it means that the men and their wives are partners in eating it, and they do not forbid it to any of them, as we mentioned from those commentators cited earlier.

* * *

Ibn Zayd used to say about this:

13945.
