Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿but if it is stillborn, then they are partners in it﴾, he said: the women eat with the men if what comes out of their wombs is stillborn; "they are partners in it," and they said: "If we wish, we will assign a share of it to the daughters, and if we wish, we will not assign it."

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The apparent recitation contradicts what Ibn Zayd interpreted, because its apparent meaning indicates that they said: "If what is in their wombs is stillborn, then we are partners in it," without any condition of will. Yet Ibn Zayd claimed that they made that subject to their own will.

* * *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿He will repay them for their description. Indeed He is Wise, Knowing﴾ [Surah 6: 139]

Abu Ja'far said: His Mighty and Majestic saying means: "He will repay," i.e., He will reward and recompense these ones who fabricated lies against Him in forbidding what God had not forbidden, and permitting what God had not permitted, and attributing their lies in that to God [see the explanation of "al-jaza'" above, p. 146, note 2, and the references there] = and His saying: ﴿their description﴾ means by "their description" the lie against God; and that is as He said elsewhere in His Book: ﴿and their tongues describe the lie﴾ [Surah al-Nahl: 62]. [See the explanation of "al-wasf" above, ﷺ: 10, 11.]

* * *

"Al-waṣf" and "al-ṣifa" are one in the speech of the Arabs; they are two verbal nouns, like "al-wazn" and "al-zina."

* * *

The commentators said things similar to what we said about the meaning of "al-waṣf."

Those who said this:

13946. Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, who said: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿He will repay them for their description﴾: "Their saying of the lie concerning that."

13947. al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, who said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

13948. Ibn WakI' related to us, who said: Ibn Numayr related to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliya: ﴿He will repay them for their description﴾, he said: "Their lie."

13949. Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: ﴿He will repay them for their description﴾, i.e., their lie.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed He is Wise, Knowing﴾, He, Mighty and Majestic, says: indeed God, in recompensing them for their description of the lie and their saying of falsehood against Him, is "Wise" in all His management of His creation, and "Knowing" of what benefits them, and of other than that among their affairs. [See the explanation of "Wise" (ḥakīm) and "Knowing" (‘alīm) above in the indexes of vocabulary, roots (ḥ-k-m) and (‘-l-m).]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 140:

The explanation of His words: ﴿Those who have killed their children in foolishness, without knowledge, and have forbidden what God has provided for them, fabricating against God, have certainly lost. They have indeed gone astray, and they were not guided.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Those who fabricate lies against their Lord have perished,[[See the explanation of "al-khasar" (loss) above, 11:324, note 3, and the references there.]] those who ascribe equals to Him, the idols and images, whose associates made the killing of their children and the forbidding of [what He had bestowed upon them] of their wealth seem attractive to them.[[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "and the forbidding of what I forbade them of their wealth," which does not match the interpretation of the verse but contradicts it; I have preferred the reading placed between the brackets.]] So they killed their children in obedience to them, and they forbade what God had made lawful for them and had made as their provision from their livestock, "in foolishness," from them. He says: they did what they did of that out of ignorance on their part of what benefits and harms them, deficiency of intellect, weakness of judgment, and lack of understanding of its immediate harm and its ultimate evil, and of the great punishment of God upon them for it.[[See the explanation of "al-safah" (foolishness) above, 1:293-295; 3:90, 129; 6:57.]] ﴿Fabricating against God﴾: he says, lying against God and inventing falsehood concerning Him. ﴿They have indeed gone astray﴾: he says, they have abandoned the path of truth in their doing that and have deviated from the right way.[[See the explanation of "al-dalal" (going astray) above, in the lexical indices under (ḍ-l-l).]] ﴿And they were not guided﴾: he says, those who did that were not upon guidance and rectitude in their actions which they used to do before that, nor were they guided to the right course in them, nor granted success in it.[[See the explanation of "al-ihtida'" (being guided) above, in the lexical indices under (h-d-y).]]

* *

This verse was revealed concerning those whose report God mentioned in these verses from His words: ﴿And they assign to God a share of what He has created of crops and livestock﴾, who used to slit the ears of camels (baḥā'ir), let animals loose (sawā'ib), and bury daughters alive, as:

13950 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ikrimah said, concerning His words: ﴿Those who killed their children in foolishness, without knowledge﴾: It was revealed concerning those among Rabi'ah and Mudar who buried daughters alive. A man would stipulate to his wife that she should keep a girl alive and bury another. When the girl whom she was to bury was born, the man would go out in the morning or return in the evening from his wife,[[In the printed edition: "When the girl whom she was to bury, the man went out in the morning ..."; in the manuscript: "When the girl whom she was to bury was born, the man would go out in the morning or return from his wife," and the correct reading is what is given here. The meaning: when the woman gave birth to the girl whom he had stipulated she should bury, he would go out in the morning or return in the evening and say to her: "You are to me like my mother's back if I return to you and you have not buried her."]] and say to her: "You are to me like my mother's back if I return to you and you have not buried her." She would dig a trench (khadd) for her in the ground,[[Khadda fi'l-ard khadan: he split the ground with a cut.]] and send for her women, who would gather around her, and then they would pass her around, until when she saw him returning, she would push her into her grave and then smooth the earth over her.

13951 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: Then he mentioned what they did with their children and their wealth, and said: ﴿Those who killed their children in foolishness, without knowledge, and forbade what God provided﴾.

13952 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah concerning His words: ﴿Those who killed their children in foolishness, without knowledge﴾, he said: This was the practice of the people of the Jahiliyyah. One of them would kill his daughter for fear of captivity and poverty, and would feed his dog. As for His words: ﴿And forbade what God provided﴾, the verse, they were the people of the Jahiliyyah. They made baḥīrah, sā'ibah, waṣīlah and ḥāmī, a decree of the devils concerning their wealth.

13953 - Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: If you wish to know the ignorance of the Arabs, then recite what follows the hundredth verse of Surat al-An'am, His words: ﴿Those who killed their children in foolishness without knowledge﴾, the verse.

* *

Abu Razin used to interpret His words: ﴿They have indeed gone astray﴾, as referring to: they had gone astray before these acts, namely the killing of children and the forbidding of the provision which God had provided for them, by other matters besides that.

13954 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Abu Razin concerning His words: ﴿Those who killed their children﴾, to His words: ﴿They have indeed gone astray﴾, he said: They had gone astray before that.

**The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿It is He who brings into being gardens, [some] trellised and [some] untrellised﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is an announcement from God, may His remembrance be exalted, of what He has bestowed upon them of His bounty, a reminder to them of the place of His favour, and an informing them of what He has made lawful and unlawful, and of the rights He has apportioned in their wealth for those to whom He has assigned a share.

Its meaning: Your Lord, O people, ﴿brings into being﴾, that is, creates and originates, ﴿gardens﴾, meaning orchards, ﴿trellised﴾, which are those [vines] that people have trellised, that is, the grapevines [[See the explanation of "inshaʾa" above, p. 128, note 2, and the references there.]] ﴿and untrellised﴾, not raised or built up, which people do not plant or raise, but which God raises, plants and makes grow. [[See the explanation of "ʿarasha" above, vol. 5, p. 445.]] As follows:

13955. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Salih told us, he said: Muʿawiya told me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words: ﴿trellised﴾, he said: "raised on supports."

13956. And with the same chain, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿It is He who brings into being gardens, trellised and untrellised﴾. "The trellised" are those that people trellis; "the untrellised" are the fruits that grow in the open land and on the mountains.

13957. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: As for "gardens," they are orchards; as for "trellised," it is that which is trellised in the manner of the vine.

13958. al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAta' al-Khurasani, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words: ﴿It is He who brings into being gardens, trellised﴾, he said: "What is trellised of the vines." ﴿And untrellised﴾, he said: "What is not trellised of the vine."

* *

**The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿And the date palm and the crops, varying in their produce, and the olive and the pomegranate, similar and dissimilar. Eat of their fruit when it bears fruit﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, says: And He brings into being the date palm and the crops, varying in their produce, meaning by "produce" (ukul) the fruit. He means: He created the date palm and the crops, varying in what comes out of them that is eaten, of fruit and grain. [[See the explanation of "ukul" above, vol. 5, p. 538.]] ﴿And the olive and the pomegranate, similar and dissimilar﴾, in taste: some sweet, some sour, and some *mazz*. [[*Mazz* (with a dammed *m*): that whose taste is between sweet and sour; one says "a *mazz* drink."]] As follows:

13959. al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj regarding His words: ﴿similar and dissimilar﴾, he said: "similar" in appearance, and "dissimilar" in taste.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Eat of their fruit when it bears fruit﴾, He means: Eat of its fresh fruit while it is still fresh. As follows:

13960. al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abu Hammam al-Ahwazi told us, he said: Musa ibn ʿUbayda told us, from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb regarding His words: ﴿Eat of their fruit when it bears fruit﴾, he said: "From its fresh dates and its grapes."

13961. ʿAmr ibn ʿAli told us, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Zibriqan told us, he said: Musa ibn ʿUbayda told us regarding His words: ﴿Eat of their fruit when it bears fruit﴾, he said: "From its fresh dates and its grapes." [[The two reports: 13960 and 13961. Abu Hammam al-Ahwazi in the first report is Muhammad ibn al-Zibriqan in the second. He is trustworthy. His biography has passed under no. 877.]]

* *

**The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾**

The exegetes differed concerning the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: This is a command from God to give the obligatory charity from the fruit and the grain.

Those who said this:

13962. ʿAmr ibn ʿAli told us, he said: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ told us, he said: Yunus told us, from al-Hasan regarding His words: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "The zakat."

13963. ʿAmr told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Samad told us, he said: Yazid ibn Dirham told us, he said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "The obligatory zakat."

13964. ʿAmr told us, he said: Muʿalla ibn Asad told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, he said: al-Hajjaj ibn Artat told us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "The tenth and the half of the tenth."

13965. Ibn Wakiʿ told us, he said: Hani' ibn Saʿid told us, from Hajjaj, from Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd Allah, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Shaddad, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "The tenth and the half of the tenth." [[Report 13965: Hani' ibn Saʿid al-Nakhaʿi, who has passed under no. 13159. "Hajjaj" is Hajjaj ibn Artat, who has passed many times. "Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd Allah ibn Saʿid" is Abu ʿAwn al-Thaqafi, who has passed under no. 7595.]]

13966. ʿAmr ibn ʿAli, Ibn Wakiʿ and Ibn Bashshar said, they told us: ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, he said: Ibrahim ibn Nafiʿ al-Makki told us, from Ibn ʿAbbas, from his father, regarding His words: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "The zakat." [[Report 13966: Ibrahim ibn Nafiʿ al-Makki al-Makhzumi, who has passed under no. 4305. As for "Ibn ʿAbbas, from his father," I do not know who this is, and it is without doubt not ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas, the scholar of the Community. I fear that the correct reading is: "from Ibn Tawus, from his father."]]

13967. ʿAmr told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, he said: Abu Hilal told us, from Hayyan al-Aʿraj, from Jabir ibn Zayd: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "The zakat." [[Report 13967: "ʿAbd al-Rahman" is ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, who has passed many times. "Abu Hilal" is Muhammad ibn Sulaym al-Rasibi al-Basri, trustworthy, who has passed under nos. 2996 and 4681. "Hayyan al-Aʿraj" al-Jawfi, al-Basri: trustworthy, of the successors of the successors. He related from Jabir ibn Zayd. Qatada, Ibn Jurayj, Saʿid ibn Abi ʿArූba and others related from him. He is biographed in the Tahdhib and in Ibn Abi Hatim, 1/2/246.]]

13968. Yaʿqub told me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayya told us, he said: Yunus informed us, from al-Hasan regarding His words: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "It is the charity." He said: Then he was asked about it again, and he said: "It is the charity from the grain and the fruits."

13969. Ibn Wakiʿ told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allah informed me, from ʿAmr ibn Sulayman and others, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab that he said regarding: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾: "The obligatory charity."

13970. Yaʿqub told me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayya told us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan regarding His words: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "It is the charity from the grain and the fruits."

13971. al-Muthanna told me, he said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih told us, he said: Muʿawiya told me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, meaning by "its right" its obligatory zakat, on the day it is measured or its measure is known.

13972. Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My paternal uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾: That was because a man, when he sowed and it was the day of his harvest, would know its measure and its due, and would give one out of every ten, and [also] what people gleaned from its ears. [[In the printed edition: "wa-ma yaltaqit" (and what is picked up). I have followed the manuscript.]]

13973. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saʿid told us, from Qatada regarding His words: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾: "Its right on the day of its harvest" is the obligatory charity. It has been reported to us that the Prophet ﷺ prescribed for what the sky waters, or a flowing spring, or what is watered by dew, [[*al-tall* is the dew.]] or what is *baʿl* [[*Baʿl* among plants is that which drinks by its roots from the earth, without irrigation from rain or anything else.]] — the full tenth; and for what is watered with a bucket: the half of the tenth. Qatada said: This applies to what is measured of the fruit. When the fruit reaches five *awsuq*, [[*Awsuq* is the plural of *wasq*, which is sixty *sa*ʿ, as he explains afterwards, according to their differing opinions about the measure of the *saʿ*.]] that is three hundred *saʿ*, then the zakat is due upon it. And they used to prefer to give from what is not measured of the fruit in proportion to that.

13974. Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada and Tawus: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, they both said: "It is the zakat."

13975. al-Muthanna told me, he said: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn told us, he said: Hushaym informed us, from al-Hajjaj, from Salim al-Makki, from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya regarding His words: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "On the day of its measuring, he gives a tenth or half a tenth." [[Report 13975: "Salim al-Makki" is Salim ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Khayyat, biographed in the Tahdhib, the Kabir 2/2/116, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/184.]]

13976. al-Muthanna told me, he said: al-Hammani told us, he said: Sharik told us, from Salim al-Makki, from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya regarding His words: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "The tenth, and the half of the tenth."

13977. al-Muthanna told me, he said: Suwayd told us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, and from Qatada: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, they both said: "The zakat."

13978. al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abu Muʿawiya al-Darir told us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "The tenth and the half of the tenth."

13979. al-Muthanna told me, he said: Suwayd told us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sharik, from al-Hakam ibn ʿUtayba, from Ibn ʿAbbas, the like of it.

13980. It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, he said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾: "Meaning: its day of measuring, [what is] of wheat, dates or raisins. And 'its right' is its zakat."

13981. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit, and give its right on the day of its harvest﴾: "Eat of it, and when you harvest it, give its right; and 'its right' is its tithes."

13982. Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said: Shuʿba told us, from Yunus ibn ʿUbayd, from al-Hasan that he said regarding this verse: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾: "The zakat, when you measure it."

13983. ʿAmr told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said: Shuʿba told us, from Abu Raja', he said: I asked al-Hasan about His words: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, and he said: "The zakat."

13984. Ibn al-Barqi told me, he said: ʿAmr ibn Abi Salama told us, he said: I asked Ibn Zayd ibn Aslam about God's words: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, and I said to him: "Is it the tithes?" He said: "Yes!" I said to him: "From your father?" He said: "From my father and others."

* *

Others said: Rather, that is a right which God made obligatory in the wealth of the owners of property, other than the obligatory charity.

Those who said this:

13985. ʿAmr ibn ʿAli told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wahhab told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, from his father: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "Something other than the obligatory due." He said: And in his book it was: "from ʿAli ibn al-Husayn."

13986. ʿAmr told us, he said: Yahya told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Malik told us, from ʿAta' regarding His words: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "The handful of food."

13987. Ibn Wakiʿ told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAta': ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "From the date palm, the grape and all grain."

13988. Ibn Wakiʿ told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: I said to ʿAta': "Do you see what I harvest of fruits?" He said: "From them too you give." And he said: "From everything you harvest you give its right on the day of its harvest, from date palm, grape, grain, fruits, greens or cane, from every such thing." I said to ʿAta': "Is it obligatory on people, all of that?" He said: "Yes!" Then he recited: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾. He said: I said to ʿAta': "Regarding His words: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, is there in that anything fixed and known?" He said: "No."

13989. al-Muthanna told me, he said: Suwayd told us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from ʿAta' regarding His words: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "He gives from what is present on that day what is easy, and it is not the zakat." [[In the printed edition: "yuʿti min hasadihi yawmaʾidhin" (gives from its harvest that day), which is not correct. In the manuscript: "min husul yawmaʾidhin" (from what is present that day). The manuscript reading is correct, as the next report shows. He means: whoever of the people and the needy is present.]]

13990. Ibn Wakiʿ told us, he said: ʿIsa ibn Yunus told us, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from ʿAta': ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "It is not the zakat, but he feeds whoever is present at that moment of its harvested [crop]." [[In the printed edition: "hasdah" (its harvest). I have followed the manuscript. "al-Hasad" and "al-Hasid" (with the vowels fatha on the ḥ and ṣ) are what is cut from the crop after it has been harvested.]]

13991. Ibn Wakiʿ told us, he said: Jarir told us, from al-ʿAla' ibn al-Musayyab, from Hammad: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "They used to give fresh dates."

13992. Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakiʿ told us, both said: Jarir told us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "When the needy are present, you cast some of it for them. When you have cleaned it and begun to measure it, you scatter some of it for them by handfuls. When you know its measure, you set aside its zakat. When you begin the picking of the palm, you cast for them some of the *thafarIq*. [[In the printed edition: "judhadh al-ard" (with a dhal), which is plain error. "Judad al-nakhl" (with a fatha or kasra on the j) is the time of its cutting, which is the cutting of its fruit. The *thafarIq* are the plural of *thafruq*, which is the cap of an unripe date or of the date that clings to it. Mujahid did not mean this; he meant the clusters: one strips what is on them, and one or two or three dates remain on them, which the stripping tool misses, and these are thrown to the needy. So he used *thafarIq* as a metaphor for the little that remains in its cluster and stalk.]] When you begin measuring it, you scatter some of it for them by handfuls. When you know its measure, you set aside its zakat."

13993. Ibn Wakiʿ told us, he said: Jarir told us, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "Apart from the obligatory [zakat]."

13994. Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Hakkam told us, from ʿAmr, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "He casts to the beggars at the harvest from the ears [of grain]. [[*Al-suʾal* is the plural of *sail*, like *jahil* and *juhal*.]] When it is threshed, or it is plastered, the doubt is from Abu Jaʿfar [[In the manuscript: "fa-idha tin aw tiyn" (unpointed). In the printed edition: "fa-idha tin, aw tin," which is with a bāʾ in the first and a yāʾ in the second, and neither has meaning. I fear that the correct reading is what I have given, meaning that which is with the wheat and grain of clay. I do not know this. And above every knowledgeable one is the All-Knowing. I did not find the report elsewhere. See no. 14000, and his words: "when he brings it to the threshing floor," for it seems he means this.]] — he cast to them. When he carries it and wants to make it a heap, he casts to them. When he threshes, he feeds them from it. When he finishes and knows how much it measures, he sets aside its zakat." And he said: "For the date palm, at the time of cutting, he feeds [them] from the fruit and the stalks. [[In the printed edition: "al-judhadh" with a dhal; see the previous note.]] When it is at its measuring, he feeds [them] from the dates. When he finishes, he sets aside its zakat." [[*Al-kudas* (with a ḍamma and then a sukūn) is the heap of wheat when it is gathered.]]

13995. ʿAmr ibn ʿAli and Muhammad ibn Bashshar both said: ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, from Mansur, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿And give its right on the day of its harvest﴾, he said: "When the grain is harvested, he casts [some] of the ears, and when the palm is cut, he casts [some] of the stalks. [[*Judd al-nakhl yajudduhu judadan*: he cut it and severed it. It is in the printed edition with a dhal, as in the previous note. I will correct it later without indicating the error.]] When he measures it, he gives its zakat."

13996. Ibn Wakiʿ told us, he said: My father told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, he said: "At the harvest, and at the threshing, and at the cutting of the dates, he hands over some of it to them, and when he measures it, he sets aside its zakat."

13997. And with the same chain, from Sufyan, from Mujahid, the like of it, except that he said: "Apart from the zakat."

**Abu Ja'far al-Tabari, Jami' al-Bayan, on Surah 6, verse 141 (part 2 of 3)**

13998. Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾. He said: "It is something apart from the zakat (obligatory almsgiving), at the time of the harvest and the gleaning (al-jadad), when they reap and when they estimate (hazaru)."[[In the printed edition: "wa-idha juddu" ("when they cut"), and I have affirmed what is in the manuscript, which is correct in meaning. "Hazara al-ta'am wa-al-nakhl wa-ghayruhu" (he estimated the food, the palm trees, and other things): when he measured them by conjecture. The "hazir" is also the "kharis" (the one who estimates the yield of dates), "kharasahu": he estimated it by conjecture.]]

13999. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, concerning the words of God: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾. He said: "It is obligatory, when it is cut."

14000. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, that he said concerning this verse: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾. He said: "When it is harvested, he feeds [the poor]; when he brings it to the threshing floor [al-baydar],[[al-baydar: the place where food is threshed.]] and when he threshes it, he feeds from it."

14001. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ash'ath, from Ibn Umar, who said: "He feeds the one who comes begging (al-mu'tarr),[[al-mu'tarr: the one who circles around you seeking what you have, whether he asks you or remains silent about asking. "A'arra" ("he came to him seeking his kindness") and "i'tarra bihi."]] apart from what he gives of the tithe and half-tithe."

14002. And with the same chain, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid who said: "A handful at the harvest, and a handful at the gleaning."

14003. Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Hafs narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ibn Sirin, who said: "They used to give to whoever came begging to them something."

14004. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: "The dighth." [[al-dighth (with a kasrah and then a sukun): a handful of mixed grass, and what is similar to it of herbs.]]

14005. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: "He gives like the dighth."

14006. Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾, who said: "Like this, from the dighth" — and Yahya placed his thumb on the second joint of his index finger.

14007. Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: "Like the dighth."

14008. Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, and from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Ibrahim; both said: "He gives a dighth."[[In the printed edition, this chain appeared as it is here, except that it read "... 'an Abi Ja'far, 'an Sufyan" without the conjunctive waw. It also had "qal" in the singular, which is a change from the manuscript. In the manuscript, after the chain mentioned earlier ("al-Dighth"), there was a blank space preceded by the letter (ṭ), indicating an error; then after the blank: "qal haddathana Abi, 'an Isra'il," and the rest of the chain as in the printed edition, without a conjunctive waw before "'an Sufyan," but with "qala" in the dual form, which is a distorted chain. The insertion of "haddathana Ibn Wakī'" in place of the blank is undoubtedly correct, as in the printed edition, but the error lies in the omission of the waw before "'an Sufyan." So they are two chains, as I have shown. "Isra'il" is Isra'il ibn Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, who narrates from Jabir ibn Yazid ibn al-Harith al-Ju'fi, and "Abu Ja'far" is, in my view, Abu Ja'far al-Baqir. As for the second chain, it is from the narration of Ibn Wakī', from his father, from Sufyan... And this appears to be the correct reading, God willing.]]

14009. Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Kathir ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Burqan narrated to us, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, who said: "When the palm trees were harvested, a man would bring a bunch (al-'idhq) from his palm trees and hang it on the side of the mosque. A needy man would come and strike it with his stick, and whatever fell, he would eat. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered with al-Hasan or al-Husayn, and he took a date and pulled it out of his mouth. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) would not eat charity, nor would his household." That is His saying: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾.

14010. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn Hayyan narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Maymun ibn Mihran and Yazid ibn al-Asamm, who both said: "The people of Madinah, when they harvested, would bring the bunch and place it in the mosque. Then the beggar would come and strike it with his stick, so that some would fall from it." And that is His saying: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾.

14011. Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Abi al-Zarqa' narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Yazid and Maymun,[[In the printed and manuscript editions: "from Zayd" — the correct reading is "Yazid ibn al-Asamm," mentioned in the two previous chains.]] concerning His saying: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾, who both said: "When a man harvested his palm trees, he would bring the bunch, hang it on the side of the mosque, and the needy man would come and strike it with his stick, and eat whatever fell from it."

14012. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾. He said: "The gleanings of the ears of grain (laqt al-sunbul)." [[al-laqt (with a fatha on the lam and the qaf): and "luqat al-sunbul" (with a damma or fatha on the lam): that which the sickles miss and people pick up; it is the scattered remnants of the ears of grain.]]

14013. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from 'Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, from Mujahid, who said: "They used to hang the bunch in the mosque at the time of the harvest, and the weak would eat from it."

14014. And with the same chain, from Ma'mar, who said: Mujahid said: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾: "He feeds something at the time of its cutting."

14015. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾. He said: "The dighth, and what falls of the ears of grain."

14016. And with the same chain, from Salim, from Sa'id: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾. He said: "The fodder (al-'alaf)."

14017. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Shurayk, from Salim, from Sa'id, concerning His saying: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾. He said: "This was before the zakat, for the needy: the handful and the dighth for the fodder of his animal."

14018. Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Rifa'ah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, concerning His saying: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾. He said: "Whatever is little or much of it." [[The narration 14018: Muhammad ibn Rifa'ah ibn Tha'labah ibn Abi Malik al-Qurazi, trustworthy, whose biography is in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/1/82, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/254.]]

14019. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾. He said: "At the time of sowing, he gives a qabd, and at the time of cutting he gives a qabd,[[Perhaps it is "yu'ti al-qabdah" (he gives a handful), for that is what the language indicates; but it occurs thus in both places, and it is permissible though weak.]] and he leaves them, so they follow the traces of the cutting."

* *

Others said: This was something God commanded the believers before the time-limited charity was made obligatory upon them. Then it was abrogated (naskh, abrogation) by the known charity, so there is no obligation on any wealth, whatever it may be, whether crops or plantings, except the charity which God has imposed on it.

Mention of those who said this:

14020. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The tenth and half-tenth abrogated it."

14021. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Hafs narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hakam, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The tenth and half-tenth abrogated it."

14022. And with the same chain, from al-Hajjaj, from Salim, from Ibn al-Hanafiyyah, who said: "The tenth abrogated it, and the half-tenth."

14023. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Shurayk, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾. He said: "This was before the zakat. When the zakat was revealed, it abrogated it, and they gave the dighth."

14024. Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Shabbak, from Ibrahim: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾. He said: "They used to do that, until the tenth and half-tenth became the sunnah. When the tenth and half-tenth became the sunnah, it was abandoned." [[The narrations 14024–14025: Shabbak al-Dabbi al-Kufi, the blind. He narrated from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, and Abu al-Duha. He was narrated from by Mughirah ibn Miqsam, Fudayl ibn Ghazwan, and Nuhashl ibn Majma'. Ahmad said: "a trustworthy shaykh." His biography is in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/2/270; see also nos. 14027, 14030, 14031.]]

14025. Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Shabbak, from Ibrahim: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾. He said: "It is abrogated; the tenth and half-tenth abrogated it." [[The narrations 14024–14025: Shabbak al-Dabbi al-Kufi, the blind... (as above).]]

14026. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾. He said: "The tenth and half-tenth abrogated it."

14027. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mughirah, from Shabbak, from Ibrahim, who said: "The tenth and half-tenth abrogated it."

14028. And with the same chain, from Sufyan, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, who said: "The zakat abrogated it."

14029. And with the same chain, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, who said: "The zakat abrogated it: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾."

14030. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mughirah informed us, from Shabbak, from Ibrahim, concerning His saying: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾. He said: "This sūrah is Meccan; the tenth and half-tenth abrogated it." I said: "From whom?" He said: "From the scholars."

14031. And with the same chain, from Sufyan, from Mughirah, from Shabbak, from Ibrahim, who said: "The tenth and half-tenth abrogated it."

14032. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: As for ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾, they used to feed whoever passed by them on the day of the harvest or the gleaning. God abrogated it for them by the zakat, and what the earth produced was subject to a tenth and half-tenth.

14033. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, who said: "They used to give a small gift (yarkhasun) to their relatives among the polytheists." [[ "Rakhkha lahu min malihi rakhiyyah": when he gave him from his wealth a gift close to it, small.]]

14034. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from his father, from 'Atiyyah: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾. He said: "Its abrogation was the tenth and half-tenth. They used to give when they harvested and when they winnowed, and the tenth and half-tenth abrogated it."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings in this matter, in my view, is the saying of the one who said: This was an obligation which God imposed upon the believers concerning their food and fruits, which their crops and plantings produced; then God abrogated it by the obligatory charity and the known prescribed portion of the tenth and half-tenth. This is because all of them agree, without any disagreement among them, that the charity of the field is not taken except after threshing, cleaning and winnowing, and that the charity of dates is not taken except after their drying. [[In the printed edition: "ba'd al-jafaf" (after drying), which differs entirely from the manuscript. In the manuscript it was: "ba'd al-ahrār" (without dots), and this is the correct reading. It is said "jazza al-nakhl wa-al-tamr" and "ajazza al-nakhl wa-al-tamr": its dates dried, and it was time to cut it, i.e., to cut its fruit and harvest it.]]

So, if this is so, and His saying, may His praise be exalted: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾ indicates a command from God, may His praise be exalted, to give its due on the day of its harvest, and the day of its harvest is the day of its cutting and gathering, and the grain is undoubtedly in its ear on that day, and the dates, even if they are the fruit of palm trees or vines, have not yet fully dried and become dry, and the charity from the grain is taken only after its threshing, winnowing and cleaning, by measure, and the charity of dates is taken only after they are fully dry and desiccated, by measure: it is known that what is taken as charity after the time of harvest is other than what must be given to the needy on the day of harvest.

* *

If someone says: What would prevent you from holding that this is a command from God concerning wealth, a right apart from the prescribed charity?

It is said: Because it is not free of being either an obligatory duty or a voluntary act.

If it is an obligatory duty, then its course must be that of the prescribed charities, for whoever neglects to pay them to their recipients is sinful before his Lord and disobedient to His command. [[See the explanation of His saying "sinful before his Lord" in what has passed: 4:530, note; 3/6:92, note; 2/11:180, note; 3/11:328, note 2.]] And in the establishing of proof that there is no obligation from God on wealth after the zakat, binding as the zakat is binding, apart from what is binding of maintenance for those whom a man is obligated to support, there is an indication that this is not so.

Or it is a voluntary act. If it is so, then the choice in giving that to the owner of the field and the fruit would belong to him. And in the obligation imposed by those who hold that it is obligatory, there is an indication that this is not so.

Since the verse has been removed from the possibility of being meant as a recommendation (nadb), and since it is impossible for it to have a basis for an obligatory duty at this time, it is known that it is abrogated.

What further supports what we have said in this matter, as evidence for its soundness, is that He, may His praise be exalted, followed His saying: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾ with: ﴿And do not be wasteful; indeed He does not love the wasteful﴾. It is well known that among God's rulings concerning His servants, since the time-limited charity of fixed measure was made obligatory on their wealth, the one who collects it is their rulers and guardians. And if that is so, what is the meaning of forbidding the owner of the wealth from excess in giving that, when the collector is compelled, and he only takes the right which God has made obligatory on it?

* *

If someone supposes that this is only a prohibition from God to the one in charge of collecting that from the herdsmen, against transgressing upon the wealth of its owner and exceeding to take what he is not permitted to take, then the end of the verse, namely His saying: ﴿And do not be wasteful﴾, is joined to its beginning, namely His saying: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾. If the one forbidden from excess is the one in charge of receiving that, then it would follow that the one commanded to give it, the one forbidden from excess in it, would be the ruler.

That is a saying which, if anyone were to say it, would be outside the statement of all the people of interpretation (ta'wil), and contrary to the familiar form of address; and that suffices as a witness to its error.

* *

If someone says: What would prevent you from holding that the meaning of His saying: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾ is: "give its due on the day of its measuring," not on the day of its cutting and picking, [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "yawm fasilihi" with a fa'; the correct reading is with a qaf. "Qasala al-nabat yaqsiluhu qaslan, wa-iqtasalahu": he cut it while green.]] nor on the day of its gleaning and plucking? Do you know who among the people of interpretation said that? And that is what:

14035. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, concerning His saying: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾. He said: "On the day of its measuring."

14036. And Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from al-Hajjaj, from Salim al-Makki, from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, concerning His saying: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾. He said: "On the day of its measuring; he gives the tenth and half-tenth." [[The narration 14036: see what has passed, no. 13975.]]

* *

Along with others from whom the narration was already related in what has passed, with that meaning? [[See the earlier narrations from the beginning of the explanation of the verse.]] It is said: Because the day of its measuring is other than the day of its harvest. The meaning of those who hold this view must fall into one of two matters: either they have turned the meaning of "harvest" (al-hasad) toward the meaning of "measuring" (al-kayl), and that is what is not understood in the language of the Arabs, for "al-hasad" and "al-hasd" in their speech mean cutting and severing, not measuring; or they have turned the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾ toward: "give its due after the day of its harvest, when you have measured it," and that is contrary to the apparent sense of the revelation. For the command in the apparent sense of the revelation is to give its right from it on the day of its harvest, not after the day of its harvest. And there is no difference between one who says: "God meant by His saying ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾: after the day of its harvest," and another who said: "He meant by that: before the day of its harvest," for both are speaking in a way whose apparent indication of the revelation contradicts it.

* *

The Interpretation of His words: "And do not be extravagant. Indeed, He does not like the extravagant" (6:141)

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters differed concerning "extravagance" (al-israf) which God forbade in this verse, and concerning what is forbidden.

Some of them said: What is forbidden is that the owner of the palm trees, the crops, and the fruit... and the "extravagance" which God forbade in this verse is exceeding the measure in giving to the point of harming the owner of the property. [[See the explanation of "al-israf" above: 7:272, 579; 10:579; 10:242.]]

Those who said this:

14037. Amr ibn Ali related to us, who said: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman related to us, who said: Asim related to us, from Abu al-Aliyah, concerning His words: "And give its due on the day of its harvest and do not be extravagant," the verse. He said: They used to give something apart from the zakat, then they competed in extravagance [[tasarafu: meaning they exceeded in extravagance and vied with one another in it. This is a derivation of the language that you will hardly find in the lexicons, so note it in its place.]], so God revealed: "And do not be extravagant. Indeed, He does not like the extravagant."

14038. Al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman related to us, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Abu al-Aliyah: "And give its due on the day of its harvest," he said: They used to give on the day of the harvest something apart from the zakat, then they competed in it, they were extravagant [[In the printed edition: "wa-asrafu" with the conjunction waw; I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is a sound reading.]], so God said: "And do not be extravagant. Indeed, He does not like the extravagant."

14039. Al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman related to us, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Abu al-Aliyah: "And give its due on the day of its harvest," he said: They used to give something on the day of the harvest, then they were extravagant, so God said: "And do not be extravagant. Indeed, He does not like the extravagant."

14040. Al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: It was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who harvested a palm grove and said: No one will come today except that I feed him! So he fed people until evening, and he had no fruit left, so God said: "And do not be extravagant. Indeed, He does not like the extravagant."

14041. Ibn Wakic related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Bakr related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I said to Ata': "And do not be extravagant," does it mean: do not be extravagant in what is given on the day of the harvest, or in everything? He said: Yes! In everything; it forbids extravagance. [[Bala: see the use of "bala" not preceded by a negation, in earlier volumes 10:253, note 3, and the references there.]] He said: Then I returned to him after a while and said: What is His saying: "And do not be extravagant. Indeed, He does not like the extravagant"? He said: It forbids extravagance in everything. Then he recited: "Who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy" [Surah al-Furqan: 67].

14042. Amr ibn Ali related to us, who said: Yazid ibn Harun related to us, who said: Sufyan ibn Husayn informed us, from Abu Bishr, who said: People gathered around Iyas ibn Mu'awiyah in Kufa and asked him: What is al-saraf (extravagance)? He said: Whatever falls short of God's command is extravagance. [[In the printed edition: "What exceeds God's command is extravagance," which differs from the manuscript, where it reads "ma wazahu amr Allah fahuwa sarf," with the letter ha' placed over zay and a ta' marking doubt. The wording that is transmitted from Iyas ibn Mu'awiyah is: "Extravagance is what falls short of God's right" (Lisan: s-r-f), so it is clear to me that "ma wazahu" means "ma dun amr Allah," to match the other wording transmitted from Iyas. Abu Hayyan in his tafsir (4:238) wrote "Whatever you exceed God's command in is extravagance," and likewise al-Qurtubi (7:110). This is narrated as I have recorded it or in its meaning, from Mu'awiyah, may God be pleased with him.]]

14043. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, who said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "And do not be extravagant," do not give away your wealth so that you become poor.

* *

Others said: "Extravagance" which God forbade in this passage is withholding charity and the right that God commanded the owner of the property to give to its people, by His words: "And give its due on the day of its harvest."

Those who said this:

14044. Ibn Wakic related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Bakr related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah informed me, from Amr ibn Sulaym and others, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, concerning His words: "And do not be extravagant," he said: Do not withhold charity, lest you disobey. [[Report 14044: Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Sabrah al-Qurashi al-Amiri, a judge and jurist, who is abandoned (matruk). Ahmad said: "He used to fabricate hadith and lie." Ibn Jurayj said to him: "Write for me some of your hadith," and he wrote for him. Al-Waqidi said: "I saw Ibn Jurayj had included some of them in his books. He narrated much, but is not a proof." Biographed in al-Tahdhib and Mizan al-I'tidal 3:348. "Amr ibn Sulaym ibn Khallada al-Ansari al-Zurqi" was a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i), who narrated little. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

14045. Amr ibn Ali related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Zubriqan related to us, who said: Musa ibn Ubaydah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b: "And do not be extravagant. Indeed, He does not like the extravagant," and extravagance is not giving what is due. [[Report 14045: Musa ibn Ubaydah ibn Nashit al-Rabadhi, weak; his hadith is not written. He has appeared many times, the last being 11134. In the chain here, the manuscript and printed edition both read "Muhammad ibn Ubaydah," which is an undoubted error, since the one who narrates from him is Muhammad ibn al-Zubriqan, and he narrates from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and this is Musa ibn Ubaydah; this is the plain correction. The copyist has often written "Muhammad" in place of "Musa" in other names.]]

* *

Others said: This was addressed only to the ruler. He was forbidden to take from the owner of the property more than what God had obligated on his wealth.

Those who said this:

14046. Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: "And do not be extravagant," he said: He said to the ruler: "Do not be extravagant," do not take unjustly, so this verse was between the ruler and the people, meaning His words: "Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit," the verse.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in my judgment, is to say that God, may His remembrance be exalted, by His words "And do not be extravagant," forbade all the meanings of "extravagance," and did not single out one meaning over another.

Since that is so, and since "extravagance" in the speech of the Arabs means error in hitting the right in giving, either by exceeding its limit in excess, or by falling short of its required limit, it is known that one who scatters his wealth in rivalry, and gives it to people until his giving ruins him, is extravagant by exceeding God's limit to what [is not his]. [[In the printed edition: "exceeding God's limit to what kayyafahu lahu," and likewise in the manuscript, undotted, with no clear meaning, so I have dropped this phrase and written what is between brackets, which makes the sentence somewhat coherent.]] Likewise the one who falls short in spending where God obligated him to spend, such as withholding from him what he is obligated to give from it to the eligible recipients of zakat when it is due, or withholding from one whose maintenance God has obligated him to provide for his family and dependents what he is obligated to provide. Likewise the ruler who takes from his subjects what God has not permitted him to take. All these, in what they do of this, are extravagant, entering into the meaning of one who commits the extravagance God forbade by His words: "And do not be extravagant," in your giving from your wealth what ruins you, since what precedes it in the speech is a command from God to give what is obligatory to its people on the day of its harvest. The verse was revealed to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) because of a particular matter, and its ruling is applied generally; indeed, most verses of the Qur'an are like that. So likewise His words: "And do not be extravagant. Indeed, He does not like the extravagant."

Among the evidence for the soundness of what we have said about the meaning of "extravagance" is that it is as we have said, the words of the poet: [[He is Jarir.]]

They gave Hunaydah, who was driven by eight camels, and in their giving there is neither reproach nor extravagance. [[The first verse has passed with its takhrij and explanation above, 7:579.]]

By "sarf" he means: error in giving.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 142:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And of the livestock, some for carrying and some for fleece/for lying down upon⟩

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be remembered, says: He produced, of the livestock, what is for carrying and what is for spreading (furshan), in addition to what He produced of the trellised gardens and the untrellised ones.

* *

"Al-hamulah" is that which is carried upon, of camels and others.

"Al-farsh" is the young camels that have not reached the age at which they can be ridden.

* *

The people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: "Al-hamulah" is that which is carried upon of the mature camels and their likes, and "al-farsh" is their young ones which are not carried upon because of their youth.

Those who said this:

14047. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abd Allah, regarding His saying: ﴿hamulah and farsh﴾. He said: "Al-hamulah" are the mature camels; "farsh" are the young camels.

14048. ... And he said: My father narrated to us, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: "Al-hamulah" are the mature ones, and "al-farsh" are the young camels.

14049. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Israil, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, who said: "Al-hamulah" is that which is carried of the camels, and "al-farsh" is that which is not carried.

14050. And with this chain, from Israil, from Khusayf, from Mujahid: "Al-hamulah" is that which is carried of the camels, and "al-farsh" is that which is not carried.

14051. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding the saying of God: ﴿and farsh﴾. He said: the young camels.

14052. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abd Allah regarding His saying: ﴿hamulah and farsh﴾. He said: "Al-hamulah" are the mature ones, and "al-farsh" are the young ones.

14053. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Ibn Mas'ud regarding His saying: ﴿hamulah and farsh﴾: "Al-hamulah" is that which is carried of the camels, and "al-farsh" is the young ones.

14054. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abd Allah, that he said regarding this verse: ﴿hamulah and farsh﴾: "Al-hamulah" is that which is carried upon of the camels, and "al-farsh" is the young ones. Ibn al-Muthanna said: Muhammad said: Shu'bah said: "It was Sufyan who narrated to me, from Abu Ishaq."

14055. Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, who said: al-Hasan said: "Al-hamulah" are of the camels and the cattle.

* *

Some of them said: "Al-hamulah" is of the camels, and whatever is not "hamulah" is "farsh".

14056. Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan: ﴿hamulah and farsh﴾. He said: "Al-hamulah" is that which is carried upon, and "al-farsh" is its edges, meaning its young ones.

14057. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And of the livestock, some for carrying and some for farsh﴾: "Al-hamulah" is that which is carried of the camels, and "al-farsh" is the young camels, the weaned young and what is below that which is not carried.

* *

It is said: "Al-hamulah" is of the cattle and camels, and "al-farsh" is the sheep and goats.

* *

Others said: "Al-hamulah" is that which is carried upon of the camels, horses, mules and other than that, and "al-farsh" is the sheep and goats.

Those who said this:

14058. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And of the livestock, some for carrying and some for farsh﴾: As for "al-hamulah", it is the camels, horses, mules, donkeys, and everything that is carried upon; and as for "al-farsh", it is the sheep and goats.

14059. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas: "Al-hamulah" is of the camels and cattle, and "farsh": the goats and sheep.

14060. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿And of the livestock, some for carrying and some for farsh﴾: As for "al-hamulah", it is the camels and cattle. He said: As for "al-farsh", it is the sheep.

14061. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said, other than al-Hasan would say: "Al-hamulah" is the camels and cattle, and "al-farsh" is the sheep.

14062. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And of the livestock, some for carrying and some for farsh﴾: As for "al-hamulah", it is the camels. As for "al-farsh", it is the weaned young, the calves and the sheep. [[al-'Ajajil is the plural of 'ujul (with the ayn vowelled with a kasra, the jim either doubled or not, and the waw silent), which is 'ijl, the young of cattle.]] And whatever is carried upon is "hamulah".

14063. It was related from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿hamulah and farsh﴾: "Al-hamulah" is the camels, and "al-farsh" is the sheep.

14064. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from al-Hasan: ﴿and farsh﴾. He said: "Al-farsh" is the sheep.

14065. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿hamulah and farsh﴾: "Al-hamulah" is that which you ride, and "al-farsh" is that which you eat and milk: a sheep which is not carried; you eat its meat, and you make from its wool blankets and bedding.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement on this matter, in my view, is that it should be said: "Al-hamulah" is that which is carried of the livestock, because that is among its attributes when it is loaded, not that it is a name for it, like the camels, horses and mules. For if it is only named "hamulah" because it carries, then it is necessary that every livestock animal which carries on its back be a "hamulah". It is a collective noun with no singular from its own form, like "al-rakubah" and "al-jazurah". Likewise "al-farsh" is only an attribute of that whose body is light and close to the ground, and it is called "al-farsh". I believe it was named thus as a likeness to it in the evenness of its stature and its lightness close to the "farsh" of the earth, which is the level land that people tread upon.

As for "hamulah" with a damma on the ha', it means loads, and "humul" also with a damma on the ha'.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Eat of what God has provided you, and do not follow the steps of Satan; indeed he is to you a clear enemy﴾ (142)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be great, says: Eat of what God has provided you, O believers, so He made lawful to you the fruits of your crops and plantings, and the meat of your livestock, when some of that was forbidden by the polytheists against themselves, who made for God a share of what He had produced of the tilth and the livestock, and for Satan a share likewise, saying: "This is for God, by their claim, and this is for our partners." ﴿And do not follow the steps of Satan﴾, as the people of the Bahirah and the Sa'ibah followed them, so that you forbid to yourselves of the good provision of God what they forbade, thereby obeying Satan and disobeying the Merciful, as:

14066. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿and do not follow the steps of Satan﴾: Do not follow his obedience; these are sins for you, and they are obedience to the wicked one.

* *

= Indeed Satan is an enemy to you, seeking your destruction and turning you away from the path of your Lord = ﴿clear﴾: he has made his enmity plain to you, [[In the printed and manuscript: "abana lakum 'udwanahu" (he made his enmity clear to you); the correct reading is as given.]] by opposing your father with enmity, until he expelled him from the Garden through his cunning, and deceived him out of envy toward him and transgression against him. [[See the explanation of "steps of Satan" previously, 2:300-302 / 4:258.]]

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 143:

The interpretation of His words, ﴿eight pairs: of sheep two and of goats two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain? Inform me with knowledge, if you are truthful.﴾ (6:143)

Abu Ja'far said: This is a rebuke from God, may His praise be exalted, to those who associate others with Him, the idol-worshippers who worship images, who slit the ears of the camels (called *baḥā'ir*, the slit-eared she-camels), who let loose the *sawā'ib* (camels set free), and who designated the *waṣā'il* (sheep that bear twins in succession). It is also His instruction to His Prophet (ﷺ) and to the believers in Him, establishing the proof against them for their prohibitions of such things. He said to the believers in Him and in His Messenger: It is He who produced gardens, trellised and untrellised, and of the livestock He produced beasts of burden and [animals for] lying down. Then He, may His praise be exalted, explained the "beasts of burden" and the "[animals for] lying down," saying: ﴿eight pairs﴾.

* *

The word "eight" (*al-thamāniya*) is in the accusative because it is an explanation of ("a substitute for") "beasts of burden" and "[animals for] lying down." The meaning of the sentence is: "And of the livestock He produced eight pairs." When He first mentioned "beasts of burden" and "[animals for] lying down," He then clarified it afterward by saying: ﴿eight pairs﴾, according to that meaning.

* *

﴿Of sheep two and of goats two﴾: that makes four, because each of the two of each kind is a mate (*zawj*): the female of it is the mate of the male, and the male of it is the mate of the female. The same applies to goats and to the rest of the animals. Therefore He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿eight pairs﴾, just as He said: ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾ (51:49), because the male is a mate to the female and the female a mate to the male. Although the two of them are a pair, each of them is also a mate, just as He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿And He made from it its mate that he might find comfort in her﴾ (7:189), and as He said: ﴿Keep your wife to yourself﴾ (33:37). And as:

14067 – Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿Of sheep two﴾, a male and a female; ﴿and of cattle two﴾, a male and a female; ﴿and of camels two﴾, a male and a female.

* *

It is said of the two: "they are a pair" (*zawj*), as Labid said:

*From every curtained litter whose poles it shelters,*
*a pair, over which are its sheet and its embroidered curtain.*

[Note: This is from his famous *Mu'allaqa* ode, and this verse is at the beginning of the poem, describing the litters of the women of the tribe as they travel. *Al-maḥfūf* means the litter, enclosed by garments and rugs. *Al-'uṣiyy* means the wooden poles of the litter, which are shaded and covered by the garments and rugs. *Al-killa* means a thin veil. *Al-qiram* means a curtain that has designs, patterns and figures.]

* *

Then He said to them: Eat of what God has provided you of these fruits and meats, and ride these beasts of burden, O believers, and do not follow the steps of Satan by prohibiting what these ignorant people have forbidden without My command to them to do so.

= Say, O Muhammad, to those who have forbidden what they have forbidden of the tilth and livestock, following Satan, [namely] the idol-worshippers who claim that God forbade them what they have forbidden: ﴿Has He forbidden the two males, your Lord, O liars against God, of the sheep and goats?﴾ For if they claim that and affirm it, they have lied against themselves and revealed their ignorance. For if they say, "He has forbidden the two males of these," they would be obliged to forbid every pair of males among the young of sheep and goats, yet they enjoy the flesh of the males of them and their backs. In that lies the corruption of their claim and the refutation of their statement. ﴿Or the two females?﴾ For if they say, "Our Lord has forbidden the two females," they would be obliged to forbid to themselves the flesh of every female of the young of sheep and goats and their backs. In that too is a refutation of them, and a rejection of their claim that their Lord forbade this to them, since they used to enjoy the flesh of some of that and its backs. ﴿Or what the wombs of the two females contain?﴾ That is, "Or has He forbidden what the wombs of the two females contain," meaning the wombs of the female sheep and the female goat; that is why He said "the wombs of the two females." In that too, if they acknowledged it and said, "What the wombs of the two females contain has been forbidden to us," their statement would be proven false and their lie made clear, because by acknowledging that, they would be admitting that God forbade them the males and females of sheep and goats, that they eat their flesh or ride their backs, while they had been enjoying some of their males and females.

* *

The *mā* in His words ﴿or what the wombs of the two females contain﴾ is in the accusative, conjoined by it to "the two females" (*al-unthayayn*). [Note: See *Ma'ani al-Qur'an* of al-Farra', 1:360.]

* *

= ﴿Inform me with knowledge﴾: that is, say to them: "Inform me with knowledge of it, a sound knowledge: which of these has your Lord forbidden you, and how did He forbid it?" [Note: See the explanation of *al-naba'* (information) in the lexical indexes of earlier volumes, under the root n-b-'.] = ﴿if you are truthful﴾ in what you ascribe to your Lord of your claims and attribute to Him of your prohibitions.

* *

This is only an announcement from God, may His praise be exalted, to His Prophet that everything these polytheists said about that and attributed to God is a lie against God, and that He has not forbidden any of it, and that they only followed the steps of Satan in this and opposed His command.

* *

The people of interpretation (*ahl al-ta'wil*) have said something similar to what we have said about the interpretation of this.

Those who said so:

14068 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿eight pairs: of sheep two and of goats two﴾, the verse: all of this, I have not forbidden any of it, little or much, male or female.

14069 – Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿of sheep two and of goats two﴾. He said: Ask them: "Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain?" That is, I have not forbidden any of this = ﴿Inform me with knowledge if you are truthful﴾. And he mentioned the same regarding camels and cattle.

14070 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's words: ﴿eight pairs﴾, in the matter of what God forbade of the *baḥīra* (the slit-eared she-camel).

14071 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿eight pairs﴾. He said: This refers to what God forbade of the *baḥā'ir* and the *sawā'ib*. = Ibn Jurayj said: He says, "From where did you forbid this? From the side of the males or from the side of the females? Does not what the wombs of the two females contain consist only of a male or a female? So from where did the prohibition come?" Then they answered: "We found our fathers doing so."

14072 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿eight pairs: of sheep two and of goats two, and of cattle two and of camels two﴾. He says: There were sent down to you eight pairs from what I have enumerated, a male and a female. "Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain?" That is, what the wombs of the two females contain consists only of a male or a female; so I have not forbidden to you any male or female of the eight. This was mentioned only because of what they forbade of the livestock.

14073 – Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan: ﴿or what the wombs of the two females contain﴾. He said: What the womb carries.

14074 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿Has He forbidden the two males or the two females?﴾ He said: This is in response to their saying: ﴿What is in the bellies of these cattle is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives﴾ (6:139). He said: Ibn Zayd also said regarding His words: ﴿eight pairs: of sheep two and of goats two﴾: "the cattle" are the camels, cattle, sheep and goats; these are the "cattle" of which God said "eight pairs." He said: And he said regarding His words: ﴿These are cattle and tilth set apart (ḥijr)﴾ (6:138): we restrict them to whom we wish and from whom we wish. And His words: ﴿and cattle whose backs have been forbidden﴾: no one rides them. = ﴿and cattle over which the name of God is not mentioned﴾. Then He said: ﴿Has He forbidden the two males or the two females?﴾: which of these two has He forbidden to these people? That is, that they be lawful to these people and forbidden to those.

14075 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: ﴿eight pairs: of sheep two and of goats two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females? Or what the wombs of the two females contain?﴾ He means: does the womb contain only a male or a female? So do they forbid some and allow others?

14076 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: ﴿eight pairs: of sheep two and of goats two﴾. These are four pairs = ﴿and of camels two and of cattle two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females?﴾ He says: I have not forbidden any of that = ﴿Inform me with knowledge if you are truthful﴾. He says: All of it is lawful.

* *

*Al-ḍa'n* (sheep) is a collective noun with no singular of its own from its form, though *al-ḍa'n* may also be pluralized as *al-ḍa'īn* and *al-ḍi'īn*, like *al-sha'īr* and *al-shi'īr* (barley). The singular for its males is *ḍā'in*, the female is *ḍā'inah*, and the plural of *ḍā'inah* is *ḍawā'in*.

Likewise *al-ma'z* (goats) is a collective with no singular of its own, and so is *al-ma'zā*. As for *mā'iz*, its plural is *mawā'iz*.

[Note: All of these are with a fatha on the *ḍād*, the *shīn* and the *'ayn* (i.e., *ḍa'īn*, *shi'īr*, etc.), and then with a kasra on the *ḍād*, the *shīn* and the *'ayn*. They have stated this regarding *ḍa'īn* and *sha'īr*, and I have not been able to find it regarding *'abīd*, though it exists, God willing, as I recall. They said that the kasra on the *ḍād* is a Tamimi dialect form.]

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 144:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And of camels two, and of cattle two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain? Or were you witnesses when Allah enjoined this upon you? Who then is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah to lead people astray without knowledge? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (6:144)

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of His words, ﴿And of camels two, and of cattle two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain?﴾ is like the interpretation of His words, ﴿Of sheep two, and of goats two﴾ (6:143). These are four pairs, in the manner of the four pairs we explained earlier, of sheep and goats. Thus there are eight pairs, as He, may His praise be exalted, described.

* *

As for His words, ﴿Or were you witnesses when Allah enjoined this upon you? Who then is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah to lead people astray without knowledge?﴾, this is a command from Allah, may His praise be exalted, to His Prophet ﷺ to say to these ignorant polytheists whose accounts He related in these verses that have passed. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to him: Say to them, O Muhammad: Which of these, of the eight pairs, has your Lord forbidden to you, concerning which I ask you? If they answer you about something of what you ask them about, then say to them: Did you say, "Allah has forbidden this to you," as news conveyed to you by a messenger from your Lord? Or did you witness your Lord, see Him, and He enjoined upon you this which you say and attribute falsely to Allah? [[In the printed edition: "and you return upon Allah", and in the manuscript: "and you tarrur", and the correct reading is what I have established.]] For this that you say, your reporting about Allah that He has forbidden it, by what you claim, as you claim, can only be known through revelation from Him together with a messenger He sends to His creatures, or by hearing it from Him. So by which of these two ways did you know that Allah forbade that thus, through a messenger He sent to you? Then inform me with knowledge if you are truthful. Or did you witness your Lord, so that He enjoined that upon you and said to you, "I have forbidden that to you," so that you heard its prohibition from Him and His covenant to you concerning it? [[See the explanation of "witnesses" in the earlier word index (shahida), and the explanation of "enjoined" (wassa) earlier, 9:295, footnote 2, and the references there.]] But neither of these two matters occurred. He, may His praise be exalted, says: ﴿Who then is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah﴾, meaning: who is more greatly unjust to himself and further from the truth than one who fabricates a false saying against Allah, and adds to Him the prohibition of what He did not forbid and the permission of what He did not permit? [[See the explanation of "fabrication" (iftira') earlier, p. 153, footnote 5, and the references there.]] ﴿to lead people astray without knowledge﴾, meaning: to turn them away from His path. [[See the explanation of "going astray" (dalal) earlier in the word index (dalla).]] ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾, meaning: Allah does not grant success to the right course for one who fabricates against Allah, speaks falsehood and lies about Him, and adds to Him the prohibition of what He did not forbid, out of disbelief in Allah and denial of the prophethood of His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. [[See the explanation of "guidance" (huda) earlier in the word index (hada), and the explanation of "wrongdoing" (zulm) earlier in it (zalama).]] Like what was reported:

14077 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words, ﴿Or were you witnesses when Allah enjoined this upon you?﴾: "what you say."
