14078 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: They used to say (meaning those who took the baheera and the sa'iba): "Allah commanded this." So Allah said: ﴿Who then is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah to lead people astray without knowledge?﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 145:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Say: I find not in that which has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who would eat it, unless it be carrion, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine—for it is an abomination—or a transgression, over which the name of other than Allah has been invoked.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His majesty, may His praise be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to these people who have assigned to God a share of what He created of the tilth and the cattle, and to their associates among the gods and rivals a similar share, and who say, "These are cattle and tilth, forbidden; none may eat of them except whom we wish," by their claim, and who forbid the backs of other cattle, and who leave unmentioned the name of God over others of them, and who forbid some of what is in the bellies of some of their cattle to their females and make it lawful for their males, forbidding what God has provided for them, fabricating against God, and attributing what they forbid of that to God having forbidden it to them: Has there come to you from God a messenger with the prohibition of that upon you, so inform us of it? Or has God enjoined upon you its prohibition, by witnessing it yourselves, so that you heard from Him the prohibition of that upon you, and so you forbade it? For you are liars if you claim that, and you cannot claim it, for if you claimed it, the people would know your lie. ﴿Indeed, I find not in what has been revealed to me of His Book and the verses of His revelation﴾ [[See the explanation of "al-wahy" (revelation) in the preceding indices of language, under (w-h-y).]] anything forbidden to an eater who eats of what you claim He has forbidden of these cattle, whose forbidding of what He has forbidden to you of them you describe by your claim [[See the explanation of "ta'im" (eating) in the preceding passages: 5:342 / 10:576.]] = "unless it be carrion," which has died without slaughter; "or blood poured forth," which is that which is spilled; = or unless it be the flesh of swine; = ﴿for it is an abomination, or a transgression﴾. He says: or unless it be a transgression, meaning by that: or unless it be what has been slaughtered by a slaughterer from among the polytheists, the worshippers of idols, for his idol and his gods, so that the name of his idol is mentioned over it. For that slaughter is a transgression which God has forbidden and prohibited, and He forbade those who believe in Him from eating what is slaughtered in this way, since it is carrion.

* *

This is an announcement from God, may His praise be exalted, to the polytheists who disputed with the Prophet of God and his companions over the prohibition of carrion, with what they argued with them: that what they disputed concerning of that is the forbidden thing which God has forbidden, and that what they claimed God had forbidden is lawful, which God has made lawful, and that they are liars in attributing its prohibition to God.

* *

In accordance with what we have said on this, the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said so:

14079. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, regarding His saying: ﴿Say: I find not in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden﴾. He said: The people of the Jahiliyyah used to forbid some things and make others lawful. So He said: Say, I find not, of what you used to forbid and deem lawful, except this: ﴿unless it be carrion, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine—for it is an abomination—or a transgression, over which other than God has been invoked.﴾

14080. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, regarding His saying: ﴿Say: I find not in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden﴾, the verse. He said: The people of the Jahiliyyah used to deem some things lawful and forbid some things. So God said to His Prophet: Say, I find not in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden of what you used to deem lawful, except this. And there were things they used to forbid, and they are forbidden now.

14081. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Ibn Tawus, from his father: ﴿Say: I find not in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who would eat it﴾. He said: That which is eaten. I said: In the Jahiliyyah? He said: Yes! And thus he used to recite: ﴿unless it be carrion or blood poured forth﴾. Ibn Juraij said: Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr informed me, from Mujahid: ﴿Say: I find not in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden﴾. He said: Of what they used to eat in the Jahiliyyah; I find not forbidden of that to an eater who would eat it, except that it be carrion or blood poured forth.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿or blood poured forth﴾, its meaning is: or blood flowing and spilled. It is said of it: "I poured out his blood" when one spills it; I pour it forth, pouring; so it is blood poured forth, as Tarafa ibn al-'Abd said:

"By your grandfather, I did not satirize you... over the idols, upon which blood flows" [[Diwan of the Six Pre-Islamic Poets, p. 347, from three verses in which he apologizes to 'Amr ibn Hind, when it reached him that he had satirized him, and he threatened him; after it he says: "I had resolved upon that, when... and I fear your punishment if you prevail, and I did not betray, so that the words between us are multiplied."]]

And as 'Ubayd ibn al-Abras said:

"When women visited him from among them, they poured tears after the groaning" [[His Diwan, p. 45. In the printed edition and manuscript it read "mina" (from us), which is an undoubted error; the correct reading is that of the Diwan, from his qasida in which he rebuked his wife when she turned away from him in his old age and grew white-haired, and she mocked him with her eyebrows; so he reminded her of his past in play, youth and war... The verses describe a spear that struck a man of nobility, the wound pierced him, and women visiting the wounded man wept after the groaning.]] meaning: they poured out, and let flow the tears.

* *

In His stipulation, may His praise be exalted, regarding blood, when He informed His servants of its prohibition, that only the blood that is poured forth is meant, not other than it, is clear evidence that what is not poured forth is lawful and not impure. [[Context: "In His stipulation ... the blood poured forth ... clear evidence."]] Like that which:

14082. Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr, from 'Ikrimah: ﴿or blood poured forth﴾. He said: Were it not for this verse, the Muslims would have pursued the veins as the Jews pursued them.

14083. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ikrimah, similarly, except that he said: The Muslims would have pursued.

14084. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ikrimah, similarly.

14085. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' informed us, from 'Imran ibn Hudayr, from Abu Mijlaz, concerning a cooking pot in which redness of blood appears. He said: God only forbade the poured-forth blood.

14086. Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from 'Imran ibn Hudayr, from Abu Mijlaz, who said: I asked him about blood and what smears the slaughtering place of the head, and about a pot in which redness is seen? He said: God only forbade the poured-forth blood.

14087. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿or blood poured forth﴾. He said: Blood is forbidden when it is poured forth; but meat mixed with blood is no harm.

14088. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Say: I find not in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who would eat it, unless it be carrion or blood poured forth﴾. He said: That is, spilled.

14089. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, Ibn Dinar informed me, from 'Ikrimah: ﴿or blood poured forth﴾. He said: Were it not for this verse, the Muslims would have pursued the veins of the flesh as the Jews pursued them.

14090. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'A'ishah: that she did not see any harm in the flesh of beasts of prey, and that redness and blood appearing on the pot was harmful; and she recited this verse: ﴿Say: I find not in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who would eat it﴾... the verse. [[The report: 14090 - Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 3:415 mentioned this report and said it is "sahih gharib" (authentic but strange).]]

14091. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, who said: al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from 'A'ishah, who said, mentioning this verse: ﴿or blood poured forth﴾: I said: Indeed the cooking pot shows yellowness in its water. [[The report: 14091 - This is a truncated report, undoubtedly; the preceding one explains it, as it is another chain for it. In the printed edition, the word "ma" before "fi maihā" was omitted; it is present in the manuscript, and I added what is between the brackets to make the phrase sound. I did not find the report elsewhere in this wording.]]

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "rijs" (abomination) earlier in this book, that it is impurity and filth, and what is disobedience to God, with its evidences, so that it suffices without repeating it in this place. [[See the explanation of "rijs" in the preceding passages: 10:564, 565 / 12:110–112.]]

Likewise the statement concerning the meaning of "fisq" (transgression), and in His saying: ﴿over which the name of other than God has been invoked﴾ — all of that has passed with its sufficient evidences for whoever has been granted understanding of it, without repetition or restatement. [[See the explanation of "fisq" in the preceding passages, p. 76, note 2, and the references there. And the explanation of "uhilla li-ghayri Allah bihi" in the preceding passages: 3:319–321 / 9:493.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying: ﴿unless it be carrion﴾.

Some of the readers of Medina, Kufa and Basra recited it: ﴿illā an yakūna﴾ with the yā' (masculine), ﴿maytatan﴾ with the yā' lightened and in the accusative, = on the basis that in "yakūna" there is an unnamed (implicit) subject, and "al-maytah" is its "fi'l" (predicate), [[The term "fi'l" here refers to the predicate of the subject, an ancient usage as you see; its meaning is that the predicate of the subject is as if it were its verb. You say "Muhammad qā'im" (Muhammad is standing), meaning that Muhammad performs the standing; this is a Kufan terminology.]] so it was put in the accusative as the "fi'l" of "yakūna", and they mentioned "yakūna" in the masculine, because of the masculine implicit pronoun in "yakūna".

* *

Some of the readers of Mecca and Kufa recited it: "illā an takūna", with the tā' (feminine), "maytatan", with the yā' of "al-maytah" lightened and in the accusative = and their meaning of putting "al-maytah" in the accusative is the meaning of the first group; and they made "takūna" feminine because of the femininity of "al-maytah", as one says: "innahā qā'imatun jāriyatuka" and "innahu qā'imun jāriyatuka", mentioning the unnamed once in the masculine and once in the feminine, because of the femininity of the noun that follows it.

* *

Some of the Medinese recited it: "illā an takūna maytatun", with the tā' in "takūna", and the yā' of "maytah" doubled and in the nominative = so they made "maytatun" the subject of "takūna", and made "takūna" feminine because of the femininity of "maytatun", and made "takūna" sufficient with the noun without the verb, because His saying "illā an takūna maytatun" is an exception, and the Arabs in exception are content with nouns without verbs, saying: "qāma al-qawm illā an yakūna akhāka" and "illā an yakūna akhūka", so they do not bring a verb after "yakūna", and they make it self-sufficient with the noun, as one says: "qāma al-qawm illā akhāka" and "illā akhūka", [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:360–363, where this topic is fully treated.]] so the noun after the particle of exception does not need a verb. [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "fa-lā ya'taddu al-ism alladhi ba'da harf al-istithna' nafalan" ("nafal" is an unclear reading in the manuscript, and the expression has no meaning); the correct reading is, God willing, what I have adopted. "Iftaqada al-shay'" means to seek something; and his saying "fi'lan" is the "predicate of the subject", as I explained in the preceding note on p. 195 note 2; and I inferred the correctness of this reading from al-Farra's words in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:361: "As for one who puts 'maytah' in the nominative, he makes 'yakūna' its verb, content with 'yakūna' without a verb. Likewise 'yakūna' in all exception does not need a verb..." So his saying "does not need a verb" is the meaning of what I have written: "does not need the noun after the particle of exception to have a verb".]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in this matter, in my view, is: ﴿illā an yakūna﴾ with the yā', ﴿maytatan﴾, with the yā' lightened and "al-maytah" in the accusative, because what is in "yakūna" refers to a masculine (the referent being masculine) [[See the explanation of "al-maytah" in the preceding passages, and its lightening and doubling of the yā' in the preceding passages: 3:318, 319 / 6:310 / 9:492.]] = and it is only: Say, I find not in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who would eat it, unless that be carrion or blood poured forth.

* *

As for the recitation "maytatun" in the nominative, although it is not an error in Arabic, it is not the correct recitation in this place. For God says: ﴿or blood poured forth﴾, and there is no disagreement among all in reciting "al-dam" (blood) in the accusative; and so it is in the copies of the Qur'an of the Muslims, and it is conjoined to "al-maytah". Since that is so, it is known that if "al-maytah" were in the nominative, then "al-dam" and His saying "or transgression" would be in the nominative too; but they are in the accusative, so they are conjoined to it in the accusative.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor transgressing, indeed your Lord is Forgiving, Merciful﴾ (145)

Abu Ja'far said: We have mentioned the disagreement of the people of interpretation regarding His saying: ﴿whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor transgressing﴾, and the correct statement on it in our view has passed in this book, in the chapter of al-Baqarah, sufficient to avoid repeating it here [[See the explanation of that in the preceding passages: 3:321–327, and the explanation of the words of the verse in the preceding indices of language.]]: that its meaning is: whoever is compelled to eat what God has forbidden of eating carrion, blood poured forth, the flesh of swine, or what has been invoked over other than God, neither desiring it in his eating for pleasure, without necessity of hunger, nor transgressing in his eating by exceeding what God has limited and permitted him to eat, namely that he eats of it only what averts from himself the fear of destruction by abandoning eating; he does not go beyond that to more; there is no blame upon him for what he eats of that. ﴿Indeed God is Forgiving﴾, regarding what he did of that, covering it, leaving off punishing him for it, and had He willed, He would have punished him for it; ﴿Merciful﴾, by permitting him to eat that when he is in need of it, and had He willed, He would have forbidden it to him and prevented him from it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 146:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And to those who were Jews We prohibited every animal with claws﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We prohibited to the Jews [[See the explanation of "hada" (Jews) above, vol. 10: 476, note 1, and the references there.]] "every animal with claws", which means, among beasts and birds, whatever does not have split toes, such as camels, ostriches, geese and ducks.

* *

Those who held the view of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

14092- Al-Muthanna and Ali ibn Dawud told me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih told me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And to those who were Jews We prohibited every animal with claws﴾, that it is the camel and the ostrich.

14093- Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And to those who were Jews We prohibited every animal with claws﴾. He said: The camel, the ostrich, and similar animals.

4094- Ibn Wakf'i told us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam told us, from Sharik, from Ata', from Sa'id: ﴿And to those who were Jews We prohibited every animal with claws﴾. He said: It is that which does not have split toes.

14095- Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Azdi told me, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman told us, from Sharik, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His saying: ﴿And to those who were Jews We prohibited every animal with claws﴾. He said: Everything with separated toes, and among them the rooster. [[His words: "everything with separated toes, and among them the rooster" are as they stand in the manuscript. What came to the mind of those who published the tafsir earlier was that the correct reading is "not with separated toes", to match what precedes and follows. But I found Ibn Kathir in his tafsir, vol. 3: 417, saying: "And in a narration from him: 'Every one with separated toes, and among them the rooster'", so I preferred the reading of the manuscript and the printed edition.]]

14096- Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: ﴿every animal with claws﴾: the ostrich and the camel.

14097- Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, similarly.

14098- Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada regarding His saying: ﴿And to those who were Jews We prohibited every animal with claws﴾. It was said: the camel, the ostrich, and what resembles them among birds and fish.

14098- Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, saying: Ma'mar told us, from Qatada: ﴿every animal with claws﴾. He said: The camels and the ostriches; the claw of the camel's hand and foot, and the ostrich likewise. And He also prohibited to them from birds the duck and similar, and everything that does not have split toes.

14099- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "As for every animal with claws", it is the camel and the ostrich.

14100- Al-Harith told me, saying: Abd al-Aziz told us, saying: A shaykh told us, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿And to those who were Jews We prohibited every animal with claws﴾. He said: The ostrich and the camel, "shaqqan shaqqan" (split by split). I said: "What is shaqqan shaqqan?" He said: Whatever its legs are not spread apart, the Jews do not eat it, such as the camel and the ostrich. Chickens and sparrows the Jews eat, because their legs are spread apart.

14101- Al-Qasim told us, saying: Al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿every animal with claws﴾. He said: The ostrich and the camel, "shaqqan shaqqan". I said to al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, and he narrated it to me: What is "shaqqan shaqqan"? He said: Everything among the legs of beasts that is not spread apart. He said: And whatever is spread apart, the Jews eat it. He said: The legs of chickens and sparrows are spread apart, so the Jews eat them. He said: The leg of the camel, its sole, is not spread apart, nor is the ostrich's sole, nor the leg of the waziyna, [[al-Wazzina" (with fatha on the waw and shadda on the zay with kasra) is the goose, and its plural is "al-wuzzin", like it in pattern without the ha'.]] so the Jews do not eat the camel, the ostrich, or the wuzzin, nor anything whose leg is not spread apart. Likewise, they do not eat the wild donkey.

* *

Ibn Zayd used to say about this:

14102- Yunus told me with it, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And to those who were Jews We prohibited every animal with claws﴾: only the camel. [[In the printed edition: "faqat" (only), and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is entirely correct. One says "ma lahu ila 'ashara qatt" (with fatha and sukun on the ta') and "qatt" (with shadda on the ta' and its kasra), meaning: exactly, and not more than that, in the sense of "hasb" (just).]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Of the two sayings on this matter, the more correct is the saying we have mentioned from Ibn Abbas and those who said the like of his statement, because Allah, mighty is His praise, informed that He prohibited to the Jews every animal with claws. It is not permissible to exclude anything from the generality of this report except what the scholars unanimously agree is excluded from it. Since that is the case, and the ostrich and every beast or bird that has a claw not split into toes are included in the apparent sense of the revelation, it is required to judge that it is included in the report, since no report from Allah or from His Messenger came to say that some of it is not included in the verse, and the majority of the community agreed that it is included.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And of the cattle and sheep We prohibited to them their fats, except what their backs carried﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed regarding the "fats" which Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, informed that He prohibited to the Jews from cattle and sheep.

Some of them said: They are only the fat of the kidney-covering (al-thurub). [[al-Thurub" is the plural of "thurb" (with fatha then sukun), which is thin fat that covers the stomach and intestines.]]

Mention of those who said that:

14103- Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada: ﴿And of the cattle and sheep We prohibited to them their fats﴾, the thurub. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: May Allah fight the Jews! Allah prohibited to them the thurub, then they sold its price and ate it! [[The report: 14103 is the khabar narrated by Qatada as a mursal; al-Bukhari narrated it with its chain as marfu' (Fath 4: 344, 345), with something similar, and the group narrated it. See the following note.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, that was every fat that was not mixed with bone nor upon bone.

Mention of those who said that:

14104- Al-Qasim told us, saying: Al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said regarding His saying: ﴿We prohibited to them their fats﴾: He only prohibited to them the thurb, and every fat that was like that, not on bone.

* *

Others said: Rather, that is the fat of the thurb and the kidneys.

Mention of those who said that:

14105- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi regarding His saying: ﴿We prohibited to them their fats﴾: the thurb and the fat of the two kidneys. The Jews used to say: Israel only prohibited it, so we prohibit it.

14106- Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿We prohibited to them their fats﴾: He only prohibited to them the thurub and the two kidneys. [So it is in my book from Yunus, and I think it is: "al-kuli" (the kidneys).]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement on this is to say: Allah informed that He had prohibited to the Jews the fats of cattle and sheep, except what He excluded from them, namely what their backs carried, or the intestines, or what is mixed with bone. So every fat other than what Allah excluded in His Book from cattle and sheep was prohibited to them.

The reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) have been consistent in agreement with this, namely his saying: "May Allah fight the Jews! The fats were prohibited to them, so they melted them, then sold them and ate their price." [[Narrated by the group; see (Fath 4: 344, 345). "Jamala al-shahm" means he melted it and extracted its grease. "Al-jamil" is melted fat.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿except what their backs carried﴾, it means: except the fat of the flank and what clings to the back, for these were not prohibited to them.

* *

Those who held the view of the people of interpretation said the same as what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

14107- Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿except what their backs carried﴾, meaning: the fat that clings to the back.

14108- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: as for "what their backs carried", it is the rump-fat (al-alyat).

14108m- Ibn Wakf'i told us, saying: Abu Usama told us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, who said: The rump, of what their backs carried.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿or the intestines﴾

Abu Ja'far said: "Al-hawaya" is a plural whose singular is "hawaya'", "hawiya", and "hawiyya", and it is what gathers in the belly, coiling and curving, and it is "banat al-laban" and it is "al-mabi'r" (the dung-passage), and it is called "al-marabid", and in it are the intestines. [[Al-rabd" (with two fathas) and "al-mirbad" (with fatha on the mim, and fatha or kasra on the ba'), and "al-rabid" is the gathering of the intestines, or what coils within the intestines of the belly. "Banat al-laban" is what is small of the intestines. See the following report no. 14121.]]

* *

The meaning of the speech: And of the cattle and sheep We prohibited to them their fats, except what their backs carried, or what the intestines carried. So "al-hawaya" is in the nominative, conjoined to "al-zuhur" (the backs), and the "ma" after "illa" is in the accusative as an exception from "al-shuhum" (the fats). [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 363.]]

* *

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

14109- Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya told me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿or the intestines﴾, and it is the dung-passage.

14110- Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding God's saying: ﴿or the intestines﴾, he said: the dung-passage.

14111- Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "al-hawaya", the dung-passage and the marbad.

14112- Ibn Wakf'i told us, saying: Abu Usama told us, from Shibl, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿or the intestines﴾, he said: the dung-passage.

14113- Ibn Wakf'i told us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman told us, from Sufyan, from Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿or the intestines﴾, he said: the mabi'r.

14114- Ibn Wakf'i told us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam told us, from Sharik, from Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿or the intestines﴾, he said: the mabi'r.

14115- Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada: ﴿or the intestines﴾, he said: the dung-passage.

14116- Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿or the intestines﴾, he said: the dung-passage.

14117- Ibn Wakf'i told us, saying: Abu Usama and al-Mihbari told us, from Jawbar, from al-Dahhak who said: the dung-passage.

14118- I was told by al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿or the intestines﴾: meaning the bellies other than the thurub.

14119- Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿or the intestines﴾: it is the dung-passage.

14120- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: ﴿or the intestines﴾, he said: the mabi'r.

* *

Ibn Zayd said about this:

14121- Yunus told me with it, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿or the intestines﴾, he said: "al-hawaya" are the marabid in which the intestines are, situated in its middle, and they are "banat al-laban", and in the speech of the Arabs they are called "al-marabid".

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿or what is mixed with bone﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And of the cattle and sheep We prohibited to those who were Jews their fats, apart from what their backs carried, or what their intestines carried, for We made that lawful to them; and except what is mixed with bone, which is also lawful to them.

* *

He returned His saying ﴿or what is mixed with bone﴾ to His saying ﴿except what their backs carried﴾, so the "ma" in His saying ﴿or what is mixed with bone﴾ is in the accusative position, conjoined to the "ma" in His saying ﴿except what their backs carried﴾. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 363.]]

* *

By His saying ﴿or what is mixed with bone﴾ He meant the fat of the rump and the flank, and what is similar to that, as:

14122- Al-Qasim told us, saying: Al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿or what is mixed with bone﴾, he said: the rump-fat with the coccyx, [[al-'Usus" is the bone of the tailbone end.]] so it is lawful. And everything in the legs, flank, head and eye that is mixed with bone is lawful.

14123- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: ﴿or what is mixed with bone﴾, that which was fat upon bone.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿That We requited them for their rebellion, and indeed We are truthful﴾ (146)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So this which We prohibited to those who were Jews of the livestock and birds with unsplit claws, and of the cattle and sheep, what We prohibited to them of their fats which we mentioned in this verse, We prohibited it to them as a punishment from Us upon them and as a recompense for their evil deeds and their rebellion against their Lord, [[See the explanation of "jaza" in the lexical indices above (jaza), and the explanation of "baghy" above, vol. 2: 342 / 4: 281 / 6: 276.]] as:

14124- Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada: ﴿That We requited them for their rebellion, and indeed We are truthful﴾: Only that was prohibited to them as a punishment for their rebellion.

14125- Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿That We requited them for their rebellion﴾: We did that to them because of their rebellion.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and indeed We are truthful﴾, it means: and indeed We are truthful in this report of Ours about these Jews, concerning what We prohibited to them of the fats and flesh of the cattle and birds which We mentioned that We prohibited to them, and in other of Our reports; and they are liars in their claim that this was prohibited only by Israel upon himself, and that they prohibited it only because Israel prohibited it upon himself.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 147:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿So if they deny you, say: "Your Lord is possessed of vast mercy; and His punishment will not be averted from the guilty people."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His saying, may His praise be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "If they deny you, O Muhammad" [In the printed edition: "kadhdhabukum" (you all deny you), and the correct reading from the manuscript is "kadhdhabuka."] — these Jews, concerning what We informed you, that We prohibited for them and made lawful for them, as We have explained in this verse — "then say: Your Lord is possessed of vast mercy," toward us and toward whoever among His servants believes in Him, and toward others of His creation, "vast," encompassing all His creation [See the explanation of "wasi'" (vast) above, vol. 11, p. 489, footnote 2, and the references there], the good-doer and the wrongdoer alike. He does not hasten to punish those who disbelieve in Him, nor those who disobey Him with retribution, nor does He forgo the honour of those who believe in Him and obey Him, nor deprive them of the reward of their deeds, out of mercy from Him toward both groups. But His might — that is, His force and His punishment [See the explanation of "al-ba's" (might) above, vol. 11, p. 357, footnote 1, and the references there] — is not turned back when He lets it fall in His anger upon the guilty; nothing can avert it from them. And "the guilty" (al-mujrimun) are those who commit crimes, who acquire sins and perpetrate evil deeds. [See the explanation of "al-mujrim" (the guilty one) above, p. 93.]

* *

And those who interpret the Qur'an said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

14126. Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿So if they deny you﴾ — the Jews.

14127. al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿So if they deny you﴾ — the Jews; ﴿say: Your Lord is possessed of vast mercy﴾.

14128. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: The Jews used to say: "Israel only prohibited it" — meaning the tharb (the membrane covering the intestines) and the fat of the two kidneys — "so we prohibit it." That is His saying: ﴿So if they deny you, say: Your Lord is possessed of vast mercy; and His punishment will not be averted from the guilty people.﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 148:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿The idolaters will say: "Had God willed, we would not have associated anything with Him, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything." Likewise did those before them deny until they tasted Our might﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, may His praise be exalted, ﴿The idolaters will say﴾, meaning those who ascribe equals to God, the idols and images, from among the polytheists of Quraysh, ﴿Had God willed, we would not have associated﴾ — He says: they say this, seeking to shield themselves from submitting to the truth with falsehood as argument, after the truth had become clear to them and they knew the falsity of what they were upholding of their polytheism and their prohibition of what they used to forbid of the tilth and the livestock, as God, may His remembrance be exalted, has explained in the verses before it: ﴿And they assign to God a share of what He has created of the tilth and the livestock﴾, and what follows it. Their meaning: Had God desired from us that we believe in Him and single Him out in worship apart from the idols and the deities, and permit what He has forbidden of the baḥā'ir, the sawā'ib and other of our property, we would not have set up partners with God, nor would our fathers before us have done so, nor would we have forbidden what we forbid of these things which we persist in forbidding, because He is able to come between us and that, so that there is no path for us to do any of that: either by compelling us to believe and abandon associating with Him, and to say the permission of what we have forbidden; or by granting us grace through His guidance, so that we would come to acknowledge His oneness and abandon worshipping what is other than Him of rivals and idols, and to permit what we have forbidden. But He was content with us in what we are upon of worshipping idols and images, and taking partners in worship with Him as rivals, and He willed what we forbid of the tilth and the livestock, so He did not come between us and what we are upon of that.

God said, refuting them in their saying — "Indeed God is content with us in what we are upon of polytheism and forbidding what we forbid" — and rejecting the falsehood of the argument they made in this matter: ﴿Likewise did those before them deny﴾. He says: just as these polytheists, O Muhammad, denied what you brought them of truth and clarity, so did those before them of the sinful peoples who transgressed against their Lord deny what their prophets brought them of God's signs and clear proofs, and rejected their counsels. ﴿Until they tasted Our might﴾ — He says: until they provoked us, so we became angry with them, and We inflicted Our might upon them, and they tasted it, and by their tasting it they perished, and they lost this world and the next. [See the explanation of "tasted" earlier: 11:420, note 1, and the references there.] He says: these latter ones are being made to follow their path, if they do not turn back, believe and affirm what I have brought them from their Lord.

* *

Those who said the same as what we have said in this matter include the people of interpretation.

Mentioning those who said that:

14129 — Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Had God willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers﴾, and He said: ﴿Likewise did those before them deny﴾, then He said: ﴿Had God willed, they would not have associated﴾. They said: "Our worship of the deities brings us near to God in nearness", so God informed them that they would not bring them near. And His saying: ﴿Had God willed, they would not have associated﴾ — God, glorified is He, says: Had I willed, I would have gathered them all upon guidance.

14130 — Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿nor have we forbidden anything﴾, he said: the saying of Quraysh — meaning: God forbade this baḥīra and sā'iba.

14131 — Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿nor have we forbidden anything﴾ — the saying of Quraysh without certainty: that God forbade this baḥīra and sā'iba.

* *

If someone says: What is your proof that God, exalted is He, only denied the saying of these polytheists, their saying "God is content with us worshipping idols, and desires from us the prohibition of what we have forbidden of the tilth and the livestock," and not that His denial of them was on their saying: ﴿Had God willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything﴾, and on their description of Him that He willed their polytheism, their fathers' polytheism, and their prohibition of what they used to forbid?

It is said to him: The evidence for that is His saying: ﴿Likewise did those before them deny﴾. He, may His praise be exalted, informed about them that in denying their prophet Muhammad ﷺ in what he brought them from God — prohibiting the worship of anything other than God, may His remembrance be exalted, and forbidding other than what God forbade in His Book and on the tongue of His Messenger — they followed the path of their predecessors from the bygone nations who denied God and His Messenger. And their denial was only of one denied; and if that were a report from God of their lying in their saying "Had God willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers," He would have said "Likewise did those before them lie" with the "dhal" lightened, and would have attributed to them in that saying lying against God, not denial — along with many other reasons whose mention would lengthen the book; and what we have mentioned is sufficient for whoever is granted understanding of it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Say: "Have you any knowledge that you can produce for us? You follow only conjecture, and you merely guess."﴾ (148)

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to these who ascribe equals to their Lord, the idols and images, who forbid what they forbid of the tilth and the livestock, who say: ﴿Had God willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything﴾, but He was content with us in what we are upon of polytheism and forbidding what we forbid: "Have you," — by your claim that you make against God, that He is content with your associating others in His worship, and with your forbidding of your property what you forbid — "knowledge" of certainty, from a report whose transmitter cuts off excuse, or a proof that necessitates certainty for us, from knowledge, "that you may produce it for us" — meaning: that you may make it manifest to us and clarify it, as we have shown you the points of error in your saying and your action, and the contradiction and impossibility of that in reason and in what is heard [See the explanation of "ikhrāj" (bringing forth) earlier: 2:228.] ﴿You follow only conjecture﴾ — he says to him: Say to them: You, O polytheists, say what you say, and worship what you worship of idols and images, and forbid what you forbid of the tilth and the livestock, only by conjecture and supposition that it is true and that you are upon the truth, and it is false, and you are upon falsehood; ﴿and you merely guess﴾ — meaning: "and you," and you in all of that are only ﴿guessing﴾, meaning: you merely fabricate falsehood against God, by conjecture without the certainty of knowledge or clear proof. [See the explanation of "takhruṣ" (guessing) earlier: p. 65.]

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Say: "To God belongs the conclusive proof. So if He had willed, He would have guided you all."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these who ascribe equals to their Lord, worshipping idols and images, and who utter lies against their Lord regarding their prohibition of what they have forbidden of the tilth and the cattle: if they are unable to establish proof when you say to them, "Do you have any knowledge of what you claim against your Lord, so that you may produce it for us?" and to produce and display knowledge of that to you, and they are undoubtedly unable to do so and fall short in displaying it, because it is falsehood with no reality, then ﴿to God belongs﴾, who has forbidden you to associate anything with Him and to follow the steps of Satan regarding your wealth, the tilth and the cattle, ﴿the conclusive proof﴾, not you, O polytheists.

By "conclusive" (al-Balighah) is meant that it reaches its intended aim in its establishment against whoever is argued against by it among His creatures, and cuts off their excuse once it reaches them concerning that for which it was made a proof.

* *

﴿So if He had willed, He would have guided you all﴾: meaning, if your Lord had willed, He would have granted you all success in unanimously affirming His sole worship, disavowing rivals and deities, acknowledging the prohibition of what God has prohibited and the permission of what God has permitted, abandoning the following of Satan's steps, and other acts of obedience. But He did not will that, so He differentiated among His creatures in what He willed for them, so some of them are disbelievers and some are believers.

* *

A group of the people of interpretation said similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

14132. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, who said: There is no proof for anyone who disobeys God, but to God belongs the conclusive proof over His servants. And he said, regarding ﴿So if He had willed, He would have guided you all﴾: ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ [Al-Anbiya' 21:23].

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 150:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Say: Bring forth your witnesses who testify that Allah has forbidden this. And if they testify, do not testify with them, and do not follow the desires of those who denied Our signs and those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and they associate others with their Lord.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to these slanderers against their Lord, the worshippers of idols, who claim that Allah has forbidden them what they have forbidden of their tilth and cattle: ﴿Halumma shuhadaakum﴾ (come forth your witnesses), meaning: bring your witnesses who testify concerning Allah that He has forbidden you what you claim He has forbidden you. [[See the explanation of "al-shuhada'" (witnesses) in what has preceded in the lexical indices under the root "shahida".]]

* *

The people of al-'Aliyah in Tihamah use "halumma" as a single invariable form for the singular, dual and plural, and they mention it for feminine and masculine alike. So they say to one person: "Halumma, ya fulan," and likewise to two and to a group, and to a woman the same. Among the examples is the verse of al-A'sha:

"He had called his people with a call: 'Halumma to your affair, which has been cut off'"

[[Diwanuh 34; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:208. From a long qasidah, some verses of which have passed in various places; this verse is within the story of al-Hadr and what befell its people. I have left out transmitting its verses due to their length.]]

He recites: "halumma" and "halummu." As for the people of the lower region of Najd, they use the singular form for one, the dual for two, and the plural for a group. So it is said to a single man: "halumma," to a single woman: "halummi," to two: "halumma," to a group of men: "halummu," and to women: "halummna."

[[See Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:208, as this is the text of his statement.]]

* *

Allah said to His Prophet: ﴿Fa-in shahidu﴾ (And if they testify), meaning: O Muhammad, if they come to you with witnesses who testify that Allah has forbidden what they claim Allah forbade them, ﴿fa-la tashhad ma'ahum﴾ (then do not testify with them), for they are liars and false witnesses in their testimony about what they testify concerning Allah. He, exalted is His praise, addressed His Prophet ﷺ with this, while meaning his companions and the believers in him. ﴿Wa-la tattabi' ahwa'a alladhina kadhdhabu bi-ayatina﴾ (And do not follow the desires of those who denied Our signs), meaning: do not follow them in what they are upon of denial of Allah's revelation and His sending down, in forbidding what He has forbidden and permitting what He has permitted for them; rather, follow what has been revealed to you from the Book of your Lord, which falsehood does not reach from before it or behind it. ﴿Wa-alladhina la yu'minuna bil-akhirah﴾ (and those who do not believe in the Hereafter), meaning: and do not follow the desires of those who do not believe in the Hereafter, lest you deny what they deny of Allah's bringing His creation back to life after their death and raising them after their annihilation. ﴿Wa-hum bi-rabbihim ya'dilun﴾ (and they associate others with their Lord), meaning: and they, along with their denial of resurrection after death and their rejection of the establishment of the Hour, make equals to Allah the idols and images, taking them as equals to Him and adopting them as rivals whom they worship besides Him. [[See the explanation of "al-'adl" (equivalence) in what has preceded, 11:251-254.]]

* *

Groups of the people of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

14133 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿Halumma shuhadaakum alladhina yashhaduna anna Allaha harrama hadha﴾, he said: Say, "Show us those who testify that Allah has forbidden this, of what the Arabs forbade, and said: Allah commanded us with it." Allah said to His Messenger: ﴿Fa-in shahidu fa-la tashhad ma'ahum﴾.

14134 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿Halumma shuhadaakum alladhina yashhaduna anna Allaha harrama hadha﴾, he said: the baha'ir and the sawa'ib.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 151:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Say: "Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him, and be good to your parents."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these people who ascribe equals to their Lord, the idols and images, who claim that God has forbidden them what they themselves have forbidden of their crops and livestock, as I have mentioned to you in My revelation to you: "Come, O people," [[See the explanation of "come" (ta'alaw) above, 11:137, note 1, and the references there.]] "I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden, as a definite truth, not as falsehood, a fabrication of your conjecture, your lies and slander against God, by mere guesswork" [[In the printed edition: "like your conjecture about God", and I have retained what is in the manuscript.]] "but as a revelation from God that He sent to me, and a revelation He sent down to me: that you must not associate anything with God from His creation, nor set up idols and images as His equals, nor worship anything other than Him." ﴿And to be good to your parents﴾, that is, He enjoined goodness to parents. [The verb "enjoined" and "commanded" have been omitted, as the context indicates them and the listener understands their meaning.] [[See the explanation of "goodness" (ihsan) above, 2:292 / 8:334, 514 / 9:283 / 10:512, 576.]] We have explained this with its evidence earlier in the book. [[See above, 2:290–292 / 8:334.]]

* *

As for "an" (that) in His saying: ﴿that you associate nothing with Him﴾, it is in the nominative case, because the meaning of the speech is: "Say, come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: it is that you associate nothing with Him."

Given that this is its meaning, there are two possibilities for the word "tushrikū" (you associate):

- The jussive, by directing the "lā" to the sense of a prohibition.
- The accusative, by directing the speech to a declarative statement, with "tushrikū" in the accusative after "an lā", as one says: "I commanded you not to stand."

If you wish, you may make "an" in the accusative position, in apposition to "mā" and as its clarification, in which case "tushrikū" also carries the two grammatical possibilities that occur in it. "An" is then in the nominative position.

In that case the interpretation of the speech becomes: "Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: I will recite that you associate nothing with Him."

* *

If someone says: How is it permissible for "tushrikū" to be accusative after "an lā", or how is it permissible to construe "an lā tushrikū bihi" as a declarative statement, when it is coordinated with His saying: ﴿and do not kill your children out of poverty﴾, and what follows it of jussive prohibitions? It is said: That is permissible, just as He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿Say: I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit﴾, where He makes "an akūn" (that I be) a declarative statement and "an" a noun, then coordinates with it "and do not be among the associators" [Surat al-An'am: 14]. [[The phrase "and do not be among the associators" is missing from the printed and manuscript editions; I have inferred its inclusion from al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:364, and its omission would corrupt the meaning.]] And as the poet said: [[I do not know who said it.]]

He performed the pilgrimage and bequeathed Sulaymā's camels, [saying] that you should not see and should not speak to anyone,

and that her drink should never be cold.

[[Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra 1:364. It does not contain the third line; in its place is: "and do not walk in a far-off wilderness."]]

Here he makes "an lā tarā" (that you not see) a declarative statement, then coordinates with the prohibition, saying "wa lā tukallim" (and do not speak) and "wa lā yazal" (and let not cease).

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿and do not kill your children out of poverty; We provide for you and for them﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted is His remembrance, ﴿and do not kill your children out of poverty﴾, He means: do not bury your daughters alive, killing them out of fear of poverty for yourselves through their maintenance. God is the one who provides for you and for them; it is not your duty to provide for them, so do not fear for yourselves, because of their lives, inability to provide for their sustenance and subsistence.

* *

"Al-imlaq" (poverty) is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "I have run out of provisions, so I am destitute (amlaq), a state of destitution (imlaq)", which is when his provisions are exhausted, his wealth is gone, and he becomes bankrupt.

* *

Those of the exegetes said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Among those who said so:

14135. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, he said: Mu'awiya told me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and do not kill your children out of poverty﴾: "al-imlaq" is poverty; they killed their children out of fear of poverty.

14136. Bishr ibn Mu'adh told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿and do not kill your children out of poverty﴾, meaning: out of fear of destitution.

14137. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: ﴿and do not kill your children out of poverty﴾, he said: "al-imlaq" is poverty.

14138. Al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said regarding His saying: ﴿out of poverty﴾: their devils, commanding them to bury their children alive out of fear of want.

14139. It was reported to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying: ﴿out of poverty﴾, meaning: out of fear of poverty.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿and do not approach the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His remembrance, says: And do not approach the apparent of the forbidden things, [[See the explanation of "indecencies" (fawahish) above, 8:203, note 2, and the references there.]] which are openly among you, which you do not disavow committing, and the hidden of them, which you commit in secret, in concealment, not openly, for all of that is forbidden. [[See the explanation of "apparent" (zahara) and "hidden" (batana) above, pp. 72–75, then see the report no. 9075.]]

* *

It has been said: The reason it was said "do not approach what is apparent of the indecencies and what is hidden" is that they used to find some of the meanings of fornication reprehensible [but not others].

What they said in this is not refuted, but the evident indication of the revelation is a prohibition against the apparent and hidden of every indecency, and there is no report that cuts off the excuse to show it meant some and not all. It is not permissible to turn the apparent of God's Book into the hidden except by a proof that must be accepted.

* *

Those who said what we have mentioned, that the verse has a specific meaning:

14140. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: ﴿and do not approach the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden﴾. As for "what is apparent of them", it is the prostitutes of the shops; as for "what is hidden", it is what is concealed. [[The "prostitutes of the shops": prostitutes would take a shop bearing a banner, as a sign that they were prostitutes. See the earlier report no. 13801.]]

14141. It was reported to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying: ﴿and do not approach the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden﴾: The people of the Jahiliyya would conceal fornication, considering it lawful as long as it was secret. So God forbade both its secret and its public forms. ﴿What is apparent of them﴾ means the public; ﴿and what is hidden﴾ means the secret. [[Report 14141: this report was mentioned earlier as no. 13802.]]

14142. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, he said: Mu'awiya told me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and do not approach the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden﴾: He said: In the Jahiliyya they saw no harm in fornication in secret, but found it reprehensible in public, so God forbade fornication both in secret and in public.

* *

Others said in this what we have said.

Among those who said so:

14143. Bishr ibn Mu'adh told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada: ﴿and do not approach the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden﴾: its secret and its public.

14144. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la told me, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, similarly.

* *

Others said: "What is apparent" is marrying mothers and the wives of fathers, "and what is hidden" is fornication.

Among those who said so:

14145. Ibn Wakî' told us, he said: My father told us, from his father, from Khusayf, from Mujahid: ﴿and do not approach the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden﴾, he said: "What is apparent" is combining two sisters and a man marrying his father's wife after him; "and what is hidden" is fornication. [[Report 14145: this was mentioned earlier as no. 13803.]]

* *

Others said in this:

14146. Ishaq ibn Ziyad al-'Attar al-Nasri told me, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Balkhi told us, he said: Tamim ibn Shakir al-Bahili told us, from Isa ibn Abi Hafsa, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿and do not approach the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden﴾: "What is apparent" is wine, "and what is hidden" is fornication. [[Report 14146: I have not found a biography of "Ishaq ibn Ziyad al-'Attar al-Nasri"; the printed edition has "al-Basri", and I have retained what is in the manuscript. As for "Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Balkhi al-Jawhari", I have found only one entry in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/195, which says: "He narrated from Mutarrif ibn Mazin, Abu Umayya ibn Ya'la, Qirat the cupper, Muhammad ibn Harb al-Abrash, and Isa ibn Yunus. My father wrote from him in al-Rayy." As for "Tamim ibn Shakir al-Bahili" and "Isa ibn Abi Hafsa", I have found no biography or mention of either.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿and do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right. That is what He has enjoined upon you, that perhaps you will understand (151)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him﴾, ﴿and do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right﴾, meaning by the soul which God has forbidden to kill, the soul of a believer or of one under covenant. And His saying: ﴿except by right﴾ means: by what He has permitted it to be killed for: that one who kills a soul is killed in retribution for it, or one who commits adultery while married is stoned, or one who apostatizes from his true religion is killed. That "right" by which God, exalted is His praise, permitted the killing of the soul which He forbade the believers to kill is what is meant. ﴿That﴾, meaning these matters about which our Lord has enjoined upon us that we should not approach them and should not abandon them, are the matters He has enjoined upon us and upon the unbelievers, that we should all act upon them. ﴿That perhaps you will understand﴾ means: He enjoined that upon you so that you would understand what your Lord has enjoined upon you. [[See the explanation of "enjoined" (wasa) above, p. 189, note 1, and the references there.]]

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 152:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And do not approach the property of an orphan except in the best manner until he reaches his maturity﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, ﴿And do not approach the property of an orphan except in the best manner﴾, He means: do not approach his property except in what makes it sound and increases it, as:

14147 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: al-Hammani narrated to us, he said: Sharik narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And do not approach the property of an orphan except in the best manner﴾, he said: "Trading with it."

14148 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And do not approach the property of an orphan except in the best manner﴾, he said: "Let him make his property grow."

14149 - al-Harith narrated to me, he said: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, he said: Fudayl ibn Marzuq al-Anazi narrated to us, from Sulayt ibn Bilal, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding His saying ﴿And do not approach the property of an orphan except in the best manner﴾, he said: "He should seek gain for him in it, and not take any of its profit." [Report 14149: Fudayl ibn Marzuq al-Anazi is al-Raqqashi, al-Aghharr; passed as no. 5437. As for Sulayt ibn Bilal, I do not know who he is, and I have not found a biography for him.]

14150 - Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And do not approach the property of an orphan except in the best manner﴾, he said: "'The best manner' is that he may eat in accordance with what is reasonable if he is poor, and if he is rich he should not eat. God said: ﴿And whoever is rich, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat in accordance with what is reasonable﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 6]." He said: And he was asked about clothing, and he said: "God did not mention clothing; He mentioned only eating."

* *

As for His saying ﴿until he reaches his maturity﴾, "al-Ashudd" is the plural of "shadd", as "al-Adurr" is the plural of "darr", and as "al-Ashurr" is the plural of "sharr" [Thus it appears in the manuscript and the printed edition: "al-Adurr" and "al-Ashurr". I have not found any basis for these forms in the books of Arabic grammar, and I think these two words are corrupted, but I have left them as they are until I can reach the correct reading of them, God willing. They gave as examples for it their saying "qad" and "aqad", and the first is close to a corruption, but the second is obscure.]. "Al-Shadd" means strength, and it is the consolidation of the strength of his youth and his age, as "shadd al-nahar" means the height and extension of the day. It is said: "I came to him at shadd al-nahar and madd al-nahar", and that is at the time of its extension and height. And al-Mufaddal, as it has reached me, used to recite the verse of Antarah:

"I last saw him at the shadd of the day, as if his chest and his head were dyed with al-'Ithlim."

[From his famous mu'allaqa. This verse is one of the verses in which he describes a hero like himself, and before it he says: "When he saw me heading toward him, he showed his teeth, not in a smile..." and "So I struck him with the spear, then I mounted him with a polished, edged sword..." Al-Lubban is the chest. Al-'Ithlim is a red dye. He describes him as a slain man whose blood flowed, so that his head and extremities were dyed, without any movement in him.]

And from it is the saying of another [I do not know who said it]:

"A wife, long-boned of the forearms, tall as a palm tree stripped of its branches, circles him at the shadd of the day."

[Al-Zaʻina means his wife. Al-Anqa' is the plural of naqw, which is every bone containing marrow, such as the bones of the arms and legs. A woman who is sahuq is tall as if she were a straight palm tree from which its branches have been stripped.]

Some of the Basrans claimed that "al-Ashudd" is like "al-Anukk" [Anukk, with a long vowel and a u on the nun, is tin-lead, that is, tin. It means that it is a singular, not a plural.].

* *

As for the interpreters, they differ regarding the time at which, when a person reaches it, it is said: "He has reached his maturity."

Some of them said: It is said of him when he reaches puberty (al-hulum).

Those who said that:

14151 - Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Ayyub informed me, from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Rabi'ah, regarding His saying ﴿until he reaches his maturity﴾, he said: "Puberty."

14152 - Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to me, from his father, the like of it. Ibn Wahb said: Malik also said to me the like of it. [Reports 14151 and 14152: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb al-Misri, passed as nos. 2747, 6613, 10330; he is the nephew of Abdullah ibn Wahb, and his uncle is Abdullah ibn Wahb.]

14153 - It was reported to me from al-Hammani, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mujahid, from Amir, regarding ﴿until he reaches his maturity﴾, he said: "'Al-Ashudd' is puberty, when good deeds are recorded for him and bad deeds are recorded against him."

* *

Others said: It is said of him only when he reaches thirty years.

Those who said that:

14154 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿until he reaches his maturity﴾, he said: "As for 'ashuddahu', it is thirty years; then after it came: ﴿until, when they reach marriageable age﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 6]."

* *

There is an omitted element in the speech, the mention of which was left out being sufficient through the indication of what appears of what is omitted. The meaning of the speech is: "And do not approach the property of an orphan except in the best manner until he reaches his maturity"; then, when he reaches his maturity and you perceive in him sound judgment, hand over to him his property. For He, may His praise be exalted, did not forbid approaching the property of an orphan during his orphanhood except in the best manner until he reaches his maturity, so that it would be permitted to his guardian after his reaching maturity to approach it in the worst manner [In the printed edition: "wa-yahill" with a waw, while what is in the manuscript fits the context.]; but He forbade them from approaching it out of protection of him and safeguarding it for him, so that they might deliver it to him when he reaches his maturity.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And give full measure and weight with justice. We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, says: "Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him" [and that you give full measure and weight]. He means: do not defraud people of the measure when you measure for them, nor of the weight when you weigh for them, but give them their rights in full. Giving them that in full means giving them their rights complete ["with justice"], meaning with fairness, as:

14155 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿with justice﴾, "with fairness."

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "justice" with its evidences earlier, and we disliked repeating it.

* *

As for His saying ﴿We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾, He says: We do not burden a soul, regarding the giving of full measure and weight, except with what it can bear, so that it is lawful for it and it is not distressed by it. That is because God, may His praise be exalted, knew of His servants that many of them feel constrained from being pleased to give another what is not obligatory for them to give. So He commanded the one who gives to deliver to the owner of the right his right which is his, and He did not burden him with an increase, because of the constriction of his soul in giving more. And He commanded the one who has the right to take his right, and did not burden him with being content with less than it, because of the constriction of his soul in receiving less. Thus He did not burden either of them with anything except what involves no distress or constriction; therefore He said: ﴿We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾.

We have fully explained this with its evidences in a place other than this, enough to dispense with repeating it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And when you speak, be just, even if it concerns a near relative. And fulfill the covenant of God. This He has enjoined upon you that you may remember﴾ (152)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, ﴿And when you speak, be just﴾, He means: when you judge between people and speak, say the truth between them, be equitable and fair, and do not be unjust, even if the one against whom the truth is due and the judgment is a relative of yours, and let not the kinship of a relative or the friendship of a friend compel you, when you judge between him and another, to say other than the truth regarding what is brought before you for judgment. ﴿And fulfill the covenant of God﴾, meaning: and fulfill the charge of God with which He charged you. Fulfilling it means obeying Him in what He commanded and forbade them, and acting by His Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ, and that is the fulfilling of God's covenant.

As for His saying ﴿This He has enjoined upon you﴾, God, may His praise be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say to those among your people who make equals to God idols and images: these matters which I have mentioned to you in these two verses are the things our Lord has charged us with, and your Lord has enjoined upon you and commanded you to act upon, not the baheerah, the sawa'ib, the wasila, the ham, the killing of children, the burying of daughters alive, or following the footsteps of Satan. ﴿That you may remember﴾, meaning: He commanded you with these matters which He commanded you in these two verses, charged you with them and made a covenant with you concerning them, so that you may remember the consequences of your command and the error of what you are persisting in, and so that you may refrain from them, desist, and turn in repentance to obedience to your Lord.

* *

Ibn Abbas used to say: These verses are the decisive verses (al-ayat al-muhkamat).

14156 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Ali ibn Salih, from Abu Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Qays, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "They are the decisive verses: His saying: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him﴾." [Report 14156: Ali ibn Salih ibn Salih ibn Hayy al-Hamdani, trustworthy; passed as nos. 178, 11975. In the manuscript and printed edition: "Ali ibn Abi Salih", which is an undoubted error; the addition is a slip of the copyist, and it is "Ali ibn Salih", the one who narrates from Isra'il al-Subay'i and from whom Waki' narrates, as in al-Mustadrak, as will come in the takhrij. "Abu Ishaq" is al-Subay'i. "Abdullah ibn Qays", the narrator of this report, is singled out for narrating this report from Ibn Abbas and Abu Ishaq al-Subay'i's narration from him. Biographed in al-Tahdhib (5: 365) and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/138. This report was narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 2: 288, and he said: "Sahih", and al-Dhahabi agreed. I have indicated this in the takhrij of report no. 6573, so refer to it. Al-Hakim also narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2: 317, with another chain, through Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Khalifah, from Ibn Abbas, and said: "This is a hadith with a sahih chain, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed. "Abdullah ibn Khalifah al-Hamdani" passed as no. 5796.]

14157 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, both said: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, he said: I heard Yahya ibn Ayyub narrating, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Murthid ibn Abdullah, from Ubayd Allah ibn Adi ibn al-Khiyar, who said: Ka'b al-Ahbar heard a man reciting: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you﴾, and he said: "By Him in whose hand is Ka'b's soul, this is indeed the first thing in the Torah: 'In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful. Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you.'" [Report 14157: Wahb ibn Jarir ibn Hazim al-Azdi, the trustworthy memorizer. His father Jarir ibn Hazim al-Azdi is trustworthy, and the group narrated from him. Yahya ibn Ayyub al-Ghafiqi is trustworthy, passed as nos. 3877, 4330. Yazid ibn Abi Habib al-Misri, passed several times, the last being 11871. Murthid ibn Abdullah al-Yazani, the Misri jurist, passed as nos. 2839, 2840, 10890. Ubayd Allah ibn Adi ibn al-Khiyar al-Nawfali al-Qurashi, trustworthy, of few narrations, one of the jurists and scholars of Quraysh, who met the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ in large numbers. Biographed in al-Tahdhib. This report's chain is sahih up to Ka'b al-Ahbar.]

14158 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from his father, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, from a man, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, that he said to a man: "Would you like a sheet on which is the seal of Muhammad?" Then he recited these verses: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him﴾.

14159 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: Isḥaq al-Razi narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Amr ibn Murrah, who said: al-Rabi' said: "Shall I not recite to you a sheet from the Messenger of God ﷺ?" [He did not say: "its seal"], and then he recited these verses: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you﴾.

14160 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, who said: A group came to him and said: "You have sat with the Companions of Muhammad, so tell us about the revelation." Then he recited to them these verses from "al-An'am": ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him﴾. They said: "It is not about this that we ask you!" He said: "We have no revelation other than this."

14161 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: "These are the verses which He enjoined, from the decisive Qur'an."

14162 - Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And when you speak, be just﴾: "Speak the truth."

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿And that this is My path, [being] straight, so follow it; and do not follow [other] ways, lest they separate you from His way. That is what He has enjoined upon you, that you may become righteous﴾ (6:153)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: May His remembrance be exalted. He says: This which your Lord has enjoined upon you, O people, in these two verses, from His words: ﴿Say, "Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you"﴾ and commanded you to fulfil, is "His path" (sirat), meaning: His way and His religion which He has approved for His servants, ﴿straight﴾, meaning: upright, without any deviation from the truth (see the commentary on "the straight path" above, p. 113, note 1, and the references there). ﴿So follow it﴾: he says, act upon it, and make it for yourselves a method that you travel; so follow it (see the commentary on "following" in the lexical indices above, under t-b-'). ﴿And do not follow the ways﴾: he says, do not take any path other than it, do not ride any method other than it, and do not seek a religion contrary to it, from Judaism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, the worship of idols, and other creeds, for they are innovations and misguidance. [[In the manuscript: "dinan khalahu" (another religion); above "khalahu" the letter (ṭ) indicates an error or doubt, and what is in the manuscript is a sound reading.]] ﴿Lest they separate you from His way﴾: he says, they will scatter you if you follow the innovated ways which are not ways, paths or religions of God. Your following them is "away from His way", meaning: away from His path and His religion which He has legislated for you and approved, which is Islam, the religion with which the prophets were charged and which was commanded to the nations before you (see the commentary on "the way" in the lexical indices above, under s-b-l). ﴿That is what He has enjoined upon you﴾: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: This which your Lord has enjoined upon you, in His words to you: "Indeed, this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow the ways," He has enjoined upon you, ﴿that you may become righteous﴾, he says: that you may fear God regarding yourselves, so that you do not destroy them, and beware of your Lord regarding them, so that you do not incur His wrath upon them, whereupon His vengeance and punishment would befall you (see the commentary on "enjoining" and "righteousness" in the lexical indices above, under w-ṣ-y and w-q-y).

* *

Those of the people of interpretation said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

14163 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God: ﴿And do not follow the ways, lest they separate you from His way﴾, he said: innovations and doubts.

14164 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Shibl, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

14165 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And do not follow the ways﴾: innovations and doubts.
