14166 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: (So follow it, and do not follow the ways, lest they separate you from His way), and His words: ﴿Establish the religion and do not be divided therein﴾ [Surah al-Shura: 13], and the like of this in the Qur'an. He said: God commanded the believers to unity, and forbade them from disagreement and division, and informed them that those before them were destroyed only through disputation and quarrels over the religion of God.

14167 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: ﴿And do not follow the ways, lest they separate you from His way﴾, he says: do not follow the misguidances.

14168 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) drew for us a line one day and said: "This is the way of God." Then he drew lines to the right and left of that line and said: "These are ways; on each way there is a devil calling to it." Then he recited this verse: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow the ways, lest they separate you from His way﴾. [[Report 14168: its isnad is sound; Ahmad related it in al-Musnad, nos. 4142 and 4437, in similar wording. Ibn Kathir discussed the isnad and its variants in his commentary, 3:427–429. It will come below as no. 14170, as a report from Ibn Mas'ud.]]

14169 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow the ways, lest they separate you from His way﴾: "His way" is Islam, and "His path" is Islam. He forbade them to follow other ways, ﴿lest they separate you from His way﴾, from Islam.

14170 – Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Aban: that a man said to Ibn Mas'ud: What is the straight path? He said: Muhammad (ﷺ) left us at its beginning, its end is in Paradise, and to its right are side-paths, and to its left are side-paths, and there are men calling out to whoever passes by them. Whoever takes one of those side-paths is led to the Fire, and whoever takes the path is led to Paradise. Then Ibn Mas'ud recited: ﴿And that this is My path, straight﴾, the verse.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed in reading His words: ﴿And that this is My path, straight﴾.

The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufans, read ﴿wa-anna﴾ with a fath-ha on the alif of "anna" and a shadda on the nun, as a continuation of His words: ﴿that you do not associate anything with Him﴾, meaning: "Say, 'Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: that you do not associate anything with Him,' and 'that this is My path, straight.'"

* *

The majority of the Kufan readers read ﴿wa-inna﴾ with a kasra on the alif of "inna" and a shadda on the nun, as a new beginning, cut off from the first, since in their view the speech had already concluded with the report of the charge which God enjoined upon His servants apart from Him. [[Meaning by "apart from him, in their view": apart from the Prophet (ﷺ), according to those who read it thus, as will become clear from what follows; see note 3.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in my judgment, is that both are widely transmitted readings among the readers of the regions and the common Muslims, [[""Common Muslims" means the general body of Muslims, not "the common people" in the sense of those who have not studied knowledge.]] and both meanings are sound; whichever reading the reciter uses, he is correct in his recitation.

This is because God, may His remembrance be exalted, has commanded the following of His path, just as He commanded His servant the prophets. [[In the printed edition: "ʿibādahu bi-al-ashyāʾ" (His servants with things), which is a corrupt text, the editor having misread the manuscript and altered it. In the manuscript: "ʿibādahu al-asāʾ", and the correct reading is what has been adopted. It means that this is an address to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and all the prophets.]] If someone includes that within what God commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to say to the polytheists, "Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you," and what He has commanded you, and so reads "anna" with a fath-ha, he is correct; and if he reads it with a kasra, meaning a new beginning cut off from the first, since "recitation" is speech even if not in the wording of "saying", because of its distance from His word "I will recite", and he intends it to operate upon it, he is correct; and if he reads it with a kasra, meaning a new beginning cut off from the first and from "recitation", and that what the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to recite to those to whom he was commanded to recite it has ended before that, he is correct.

* *

And 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ishaq al-Basri read ﴿wa-anna﴾ with a fath-ha on the alif of "anna" and a light nun, meaning: "Say, 'Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: that you do not associate anything with Him,' and 'that this is My path'," so he lightened it, since the "anna" in His words ﴿that you do not associate anything with Him﴾ is light, and the "anna" in His words ﴿and that this is My path﴾ is coordinated with it, making it parallel to what it is coordinated with.

Although this is a valid approach, I do not favour this reading, because it is anomalous compared with the reading of the readers of the regions and contrary to what they follow in their regions.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Then We gave Moses the Book, complete [in blessing] for him who did good, and a detailed explanation of all things﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, may His praise be exalted, ﴿Then We gave Moses the Book﴾ means: then say after that, O Muhammad: "Your Lord gave Moses the Book." So the word "say" has been omitted, since something earlier in the story already indicates that it is intended, namely His saying: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you﴾. He recounted what was forbidden to them and what was made lawful, then said: "Then say: 'We gave Moses'," so "say" was omitted, its being indicated by the earlier "say," and it being intended in the speech.

We say that this is intended in the speech because Muhammad (ﷺ) was undoubtedly sent long after Moses, and he was commanded to recite these verses to those to whom he was commanded to recite them after his mission. And it is known that Moses was given the Book before God commanded Muhammad to recite these verses to those to whom they were to be recited. In the speech of the Arabs, "thumma" (then) is a particle indicating that what follows in the speech and report comes after what precedes it.

* *

Then the interpreters differed regarding the meaning of His saying: ﴿complete for him who did good﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is: complete for the doers of good.

Mention of those who said that:

14171 – Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿complete for him who did good﴾: he said, "For the believers."

14172 – Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿complete for him who did good﴾: "The believers and the doers of good."

* *

= It seems that Mujahid directed the interpretation and meaning of the speech toward the view that God, may His praise be exalted, informed about Moses that He gave him the Book as a favour over what He gave to the doers of good among His servants.

* *

If someone says: How is it permissible to say ﴿on him who did good﴾ in the singular "him" (alladhi), when the interpretation is "on those who did good"?

It is said: The Arabs do this specifically with "alladhi" and with the "al-" definite article when they intend by it the whole and the totality, as His saying, may His praise be exalted: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss﴾ [Surah al-Asr: 1–2], and as they say: "The dirham is abundant in the hands of people" (kathura al-dirham fihi fi aydi al-nas). [Note: the printed edition has a corrupt reading here; the manuscript reading is retained.] It has been reported from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that he used to recite it: "complete for those who did good" (ʿala alladhina ahsanu), and this reading of his supports Mujahid's view.

And if the meaning is so, then His saying "ahsana" (did good) is a past verb, and its being in the accusative case is due to that.

* *

It is also permissible that "ahsana" be in the genitive position, but it is in the accusative because "af'ala" (the elative form) does not take tanwin in their speech.

If it is asked: then by what is it in the genitive?

It is said: as a substitute for "alladhi," since no word appeared to govern it in the nominative. The meaning of the speech then becomes: "Then We gave Moses the Book, complete for him who is best," then "huwa" (he/it) was omitted, and "ahsana" was placed adjacent to "alladhi," so it took its case as the definite word does, since it is like a definite noun because "al-" does not enter it and "alladhi" is similar to it, as the Arabs say: "I passed by the one who is better than you, and worse than you" (marartu bi-alladhi khayrin minka wa-sharrin minka), as the rajiz said: [Verse on al-Zubayri, meaning he stripped his garments...] and so "mithl" follows "alladhi" in case. Whoever says this does not say "marartu bi-alladhi ʿalimin," because "ʿalimin" is indefinite and "alladhi" is definite, and an indefinite word does not follow a definite one.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: complete for him who did good, Moses, in what God tested him with in this world of His commands and prohibitions.

Mention of those who said that:

14173 – Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far told us, from his father, from al-Rabi': ﴿Then We gave Moses the Book, complete for those who did good﴾, in what God gave him.

14174 – Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told me, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Then We gave Moses the Book, complete for him who did good﴾: he said, "Whoever does good in this world, God will complete that for him in the Hereafter."

14175 – Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Then We gave Moses the Book, complete for him who did good﴾, he says, "Whoever does good in this world, God's honour will be completed upon him in the Hereafter."

* *

According to this interpretation that al-Rabi' gave, "ahsana" is in the accusative because it is a past verb, and "alladhi" has the meaning of "ma" (what). It is as if the speech then means: "Then We gave Moses the Book, complete for what Moses did well," i.e., We gave him the Book so that We might complete His honour for him in the Hereafter, in reward for his goodness in this world in worshipping God and fulfilling what He charged him with of obedience.

* *

Others said regarding this: its meaning is: Then We gave Moses the Book, complete in return for God's kindness to His prophets and His bounties upon them.

Mention of those who said that:

14176 – Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿Then We gave Moses the Book, complete for him who did good﴾: "Complete from God and His kindness, which He showed to them and guided them to Islam, and gave them that Book complete, for His favour upon him and His kindness."

* *

"Ahsana" in this interpretation also is in the accusative position, as a past verb, and "alladhi" in this view and the view that al-Rabi' stated means "ma" (what).

* *

It is reported from Yahya ibn Ya'mar that he used to recite it: "tamaman ʿala alladhi ahsanu" in the nominative, meaning: "on him who is best."

14177 – Ahmad ibn Yusuf told me this, he said: Al-Qasim ibn Sallam told us, he said: Al-Hajjaj told us, from Harun, from Abu Amr ibn al-Ala', from Yahya ibn Ya'mar.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This is a reading I do not consider permissible to recite with, although it has a sound grammatical basis in Arabic, because it contradicts what the consensus of the readers of the cities has established.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these views in my opinion is the view of the one who said: its meaning is: Then We gave Moses the Book, complete in return for Our favour to him, for what Moses did well in carrying out Our command and prohibition. This is because that is the most apparent meaning of it in the speech, and because Moses' being given his Book was a favour from God upon him and a great bounty. So He informed, may His praise be exalted, that He bestowed this favour upon him because of the good work and fine obedience that had preceded from him.

* *

If the interpretation were as Ibn Zayd said, the speech would be: "Then We gave Moses the Book, complete for what We did well," or "Then God gave Moses the Book, complete for what he did well."

And in His describing Himself, may His praise be exalted, with giving the Book, then turning the report with His saying "ahsana" to someone other than the one speaking about himself, given the closeness between the two reports, is the clear evidence that the saying is other than what Ibn Zayd said.

* *

As for what is reported from Mujahid about directing "alladhi" to the meaning of the plural, there is no evidence in the speech that establishes the correctness of what he said. Rather, the apparent meaning of the speech fits the view we chose better. And when interpretations of a passage are disputed, the most correct meaning is the one most consistent with its outward sense, unless there is clear evidence from reason or report that it intends something else.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and a detailed explanation of all things﴾, it means: and a clarification of every matter of the religion that they were commanded with.

* *

Thus the meaning of the speech is: Then We gave Moses the Torah, complete as a favour to Us and Our bounties with Him, through which Our honour upon him is completed, for his goodness and his obedience to his Lord and his fulfilment of the laws of his religion with which He charged him, and a clarification of everything that his people and followers need in matters of their religion, as:

14178 – Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: ﴿and a detailed explanation of all things﴾: in it are its lawful and unlawful things.

* *

Interpretation of His saying: ﴿And a guidance and a mercy, that they may believe in the meeting with their Lord﴾ (154)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We gave Moses the Book, complete and a detailed explanation of all things. ﴿And guidance﴾: by His saying "guidance" He means setting them straight on the right path and making clear to them the ways of rectitude so that they would not go astray. ﴿And mercy﴾: He says, and mercy from Us to them and compassion, that We might save them from error and the blindness of confusion.

As for His saying: ﴿that they may believe in the meeting with their Lord﴾, it means: My giving Moses the Book complete, for the honour of God to Moses, for Moses' goodness, and as a detailed explanation of the laws of his religion, and guidance for whoever followed him, and mercy for whoever among them was astray, so that God might save him from error thereby, and that he might believe in the meeting with his Lord when he hears the admonitions of God with which He admonished His creation, so that he would refrain from what he persists in of disbelief in Him and in meeting Him after death, and obey his Lord, and confirm what his Prophet Moses (ﷺ) brought him.

* *

Interpretation of His saying: ﴿And this is a Book We have sent down, blessed, so follow it and be mindful of God, that you may receive mercy﴾ (155)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His praise be exalted, by His saying: ﴿And this is a Book We have sent down, blessed﴾ means: this Qur'an which We sent down to Our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) is a Book We sent down, blessed. ﴿So follow it﴾: so make it your leader that you follow and act by what is in it, O people. ﴿And be mindful﴾: that is, beware of God regarding yourselves, lest you neglect acting upon what is in it, transgress its limits, and make lawful what He has forbidden. As:

14179 – Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And this is a Book We have sent down, blessed﴾, and it is the Qur'an that God sent down to Muhammad (peace be upon him): ﴿so follow it﴾: follow its lawful things and hold its unlawful things as forbidden.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿that you may receive mercy﴾: that is, so that you may be shown mercy, and escape the punishment of God and His painful retribution.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿that you may receive mercy﴾: that is, so that you may be shown mercy, and escape the punishment of God and His painful retribution.

The exposition of His saying: ﴿Lest you should say: "The Scripture was only sent down to two groups before us, and we were indeed unaware of their study."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The grammarians disagreed about the governing element (al-'amil) of "an" (that) in His saying ﴿an taqulu﴾ (lest you say), and about the meaning of this statement.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: its meaning is: "Then We gave Moses the Book, complete, upon the one who did good..." [[I think the correct wording of the expression is: "its meaning is: and this is a blessed Book which We have sent down, out of aversion that you should say ..." for this is the view which Abu Ja'far adopted afterwards. Perhaps it is an error on his part or on the part of the copyist.]] out of aversion that you should say: "The Scripture was only sent down to two groups before us."

* *

And some of the grammarians of Kufa said: rather, it is in the position of an accusative governed by a hidden verb. He said: the meaning of the statement is: "Follow it and fear God, that you may receive mercy" = "fear lest you say." He said: and similar to it is God's saying ﴿lest your deeds be nullified while you do not perceive﴾ [Surah al-Hujurat: 2].

* *

And others among them said: it is in the accusative position. He said: its accusative status is from two places: one of them: We sent it down lest they say "The Scripture was only sent down to two groups before us" [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "The Scripture was only sent down to" and a break; I added the remainder of the verse.]] = and the other from His saying ﴿fear God﴾. He said: it is not suitable in the position of "an", like His saying ﴿God makes clear to you lest you go astray﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 176]. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 36.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions in my view is the view of the one who said: the accusative of "an" is due to its connection with the sending down, because the meaning of the statement is: "And this is a blessed Book which We have sent down, lest you say: 'The Scripture was only sent down to two groups before us.'"

* *

As for the two groups which God mentioned, and informed that He sent down His Book upon His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) lest the polytheists say: "No Book was sent down to us that we might follow it, and we were not commanded nor forbidden, so there is no proof against us in what we do and leave undone, since no Book or Messenger came from God," [[In the printed edition: "lam yati" and in the manuscript likewise, but it was struck through and a (ṭ) mark placed to indicate error or doubt; and I saw its reading, as this is what the context requires.]] the proof lies only against the two groups upon whom the Book was sent down before us, namely the Jews and the Christians. [[See the explanation of "al-ṭā'ifah" (group) above: 6: 500, 506 / 9: 141.]] And thus the people of interpretation said.

14181- Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿lest you say: "The Scripture was only sent down to two groups before us"﴾: the Jews and the Christians, whom it is feared Quraysh might say.

14182- Al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿lest you say...﴾, he said: the Jews and the Christians. He said: lest Quraysh say.

14183- Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: ﴿lest you say...﴾: they are the Jews and the Christians.

14184- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: ﴿The Scripture was only sent down to two groups before us﴾: as for the two groups, they are the Jews and the Christians.

* *

As for ﴿and we were indeed unaware of their study﴾, it means: lest you say: "And we were indeed unaware of the recitation of the two groups of the Book which I sent down to them," [[See the explanation of "al-dirasah" (study) above: 6: 546 / 12: 25–31.]] "unaware," not knowing what it is, nor knowing what they recite, what they say, and what was sent down to them in their Book, because they were its people to the exclusion of us, and we were not concerned with it nor commanded with what is in it, and it is not in our tongue, so that they might take that as a proof. Thus God, by sending down the Qur'an upon His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), cut off that argument. [[See the explanation of "al-ghaflah" (heedlessness) in the language indexes under the root gh-f-l.]]

* *

And the people of interpretation said in a manner similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

14185- Al-Muthanna told me, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, he said: Mu'awiyah told me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and we were indeed unaware of their study﴾, he says: "and we were indeed unaware of their recitation."

14186- Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: ﴿and we were indeed unaware of their study﴾, i.e., of their reading.

14187- Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿and we were indeed unaware of their study﴾, he said: "Study" is recitation and knowledge. And he recited: ﴿and they studied what is in it﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 169]. He said: they knew what is in it; they did not come to it in ignorance.

14188- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: ﴿and we were indeed unaware of their study﴾, he says: "and we were indeed unaware of their recitation, not knowing what it is."

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Or [lest] you should say: "If only the Book had been sent down to us, we would surely have been better guided than they."﴾ ﴿Now there has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord, and guidance and mercy﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And this is a Book We have sent down, blessed," lest the polytheists, the idol-worshippers among Quraysh, should say: "The Book was only sent down to two groups before us," or lest they should say: "If only the Book had been sent down to us as it was sent down to those two groups before us, we would have been commanded and forbidden in it, and the error of what we are upon would have been made clear to us from its correctness." ﴿We would surely have been better guided than they﴾, that is: we would have been more steadfast upon the path of truth, more following of the Book, and better in acting by what is in it, than the two groups to whom the Book was sent down before us. [[See the explanation of "guidance" (al-huda) in the earlier vocabulary indexes, under (h-d-y).]] God says: ﴿Now there has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord﴾, meaning: there has come to you a Book in your tongue, Arabic and clear, a proof against you, evident and manifest, from your Lord. [[See the explanation of "clear evidence" (al-bayyinah) in the earlier vocabulary indexes, under (b-y-n).]] ﴿and guidance﴾, meaning: and a clarification of the truth, and a criterion between right and wrong; ﴿and mercy﴾ for whoever acts by it and follows it, as:

14189 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding: ﴿Or [lest] you should say: "If only the Book had been sent down to us, we would surely have been better guided than they." Now there has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord﴾: he said: "There has come to you clear evidence, a clear Arabic tongue, when you did not know the study of the two groups, and when you said: 'If a Book had come to us, we would surely have been better guided than them.'"

14190 – Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding: ﴿Or [lest] you should say: "If only the Book had been sent down to us, we would surely have been better guided than they."﴾ This is the saying of the disbelieving Arabs. ﴿Now there has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord, and guidance and mercy﴾.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So who is more unjust than one who denies the signs of God and turns away from them? We shall repay those who turn away from Our signs with the worst of punishment for what they used to turn away﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His majesty be praised, says: "Who has erred in action and is more aggressive than you, O polytheists, who deny the proofs of God and His evidences—and these are His signs [[See the explanation of "injustice" (al-zulm) in the earlier vocabulary indexes, under (z-l-m), and the explanation of "sign" (al-ayah) in the earlier vocabulary indexes, under (a-y-y).]]— ﴿and turns away from them﴾, meaning: and turns aside from them after they have come to him, so he does not believe in them and does not affirm their reality."

God, may His remembrance be exalted, expressed the report in His saying: ﴿So who is more unjust than one who denies the signs of God﴾ in the form of a report about an absent party, while meaning by it the addressees, the polytheists of Quraysh.

* *

Those who interpreted it said the same as what we have said regarding the interpretation of His saying: ﴿and turns away from them﴾. [[See the explanation of "turning away" (sadafa) in the earlier volumes, 11:366.]]

Those who said so:

14191 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿and turns away from them﴾: he said: "He turns aside from them."

14192 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding: ﴿turn away from Our signs﴾: "they turn aside from them, and 'al-sadf' is turning away."

14193 – Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah regarding: ﴿and turns away from them﴾: "he turned aside from them." ﴿We shall repay those who turn away from Our signs with the worst of punishment for what they used to turn away﴾: that is, "they turn aside."

14194 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi regarding: ﴿and turns away from them﴾: so he turned aside from them.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿We shall repay those who turn away from Our signs with the worst of punishment﴾, it means: God will recompense those who turn aside from His signs and proofs and do not reflect upon them, and do not come to know their reality so that they believe in what they indicate of the Oneness of God and the reality of the prophethood of His Prophet, and the truth of what came to them from their Lord [[In the printed edition: "wa-haqiyat nubuwat nabiyyihi" — the same error was made with its sister words before; see earlier 11:475 note 3 and the references there. "Haqiqah" here is a verbal noun meaning "haqq" (truth).]] — ﴿the worst of punishment﴾, meaning: severe retribution, which is the punishment of the Fire that God prepared for the disbelievers among His creatures — ﴿for what they used to turn away﴾, meaning: God will do that to them as recompense for what they used to turn away from His signs in this world, so they would not accept what their Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) brought them.

**The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them, or your Lord should come, or some of the signs of your Lord should come?﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His majestic praise says: Do these people who ascribe equals to their Lord, the idols and images, await anything [[see the earlier discussion of this word: 1: 467–469 / 8: 437, 438]] other than that the angels should come to them, to take their souls at death; or that your Lord, O Muhammad, should come among His creation at the standing place of the Resurrection; or that some of the signs of your Lord should come? That is, or that some of the signs of your Lord should come to them. The people of ta'wil (interpretation, i.e., tafsir) have said that this sign is the rising of the sun from its west.

**Those among the people of ta'wil who said this:**

14195. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿other than that the angels should come to them﴾, he said: at death, when they take them. "Or your Lord should come" means on the Day of Resurrection. "Or some of the signs of your Lord should come" means the rising of the sun from its west.

14196. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿other than that the angels should come to them﴾: with death. "Or your Lord should come": on the Day of Resurrection. "Or some of the signs of your Lord should come": he said, a decisive sign, the rising of the sun from its west, or whatever God wills.

14197. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: "Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them": he said: with death. "Or your Lord should come": and that is the Day of Resurrection. "Or some of the signs of your Lord should come."

14198. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them": at death. "Or your Lord should come" and "or some of the signs of your Lord should come": he said, the rising of the sun from its west.

14199. Ibn WakI' and Ibn Humayd related to us, both saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) said, concerning His words: "Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them, or your Lord should come, or some of the signs of your Lord should come": He said: "They will rise in the morning, and the sun and the moon will be from here, from the direction of the west, like two camels yoked together." Ibn Humayd added in his narration: "That is the time when faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith," and he said: "like two camels that are yoked together."

[[The report of 14199 is the report of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. None of the authors of the Six Books has recorded it, and its chain is sound. Al-Haythami recorded it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 7: 22 and said: "Al-Tabarani related it through two routes; this one, in which is Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam, who is weak, and the other, abridged, whose narrators are trustworthy." I say: he probably means this route, or one of the other routes that follow.
Al-Suyuti recorded it in al-Durr al-Manthur 3: 57, attributing it to Sa'id ibn Mansur, al-Firyabi, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Tabarani, and he omitted what Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) recorded.
Then see the report of Ibn Mas'ud through many other routes, numbers 14227–14236.]]

14200. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, concerning His words: "Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them": the souls are seized by death. "Or your Lord should come": on the Day of Resurrection. "Or some of the signs of your Lord should come."

**The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: His exalted remembrance says: "On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come," faith will not benefit one who was a polytheist before that, after the coming of that sign.

* *

It has been said that the sign about which God, His majestic praise, informed that the disbeliever's faith will not benefit him when it comes is the rising of the sun from its west.

**Those who said this, and what was related from the Messenger of God ﷺ concerning it:**

14201. Isa ibn 'Uthman al-Ramli related to me, saying: Yahya ibn Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, faith will not benefit a soul that..." he said: the rising of the sun from its west.

[[The two reports 14201 and 14202 are the hadith of al-Khudri, related through two routes, this one and the one that follows.
Isa ibn 'Uthman ibn Isa al-Ramli, a teacher of al-Tabari, is sound in hadith; he passed as number 300.
Yahya ibn Isa al-Tamimi, the paternal uncle of Isa ibn 'Uthman, is trustworthy. He passed as numbers 300, 6317, 9035.
Ibn Abi Layla is Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla. He was a jurist and truthful, but he had poor memory and his hadith was confused. Ahmad abandoned him. He passed as numbers 32, 33, 631, 3914, 5434.
'Atiyyah is 'Atiyyah ibn Sa'd ibn Janadah al-'Awfi, whose weakness was noted at number 305.
'Atiyyah had several hadiths from Sa'id al-Khudri. Ibn Hibban said: he heard hadiths from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, but after he died, he began to sit with al-Kalbi... so when al-Kalbi said, "The Messenger of God ﷺ said such-and-such," he would memorize it, and he gave him the kunyah Abu Sa'id, and narrated from him. If someone asked him, "Who related this to you?" he would say, "Abu Sa'id related it to me," and people would assume he meant Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, when he meant al-Kalbi. He said: It is not permissible to write down his hadith except as a matter of wonder.
This report was recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad 3: 31, by the second chain, and al-Tirmidhi also recorded it with it in the Book of Tafsir, and said: "This is a strange hadith. Some of them related it without raising it to the Prophet." It is a report of weak chain.]]

14202. Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.

14203. Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl and Jarir related to us, from 'Umarah, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "The Hour will not be established until the sun rises from its west." He said: "When people see it, whoever is on the earth will believe, and that is 'the time when faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith.'"

[[The report 14203 is the report of Abu Hurayrah, which Abu Ja'far related through several routes.
The first: by way of 'Umarah, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, numbers 14203, 14209.
The second: by way of al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, numbers 14210, 14236.
The third: by way of Ibn 'Awn, from Abu Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, number 14211.
The fourth: by way of Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, number 14220.
The fifth: by way of Ja'far ibn Rabi'ah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz, from Abu Hurayrah, number 14219.
The sixth: by way of Ibn Juraij, from Salih, mawla of al-Tawamah, from Abu Hurayrah, number 14225.
The seventh: by way of Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, number 14247, but in different wording.
Because these reports are scattered, I will gather each pair of similar narrations in the takhrij (sourcing) in one place. This report, numbers 14203 and 14209, was recorded by al-Bukhari through this same route (Fath al-Bari 8: 223 / 11: 304). It was recorded by Muslim in his Sahih 2: 194; by Ahmad, number 7161; by Abu Dawud in his Sunan 4: 163; by Ibn Majah, p. 1352; Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir 3: 433; al-Suyuti recorded it in al-Durr al-Manthur 3: 57, adding attributions to 'Abd ibn Humayd, 'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Nasa'i, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th, and al-Tabarani, Abu 'Adi.
'Umarah is 'Umarah ibn al-Qa'qa' ibn Shubrumah al-Dabbi. The group of compilers related from him; he is trustworthy. He is discussed in al-Tahdhib.
Abu Zur'ah is Ibn 'Amr ibn Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bajali; he passed as numbers 4841, 8155, 9161.
This is a hadith of sound chain.]]

14204. 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan al-Sukkari and Ishaq ibn Shahin related to us, both saying: Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah al-Tahhan informed us, from Yunus, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said one day: "Do you know where this sun goes?" They said: "God and His Messenger know best!" He said: "It goes to its resting place beneath the Throne, and it prostrates, and it does not cease to be so until it is said to it: 'Rise from wherever you wish,' and it rises in the morning from its rising place. Then it runs on until it reaches a resting place beneath the Throne, and it prostrates, and it does not cease to be so until it is said to it: 'Rise from wherever you wish,' and it rises in the morning from its rising place. Then it runs without people noticing anything from it, until it reaches its resting place beneath the Throne and prostrates; then the people rise in the morning without noticing anything from it, and it is said to it: 'Rise from your west,' and it rises in the morning from its west." The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Do you know what day that is?" They said: "God and His Messenger know best!" He said: "That is the day when 'faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith.'"

[[The reports 14204 and 14205 are the hadith of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, related through several routes, both long and short; these two, and then numbers 14221–14223, which I will mention separately.
'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan al-Sukkari, al-Qannad, a teacher of al-Tabari, has passed many times, last at number 10154. In the printed edition here it was "al-Yashkuri," which is an error; the correct reading is what appears in the manuscript.
Ishaq ibn Shahin al-Wasiti, a teacher of al-Tabari, passed as numbers 7211, 9788.
Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah al-Tahhan has passed many times, last at number 11504.
Yunus is Yunus ibn 'Ubayd ibn Dinar al-'Abdi; he also passed, with numbers, the last at 10574.
Ibrahim al-Taymi is Ibrahim ibn Yazid ibn Shurayk al-Taymi, a Successor, trustworthy. He passed in numbers, the last at 10284.
And Abu [his father] Yazid ibn Shurayk al-Taymi, a trustworthy Successor, passed as number 2998.
This report is of sound chain. Al-Bukhari recorded it (Fath al-Bari 6: 214 / 8: 416); Muslim recorded it, 2: 195, 196; al-Tayalisi, 62; al-Tirmidhi in Tafsir and in Fitan. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir 3: 433; al-Suyuti recorded it in al-Durr al-Manthur 3: 57, adding attributions to 'Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi. Its explanation has been fully treated in Fath al-Bari (8: 416).]]

14205. Mu'ammal ibn Hisham and Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to us, both saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Yunus, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Taymi, from his father, from Abu Dharr, from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to it.

[[Report 14205: its chain is sound; it duplicates the preceding one.]]

14206. Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah related to us, from Isra'il, from 'Asim, from Zirr, from Safwan ibn 'Assal, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ related to us: "Indeed, from the direction of the setting of the sun there is a door opened for repentance, until the sun rises from its direction. When the sun rises from its direction, faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith."

[[Report 14206 is the hadith of Safwan ibn 'Assal al-Muradi, a companion of the Messenger of God ﷺ, which Abu Ja'far related through two routes:
The first: by way of 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud ('Asim ibn Bahdalah), from Zirr, from Safwan, numbers 14206, 14208, 14216–14218, 14242.
The second: by way of Zubayd al-Iyami, from Zirr, from Safwan, number 14207.
The report was recorded by Ahmad in al-Musnad 4: 240; al-Tayalisi, 160; Ibn Majah, p. 1353; al-Tirmidhi; and al-Nasa'i. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir 3: 435; al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 3: 59, adding attributions to Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tabarani, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Bayhaqi, and Ibn Mardawayh. Ibn Kathir said: "al-Nasa'i authenticated it."
Al-Bukhari recorded it in al-Tarikh al-Kabir 2/2/305, through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Marzuq, from Zirr Hubaysh, from Safwan ibn 'Assal, then said: "The hearing of 'Abd al-Rahman from Zirr is not established."]]

14207. al-Mufaddal ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Ash'ath ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zubayd al-Iyami related to us, from his father, from Zubayd, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Safwan ibn 'Assal al-Muradi, who said: Repentance was mentioned, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "For repentance there is a door in the west, a journey of seventy years" — or: "forty years" — "and it remains so until some of the signs of your Lord come."

[[Report 14207: al-Mufaddal ibn Ishaq, a teacher of al-Tabari, I have found no biography of him. Ash'ath ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zubayd al-Iyami, also called al-Yami. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy, and Ibn Khuzaymah related from him in his Sahih. Abu Hatim said: "His standing is truthful." As for al-Nasa'i, he said: "He is not trustworthy, and his hadith is not written." Ibn 'Adi said: "al-Nasa'i was extreme in his case; I have examined his hadith, and I have not found any strange hadith from him."
In the printed edition it was "al-Yami," and the manuscript reading is what I have adopted.
His father, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zubayd al-Iyami, was related from by Yahya ibn 'Uqbah ibn Abi al-'Izar. Al-Bukhari said: "Munkar al-hadith." It was said: "The denunciation is from Yahya," which is also reported from al-Bukhari. Al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) said in Lisan al-Mizan: "This was said by al-Bukhari, the one who related from him. As for 'Abd al-Rahman, Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy."
As for his father, Zubayd ibn al-Harith al-Iyami, he is trustworthy; he passed as numbers 180, 2521, 5420. Zirr ibn Hubaysh has passed many times.
I have not found this report through this route in any of the books available to me.]]

14208. Muhammad ibn 'Umarah related to me, saying: Sahl ibn 'Amir related to us, saying: Malik related to us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Safwan ibn 'Assal, that he said: "Indeed, in the west there is a door open for repentance, a journey of seventy years. When the sun rises from its west, faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith."

[[Report 14208: Muhammad ibn 'Umarah al-Asadi, a teacher of al-Tabari, has passed many times. Sahl ibn 'Amir al-Bajali is very weak, and denounced in hadith; he passed as numbers 1971, 5431, 6313. "Malik" is Malik ibn Mighwal ibn 'Asim al-Bajali, trustworthy; he passed as numbers 5431, 10872. This report is weak in chain, because of the weakness of Sahl ibn 'Amir al-Bajali.]]

14209. Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl related to us, from 'Umarah ibn al-Qa'qa', from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: "The Hour will not be established until the sun rises from its west. When it rises and people see it, whoever is on the earth believes, and that is the time when 'faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before.'"

[[Report 14209 is a repetition of the report already mentioned as number 14203.]]

14210. Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Khalid ibn Makhlad related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "The Hour will not be established until the sun rises from its west. On that day all people will believe together, and that is the time when 'faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith.'"

[[Report 14210 is the second route of the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, as already mentioned at the start of the note on number 14203.
Khalid ibn Makhlad al-Qatwani, a trustworthy teacher of al-Bukhari, passed as numbers 2606, 4577, 8166, 8397.
Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir al-Ansari is a well-known trustworthy narrator; he passed as numbers 2606, 8397.
al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'qub, mawla of al-Hurqah, is a trustworthy Successor; he passed as number 221. His father, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'qub, mawla of al-Hurqah, is a trustworthy Successor, discussed in al-Tahdhib.
This report was recorded by Muslim in his Sahih 2: 194, through Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, and 'Ali ibn Hujr, from Isma'il ibn Ja'far (the brother of Muhammad ibn Ja'far, who related this report), from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman. It is a hadith of sound chain.]]

14211. Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Abu 'Awn, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "Repentance is accepted as long as the sun has not risen from its west."

[[Report 14211 is the third route of the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, as mentioned in number 14203. "Ibn 'Awn" is 'Abd Allah ibn 'Awn al-Muzani, the jurist; he passed many times, the last at number 10559. In the printed edition it was "'an Abi 'Awn," which is an error; the correct reading is from the manuscript. This is also a sound chain, but I have not found it except in the Tafsir.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 158 (part 2 of 4):

14212- Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Tirmidhi narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ayyash narrated to us, saying: Damdam ibn Zur'ah narrated to us, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Malik ibn Yakhamir, from Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, and Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Repentance will continue to be accepted until the sun rises from the west. When it rises, a seal is set upon every heart according to what it contains, and people are relieved of (the burden of) deeds." [[The athar: 14212. (Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Junaydab al-Tirmidhi), the hafiz (memorizer of hadith), the teacher of al-Tabari, already mentioned under no. 7489.
And (Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Isa al-Tamimi al-Dimashqi). Ibn Ma'in said: "Thiqah (reliable) when he narrates from well-known transmitters." Ibn Hibban said: "His narrations are considered when he narrates from reliable, prominent transmitters; but when he narrates from unknown persons, there is in them something objectionable." Biographed in al-Tahdhib.
And "Ibn Ayyash" is Isma'il ibn Ayyash ibn Muslim al-Ansi, thiqah, but spoken of, already mentioned under nos. 5445, 8164, 10375, 10730, 11108.
And (Damdam ibn Zur'ah ibn Thawb al-Himyari), thiqah, though some declared him weak; already mentioned under no. 5445.
And (Shurayh ibn Ubayd ibn Shurayh al-Hadrami), a thabi'i (follower of the Companions) and thiqah; already mentioned under nos. 5445, 12194.
And (Malik ibn Yakhamir al-Sakuni), a thabi'i. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.
This report is sahih in its chain, abridged; Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad, no. 1671, through the route of al-Hakam ibn Nafi: "From Isma'il ibn Ayyash, from Damdam ibn Zur'ah, tracing it back to Malik ibn Yakhamir, from Ibn al-Sa'di, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Migration does not cease as long as the enemy is fighting.' Mu'awiyah, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, and Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Migration consists of two qualities: one of them is that you abandon evil deeds, and the other is that you migrate to Allah and His Messenger. Migration does not cease as long as repentance is accepted, and repentance does not cease...'" until the end of the report. It is in the hadith of Mu'awiyah in the Musnad 5: 270, by a route other than this one, and not with this wording. Al-Haythami takes it out in Majma' al-Zawa'id 5: 250. See the takhrij of my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad in the Musnad, no. 1671. My brother al-Sayyid Ahmad will come (to it) in the Musnad, no. 1671.]]

14213- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah and Ja'far ibn Awn narrated to us, (the report) in a similar manner.

14214- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Hayyan al-Taymi, from Abu Zur'ah, who said: Three men from among the Muslims sat with Marwan ibn al-Hakam in Medina, and they heard him narrating about the signs, that the first of them to emerge would be the Dajjal (Antichrist). So the people went off to Abd Allah ibn Amr and told him this. He said: "Marwan has not said anything! I have memorized from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) something about this which I have not forgotten. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The first of the signs to emerge is the rising of the sun from the west, or the emergence of the beast before the people in the forenoon, whichever of the two is before the other, the second will follow soon after it.'" Then Abd Allah ibn Amr, who used to read the (previous) books, said: "I think the first of them to emerge is the rising of the sun from the west, because whenever it sets, it comes beneath the Throne, prostrates, and asks permission to return, and permission is granted to it to return; until, when Allah wills that it rise from the west, it does as it used to do: it comes beneath the Throne, prostrates, and asks permission to return, but it is given no reply. It does this three times, and is given no answer. Then, when a part of the night passes as Allah wills, and it knows that if it were permitted it would not reach the east, it says: 'How far is the east! My Lord, who will be responsible for the people?' Until the horizon becomes like a collar, it asks permission to return, and it is told: 'Rise from your place,' and so it rises from its west." Then he recited: "On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, faith will not benefit a soul that did not believe before," to the end of the verse. [[The athar: 14214. A hadith of Abd Allah ibn Amr, narrated at length through two routes, this one and the next, and narrated in abridged form under nos. 14226-14243.
(Abu Hayyan al-Taymi) is Yahya ibn Sa'id ibn Hayyan al-Taymi, thiqah, already mentioned several times, the last under no. 10883.
And (Abu Zur'ah ibn Amr ibn Jarir), thiqah, mentioned recently under no. 14203.
This report was narrated by Ahmad in the Musnad, no. 6881, through this very route. Al-Haythami takes it out in Majma' al-Zawa'id 8: 8, 9, and says: "Part of its beginning is in the Sahih; narrated by Ahmad, al-Bazzar, and al-Tabarani in al-Kabir, and its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."
Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 4: 547, 548, in a similar form, through the route of Ja'far ibn Awn al-Umari, from Abu Hayyan al-Taymi, and said: "This is a hadith sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not narrate it." Al-Dhahabi agreed, without explicitly stating agreement.
Al-Hakim also narrated in al-Mustadrak 4: 500, 501, a hadith from this Abd Allah ibn Amr with additions and variations, through the route of Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Ishaq ibn Wahb, from Jabir al-Khuyawani, who said: "I was with Abd Allah ibn Amr when his steward (qahraman) came to him from Syria, and two nights of Ramadan remained..." and he related the report. Then he said: "This is a hadith sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not narrate it." Al-Dhahabi agreed.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir 3: 436, and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 3: 57, and he added its attribution to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi. What Muslim, Abu Dawud, and Ibn Majah narrated is the abridged form, not this lengthy one.]]

14215- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Rabi'ah Fahd narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id Abu Hayyan, from al-Sha'bi, that three men entered upon Marwan ibn al-Hakam, and he mentioned something similar, from Abd Allah ibn Amr. [[The athar: 14215. This is another route of the earlier report, and its isnad is weak. (Abu Rabi'ah), whose laqab (epithet) is Fahd, and whose name is Zayd ibn Awf al-Qat'i, is matruk (abandoned, rejected in narration). Al-Bukhari said: "They kept silent about him." Abu Zur'ah accused him of stealing two hadiths, as is detailed in Ibn Abi Hatim. Biographed in al-Kabir 2/1/369, Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/570, Mizan al-I'tidal 1: 364, and Lisan al-Mizan 2: 509.]]

14216- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: I heard Asim ibn Abi al-Najud narrate from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Safwan ibn Assal, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "In the west there is a door, open for repentance, a distance of seventy years, which will not be closed until the sun rises from its direction." [[The athar: 14216, 14217. Two routes of the hadith of Safwan, whose takhrij was mentioned earlier under nos. 14206-14208. Ahmad narrated it in the Musnad 4: 240, 241, in a long hadith.]]

14217- Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid narrated to us, from Hajjaj, from Asim, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Safwan ibn Assal, who said: "When the sun rises from its west, on that day faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before." [[The athar: 14216, 14217. Two routes of the hadith of Safwan, whose takhrij was mentioned earlier under nos. 14206-14208. Ahmad narrated it in the Musnad 4: 240, 241, in a long hadith.]]

14218- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Rabi'ah Fahd narrated to us, saying: Asim ibn Bahdalah narrated to us, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: "I went early in the morning to Safwan ibn Assal, and he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The door of repentance is open from the direction of the west; its width is a distance of seventy years, and it will remain open until the sun rises from its direction.'" Then he recited: "Do they wait for anything but that the angels should come to them, or your Lord should come, or some of the signs of your Lord should come?" up to: "good." [[The athar: 14218. One route of the hadith of Safwan, whose takhrij is mentioned under nos. 14206-14208, but this isnad is weak, because of the weakness of Abu Rabi'ah Fahd, who was mentioned under no. 14215.]]

14219- al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman narrated to me, saying: Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Rabi'ah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz, that he said: Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Hour will not be established until the sun rises from the west." He said: "When the sun rises from the west, all the people will believe, and that is the time when 'faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith.'" [[The athar: 14219. This is the fifth route of the hadith of Abu Hurayrah mentioned under no. 14203.
(Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth ibn Sa'd al-Misri), a well-known thiqah, already mentioned under nos. 3034, 5314. And (al-Layth ibn Sa'd al-Misri), the famous imam, already mentioned several times.
And (Ja'far ibn Rabi'ah ibn Shurahbil ibn Hasanah al-Kindi), al-Misri, thiqah, already mentioned under nos. 5005, 6897.
And (Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz al-A'raj), already mentioned several times. This report was narrated by al-Bukhari (Fath al-Bari 11: 303, and 13: 72), through the route of Abu al-Yaman, from Shu'ayb, from Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah.]]

14220- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever repents before the sun rises from the west, his repentance will be accepted." [[The athar: 14220. This is the fourth route of the hadith of Abu Hurayrah mentioned under no. 14203. Ahmad narrated it in the Musnad under no. 7697, and Muslim narrated it in his Sahih through this route. My brother al-Sayyid Ahmad takes it out there.]]

14221- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Fahd narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Ubayd, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Taymi, from Abu Dharr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the sun sets, it comes beneath the Throne and prostrates, and it is said to it: 'Rise from where you set.'" Then he recited this verse: "Do they wait for anything but that the angels should come to them," to the end of the verse. [[The athar: 14221. This is one of the five routes of the hadith of Abu Dharr that I mentioned in the takhrij of the report under no. 14204. There is a break (inqita') in the isnad of this report, for Ibrahim al-Taymi did not narrate from Abu Dharr. Ahmad said: "He did not meet Abu Dharr." Perhaps this broken link is the reason for Muslim's statement in narrating this hadith (2: 195): "Yunus, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Taymi, who heard it, as far as I know, from his father, from Abu Dharr." So this isnad is weak because of its break. It is also a weak isnad, because of the weakness of "Fahd," who is "Abu Rabi'ah," "Zayd ibn Awf," whose biography passed under nos. 14215 and 14218. In the manuscript it reads "Yusuf ibn Ubayd," and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.]]

14222- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Hakam, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, from Abu Dharr, who said: "One day I was riding behind the Prophet (ﷺ) on a donkey, and he looked at the sun when it set, and said: 'It sets in a muddy spring (ayn hamiyah); it proceeds until it prostrates to its Lord beneath the Throne, until He permits it. When He wishes to make it rise from its west, He holds it back, and it says: "My Lord, my journey is far!" Then He says to it: "Rise from where you set!" That is the time when "faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before."'" [[The athar: 14222. This is one of the five routes mentioned under no. 14204. In the printed edition it reads "a muddy spring (ayn hamitah)," and I have restored what is in the manuscript. (Hamiyah) means: having black mud, which is foul-smelling black clay. (Hamiyah) means hot. The verse of Surah al-Kahf 18:86: "until, when he reached the setting-place of the sun, he found it setting in a muddy spring," has also been read as "hamiyah." Abu Ja'far said in his Tafsir 16: 10 (Bulaq edition): they are "two readings, widely transmitted among the reciters of the regions, and each of them has a correct aspect and a understood meaning."
(Sufyan ibn Husayn al-Wasiti), thiqah, though they spoke about his narrations from al-Zuhri. Already mentioned several times, the last under no. 11285.
And (al-Hakam), he is (al-Hakam ibn Utaybah al-Kindi), thiqah, already mentioned several times, the last under no. 11085.]]

14223- Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Abdah narrated to us, from Musa ibn al-Musayyab, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, from Abu Dharr, who said: "One day the Prophet (ﷺ) looked at the sun and said: 'It is about to come until it stands before Allah, and He will say: "Return from where you came!"' At that moment: 'faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith.'" [[The athar: 14223. This is the last route of the hadith of Abu Dharr mentioned under no. 14204. (Abdah) is (Abdah ibn Sulayman al-Kilabi), thiqah, one of the teachers of Ahmad. Already mentioned several times, the last under no. 8315.
And (Musa ibn al-Musayyab al-Thaqafi), also called (Musa ibn al-Sa'ib). Al-Bukhari did not mention any criticism of him, and Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the thiqat (reliable ones), and Ahmad said: "I know nothing but good about him," while al-Azdi declared him weak. Biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/294, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/161.]]

14224- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, his statement: "On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith." It means that faith will not benefit a polytheist at the (appearance of the) signs, while it benefits the people of faith at the signs if they had earned good before that. Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out one evening of the evenings and said to them: "O servants of Allah, repent to Allah, for you are about to see the sun from the direction of the west. When it does that, repentance will be withheld, deeds will be rolled up, and faith will be sealed." [[In the manuscript it reads: "deeds will be rolled up, and the deed will be sealed," which the first editor of al-Durr al-Manthur corrected.]] The people said: "Is there a sign of that, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The sign of that is tonight, that it will be lengthened to the measure of three nights. Those who fear their Lord will wake up and pray to Him, then they will finish their prayer while the night is still in its place, not yet ended. Then they will return to their beds and sleep. When they awake and the night is still in its place, they will see that, and they will fear that it is before a great matter." [[In the printed edition and in al-Durr al-Manthur it reads: "they will fear that this is before a great matter," but what is in the manuscript is correct.]] When they rise in the morning and the rising of the sun seems long to them, while they are waiting for it, it rises upon them from the direction of the west. When that happens, faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before." [[The athar: 14224. (Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-Awfi), and the chain of his isnad, whose explanation my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad gave in the comment on the athar no. 305. All its narrators are weak.]]

14225- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Salih the mawla (client) of al-Tawwamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that he heard him say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Hour will not be established until the sun rises from its west. When it rises and the people see it, they will all believe, all of them together; on that day 'faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before,'" the verse. [[The athar: 14225. This is the sixth route of the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, which I mentioned at the beginning of the comment on no. 14203.
(Salih mawla al-Tawwamah) is (Salih ibn Nabhan), already mentioned under nos. 1020, 3959. He is thiqah, but they spoke about him earlier because of a senility that afflicted him, which caused confusion (ikhtilat). Ahmad said: "Whoever heard from him in his early period, that is fine." Ibn Jurayj is among the earlier people who narrated from him, so this hadith of his is acceptable. I did not find the report in another place.]]

14226- And with this same isnad (he said): Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abi Atiq informed me that he heard Ubayd ibn Umayr reciting: "On the day when some of His signs come, faith will not benefit a soul," and he said: "He says: [We] used to be told, and Allah knows best, that it is the sun rising from the west." Ibn Jurayj said: Amr ibn Dinar informed me that he heard Ubayd ibn Umayr say that. Ibn Jurayj said: Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me that he heard Abd Allah ibn Amr say: "The sign by which faith will not benefit a soul is when the sun rises from the west." Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid also said that. [[The athar: 14226. This is another route of the report of Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As, an abridgement of the earlier report no. 14212. It is through the route of Ibn Jurayj, from Abd Allah ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, and it is a sahih isnad.]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 158 (part 3 of 4):**

14227. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Qatādah, from Zurārah ibn Awfā, from Ibn Mas'ūd, regarding ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith﴾: "It is the rising of the sun from its west."

[[The report 14227 and 14228 is the report of Abdullah ibn Mas'ūd. Al-Tabari transmitted it earlier by a chain numbered 14199, and then transmitted it here through several chains, numbered 14227 to 14234 and 14239. This is an explanation of its chains.
The first: through Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Ibn Mas'ūd, numbered 14199, then 14230, 14232 and 14233.
The second: through Qatādah, from Zurārah ibn Awfā, from Ibn Mas'ūd, numbered 14227, 14228 and 14231.
The third: through Ibn Sirin, from Abu 'Ubaydah ibn Abdullah ibn Mas'ūd, from Ibn Mas'ūd, numbered 14229.
The fourth: through Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha', from Abu al-Sha'tha', from Abu Mas'ūd, numbered 14234 and 14239.
This report is from the second chain.
Zurārah ibn Awfā al-Harashī, the judge, is trustworthy (thiqah), and the authors of the six canonical books narrated from him. However, he did not hear from Ibn Mas'ūd, as Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said. Therefore this chain is weak because it is discontinuous (munqati').
See also the takhrij of the earlier report numbered 14199.]]

14228. Muhammad ibn Bashshār and Muhammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard Qatādah narrating from Zurārah ibn Awfā, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ūd, regarding this verse ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come﴾, that he said: "It is the rising of the sun from its west."

14229. Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adī and Abd al-Wahhāb narrated to us, from 'Awf, from Ibn Sirin, who said: Abu 'Ubaydah ibn Abdullah ibn Mas'ūd narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Mas'ūd used to say: "Of the signs, what has been mentioned has passed except four: the rising of the sun from its west, the beast of the earth, the Dajjal, and the emergence of Gog and Magog. And the sign with which the deeds are sealed is the rising of the sun from its west. Did you not see that God said: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith unless it had believed before or earned through its faith some good﴾?" He said: "It is the rising of the sun from its west."

[[The report 14229 is the third chain of the report of Ibn Mas'ūd, as I mentioned in the commentary on the two previous reports.
"Abd al-Wahhāb" is Abd al-Wahhāb ibn Abd al-Majīd al-Thaqafī, trustworthy, mentioned many times, the last being 10729.
"'Awf" is 'Awf ibn Abi Jamīlah al-'Abdī, known as 'Awf al-A'rābī, mentioned many times, the last being 5473–5477. In the printed and manuscript copies it read: "Abd al-Wahhāb ibn 'Awf, from Ibn Sirin", which is not correct; it is a pure error, and this will become clear later.
"Ibn Sirin" is Anas ibn Sirin al-Ansārī, as is clear from the chain of al-Hākim in al-Mustadrak, but Ibn Kathīr in his tafsir explicitly stated that it is "from Muhammad ibn Sirin". Both of them narrated from him 'Awf al-A'rābī, and the more probable view is that this report is from Muhammad ibn Sirin.
Anas ibn Sirin al-Ansārī was trustworthy but narrated little. He was the brother of Muhammad ibn Sirin, and Anas was lower in rank than his brother Muhammad. The group (of canonical compilers) narrated from him. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabīr 2/2/33, and Ibn Abi Hātim 1/1/287.
"Abu 'Ubaydah ibn Abdullah ibn Mas'ūd" is mentioned many times, the last being 10355, and it has been mentioned many times before that he did not live to narrate from his father Ibn Mas'ūd.
Therefore this chain is discontinuous (munqati').
Al-Hākim narrated this report in al-Mustadrak 4:545, through Sufyān, from 'Awf, from Anas ibn Sirin, from Abu 'Ubaydah ibn Abdullah ibn Mas'ūd, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ūd. Al-Hākim said: "This is a hadith with a sound chain, though they (al-Bukhārī and Muslim) did not narrate it." Al-Dhahabī said: "Sound." But its defect is its discontinuity, as has been established.
Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his tafsir 3:437, and al-Suyūtī cited it in al-Durr al-Manthūr 3:59, attributing it additionally to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, and Ibn Mardawayh.]]

14230. Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adī narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Sulaymān, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: Abdullah said regarding ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith﴾: "It is the rising of the sun from its west, together with the moon, like two camels yoked together."

[[The report 14230 is the narration of the first chain of the hadith of Ibn Mas'ūd, whose explanation was given in the takhrij of the report numbered 14227, and its takhrij was given under 14199.]]

14231. ... Shu'bah said: And Qatādah narrated to us, from Zurārah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ūd: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come﴾, that he said: "It is the rising of the sun from its west."

[[The report 14231 is the narration of the second chain of the hadith of Ibn Mas'ūd, and its takhrij and the explanation of the discontinuity of its chain were given under 14227.]]

14232. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ūd: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come﴾, that he said: "It is the rising of the sun from its west, together with the moon, like two yoked camels."

[[The reports 14232 and 14233 are two narrations of the first chain of the hadith of Ibn Mas'ūd, as I explained under 14227, and its chain is sound, as was mentioned under 14199.]]

14233. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Mansūr and al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Abdullah: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith﴾, that he said: "It is the rising of the sun from its west, together with the moon, like two paired camels."

[[The reports 14232 and 14233 are two narrations of the first chain of the hadith of Ibn Mas'ūd, as I explained under 14227, and its chain is sound, as was mentioned under 14199.]]

14234. ... And he said: My father narrated to us, from Isrā'īl and his father, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha', from his father, from Abdullah, who said: "Repentance is open as long as the sun has not risen from its west."

[[The report 14234 is the fourth chain of the hadith of Ibn Mas'ūd, and it will also come later under 14239.
"Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha'" is Ash'ath ibn Aswad al-Muhāribī, trustworthy, mentioned under 10331 and 10333.
His father is Sulaym ibn Aswad Hanzalah al-Muhāribī, known as Abu al-Sha'tha', trustworthy, narrated from by the group, and biographed in al-Tahdhib.
This is a sound chain, which I have not found in any of the books before me.]]

14235. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Sa'īd narrated to us, from Qatādah, who said: "It was mentioned to us that Ibn Umm 'Abd used to say: 'The door of repentance remains open until the sun rises from its west. When people see that, they will believe, and that is when ﴿no soul will benefit from its faith unless it had believed before or earned through its faith some good﴾.'"

[[The report 14235: "Ibn Umm 'Abd" is Abdullah ibn Mas'ūd.
This is a report in which Qatādah did not mention its chain back to Ibn Mas'ūd. The report of Qatādah from Zurārah ibn Awfā, from Ibn Mas'ūd, has already passed with a different wording, numbered 14227, 14228 and 14231, in summary form.]]

14236. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: al-'Alā' ibn Abd al-Rahmān narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The Hour will not be established until the sun rises from its west. When it rises, all people will believe, and on that day ﴿no soul will benefit from its faith unless it had believed before or earned through its faith some good﴾."

[[The report 14236 is the narration of the report of Abu Hurayrah, from the second chain which I mentioned in the takhrij of the report numbered 14203. This chain was explained in the commentary on the report numbered 14210.]]

14237. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dīnār, from Ubayd ibn Umayr: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come﴾, that he said: "It is the rising of the sun from its west."

14238. ... And he said: My father narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn 'Uqbah, Abu Kīrān, from al-Dahhāk: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith﴾, that he said: "It is the rising of the sun from its west."

[[The report 14238: "al-Hasan ibn 'Uqbah al-Murādī", known as Abu Kīrān (with a ya'), trustworthy, narrated from Abd Khayr, al-Sha'bī, and al-Dahhāk. Narrated from by Wakī', Ubayd Allah ibn Mūsā, and Abu Nu'aym. He is biographed in al-Kabīr 1/2/299 and Ibn Abi Hātim 1/2/28. In the printed edition it read "Abu Kibrān" with a bā', accompanied by a sign of doubt.]]

14239. Al-Hasan ibn Yahyā narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Isrā'īl informed us, saying: Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha' informed me, from his father, from Ibn Mas'ūd, regarding His saying ﴿no soul will benefit from its faith unless it had believed before﴾, that he said: "Repentance remains open as long as the sun has not risen from its west."

[[The report 14239 is the narration of the fourth chain of the hadith of Ibn Mas'ūd, as I detailed under 14227. The explanation of this chain was given under 14234.]]

14240. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Āsim narrated to us, saying: 'Īsā narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najīh, from Mujāhid regarding the saying of God: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come﴾, that he said: "It is the rising of the sun from its west."

14241. Yūnus ibn Abd al-A'lā narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed me, from al-Qurazī, that he used to say regarding this verse: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith unless it had believed before﴾, meaning: when the signs come, faith will not benefit any soul. He means: "It is the rising of the sun from its west."

[[Abu Sakhr is Humayd ibn Ziyād al-Kharrāt, who settled in Egypt. He was mentioned under 4325, 5386 and 8391.
"Al-Qurazī" is Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazī, mentioned many times, including in a similar chain under 8391.]]

14242. Al-Hārith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-'Azīz narrated to us, saying: Sufyān al-Thawrī narrated to us, from Āsim ibn Abi al-Najūd, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Safwān ibn 'Assāl: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come﴾, that he said: "It is the rising of the sun from its west."

[[The report 14242 is the narration of the hadith of Safwān ibn 'Assāl, from the first chain, as I explained in the commentary on the report numbered 14206, where the matter was discussed.]]

14243. Al-Hārith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-'Azīz narrated to us, saying: Isrā'īl narrated to us, from Abu Ishāq, from Wahb ibn Jābir, from Abdullah ibn Amr: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come﴾, that he said: "It is the rising of the sun from its west."

[[The report 14243: "Abu Ishāq al-Hamdānī" is Abu Ishāq al-Subay'ī, mentioned many times.
"Wahb ibn Jābir al-Khaywānī al-Hamdānī" narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-'Ās, whom he met at Bayt al-Maqdis. Only Abu Ishāq al-Hamdānī narrated from him. He was a trustworthy Successor (tābi'ī). He narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-'Ās the story of Gog and Magog, and the saying "It is enough sin for a man that he neglects those he sustains," and he narrated no others than these two. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabīr 4/2/163–164, and Ibn Abi Hātim 4/2/23.
These two reports mentioned in his biography were narrated by Abu Dāwūd al-Tayālisī in his Musnad, p. 301, numbers 2281 and 2282.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, that refers to some of the three signs: the beast, Gog and Magog, and the rising of the sun from its west.

Mention of those who said that:

14244. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Awn narrated to us, from al-Mas'ūdī, from al-Qāsim, who said: Abdullah said: "Repentance is offered to the son of Adam, if it is accepted, as long as one of three things has not come forth: until the sun rises from its west, or the beast, or the opening of Gog and Magog."

[[The two reports 14244 and 14245: "Ja'far ibn Awn" is Ja'far ibn Amr ibn Huraith al-Makhzūmī, "Abu Awn", trustworthy, mentioned under 9506.
"Al-Mas'ūdī" is Abd al-Rahmān ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Abdullah ibn Mas'ūd, mentioned many times under 2156, 2937 and 5563.
"Al-Qāsim" is al-Qāsim ibn Abd al-Rahmān ibn Abdullah ibn Mas'ūd, who narrated from his father and his grandfather Abdullah ibn Mas'ūd, as a mursal report (one missing the companion in the chain). He was trustworthy and narrated little. He is mentioned under 9519.
My brother al-Sayyid Ahmad mentioned, in the commentary on the report 9515, that "al-Mas'ūdī, from al-Qāsim" is "Ma'n ibn Abd al-Rahmān", and that al-Qāsim, as he inferred, is his brother "al-Qāsim ibn Abd al-Rahmān ibn Abdullah ibn Mas'ūd". The correct view is that al-Mas'ūdī, who narrated from "al-Qāsim ibn Abd al-Rahmān", is "Abd al-Rahmān ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah", as I previously stated. The chain of this report is weak because it is discontinuous.
It was cited by al-Suyūtī in al-Durr al-Manthūr 3:59, attributing it to Abd ibn Humayd and al-Tabarānī.]]

14245. Ya'qūb narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: al-Mas'ūdī narrated to us, from al-Qāsim ibn Abd al-Rahmān, who said: Abdullah said: "Repentance is offered to the son of Adam, if it is accepted, as long as one of three things has not come forth: the beast, the rising of the sun from its west, and the emergence of Gog and Magog."

14246. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Mansūr, from Āmir, from Ā'ishah, who said: "When the first of the signs comes forth, the pens will be cast aside, the guardian angels will be detained, and the bodies will bear witness to the deeds."

[[The report 14246: "Mansūr" is Mansūr ibn al-Mu'tamir. "Āmir" is al-Sha'bī.
This report was narrated by Ibn Kathīr in his tafsir 3:437, and its chain is sound. I have not found it in any of the books available to me.]]

14247.
