Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hāzim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Three, when they come forth, ﴿no soul will benefit from its faith unless it had believed before or earned through its faith some good﴾: the rising of the sun from its west, the Dajjāl, and the beast of the earth."

[[The report 14247 is the seventh chain of the reports of Abu Hurayrah, which I mentioned in the commentary on the report numbered 14203.
Muhammad ibn Fudayl ibn Ghazwān al-Dabbī, narrated from by the group, mentioned many times, the last being 8395.
His father is Fudayl ibn Ghazwān al-Dabbī, trustworthy, narrated from by the group. "Abu Hāzim" is al-Ash'jaī, whose name is "Salmān", trustworthy, narrated from by the group.
This is a sound chain. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih 2:195, al-Tirmidhī in the book of tafsir, and Ibn Kathīr cited it in his tafsir 3:434, saying: "Ahmad narrated it from Wakī', from Fudayl ibn Ghazwān," and he mentioned its other chains. Al-Suyūtī cited it in al-Durr al-Manthūr 3:57, attributing it additionally to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqī.]]

14248. Bishr ibn Mu'ādh narrated to us, saying: Mu'āwiyah ibn Abd al-Karīm narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Hasten to the deeds in six: the rising of the sun from its west, the Dajjāl, the smoke, the beast of the earth, the affair of one of you in particular, and the affair of the common people."

14249. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Sa'īd narrated to us, from Qatādah, who said: It was mentioned that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) used to say, and then he mentioned something similar.

[[The two reports 14248 and 14249: "Mu'āwiyah ibn Abd al-Karīm al-Thaqafī", known as "al-Dāll", because he went astray on the road to Mecca. He narrated from al-Hasan. Ahmad and others considered him trustworthy, though they spoke about him. I fear that a man may have dropped out of the chain between him and "Bishr ibn Mu'ādh".
As for the second chain, in it "Bishr" means "Bishr ibn Mu'ādh", from "Yazīd", meaning "Yazīd ibn Zurai'", from "Sa'īd", meaning "Sa'īd ibn Abi Arūbah".
However, this report with this wording was narrated by Muslim in his Sahih 17:87 as a marfū' report (traced to the Prophet), through Umayyah ibn Bistām al-'Aysh, from Yazīd ibn Zurai', from Shu'bah, from Qatādah, from al-Hasan, from Ziyād ibn Riyāh, from Abu Hurayrah.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the views on this matter is that which is supported by the reports from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), that he said: "That is when the sun rises from its west."

* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 158 (part 4 of 4):

As for His saying ﴿or has earned in its faith any good﴾, it means: or has done good in its belief in God, [[See the explanation of "kasb" (earning) above, p. 120, footnote 1, and the references there.]] of righteous deed that confirms its speech and makes it real, before the rising of the sun from its west. Likewise, a disbeliever who had not believed in God before its rising, his faith in God will not benefit him if he believes and affirms God and His messengers, [[In the printed edition: "lā yanfaʿu kāfiran" without a waw, but the context requires it.]] because this is a state in which no soul is prevented from acknowledging God, due to the great terror that comes upon them from the command of God. So the ruling on their faith is like the ruling on their faith at the establishment of the Hour, and that is a state in which creation is not prevented from acknowledging the oneness of God, because they witness from the horrors of that day what removes their need for reflection, deduction, inquiry and consideration. And it does not benefit one who was a believer in God and His messengers, and a neglecter of God's obligations, who had not earned any obedience to God with his limbs, when it rises from its west: his deeds, if he does them, and his earnings, if he earns them, because of his negligence that preceded its rising. As:

1425O- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, a soul's faith will not benefit it, if it had not believed before, or had earned in its faith any good﴾, he says: it earned good in its belief, a righteous deed. These are the people of the qibla. If it was affirming but had not done any good before that, and then did good after seeing the sign, it would not be accepted from it. And if it did good before the sign, and then did good after the sign, it would be accepted from it.

1425I- It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His saying: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, a soul's faith will not benefit it﴾, he said: Whoever is reached by some of the signs while he is upon a righteous deed along with his faith, God accepts from him the deed after the revelation of the sign, just as He accepted it from him before that.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Say: Wait, we too are waiting﴾

Abu Ja'far says: The Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these who equate their Lord with idols and images: Wait for the angels to come to you with death and seize your souls, or for your Lord to come for the judgment between us and you at the standing of the Resurrection, or for the rising of the sun from its west to come to you, so the scrolls of deeds are folded, and your faith will not benefit you then, if you believe, until you know then the truthful from us from the falsehood-follower, the evildoer from the good-doer, and the truthful from the liar, and you are made clear at that time by whom the punishment of God and His painful retribution will befall, and who among us and you is saved and who is destroyed. We are awaiting that, so that God may lavishly reward us for our obedience to Him, our sincerity in worship to Him, and our singling Him out in lordship apart from what is other than Him, and He will judge between us and you with truth, and He is the best of judges.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 159:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects, you have no part in them at all. Their affair is only with Allah; then He will inform them about what they used to do.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed over the reading of His words: ﴿farraqu﴾ (divided).

It is narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that:

14252 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Dinar, that Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, recited: "Inna alladhina faraqu dinahum" (Indeed, those who parted from their religion).

14253 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, saying: Hamzah al-Zayyat said: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, recited it: "faraqu dinahum".

14254 - ... And he said: al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Qatadah: "faraqu dinahum".

* *

It seems that Ali understood by his words "faraqu dinahum" that they went out and apostatized from it, from "al-mufaraqah" (parting).

* *

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud also recited it in this way, as:

14255 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Rafi' narrated to us, from Zuhayr, saying: Abu Ishaq narrated to us that Abdullah used to recite it: ﴿farraqu dinahum﴾.

* *

This reading, namely the reading of Abdullah, is that of the reciters of Medina and Basra and the general body of the reciters of Kufa. It seems that Abdullah, by his reading, interpreted it thus: that the religion of Allah is one, and it is the religion of Abraham, the upright monotheistic religion of submission; the Jews and Christians divided it, so some people became Jews and others became Christians, and they made it into scattered sects.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct position on this matter is to say that they are two well-known readings, both of which were recited by leading reciters, and their meanings agree and do not conflict. This is because every one who goes astray has parted from his religion, and the factions have divided the religion of Allah which He approved for His servants, so some became Jews, others became Christians, and some became Magians. That is "division" itself, and the outcome for its adherents is being sects scattered and not united; they are thus parting from the true religion of Allah and dividing it. [[See the explanation of "al-shi'a" above, vol. 11, p. 419.]] So whichever of the two readings the reciter uses, he is correct about the truth; however, I prefer the reading followed by the majority of the reciters, namely the emphasis on the "ra" in "farraqu".

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed concerning those meant by His words: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion﴾.

Some of them said: It means the Jews and the Christians.

Those who said this:

14256 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿and became sects﴾, he said: the Jews.

14257 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

14258 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿divided their religion﴾, he said: they are the Jews and the Christians.

14259 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects﴾, from the Jews and the Christians.

14260 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects, you have no part in them at all﴾, these are the Jews and the Christians. As for His words "faraqu dinahum", he says: they abandoned their religion and became sects. [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "faraqu" in both places, but the tafsir in the report requires "faraqu" as I have established it.]]

14261 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects﴾, that the Jews and the Christians differed before Muhammad was sent, and they split up. When Muhammad was sent, Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects, you have no part in them at all﴾.

14262 - I was told on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects﴾, that he meant the Jews and the Christians.

14263 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Husayn ibn Ali narrated to us, from Shaybān, from Qatadah: "faraqu dinahum", he said: they are the Jews and the Christians.

* *

Others said: It means the people of innovation from this community, who follow the ambiguous verses of the Qur'an and leave aside its clear ones.

Those who said this:

14264 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, from Tawus, from Abu Hurayrah who said: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion﴾, he said: this verse was revealed concerning this community. [[The two reports 14264 and 14265: their chain is sound up to Abu Hurayrah, as a mawquf report; see the note on the following report.]]

14265 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Tawus, from Abu Hurayrah: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects﴾, he said: they are the people of prayer. [[The printed edition read "people of misguidance", as in the following report, but the manuscript is clear here as "people of prayer", so I have kept it as it is, since its meaning is sound: it was revealed concerning the believers who face the qibla.]]

14266 - Sa'id ibn Amr al-Sakuni narrated to me, saying: Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Abbad ibn Kathir wrote to me, saying: Layth narrated to me, from Tawus, from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, concerning this verse: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects, you have no part in them at all﴾, "and they are not of you; they are the people of innovations, the people of doubts, and the people of misguidance from this community." [[Report 14266: Sa'id ibn Amr al-Sakuni is the teacher of al-Tabari, mentioned before. Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid al-Himsi is trustworthy, though criticized for tadlis. Abbad ibn Kathir al-Ramli al-Filastini is weak in hadith. This report, traced to the Prophet, is not authentic and its chain is weak. Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir: "But this chain is not sound, for Abbad ibn Kathir is abandoned in hadith. He did not fabricate this hadith, but erred in raising it, for Sufyan al-Thawri narrated it from Layth, that is Ibn Abi Sulaym, from Tawus, from Abu Hurayrah, regarding this verse, that he said: it was revealed concerning this community." Al-Haythami cited it in Majma' al-Zawa'id and said: "Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat, and its narrators are the narrators of the sound collection, except Mu'allal ibn Nufayl, who is trustworthy." In Majma' al-Zawa'id it is written "Mu'allal ibn Nufayl", which is undoubtedly a distortion.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct position on this matter, in my view, is to say: Allah informed His Prophet (ﷺ) that he is free of those who parted from his true religion and divided it, who were factions within it and sects, and that he is not of them, and they are not of him, because his religion with which Allah sent him is Islam, the monotheistic religion of Abraham, as his Lord said to him and commanded him to say: ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a religion upright, the religion of Abraham, a true monotheist, and he was not of the polytheists﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 161].

So whoever parted from the religion with which he (ﷺ) was sent, whether a polytheist, an idolater, a Jew, a Christian, or a hanif-claimer, an innovator who has introduced into the religion what led him astray from the straight path and the upright religion, the religion of Abraham the Muslim, is free of Muhammad (ﷺ), and Muhammad is free of him, and he falls within the general meaning of His words: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects, you have no part in them at all﴾.

* *

As for His words: ﴿You have no part in them at all; their affair is only with Allah﴾, the people of interpretation differed concerning its explanation.

Some of them said: This verse was revealed to the Prophet of Allah with a command to abandon fighting the polytheists before the obligation of fighting them was prescribed; then it was abrogated by the command to fight them in "Surah Bara'ah" (al-Tawbah), namely His words: ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 5].

Those who said this:

14267 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding His words: ﴿You have no part in them at all; their affair is only with Allah﴾, he was not commanded to fight them, then it was abrogated, and he was commanded to fight them in "Surah Bara'ah".

* *

Others said: Rather, it was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) as an informing from Allah to him that among his community there would be those who would innovate in his religion after him. It is not abrogated, because it is a report, not a command, and abrogation occurs only in commands and prohibitions.

Those who said this:

14268 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Mughul informed us, from Ali ibn al-Aqmar, from Abu al-Ahwas, that he recited this verse: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects, you have no part in them at all﴾, then said: Your Prophet (ﷺ) is free of them. [[Report 14268: Malik ibn Mughul al-Bajali is trustworthy; Ali ibn al-Aqmar al-Hamdani, the group narrated from him. This chain is sound.]]

14269 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father, Ibn Idris, Abu Usamah and Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Malik ibn Mughul, similarly.

14270 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Shuja' Abu Badr narrated to us, from Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i, who said: Umm Salamah said: Let a man beware lest he be not of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in anything! Then she recited: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects, you have no part in them at all﴾. Amr ibn Qays said: Murrah al-Tayyib used to say it, and recited this verse. [[Report 14270: Shuja' Abu Badr is Shuja' ibn al-Walid ibn Qays al-Sakuni, trustworthy and truthful; Ahmad narrated from him. Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i is trustworthy. This chain is interrupted (munqati'), as Amr ibn Qays did not meet Umm Salamah. As for the report of Murrah al-Tayyib, it is Murrah ibn Surahil al-Hamdani, and this report too is interrupted, as he did not meet her. Al-Suyuti cited the report of Umm Salamah in al-Durr al-Manthur, attributing it to Ibn Mani' in his Musnad and Abu al-Shaykh, and cited the report of Murrah al-Tayyib, attributing it to Ibn Abi Hatim.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct position on this matter is to say: His words "you have no part in them at all" are an informing from Allah to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) that he is free of the innovators of his community who deviate in his religion, and of the factions of the polytheists of his people, and of the Jews and Christians. There is nothing in this informing that requires that He forbade him from fighting them, because it is not impossible that the speech means: "You are not of the religion of the Jews and Christians in anything; so fight them. Their affair is with Allah, in that He may show grace to whomever He wills among them and accept his repentance, and destroy whomever He wills to destroy among them in disbelief, taking his soul, or [He may have you] kill him by your hand for his disbelief; then He will inform them about what they used to do when they come before Him." Since it is not impossible for the command to fight them and His words "You have no part in them at all; their affair is only with Allah" to coexist, and there is no clear proof in the verse that it is abrogated, nor has any report from the Messenger stated that it is abrogated, it is not permissible to judge it abrogated until there is a proof establishing the soundness of that view, because we have already explained that the abrogated is what cannot be combined with its abrogating text at one time, in our book "al-Latif 'an Usul al-Ahkam". [[See what passed on "al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh" vol. 10, p. 333, note 1, and the references there. The name of Abu Ja'far's book is what I have established, as stated in vol. 5, p. 414. It appeared in the manuscript and printed edition as "al-Latif 'an Usul al-Ahkam", which is not correct.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿Their affair is only with Allah﴾, He says: I am the one to whom the affair of these polytheists who parted from their religion and became sects, and the innovators of your community who strayed from your path, belongs, not you, nor anyone else: either by punishment, if they persist in their misguidance and division of religion, so I destroy them by it; or by pardoning them, by accepting their repentance and showing grace to them from Me. ﴿Then He will inform them about what they used to do﴾ [[See the explanation of "al-naba'" above, p. 37, note 4, and the references there.]] He says: Then He will inform them in the Hereafter, when they come before Me on the Day of Resurrection, about what they used to do, and I will recompense each of them for what they used to do in the world, the good-doer with good and the evildoer with evil. Then He, may His praise be exalted, informed of the measure of His recompense for those who are repaid among them with good or with evil, saying: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times its like, and whoever comes with an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its like, and they will not be wronged.﴾

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, he will have ten times the like of it, and whoever comes with an evil deed, he will not be recompensed except with the like of it, and they will not be wronged﴾ (6:160)**

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: whoever meets his Lord on the Day of Resurrection, at the place of reckoning, from among those who abandoned their religion and became sects, having repented, believed, and ceased from the error in which he persisted, that is the good deed which Allah mentioned when He said: "Whoever comes with it, he will have ten times its like." [[See the explanation of "al-hasanah" (the good deed) above, 4:203–206 / 8:555–556, and the lexical indexes under (ḥ-s-n).]]

And by His words ﴿he will have ten times its like﴾ He means: he will have ten good deeds like the good deed he brought. ﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed﴾ means: whoever among them meets the Day of Resurrection having separated from the true religion and disbelieved in Allah, he will not be recompensed except with what displeases him of recompense, just as Allah meets him with his evil deed. [[See the explanation of "al-sayyi'ah" (the evil deed) above in the lexical indexes under (s-w-').]] ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾ means: Allah does not wrong either group, neither the group of good-doers nor the group of evil-doers, by repaying the good-doer with evil or the evil-doer with good. Rather, He recompenses each of the two groups with what is due to it, because He, may His praise be exalted, is Wise, who places nothing except in its proper place that it deserves, and recompenses no one except with what he merits.

* *

We have already shown earlier, with sufficient evidence that makes its repetition here unnecessary, that the meaning of "al-zulm" (wrongdoing) is placing a thing in other than its proper place. [[See the explanation of "al-zulm" above in the lexical indexes under (z-l-m).]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says: If the matter is as you have mentioned, that the meaning of "the good deed" in this place is faith in Allah, acknowledgment of His oneness, and belief in His Messenger, and "the evil deed" in it is associating partners with Him and denying His Messenger, then is there for faith "likes" by which the believer is recompensed? [[In the printed edition: "fa-lil-iman" without the interrogative hamzah; what is in the manuscript is correct.]] And if it has a like, how is it recompensed, when "faith," in your view, is only speech and action, while the recompense from Allah to His servants for it is honour in the Hereafter and bounty bestowed upon him with what He has prepared for the people of His honour of delight in the abode of eternity, and that is tangible things that are seen, witnessed, perceived, and enjoyed, not speech that is heard or earning by the limbs?

It is said: The meaning of that is other than what you have supposed. Rather its meaning is: whoever comes with the good deed and meets Allah with it as one obedient to Him, then for him is the reward of ten good deeds like it.

If he says: You say, then, is there a like for the statement "There is no god but Allah" among the good deeds? It is said: It has a like which is other than it, [but it has a like which is the statement "There is no god but Allah"] . [[This phrase between the parentheses is written thus in the manuscript; the first printed edition's editor altered it to read: "wa-laysa lahu mithl huwa qawl lā ilāha illā Allāh" (and it has no like which is the statement "There is no god but Allah"), and I do not know what this expression means. The manuscript's wording is not intelligible, and I fear that something has fallen out of the text, so I have placed it between brackets so that its reader may pause over it, perhaps something will become clear to him that has not become clear to me.]] And that is what Allah, may His praise be exalted, promised to whoever comes to Him with it: that He will recompense him for it with a reward like ten times what its speaker deserves. Likewise it is with whoever comes with the evil deed, which is associating partners, except that its doer is not recompensed for it except with what he deserves for it, without multiplication upon him.

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said.

Then the obligatory duties were revealed after that: fasting in Ramadan and zakat.

* *

If someone says: How is it said "ten times its like," where "ten" is annexed to "its likes," and "its likes" are themselves "likes"? Can a thing be annexed to itself? It is said: It is annexed to it because what is intended by it is: ten good deeds like it. So "the likes" takes the place of the explained noun, and "ten" is annexed to it, just as one says: "I have ten women" ('indi 'ashr niswah). Because the likes are intended by their standing, it is said: "ten likes of it," so "ten" is placed in the position of the number of good deeds, [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "the number of verses," but the text indicates "the number of good deeds," and there is no mention of verses in this place.]] and "mithl" (like) is masculine, not feminine, but since it was placed in the position of the good deeds, [[In the manuscript and printed edition here too: "the position of the verses," and the correct reading is what I have set down.]] and "mithl" can be used for the masculine and the feminine, it was made a substitute for them, and it was treated as I have described. Whoever says "ʿindī ʿashru amthālihā" ("I have ten likes of it") does not say "ʿindī ʿashru ṣāliḥāt" ("I have ten good deeds"), because "ṣāliḥāt" is a verb that is not counted, whereas nouns are counted. And "mithl" is a noun, and therefore numbering with it is permissible.

* *

It is mentioned from al-Hasan al-Basri that he used to read it: "fa-lahu ʿashrun" with tanwin, and "amthāluhā" with the nominative (raf'). That is a valid form in Arabic, but the reciters in the major cities are in disagreement with it, so we do not permit departing from what they are agreed upon. [[In the printed edition: "mujtami'ah" (gathered); I have set down what is in the manuscript.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 161:

The explanation of His words: ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a correct religion, the way of Abraham, a ḥanīf; and he was not of those who associate others with Allah﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to these who ascribe equals to their Lord, the idols and the images: ﴿Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path﴾, meaning: Say to them that my Lord has guided me to the right way, which is the religion of Allah with which He sent me, and that is the upright monotheism (al-ḥanīfiyyah al-muslimah), and He has granted me success in it. [[See the explanation of "guidance" (al-hudā) in the earlier lexical indices under (h-d-y), and the explanation of "straight path" (ṣirāt mustaqīm) earlier on p. 288, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿A correct religion﴾, meaning: upright. ﴿The way of Abraham﴾, meaning: the religion of Abraham. [[See the explanation of "millah" (religious community/way) earlier at 2:563 / 3:104 / 9:250.]] ﴿A ḥanīf﴾, meaning: upright. ﴿And he was not of those who associate others with Allah﴾, meaning: and he was not of those who associated others with Allah, namely Abraham, peace be upon him, because he was not among those who worshipped idols.

* *

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His words: ﴿dīnan qayyiman﴾.

The majority of the readers of Medina and some of the Basran readers recited it as "dīnan qayyiman" with a fatḥah on the qāf and a shaddah on the yā', assimilating it to the words of Allah: ﴿That is the upright religion﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 36 / Surah Yusuf: 40 / Surah al-Rum: 30], and to His words: ﴿And that is the religion of the upright community﴾ [Surah al-Bayyinah: 5].

* *

The majority of the Kufan readers recited it as ﴿dīnan qiyaman﴾ with a kasrah on the qāf and a fatḥah on the yā' without shaddah. They said: "al-qayyim" and "al-qiyam" have one meaning, and they are two dialects, both meaning: the upright religion.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in my judgment, is that they are two well-known readings among the readers of the regions, agreeing in meaning, so whichever of the two a reader recites is correct; however, the fatḥah on the qāf and the shaddah on the yā' are more pleasing to me, because it is the more eloquent and more widely known of the two dialects.

* *

The accusative of His words ﴿dīnan﴾ is governed as a verbal noun (maṣdar) from the sense of His words: ﴿Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path﴾. The meaning is: my Lord has guided me to an upright religion, so I have been guided to it, "a correct religion." Thus "dīnan" is governed by the omitted verb "ihtadaytu" (I have been guided), for which His words ﴿Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path﴾ stand as a substitute.

* *

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is in the accusative only because, when He said ﴿my Lord has guided me to a straight path﴾, He had informed that he had come to know something, so He said "dīnan qayyiman," as if He had said: "I have known a correct religion, the community of Abraham."

* *

As for the meaning of ḥanīf, I have explained it in its place in Surah al-Baqarah with its evidences, sufficing without repeating it in this place. [[See the explanation of "ḥanīf" earlier at 3:104–108 / 6:494 / 9:250, 251 / 11:487.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verses 162–163:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer and my sacrifice, my living and my dying, are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. No partner has He. And this I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to these who ascribe equals to their Lord, the idols and images, who ask you to follow their desires in falsehood, by worshipping the deities and idols: ﴿Indeed, my prayer and my sacrifice﴾, meaning: and my slaughter [[See the explanation of "nusuk" (sacrifice, rite) in earlier passages: 3:77–80 / 4:86, 195.]] ﴿and my living﴾, meaning: and my life ﴿and my dying﴾, meaning: and my death ﴿are for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning: all of that is exclusively for Him, apart from what you, O polytheists, associate with Him of idols ﴿No partner has He﴾ in any of that, from among His creation, nor does any of them have a share in it, because it is not fitting that this be for anyone but Him exclusively. ﴿And this I have been commanded﴾, meaning: and my Lord has commanded me with this ﴿and I am the first of the Muslims﴾, meaning: and I am the first of this community to acknowledge, submit and humble himself before his Lord, that it is so. [[See the explanation of "Islam" in the earlier lexical indices, root (s-l-m).]]

* *

And the people of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verses 162–163:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer and my sacrifice, my living and my dying, are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. No partner has He. And this I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to these who ascribe equals to their Lord, the idols and images, who ask you to follow their desires in falsehood, by worshipping the deities and idols: ﴿Indeed, my prayer and my sacrifice﴾, meaning: and my slaughter [[See the explanation of "nusuk" (sacrifice, rite) in earlier passages: 3:77–80 / 4:86, 195.]] ﴿and my living﴾, meaning: and my life ﴿and my dying﴾, meaning: and my death ﴿are for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning: all of that is exclusively for Him, apart from what you, O polytheists, associate with Him of idols ﴿No partner has He﴾ in any of that, from among His creation, nor does any of them have a share in it, because it is not fitting that this be for anyone but Him exclusively. ﴿And this I have been commanded﴾, meaning: and my Lord has commanded me with this ﴿and I am the first of the Muslims﴾, meaning: and I am the first of this community to acknowledge, submit and humble himself before his Lord, that it is so. [[See the explanation of "Islam" in the earlier lexical indices, root (s-l-m).]]

* *

And the people of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

As for His saying: ﴿and I am the first of the Muslims﴾, then:

14306 - Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada: ﴿and I am the first of the Muslims﴾, he said: the first of the Muslims of this community.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 164:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Say: Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, when He is the Lord of all things? And every soul earns only against itself, and no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾

Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to these who equate the idols with their Lord, who invite you to worship idols and to follow the steps of Satan: ﴿Shall I seek a lord other than Allah?﴾ That is: Shall I seek a master other than Allah to rule over me? [See the explanation of "bagha" (seeking) earlier, vol. 11, p. 337, note 2, and the references there.] (And He is the Lord of all things), that is: He is the master of everything besides Him, its manager and its improver [See the explanation of "al-Rabb" (the Lord) earlier, vol. 1, p. 142.] ﴿And every soul earns only against itself﴾, that is: no soul commits sin except to its own detriment; that is, no one is taken to account for the disobedience of Allah, blessed and exalted is He, or the wrongdoing that another has committed, but every sinner is punished for his own sin and seized for his own wrong [See the explanation of "kasb" (earning) earlier, vol. 6, p. 266, note 2, and the references there.] ﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾, that is: no sinful soul shall sin with the sin of another soul other than itself; rather, it sins with its own sin, and for it is it punished, without the sin of any other.

What is meant by this are the polytheists, to whom Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to say this statement. That is: say to them, "We are not taken to account for your sins, and you have the punishment of your crimes, and we have the reward of our deeds." This is like the command of Allah, mighty is His praise, in another place that he say to them: ﴿To you is your religion, and to me is my religion﴾ [Surah al-Kafirun: 6]. And that is as follows:

14307 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: In that time, there was no escape for the worshipping scholars except one of two traits: one of them is better than its companion: either commanding and calling to the truth, or withdrawal. So do not share in the deeds of the people of falsehood, perform the obligations between yourself and your Lord, love for Allah and hate for Allah, and do not share in anyone's sin. He said: And in that regard a clear verse was revealed: ﴿Say: Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, when He is the Lord of all things?﴾ up to His saying: ﴿concerning which you differ﴾, and concerning that He said: ﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not divide except after clear evidence had come to them﴾ [Surah al-Bayyinah: 4].

* *

It is said from "al-wizr" (burden): "wazara yazirु wizran," and "wazara yawzaru," and "wuzira yu'zaru, fa huwa mawzur." [In the printed edition: "wazara yawzaru fa huwa wazir, and wazara yawzaru fa huwa mawzur," which differs from the manuscript, and the printed edition omitted and added on its own; its excuse is the poor writing of the manuscript's copyist, and the correct reading of what is in it is what has been established. And it conforms to the text of the lexicographical books.]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about that over which you used to differ﴾ (164)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say to these who equate the idols with their Lord: Every worker among us and among you has the reward of his work and bears its burden. So do what you are doing, ﴿then to your Lord﴾, O people, ﴿is your return﴾, that is: then to Him is your destination and your turning [See the explanation of "al-marji'" (return) earlier, p. 37, note 3, and the references there.] ﴿and He will inform you about what you used to be in﴾, in this world, ﴿differ﴾ regarding religions and creeds [See the explanation of "al-naba'" (news) earlier, p. 274, note 1, and the references there.], when some of you adhered to Judaism, some to Christianity, some to Magianism, and some to the worship of idols and claiming partners and equals with Allah. Then He will repay all of you for what you used to do in this world, of good or evil, so that you will know then who among us is the doer of good and who is the doer of evil.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And it is He who made you successors upon the earth and raised some of you above others in degrees, to test you through what He has given you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and his nation: And Allah is the One who made you, O people, ﴿successors of the earth﴾, by destroying those before you of the generations and past nations, and He made you successors from them on the earth, replacing them in it, and cultivating it after them.

* *

"Al-khala'if" is the plural of "khalifah," as "al-wasa'if" is the plural of "wasifah," and it comes from the saying of the speaker: "Fulan khalafa fulanan fi darihi yakhlufuhu khilafatan, fa huwa khalifatun fiha" [See the explanation of "al-khalifah" earlier, vol. 1, pp. 449–453.], as al-Shammakh said:

"They are struck by death, and it misses me, and I succeed in abodes after abodes" [His Diwan, p. 58; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah, vol. 1, p. 209; Lisan al-Arab (rabi'); from his qasida which he said to his wife 'A'ishah, who used to blame him for his long preoccupation with his wealth. Its beginning: "O 'A'ishah, what is with your people, I do not see them wasting the camels with the wasteful..."

He means: she blames me for reforming my wealth; why do I see your people being stingy with themselves and not squandering their wealth in generosity and liberality? Then he says to her after some verses: "The wealth of a man, when it reforms him, makes him sufficient, its needs, more chaste than begging."

"Al-qunu'" is asking. His saying "wa akhlafu fi rubu'in..." — "al-rubu'" is the plural of "rab'," which is the group of people who settle in a "rab'" they inhabit; he means: I remain among a people after a people. In my view this verse is out of place in the qasida of al-Shammakh, and something of his poetry preceding it has fallen out.]

As follows:

14308 - Al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And it is He who made you successors of the earth﴾, he said: As for "successors of the earth," He destroyed the generations and made us successors in it after them.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and raised some of you above others in degrees﴾, He says: He varied your conditions, making some of you above others, by raising this one above that one, through the provision He spread out for this one, favoring him with the wealth and riches He gave him over this poor one in the means of the world He granted him; and this one over that one through the strength and power He gave him over this weak one with feeble strength. Thus He differentiated among them, raising the rank of this one above the rank of that one, and lowering the rank of this one below the rank of that one [See the explanation of "al-daraja" (degree) earlier, p. 25, note 3, and the references there.] As follows:

14309 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿and raised some of you above others in degrees﴾, he says: in provision.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿to test you through what He has given you﴾, He means: to examine you regarding what He has granted you of His bounty and bestowed of His provision, so He knows who among you obeys Him in what He commands and forbids, and who disobeys; and who among you fulfills from what He has given him the right He commanded him to pay from it, and who neglects its payment [See the explanation of "al-ibtila'" (trial) earlier, vol. 10, p. 582, note 1, and the references there; and the explanation of "al-ita'" (giving) in the language indexes under (ataa).]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 165:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (165)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His praise, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Indeed your Lord," O Muhammad, "is swift in punishment for whoever angers Him by committing His disobedience and opposing His command and prohibition, and for whoever turns away and withdraws from Him, despite His blessing him and His bounty and generosity, and His establishing him on the earth, as He did with the past generations." ﴿And indeed He is Forgiving﴾, that is: and indeed He is one who covers the sins of whoever turns to Him in obedience when He tests him with a blessing and examines him with His command and prohibition, so He conceals those sins for him and does not expose him by them at the place of reckoning. ﴿Merciful﴾ by His leaving off punishing him for his past sins that preceded between him and Him, since he repented and turned back to Him before meeting Him and returning to Him. [[See the explanation of the words of this verse in the earlier lexical indices.
